docs.text: The card's sealed profile bootstrap-readonly-v1 pins an image with bash and a Go toolchain but no git binary, and the worker runs with a read-only rootfs and no network. An empty checkout is therefore treated as a working tree with no entries, which is what the consumer repository actually starts as, and the whole claim stays provable in the only environment that gates this card.

docs.title: The allowlist
docs.text:
demo-repo/scaffold/allowlist.manifest is line-oriented so every field is matched by an exact expression:

schema: aurum.demo-scaffold-allowlist
version: 1
tree-root: tree
limit: <name> <value>
scenario: <id> <entry-count>
entry: <scenario-id|-> <mode> <bytes> <sha256> <path>

Entries are sorted by path. - marks an entry that belongs to no scenario. The manifest describes demo-repo/scaffold/tree, which holds the payload that reaches the consumer; scaffold.sh and the manifest itself are control files and are never copied.

docs.title: What keeps private data out
docs.text:
An allowlist alone is data, and data can be tampered with, so three independent rules have to hold before anything is written:

  1. Path closure. Every file under tree/ must be an allowlist entry (path-not-allowlisted) and every entry must be present (entry-missing).
  2. Path policy, which no manifest can widen. An entry path must be a safe relative path of at most 128 bytes matching [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._/-]* with no .. segment (path-shape-denied), and no segment may name an AurumCode-private root -- .board, .git, .github, .taskmaster, .claude, .ssh, .aurum-bootstrap, credentials, secrets, internal, or a .env file (private-path-denied). A symlink is refused outright (symlink-denied), so nothing can be imported by reference.
  3. Payload screen. Bytes are read, not merely hashed. A payload carrying an AurumCode-private marker (private-marker-detected) or a value shaped like a real credential -- PEM private key headers, AKIA..., sk-..., gh?_... (credential-shape-detected) -- is refused even when the manifest seals its digest correctly.

The synthetic placeholder shape AURUM-FAKE-<NAME> is deliberately not private. The catalog contains a scenario about a leaked credential, and it has to survive the screen; that is what stops the screen from passing by refusing everything.

After the copy, path closure, digests and the payload screen are applied again to the bytes that actually landed. A copier that writes a file nobody allowlisted is caught there (unlisted-entry-copied) even though the scaffold it read was clean.

docs.title: Domain limits
docs.text:
limit value first value beyond it max_entries 64 65 entries -> too-many-entries max_file_bytes 65536 65537 bytes -> file-too-large max_total_bytes 1048576 beyond -> tree-too-large max_path_bytes 128 129 bytes -> path-too-long max_scenarios 32 33 scenarios -> too-many-scenarios

The limits are constants in the bootstrap and are also declared in the manifest. A manifest that declares a different number is refused with limit-divergence: the domain lives in the program, never in the data.

docs.title: The sealed catalog
docs.text:
Six scenarios, 15 entries, all synthetic:

scenario kind what a review of it should say clean-change clean nothing to report docs-drift documentation the document no longer matches the code flaky-test test quality the test depends on wall-clock timing null-deref correctness an absent lookup result is dereferenced secret-leak security a placeholder credential sits in source sql-injection security a query is built by string concatenation

Sealed values of the checked-in scaffold, recomputed by the acceptance on every run:

  • scaffold input digest (allowlist plus the tree it describes): sha256:c7b1832092b391d7437481ab0129380ad3d12e6ae27cc1db73035029812e92b1
  • consumer checkout digest after a nominal bootstrap: sha256:ab5a1b68eed1799a6838406959142eefae0828e05c008a08459d9809dc7c3b59

docs.title: Example (no secret involved)
docs.text:
Bootstrap the demo repository into an empty checkout. This is the same call the acceptance makes for the nominal-bootstrap vector, so the example cannot drift from the behavior:

out="$(mktemp -d)/consumer"
bash tests/e2e/consumer/bootstrap/bootstrap.sh demo-repo/scaffold "$out"
# consumer-bootstrap/bootstrapped entries=15 scenarios=6 \
#   tree_digest=sha256:ab5a1b68eed1799a6838406959142eefae0828e05c008a08459d9809dc7c3b59

Resealing the allowlist after a scenario changes, from the repository root:

cd demo-repo/scaffold
{
  sed -n '1,7p' allowlist.manifest
  for s in $(sed -n 's/^scenario: \([a-z0-9-]*\) .*/\1/p' allowlist.manifest); do
    printf 'scenario: %s %d\n' "$s" "$(cd tree && find "scenarios/$s" -type f | wc -l)"
  done
  (cd tree && find . -type f | sed 's|^\./||' | LC_ALL=C sort) | while read -r p; do
    case "$p" in scenarios/*/*) sc="${p#scenarios/}"; sc="${sc%%/*}" ;; *) sc='-' ;; esac
    printf 'entry: %s 0644 %s %s %s\n' "$sc" \
      "$(stat -c '%s' "tree/$p")" "$(sha256sum "tree/$p" | cut -d' ' -f1)" "$p"
  done
} > allowlist.manifest.new && mv allowlist.manifest.new allowlist.manifest

The acceptance recomputes the same values, so a manifest that drifts from the tree fails scaffold-manifest-divergence before any vector runs.

docs.title: Diagnosis
docs.text:
observation what it means AUR-012/AC-001/behavior-missing the scaffold or the bootstrap is absent AUR-012/AC-001/detector-missed:<vector> a planted vector was accepted AUR-012/AC-001/planted-undetected:<n> private material reached the copy stage AUR-012/AC-001/MUT-001 the copier put an unlisted file in the consumer AUR-012/AC-001/nominal:scenario-not-delivered:<path> a scenario did not arrive AUR-012/AC-001/vector-effects:<v>:want=0:got=<n> a refusal wrote to the checkout AUR-012/AC-001/inconclusive/... environment, never red evidence

consumer-bootstrap/inconclusive/... on stderr with exit 79 is likewise an environment result. Only exit 0 is green; exit 1 is behavioral red.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text: Running the scenarios is not part of this card. The bootstrap proves that an empty repository receives them; executing a review over them belongs to the end-to-end cards that consume this checkout.

docs.title: AUR-014: Versionar standard de code review
docs.text:
Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

This is a research and policy-data card. It does not ship a scanner, review engine, approval service, or publication adapter. It fixes a versioned catalog that later review cards can consume. The observable behavior is the bounded, offline acceptance lint in tests/acceptance/AUR-014.sh.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
tests/acceptance/AUR-014.sh with selector AC-001 reads the existing research baseline and standards/code-review/cases.yaml. It checks, without a network request, that each of the nine declared controls resolves exactly once to:

  1. an official source with an allowlisted HTTPS host, version, ISO date, and current status;
  2. one positive case whose expected verdict is pass;
  3. one negative case whose expected verdict is fail; and
  4. a local, non-empty fixture that names the matching control and is distinct from every other case fixture.

The acceptance program runs its own bounded synthetic self-tests before checking the repository catalog. Those tests prove that missing sources, withdrawn sources, non-allowlisted URLs, inverted verdicts, reused fixtures, identical fixtures, missing research, and missing controls are detected.

docs.title: Contract
docs.text:
• standards/code-review/cases.yaml is the sole machine-readable catalog.
  • The catalog contains exactly one row for each AUR-014 control: CR-EVD-001 through CR-EVD-003, CR-REV-001 through CR-REV-005, and CR-GATE-001.
  • A fixture path must remain below standards/code-review/, must be a regular local file, must contain its rule ID, and must not be reused by another case.
  • positive means expect: pass; negative means expect: fail.
  • Source URLs are checked as text against the allowlist embedded in the sealed acceptance program. No URL is fetched, and a citation is not evidence of external certification or conformity.
  • The crosswalk in standards/code-review/README.md records the card, AC, and mutation for every row. The card remains data-only; consumers implement behavior in dependent cards.

docs.title: Limits and compatibility
docs.text:
The catalog is bounded to 256 KiB by the acceptance program and uses only local fixtures. It does not run arbitrary fixture content, execute source code, or grant network, credential, write, or publication capabilities. Changes outside the AUR-014 paths are not part of this contract.

The delivery of this card follows the current lightweight process: one human-authored commit, the card acceptance command, and an independent validation by the coordinator. The retired multi-reviewer and candidate identity ceremony is not a behavior delivered by this card.

docs.title: Example (no secret)
docs.text:
With no network access or secret material:

$ tests/acceptance/AUR-014.sh AC-001
{"card":"AUR-014","scenario":"AC-001","result":"pass","controls":9,"rules":9,"cases":18}

The card's containerized command is:

$ ./.board/bin/oci-run --profile bootstrap-readonly-v1 --card AUR-014

docs.title: Diagnosis
docs.text:
• AUR-014/AC-001/missing-standard-dir or missing-catalog means the versioned catalog is absent from standards/code-review.
  • AUR-014/AC-001/missing-rule-case means a declared control has no catalog row, or the catalog could not be read as the bounded YAML subset.
  • duplicate-rule, missing-source, missing-version, missing-source-url, missing-source-date, or withdrawn-source identifies a source metadata defect in a catalog row.
  • source-url-not-allowlisted means the citation is not an HTTPS URL on an allowlisted primary-source host.
  • missing-positive-case, missing-negative-case, bad-case-kind, verdict-mismatch, missing-assert, missing-fixture, fixture-not-bound-to-rule, fixture-reused, or fixture-not-distinct identifies a case or fixture defect.
  • AUR-014/AC-001/infrastructure: ... is reserved for missing host tools, unreadable inputs, or an unavailable execution environment. It is never a behavioral pass or RED result.

docs.title: AUR-015: Versionar standard de secure code review
docs.text:
Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

This is a research/standard card. It does not ship an executable feature; it fixes the secure-code-review contract later security-office cards run against. The observable behavior is the acceptance lint itself: tests/acceptance/AUR-015.sh deterministically resolves the artifacts below and either passes or names exactly which one is incomplete.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
tests/acceptance/AUR-015.sh (selector AC-001) reads four artifacts this card owns and checks that they resolve to one consistent, testable crosswalk, without making any network request:

  1. .board/research/secure-code-review.md — the source-selection record and the working definitions of threat, trust boundary, and fail closed. AC-001 requires the four literal terms OWASP, threat, trust boundary, and fail closed to appear, case-insensitive, and this is the exact failure the card's Given/When/Then pins: missing any one of them prints AUR-015/AC-001: missing <term> and exits 1 before any other check runs.
  2. standards/security-review/rules.md — a ## Rules section containing exactly nine ### Rule: <ID> — <title> blocks, one per CR-* control this project already defines in .board/research/code-review-standards.md (CR-EVD-001–003, CR-REV-001–005, CR-GATE-001). Each block names an OWASP Top 10 category, a CWE identifier, and a NIST SSDF practice — each as a [label](url) | version <v> | <YYYY-MM-DD> citation — plus the bound control, a one-line trust-boundary statement, and a vulnerable and a fixed fixture path.
  3. tests/specs/AUR-015/rule-ids.txt and tests/specs/AUR-015/allowed-source-domains.txt — the single source of truth for, respectively, the nine rule IDs rules.md must resolve and the source hostnames an OWASP/CWE/NIST SSDF citation may cite.
  4. tests/specs/AUR-015/<rule-id>/vulnerable.md and tests/specs/AUR-015/<rule-id>/fixed.md — one pair per rule, each carrying a Fixture: VULNERABLE or Fixture: FIXED marker line; the lint refuses a pair that is missing, empty, mismarked, or byte-identical to its counterpart.

docs.title: Contract
docs.text:
• A rule's OWASP/CWE/NIST SSDF citation must resolve to an http(s) URL whose host is listed in tests/specs/AUR-015/allowed-source-domains.txt, a version matching [0-9]+(\.[0-9]+){0,2}, and an ISO-8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD). A missing, unversioned, undated, or non-allowlisted citation fails with the same typed code: AUR-015/AC-001/undecided-rule.
  • A rule's Control: line must match CR-(EVD|REV|GATE)-[0-9]{3} and no two rules may bind the same control; every one of the nine controls the card declares must be bound by exactly one rule.
  • A rule's CWE citation must resolve a numeric CWE-<n> identifier from its label text, independent of the URL.
  • Every rule ID in rules.md must be exactly one of the nine names in tests/specs/AUR-015/rule-ids.txt; a rule outside that set, a duplicate rule ID, or a rule-ids fixture that resolves to anything other than exactly nine names all fail with AUR-015/AC-001/undecided-rule (a corrupted or emptied fixture list is AUR-015/AC-001/behavior-missing, since the fixture is this card's own deliverable, not an external dependency).
  • This card produces no scanner, no CLI surface, and does not scan AurumCode's own source for the weaknesses it catalogs; that belongs to dependent security-office cards.

docs.title: Standard
docs.text: standards/security-review/rules.md fixes the nine-rule crosswalk this project enforces during secure code review; .board/research/secure-code-review.md fixes which three frameworks (OWASP Top 10, CWE, NIST SSDF) were selected over three rejected alternatives (ISO/IEC 27034, the SANS/CWE Top 25, and BSIMM) and why. Both are within this card's owned paths and are versioned together.

docs.title: Example (no secret)
docs.text:
Running the acceptance test directly, with no network access and no secret material of any kind:

$ ./.board/bin/oci-run --profile bootstrap-readonly-v1 --card AUR-015
{"card":"AUR-015","scenario":"AC-001","selector":"AC-001","rules":9,"result":"pass"}

A failing example — the baseline research document missing one of the four required terms:

$ tests/acceptance/AUR-015.sh
AUR-015/AC-001: missing trust boundary

A failing example — a rule's CWE citation loses its control binding:

$ tests/acceptance/AUR-015.sh
AUR-015/AC-001/undecided-rule: SCR-001: control is missing or not a CR-<FAMILY>-<NNN> id:

docs.title: Diagnosis
docs.text:
• AUR-015/AC-001: missing <term> — .board/research/secure-code-review.md is missing one of OWASP, threat, trust boundary, or fail closed, case-insensitive. Restore the term.
  • AUR-015/AC-001/behavior-missing: required artifact absent: <path> — one of the four card-owned artifacts (the research file, rules.md, or a tests/specs/AUR-015/* fixture) is missing, empty, or a symlink. Restore it from the card's owned paths.
  • AUR-015/AC-001/undecided-rule: rule id not in tests/specs/AUR-015/rule-ids.txt: <id> — rules.md names a rule ID outside the fixed nine-ID set. Either fix the ID or add it to rule-ids.txt and give it a rule block.
  • AUR-015/AC-001/undecided-rule: <id>: <label> source host is not allowlisted: <host> — a citation's URL host is not in allowed-source-domains.txt. Fix the citation or extend the allowlist with a reviewed change.
  • AUR-015/AC-001/undecided-rule: <id>: <label> has no versioned source: <v> or ... source date is not ISO 8601: <date> — the cited version or date is missing or malformed. Fix the citation.
  • AUR-015/AC-001/undecided-rule: <id>: control is missing or not a CR-<FAMILY>-<NNN> id: <value> or ... control already bound to another rule: <control> or expected control has no bound rule: <control> — the rule's control binding is missing, malformed, duplicated, or the nine-control coverage is incomplete. Fix the Control: line.
  • AUR-015/AC-001/undecided-rule: <id>: fixture absent: <path>, ... is empty: <path>, ... is missing its 'Fixture: <MARKER>' marker: <path>, or ... vulnerable and fixed fixtures are byte-identical: <path> — the named rule's fixture pair under tests/specs/AUR-015/<id>/ is missing, empty, mismarked, or not actually distinguishable. Fix the fixture pair.
  • AUR-015/AC-001/infrastructure: ... — a required host tool is missing or the repository root could not be resolved; this is never a behavioral result and never counts as RED evidence for this card.

docs.title: Integration
docs.text:
tests/integration/AUR-015_test.go::TestAUR015Boundary is a Test-prefixed Go function, discoverable and run by the ordinary go test ./... suite with no external dispatcher. It re-derives, from the source files themselves (never from tests/acceptance/AUR-015.sh's own output), the same structural contract AC-001 enforces: the four required terms in the research baseline, the nine ### Rule: blocks in rules.md each resolving a versioned, dated, allowlisted OWASP/CWE/NIST SSDF citation and exactly one of the nine expected CR-* controls, and every rule's vulnerable/fixed fixture pair existing, marked, and mutually distinguishable. If any card-owned artifact disappears, or rules.md/the crosswalk loses a rule, a citation, or a control binding, this test fails closed independently of the acceptance container.

This resolves the tests/integration/AUR-015.go::IntegrationAUR015 path the card originally declared, which the same structural defect AUR-020's first two rounds hit: a .go file without a _test.go suffix is invisible to go test's file scanner, so no function inside it is ever discovered or run. .board/cards/ready/AUR-015.md was bumped to version 2 (mirroring AUR-020's own version-2 bump) to rename the declared path to tests/integration/AUR-015_test.go::TestAUR015Boundary, which this file now implements.

docs.title: AUR-016: Definir uso evidencial de ISO 25010
docs.text:
Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

This is a research/vocabulary card. It does not ship an executable feature or a scoring engine; it fixes a vocabulary and an abstention rule that later quality-evidence cards implement against. The observable behavior is the acceptance lint itself: tests/acceptance/AUR-016.sh deterministically resolves the artifacts below and either passes or names exactly which one is incomplete.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
tests/acceptance/AUR-016.sh (selector AC-001) reads four artifacts this card owns and checks that they resolve to one consistent, evidence-honest vocabulary, without making any network request:

  1. .board/research/quality-standards.md — literally contains the string ISO/IEC 25010:2023, contains, case-insensitively, the phrase does not claim conformity, and carries a ## Sources examined table whose rows each cite a [label](url) source with an allowlisted host, a version token, and an ISO-8601 date.
  2. standards/quality/README.md — states the abstention rule in fixed terms: the literal status name not_assessed, and a sentence forbidding a score without a wired metric.
  3. standards/quality/characteristics.yaml — one entry for each of the nine ISO/IEC 25010:2023 characteristics, each carrying name, measurable, status, score, metric, and metric_source.
  4. tests/specs/AUR-016/characteristics.txt and tests/specs/AUR-016/allowed-source-domains.txt — the fixed nine characteristic names and the source-host allowlist the lint resolves against.

The lint parses characteristics.yaml structurally (no YAML library — the acceptance program runs alone inside a minimal, network-denied container) and enforces the abstention rule as data, not prose: every entry with measurable: false must have status: not_assessed and score: null; every entry with status: measured must have measurable: true, a non-null metric, a non-null metric_source, and a numeric score.

docs.title: Contract
docs.text:
• tests/specs/AUR-016/characteristics.txt and tests/specs/AUR-016/allowed-source-domains.txt are the single source of truth for, respectively, the exact nine characteristic names the standards table must resolve, and the hostnames a research-document Source link may cite. The shell acceptance test reads these two files instead of duplicating the lists.
  • A ## Sources examined row's Version cell must match Edition N, vN(.N)(.N), revYYYY, or post YYYY-MM-DD; its Date cell must be an ISO-8601 calendar date.
  • A characteristic entry may carry a numeric score only if it is measurable: true and cites both a metric and a metric_source. Any entry with measurable: false (equivalently status: not_assessed) that also carries a non-null score fails with the typed code AUR-016/AC-001/score-without-signal.
  • Naming a metric without a metric_source (or the reverse) fails with AUR-016/AC-001/malformed-entry.
  • A characteristic name outside the fixed nine, a duplicate, or a missing required characteristic all fail with a typed code (unknown-characteristic, duplicate-characteristic, or missing-characteristic) naming the offending entry.
  • This card produces no quality score for the AurumCode repository and no approval threshold. Every characteristic in the shipped characteristics.yaml is not_assessed today; wiring a real, sourced, computed metric for any one characteristic is left to a dependent card that changes only that characteristic's row.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text: There is no numeric ceiling in this card — its only "limit" is the structural invariant standards/quality/README.md states in prose and characteristics.yaml encodes in data: a characteristic without an observable, currently wired metric MUST report not_assessed, and a numeric score MUST NOT appear without one.

docs.title: Example (no secret)
docs.text:
Running the acceptance test directly, with no network access and no secret material of any kind:

$ ./.board/bin/oci-run --profile bootstrap-readonly-v1 --card AUR-016
{"card":"AUR-016","scenario":"AC-001","selector":"AC-001","characteristics":9,"measured":0,"not_assessed":9,"result":"pass"}

A failing example — a characteristic entry assigned a numeric score with no wired metric behind it (MUT-001):

$ tests/acceptance/AUR-016.sh
AUR-016/AC-001/score-without-signal: Functional suitability: measurable is false but score is not null: 87

A failing example — a researched source replaced by a non-allowlisted host (MUT-002):

$ tests/acceptance/AUR-016.sh
AUR-016/AC-001/unversioned-source: source host is not allowlisted: evil.example.com

docs.title: Diagnosis
docs.text:
• AUR-016/AC-001/behavior-missing: required artifact absent: <path> — one of the research document, standards/quality/README.md, standards/quality/characteristics.yaml, or a tests/specs/AUR-016/* fixture is missing or empty. Restore it from the card's owned paths.
  • AUR-016/AC-001/behavior-missing: ... missing the literal version string ISO/IEC 25010:2023 or ... missing the case-insensitive phrase 'does not claim conformity' — the research document lost one of the two literal markers its own Given clause requires. Restore the exact string/phrase.
  • AUR-016/AC-001/unversioned-source: ... — a ## Sources examined row is missing a [label](url) link, cites a non-allowlisted host, has no parseable version token, or has a non-ISO-8601 date. Fix the offending cell.
  • AUR-016/AC-001/unknown-characteristic / duplicate-characteristic / missing-characteristic — the characteristics.yaml entry set no longer resolves 1:1 against tests/specs/AUR-016/characteristics.txt. Fix the entry name or the fixture.
  • AUR-016/AC-001/malformed-entry — measurable or status is not one of its two literal values, or metric/metric_source are inconsistently null. Fix the offending field.
  • AUR-016/AC-001/score-without-signal — a measurable: false (or status: not_assessed) entry carries a non-null score, or a status: measured entry is missing measurable: true, metric, metric_source, or a numeric score. This is the abstention-rule violation the card exists to prevent: remove the unsupported score, or wire a real metric and source before claiming measured.
  • AUR-016/AC-001/infrastructure: ... — a required host tool (awk/grep/sed/sort/wc) is missing or the repository root could not be resolved; this is never a behavioral result and never counts as RED evidence for this card.

docs.title: AUR-017: Fixar standards de artefatos interoperáveis
docs.text:
Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

This is a research/decision card. It does not ship an emitter, parser, or publisher for any of the four standards it fixes; it fixes the design contract dependent adapter cards implement against. The observable behavior is the acceptance lint itself: tests/acceptance/AUR-017.sh deterministically resolves the artifacts below and either passes or names exactly which one is incomplete.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
tests/acceptance/AUR-017.sh (selector AC-001) reads the artifacts this card owns and checks that they resolve to one consistent, versioned decision per standard, without making any network request:

  1. .board/research/interoperability.md — a "Standards matrix" table that fixes SARIF, unified diff, JSON Schema, and OpenAPI, one row per standard, each with a [label](url) source, a Version, an ISO-8601 Date, a Validator cell, and an Interoperability role cell — plus a prose "Interoperability context: MCP" section, since MCP is the reason the JSON Schema pin is an external interoperability boundary and not an internal choice, even though MCP itself has no fixed artifact version in this card's Outcome.
  2. standards/contracts/versions.yaml — the single source of truth for the exact pinned version (and, for SARIF and JSON Schema, the exact schema/dialect URI) per standard.
  3. standards/contracts/<format>/validator.md — names the real validator tool and version a later adapter card will run, and the bounded structural rule this card's own lint checks in its place.
  4. standards/contracts/<format>/fixtures/valid.* and invalid.* — one minimal example each format's structural rule accepts and rejects.

The lint also re-checks the three literal terms the Outcome/Given clause names directly (SARIF 2.1.0, OpenAI, MCP), case-sensitive, in .board/research/interoperability.md.

docs.title: Contract
docs.text:
• tests/specs/AUR-017/formats.txt and tests/specs/AUR-017/allowed-source-domains.txt are the single source of truth for, respectively, the exact four standard names the matrix and standards/contracts must resolve, and the hostnames a matrix Source link may cite. tests/acceptance/AUR-017.sh reads both instead of duplicating the lists.
  • A matrix row's Version cell must match a semantic-version-like pattern (2.1.0, 3.10), a JSON-Schema-style draft-date identifier (2020-12), or an immutable post identifier (post 1904957253456941061) paired with its Date — the same three shapes AUR-020 fixed, reused rather than reinvented.
  • Each standard's matrix Version cell must equal standards/contracts/versions.yaml's pinned version for that standard, and each standard's fixtures/valid.* must itself declare that same pinned version (and, where applicable, the pinned schema/dialect URI). Divergence between the matrix, the pin, or the fixture — the shape of MUT-001 — fails with the same typed code: AUR-017/AC-001/undecided-standard.
  • A Source cell whose host is not in tests/specs/AUR-017/allowed-source-domains.txt, or whose Version cannot be resolved as versioned/dated — the shape of MUT-002 — fails the same way.
  • Each format's fixtures/invalid.* must be rejected by this card's own bounded structural lint for the single reason its validator.md names; a fixture that lint accepts by mistake also fails with AUR-017/AC-001/undecided-standard.
  • This card produces no SARIF emitter, diff generator, schema author, or OpenAPI publisher, and it does not install or invoke any of the named validator tools. The SARIF, unified-diff, JSON Schema, and OpenAPI surfaces it fixes are implemented by dependent O05-review, O06-scm, O04-agents/O11-mcp, and integration adapter cards, not here.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text: There is no separate limits file for this card; the only bounded quantities it fixes are the exact pinned versions and schema/dialect URIs in standards/contracts/versions.yaml, which a consumer repository may not raise past what is declared there without a separate, reviewed change to that file.

docs.title: Example (no secret)
docs.text:
Running the acceptance test directly, with no network access and no secret material of any kind:

$ ./.board/bin/oci-run --profile bootstrap-readonly-v1 --card AUR-017
{"card":"AUR-017","scenario":"AC-001","selector":"AC-001","standards_fixed":4,"criteria_columns":2,"result":"pass"}

A failing example — the SARIF fixture's $schema value edited to a different host:

$ tests/acceptance/AUR-017.sh
AUR-017/AC-001/undecided-standard: sarif valid fixture rejected by lint: schema mismatch: got "https://example.invalid/sarif-schema-2.1.0.json" want "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oasis-tcs/sarif-spec/master/Schemata/sarif-schema-2.1.0.json"

docs.title: Diagnosis
docs.text:
• AUR-017/AC-001/undecided-standard: required artifact absent: <path> (or ... is empty: <path>) — one of interoperability.md, standards/contracts/versions.yaml, standards/contracts/README.md, or a tests/specs/AUR-017/* fixture is missing or empty. Restore it from the card's owned paths.
  • AUR-017/AC-001/undecided-standard: research is missing required term: <term> — one of the three literal Outcome terms (SARIF 2.1.0, OpenAI, MCP) was removed from .board/research/interoperability.md.
  • AUR-017/AC-001/undecided-standard: standard <name> ... — the matrix row for that standard is missing, duplicated, has no versioned source, has a non-ISO date, cites a non-allowlisted source host, or has an empty criterion cell. Fix the offending cell in the "Standards matrix" table.
  • AUR-017/AC-001/undecided-standard: standard <name> matrix version (...) diverges from standards/contracts/versions.yaml (...) — the matrix Version cell and the pin in versions.yaml disagree; make them equal.
  • AUR-017/AC-001/undecided-standard: <format> valid fixture rejected by lint: <reason> — the format's fixtures/valid.* no longer satisfies its own validator.md rule (commonly: its embedded version or schema/dialect URI no longer matches versions.yaml after a version bump). Migrate the fixture.
  • AUR-017/AC-001/undecided-standard: <format> invalid fixture was accepted by lint; it must be rejected — the format's fixtures/invalid.* was edited into something the structural lint no longer rejects; restore a fixture that fails for the single reason its validator.md names.
  • AUR-017/AC-001/infrastructure: ... — a required host tool is missing or the repository root could not be resolved; this is never a behavioral result and never counts as RED evidence for this card.

docs.title: AUR-018 — Fixar contratos SCM e CI seguros
docs.text: Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
This card fixes, as data, the capability and trust-boundary matrix that any future GitHub, Gitea, or GitLab adapter must respect. It does not implement a client, a webhook receiver, or a CI pipeline. Two roles are distinguished everywhere in the matrix:

  • analyzer — reads a change, including one whose head may be hostile (a fork or an external branch not owned by a maintainer). It is presented only a read-only credential, on every forge, with no exception.
  • publisher — writes a result back (a comment, check, status, or release). It always runs in a context decoupled from the hostile-head checkout the analyzer used, and only there may it hold a write-scoped credential.

docs.title: Contract
docs.text:
• .board/research/scm-ci.md is the dated, versioned research: one row per vendor source actually consulted, and a matrix table naming the analyzer and publisher credential, scope, and trust boundary for GitHub, Gitea, and GitLab.
  • standards/scm/capabilities.yaml is the machine-readable form of that matrix: forges.<name>.analyzer, forges.<name>.publisher, and the cross-forge rule.hostile_head_read_only invariant. A future adapter card reads this file; it does not re-derive scopes from prose.
  • tests/acceptance/AUR-018.sh::AC-001 is the sole executable gate for this card: it requires .board/research/scm-ci.md to exist, be non-empty, and contain, case-insensitively, GitHub, Gitea, GitLab, analyzer, publisher, and least privilege. Absence of any one term is the invalid vector and exits non-zero before any effect outside paths.
  • tests/integration/AUR-018_test.go (TestAUR018Boundary) is the structural lint, discoverable by go test ./tests/integration/...: it parses standards/scm/capabilities.yaml, requires all three forges to declare both roles, requires allow_write_on_hostile_head: false everywhere, cross-checks that every forge named in capabilities.yaml also appears in the matrix table of scm-ci.md (so the machine-readable limits and the human-readable research can never diverge), and requires every source cited in scm-ci.md to name an allowlisted vendor-docs domain together with a version or an access date — the same shape MUT-002 targets.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• standards/scm/capabilities.yaml's limits.max_token_scopes_per_role: 3 bounds how many scope entries an adapter may request per role per forge.
  • limits.allowed_analyzer_ci_events / forbidden_analyzer_ci_events bound which CI trigger the analyzer role may run under; GitHub's pull_request_target and workflow_run are explicitly forbidden for the analyzer because GitHub's own docs describe them as privileged even when triggered from a public fork.
  • No role in any forge entry may set allow_write_on_hostile_head: true; MUT-001 proves the acceptance path rejects that change.

docs.title: Example (no secret involved)
docs.text:
$ ./.board/bin/oci-run --profile bootstrap-readonly-v1 --card AUR-018
{"card":"AUR-018","scenario":"AC-001","result":"pass"}
$ echo $?
0

Removing any one of the six required terms from .board/research/scm-ci.md (for example replacing least privilege with a paraphrase) reproduces the invalid vector:

$ sed 's/least privilege/least-priv only/' .board/research/scm-ci.md > /tmp/scm-ci-mut.md
$ f=/tmp/scm-ci-mut.md bash -c 'grep -Fiq "least privilege" "$f"'; echo $?
1

docs.title: Diagnostic procedure
docs.text:
1. Run the accept command above and capture exit_code and stdout_sha256 from the oci-run JSON envelope.
  2. If exit_code != 0, stderr names the missing term (AUR-018/AC-001: SCM/CI baseline absent when the file itself is missing or empty, or a bare non-zero exit from the term loop otherwise) — check .board/research/scm-ci.md for the six required terms first.
  3. Run go test ./tests/integration/... to check the structural lint independently of the shell gate; a failure there names which forge, role, or source row is missing or malformed in standards/scm/capabilities.yaml or .board/research/scm-ci.md.
  4. Confirm no output at any step contains AURUM_SECRET_CANARY.

docs.title: AUR-019: Fixar contratos oficiais de providers
docs.text:
Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

This is a research/decision card. It does not ship an executable client; it fixes a design contract that later O0x provider-adapter cards implement against. The observable behavior is the acceptance lint itself: tests/acceptance/AUR-019.sh deterministically resolves the artifacts below and either passes or names exactly which one is incomplete.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
tests/acceptance/AUR-019.sh (selector AC-001) reads the artifacts this card owns and checks that they resolve to one consistent, versioned, fixture-backed set of provider contracts, without making any network request:

  1. .board/research/providers.md — a "Provider contracts matrix" table that names all seven required providers (OpenAI, LiteLLM, Anthropic, Ollama, Azure, Gemini, Bedrock), each with a [label](url) source, a version, an ISO-8601 date, and exactly four canonical criterion cells (Wire format, Auth, Error taxonomy, Capabilities). Each cell is compared byte-for-byte with the corresponding projection of the matching standards/providers/<slug>.yaml record.
  2. standards/providers/<slug>.yaml, one per required provider (slug is the lowercase provider name) — a flat key/value record of the same provider's transport (http or sdk-call), wire endpoint/method/ content-type, auth scheme/header/binding/format (or, for sdk-call, wire_call), error envelope/taxonomy, and a capability_<name>: supported|unsupported entry for every capability in tests/specs/AUR-019/capabilities.txt.
  3. tests/specs/AUR-019/fixtures/<slug>/<capability>.json — a recorded, non-secret fixture for every capability_<name>: supported entry, bound to its file by matching "capability"/"provider" JSON fields and by matching the fields its own provider's declared transport requires (request.method/request.path/request.headers for transport: http; request.call/request.params for transport: sdk-call) against that same provider's wire_method/wire_endpoint/auth_header/wire_call (see "Fixture wire-binding invariant" below).

docs.title: Contract
docs.text:
• tests/specs/AUR-019/provider-names.txt, tests/specs/AUR-019/capabilities.txt and tests/specs/AUR-019/allowed-source-domains.txt are the single source of truth for, respectively, the seven required provider names, the tracked capability keys, and the hostnames a source:/matrix Source link may cite. Both the shell acceptance test and tests/integration/AUR-019_test.go read these three files instead of duplicating the lists. provider-names.txt must declare exactly 7 entries and capabilities.txt exactly 3 (streaming, tool_use, structured_output), and in both files every entry must be distinct in both readers: a count check alone does not prove a required provider (or capability) was actually validated, only that the right number of lines exist. A padded, duplicated provider-names.txt fails typed AUR-019/AC-001/undecided-provider before either reader drives a single downstream check off it. Both readers additionally tally the distinct standards/providers/<slug>.yaml paths they actually opened during the provider loop and require that tally to equal the required provider count, as a second, independent proof that every required provider's own file -- not the same file revisited -- was the one validated.
  • A matrix or standards-file version must match a semantic-version-like pattern (v2.53.0) or a dated API-version string (2024-10-21, the shape Azure's own api-version query parameter uses); date is always a separate ISO-8601 calendar date for when the cited source was read.
  • The URL inside every source link must itself contain the declared version (with an optional leading v for release tags); mutable /latest, branch, main, master, trunk, and HEAD references are rejected.
  • Every capability_<name>: supported entry in a standards/providers file must have a matching fixture_<name>: entry pointing at an existing, non-empty, JSON-valid fixture whose own capability and provider fields match the declaration; a mismatch or absence fails with the typed code AUR-019/AC-001/unfixtured-capability. "JSON-valid" is enforced, not assumed: see "Fixture canonical-form invariant" below for how the sealed accept gate actually parses every fixture as JSON instead of trusting two grepped substrings.
  • The fixture_<name> value must be exactly tests/specs/AUR-019/fixtures/<provider-slug>/<name>.json. Absolute paths, .., decoy descendants, .flat sidecars, final symlinks, and symlinked ancestors are rejected by both readers. The fixture's top-level source must equal the provider YAML source and use the same versioned URL.
  • A missing provider, a matrix row cited twice, an empty criterion cell, or a standards/providers file missing a required flat key fails with AUR-019/AC-001/undecided-provider.
  • A non-allowlisted source host, an unversioned source, or a non-ISO date — in either the matrix or a standards/providers file — fails with AUR-019/AC-001/unsourced-provider.
  • This card produces no HTTP client, no SDK dependency, and no network call. The seven provider adapters that implement pkg/types.Provider against this contract are separate, dependent cards.

docs.title: Fixtures
docs.text: tests/specs/AUR-019/fixtures/<slug>/<capability>.json records, for every provider/capability pair marked supported, the documented request and response shape transcribed from the cited source — never a live call, never a credential. Currently every one of the 7 providers × 3 tracked capabilities (streaming, tool_use, structured_output) is marked supported, so all 21 fixtures exist. Every fixture is written by hand transcribing the cited source, then normalized into this card's canonical JSON form described in "Fixture canonical-form invariant" below before it is committed; the acceptance gate's check_fixture_canonical_form is the only authority that enforces that form, and it runs inside the sealed container.

docs.title: Example (no secret)
docs.text:
Running the acceptance test directly, with no network access and no secret material of any kind:

$ ./.board/bin/oci-run --profile bootstrap-readonly-v1 --card AUR-019
{"card":"AUR-019","scenario":"AC-001","selector":"AC-001","required_providers":7,"tracked_capabilities":3,"result":"pass"}

A failing example — structured_output marked supported for OpenAI with its fixture entry removed (MUT-001):

$ tests/acceptance/AUR-019.sh
AUR-019/AC-001/unfixtured-capability: standards/providers/openai.yaml marks capability_structured_output supported with no fixture_structured_output entry

docs.title: Byte-allowlist invariant
docs.text:
standards/providers/*.yaml and .board/research/providers.md are both machine-authored policy/data, not free-form prose: neither has any legitimate reason to contain any byte other than printable ASCII (0x20-0x7E) or a bare line feed (0x0A). tests/acceptance/AUR-019.sh enforces that as its own gate, check_allowed_bytes, which runs on every standards/providers/<slug>.yaml file before check_canonical_form or flat_value ever inspect it, and on .board/research/providers.md before the "## Provider contracts matrix" awk walk ever inspects it. It fails typed AUR-019/AC-001/malformed-entry: disallowed byte 0xNN at <path>:<line> the instant it finds a byte outside that allowlist — including 0x00 (NUL), every other C0 control byte (0x01-0x09, 0x0B-0x1F), 0x7F (DEL), and every byte >= 0x80.

This exists because the bash acceptance test and tests/integration/AUR-019_test.go are two independent readers of the same flat key: value files, and a byte one of them treats as ordinary line content while the other treats as a boundary is exactly where they diverge. The clearest instance is 0x00: this card's acceptance engine runs inside a BusyBox userland (the pinned bootstrap-readonly-v1 image, currently bash@sha256:ae4668c2...), and BusyBox's awk — which both check_canonical_form and flat_value are built on — treats an embedded NUL byte as if it split the record, not as ordinary data. A single physical line that appends \x00capability_structured_output: supported\x00fixture_structured_output: <path> onto the end of a real key's value (with the genuine capability_structured_output/fixture_structured_output lines deleted) is therefore not one line to BusyBox awk — it reads as three, and each of those three is a clean, canonical key: value declaration, so the awk-based readers would wave the poisoned line through as three legitimate ones. tests/integration/AUR-019_test.go's parseFlatYAMLAUR019 never makes that mistake: Go's strings.Split only ever breaks on a real \n, so the same bytes read as a single line whose value is never recognized as declaring capability_structured_output at all, and go test fails where the bash gate had passed. This is the same shape of bug the prior "ASCII-only" gate (check_ascii_only, [\x80-\xff] only) was built to close for NBSP/NEL — but that gate's own range never covered 0x00, so it could not see this byte at all.

The fix deliberately does not enumerate byte ranges to reject (chasing NUL, then VT, then CR, then the next byte some reader treats specially, one permutation at a time — the same chase that shipped the prior rounds' bypasses). It inverts the problem: only two things are ever allowed (0x0A, 0x20-0x7E), so no byte any reader could disagree about ever reaches check_canonical_form, flat_value, or the provider-matrix walk. Detection itself deliberately avoids awk and grep: under this BusyBox userland those are exactly the tools an embedded NUL can fool. tr, wc, and od were verified against the pinned image to treat NUL as ordinary data with no special splitting behavior, so check_allowed_bytes compares the file's total byte count (wc -c) against the count that survives deleting every allowed byte (tr -cd '\012\040-\176') to detect any disallowed byte, and od -An -v -tu1 -w1 (never eliding repeats, one byte per row) to recover the first offending byte's exact value and line.

A CRLF line ending (\r\n) in either file is directly covered by this gate: \r is 0x0D, which is not in the allowlist, so a CRLF-saved file now fails malformed-entry at check_allowed_bytes itself rather than surviving to fail later, differently, on a per-key value mismatch downstream.

docs.title: Fixture canonical-form invariant
docs.text:
tests/specs/AUR-019/fixtures/<slug>/<capability>.json follows one strict canonical shape, enforced by the acceptance gate and never re-formatted after the fact: two-space indent per nesting level, one member or element per line, every object's keys in strictly ascending order, no non-ASCII byte (a non-ASCII source character comes out \uXXXX-escaped instead). This shape is checked at acceptance time only, inside the sealed bootstrap-readonly-v1 container, by check_fixture_canonical_form; there is no Python script and the container has no python3.

tests/acceptance/AUR-019.sh's check_fixture_canonical_form is what actually enforces that shape inside the sealed container, and it replaces a prior version of this gate that never did: that version pulled the fixture's "capability"/"provider" binding out with grep -m1 -E '"capability"[[:space:]]*:' | sed ... and the equivalent for "provider" — two greps for two substrings, never a JSON parse. Two concrete inputs exposed that as a real gap in the sealed accept gate itself (not just go test), both reproduced and closed by this canonical form:

  1. A file that is not JSON at all — free prose containing nothing but the two magic lines "capability": "tool_use" / "provider": "openai" — satisfied the old grep -m1 check while encoding/json.Unmarshal correctly failed it with "is not valid JSON". docs/specs/AUR-019.md's own Contract section already promised a "JSON-valid fixture"; the old gate did not check that promise, it assumed it.
  2. A file that is syntactically valid JSON with the "provider" key declared twice (RFC 8259 permits this) — grep -m1 takes the first occurrence, encoding/json.Unmarshal (like every conforming decoder) takes the last. A fixture whose first "provider" was correct and second was not passed the old sealed gate while go test read a different provider for the same file.

check_fixture_canonical_form closes both by validating the entire file, line by line, against the canonical grammar above instead of grepping two lines out of it: a strictly-ascending, duplicate-free key order at every nesting depth is required, so free-form prose fails on line 1 (not a bare {) and a duplicate key fails as soon as the second occurrence breaks the ascending-order invariant — the same check that enforces "a fixed key order" also is how a duplicate key is caught, with no second, separate pass to fall out of sync with it. The top-level "capability" and "provider" keys are additionally required to exist and to hold a plain JSON string, not an object, array, number, boolean, or null — the same requirement struct{ Capability, Provider string } plus json.Unmarshal imposes on the Go side. Because every fixture this gate accepts has exactly one legal parse, canonical_top_string_value (which replaces the old grep -m1/sed extraction) can safely read "capability"/"provider" with a single anchored match: there is no non-JSON or duplicate-key input left that could make its answer disagree with what encoding/json.Unmarshal decodes for the same field. check_allowed_bytes runs on every fixture before check_fixture_canonical_form, for the same reason it runs before check_canonical_form on a standards/providers/<slug>.yaml file: an embedded NUL is exactly the kind of byte this BusyBox awk could treat as a record boundary no other reader agrees with, and it must never reach an awk-based reader before that gate has ruled it out.

This does not attempt a general-purpose JSON parser in awk — the pinned container has no jq and no python3, and a hand-rolled full JSON parser in awk under an adversarial-review card is exactly the kind of "chasing the next permutation" this card's byte-allowlist section already explains the cost of. It instead narrows the accepted input to one generated, deterministic shape and refuses anything that is not exactly that shape, the same inversion check_allowed_bytes already applies to raw bytes.

The shell grammar also validates comma position for closing objects and arrays: an object/array close may carry a comma only when another sibling follows, and the root close may never carry one. Scalar values are restricted to JSON strings, the full JSON number grammar, true, false, or null; bare words such as BROKEN, NaN, and Infinity are rejected. encoding/json provides the same invalid-token and trailing-comma rejection in the Go reader.

docs.title: Fixture wire-binding invariant
docs.text:
check_fixture_canonical_form (and encoding/json.Unmarshal on the Go side) proves a fixture is well-formed JSON with the required top-level "capability"/"provider" string fields. It does not, by itself, prove the fixture's content actually describes the provider it claims to: nothing before this invariant compared a fixture's recorded request against the same provider's own standards/providers/<slug>.yaml contract, so a fixture consisting of one real provider's entire recorded request, with only its "provider" string edited to name a different provider, passed both readers -- standards/providers/openai.yaml could go on declaring wire_endpoint: /v1/chat/completions and auth_header: Authorization while tests/specs/AUR-019/fixtures/openai/tool_use.json was, byte for byte, Anthropic's real /v1/messages request with x-api-key/anthropic-version headers, and nothing checked the two against each other. That falsified this card's own Outcome ("cada provider tem wire format, auth, erro e capabilities versionados", with the fixture as the proof) without touching any byte outside tests/specs/AUR-019/.

A fixture's own standards/providers/<slug>.yaml declares a transport, either http or sdk-call. transport decides which fields the fixture must carry — never the other way around. An earlier round of this card bound wire format "when the fixture's request object declares the field", which meant a fixture could opt itself out of the entire binding just by omitting request.method/request.path/request.headers: a review round reproduced that as a live bypass by deleting those three keys from an HTTP-shaped body borrowed whole from a different provider (Anthropic's real /v1/messages request, relabeled "provider": "openai") and watching both engines accept it. Deleting a field can no longer opt a fixture out of a check; only its own provider's declared transport decides what is required, and that declaration is itself restricted to a closed, undecided-provider-checked vocabulary (http/sdk-call), not free text a fixture author also controls.

transport: http (every provider except LiteLLM) requires, and cross-checks, three fields, all unconditionally present or the fixture fails typed unfixtured-capability:

  • request.method must be present and equal the provider's wire_method exactly.
  • request.path must be present and match a pattern derived from the provider's wire_endpoint: every {placeholder} segment (e.g. {model}, {deployment-id}) becomes a wildcard for one real value, every other character must match literally. Capability-specific action suffixes are declared as wire_action_<capability> and are compared exactly, so Gemini's {model}:generateContent for tool_use/structured_output and {model}:streamGenerateContent for streaming cannot be interchanged. The match is anchored at a real end boundary, not merely a prefix: after the resource segment (or the placeholder's greedy run), only end-of-string, a literal ? (a query string), or — only for the streaming capability's own fixture, and only when the provider's standards/providers/<slug>.yaml declares a wire_streaming_suffix (Bedrock: -stream, for its /converse vs /converse-stream pair) — that exact literal suffix is required. /v1/chat/completions therefore does not match /v1/chat/completions-but-actually-something-else: neither terminator branch matches at the position -but-actually-something-else starts. An earlier round anchored this pattern only at ^, which made "prefix" mean "starts with", not "is", and a review round reproduced that gap by appending arbitrary literal text directly onto an otherwise-correct literal endpoint.
  • request.headers is required, and must contain a key equal to the provider's auth_header, only when that same provider's standards/providers/<slug>.yaml declares auth_binding: header (OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure), and every such value must be a JSON string. query-param requires the declared auth_query_param in the request path (Gemini's ?key=...); signed-request requires the declared non-secret auth_evidence string in request.auth (Bedrock's AWS SigV4); and none is Ollama's explicit no-auth default. auth_binding is restricted to exactly these four values, checked the same way transport is. request.headers: null fails the same "not a real recording" way as an absent header block: tests/integration/AUR-019_test.go re-decodes the field into a map[string]string before checking for the auth_header key, and decoding a JSON null into that map yields nil with no error, so the membership check that follows fails exactly as it would for a genuinely absent header block.

transport: sdk-call (LiteLLM only, whose documented completion() call is not itself an HTTP request) requires, and cross-checks, the two fields that describe an SDK call instead of a wire request, with the same "absent = typed failure" rule:

  • request.call must be present and equal the provider's own wire_call value (litellm.completion) exactly.
  • request.params must be present and be a JSON object (even an empty {}, if a future fixture ever needed it empty). A JSON null is treated as absent, not present: it is functionally the same "no object recorded" case this field exists to catch, just spelled with the key kept and the value hollowed out instead of the key deleted. Both engines enforce this the same way for request.params specifically: tests/acceptance/AUR-019.sh matches only a literal "params": { opener (so "params": null never matches and fails typed unfixtured-capability), and tests/integration/AUR-019_test.go re-decodes the field into a real Go map rather than only checking it against Go's zero value — decoding null into a map yields nil with no error, so it is caught by the same "no request.params object" check an absent field hits, not treated as presence. A JSON string, number, boolean, or array in that slot (for example the quoted string "null", which is valid JSON and not the same value as the literal null) is a third, distinct case: present, but not an object, so it fails with a type error rather than an absence message.

Because both transports now require and cross-check their own fields unconditionally, a fixture can no longer hide a borrowed body by deleting the fields that would have exposed it: an http fixture with no request.method/path/headers fails before its request.body is ever compared to anything, and an sdk-call fixture with no request.call/ params fails the same way. This is not restricted to LiteLLM's slot or to any one provider — every provider's fixture is bound by whichever transport its own standards/providers/<slug>.yaml declares, verified the same way for all seven.

A method, path, header, call, or params mismatch (or absence) fails with the same typed AUR-019/AC-001/unfixtured-capability code the "capability"/"provider" field checks already use — it is the same class of proof (a fixture that does not actually attest to what it claims), not a new one. An unrecognized transport or auth_binding value, or a sdk-call provider missing wire_call, fails typed AUR-019/AC-001/undecided-provider — the same code an incomplete standards/providers/<slug>.yaml file already uses, since this is the same kind of defect: the provider's own contract is not fully decided.

docs.title: Diagnosis
docs.text:
• AUR-019/AC-001/malformed-entry: disallowed byte 0xNN at <path>:<line> — a standards/providers/<slug>.yaml file or .board/research/providers.md contains a byte outside the printable-ASCII-plus-LF allowlist (NUL, another C0 control byte, DEL, or any byte >= 0x80). Re-save the file as plain ASCII with LF line endings; see "Byte-allowlist invariant" above for why this is rejected before the file is otherwise parsed.
  • AUR-019/AC-001/malformed-entry: <file> line <n> declares key "<key>" outside its canonical "<key>: value" form — a known schema key in a standards/providers/<slug>.yaml file is written with leading whitespace, a space before the colon, a tab, or another non-canonical shape. Rewrite the line as <key>: <value> at column 0.
  • AUR-019/AC-001/malformed-entry: <file> line <n> has trailing whitespace — a standards/providers/<slug>.yaml line ends in a space. Trim it; a trailing space on an unquoted value used to be silently accepted by go test (which trims) while this gate rejected it, so this is now refused explicitly instead of surviving as an undocumented reader split.
  • AUR-019/AC-001/malformed-entry: <fixture path>: line <n> ... — a tests/specs/AUR-019/fixtures/<slug>/<capability>.json fixture is not in the canonical form check_fixture_canonical_form enforces (not valid JSON, a duplicate or out-of-order key, a non-string "capability"/"provider" value, or another shape violation). Fix the fixture's content so it matches the shape the gate verifies.
  • AUR-019/AC-001: provider baseline absent — .board/research/providers.md is missing, empty, or missing one of the seven literal provider names. Restore it from the card's owned paths. This is the card's documented RED message and is distinct from every other typed failure below.
  • AUR-019/AC-001/undecided-provider: required provider missing from matrix: <name> (or "cited twice", "has an empty criterion cell", "matrix row has N columns...") — fix the offending row in the "Provider contracts matrix" table.
  • AUR-019/AC-001/undecided-provider: standards file absent for provider <name>: <path> (or "has no value") — restore or complete standards/providers/<slug>.yaml for that provider.
  • AUR-019/AC-001/undecided-provider: provider-names fixture declares N names but only M are distinct (or the same for capabilities.txt, or "validated N distinct standards files but required exactly M") — tests/specs/AUR-019/provider-names.txt (or capabilities.txt) has a duplicated entry padding its line count, or a provider name and its lowercased slug collided with another provider's. De-duplicate the source list; every required provider (or capability) must be validated from its own distinct file, not revalidated from a stand-in.
  • AUR-019/AC-001/unsourced-provider: ... source host is not allowlisted (or "has no versioned source", "source date is not ISO 8601") — the cited source moved off the allowlist in tests/specs/AUR-019/allowed-source-domains.txt, or lost its version/date. Either fix the citation or extend the allowlist through review.
  • AUR-019/AC-001/unfixtured-capability: ... — a capability is marked supported with no matching, valid, correctly bound fixture. Either add the fixture under tests/specs/AUR-019/fixtures/<slug>/ or mark the capability unsupported until one is recorded. This code also covers a fixture that is missing, or has a mismatching value for, whichever fields its own provider's declared transport requires: for transport: http, request.method/request.path/request.headers against wire_method/wire_endpoint/auth_header; for transport: sdk-call, request.call/request.params against wire_call (see "Fixture wire-binding invariant" above) — the fixture is well-formed JSON naming the right capability and provider by label, but its content does not actually attest to that provider's own documented wire format, or omits the very fields that would let it attest to anything.
  • AUR-019/AC-001/undecided-provider: ... transport has an unrecognized value (or "auth_binding has an unrecognized value", or "has no wire_call value") — a standards/providers/<slug>.yaml file declares a transport outside http/sdk-call, an auth_binding outside header/query-param/signed-request/none for an http provider, or omits wire_call for an sdk-call provider. Fix the offending value; this is the same code an incomplete standards file already uses, because it is the same defect (the provider's own contract is not fully decided).
  • AUR-019/AC-001/infrastructure: ... — a required host tool is missing or the repository root could not be resolved; this is never a behavioral result and never counts as RED evidence for this card.

docs.title: Integration selector
docs.text: The card's frontmatter declares paths: [..., tests/integration/AUR-019_test.go] and TDD proof Integration: \tests/integration/AUR-019_test.go::TestAUR019Boundary`.Both the filename (AUR-019_test.go) and the function name (TestAUR019Boundary,Test-prefixed) follow the discoverablego test ./...conventiontests/integration/AUR-020_test.go::TestAUR020Boundary` already established, so this card's own regression check runs in the normal suite with no external dispatcher and no dead integration code.

docs.title: AUR-020: Escolher memória e mapa incremental mínimos
docs.text:
Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

This is a research/decision card. It does not ship an executable feature; it fixes a design contract that later O10-memory and O02-index cards implement against. The observable behavior is the acceptance lint itself: tests/acceptance/AUR-020.sh deterministically resolves the artifacts below and either passes or names exactly which one is incomplete.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
tests/acceptance/AUR-020.sh (selector AC-001) reads three artifacts this card owns and checks that they resolve to one consistent decision, without making any network request:

  1. .board/research/memory-design.md — an "Alternatives matrix" table that compares five named alternatives (Aider, Karpathy, Hermes, Tree-sitter, SCIP) plus the AurumCode baseline row, one criterion set per row: a [label](url) source, a Version, an ISO-8601 Date, and one cell per decision criterion (Indexing cost, Query scope, Network dependency).
  2. .board/decisions/ADR-0001-optional-local-memory.md — names each of the five alternatives under a ### Rejected: <name> heading and closes under ### Decision: ... on SQLite FTS5 plus a relation graph. Every justification line uses the fixed form - Criterion: <name> — <text>, and <name> must be one of the criterion columns from the matrix above.
  3. standards/memory/limits.yaml — declares a positive max_index_bytes under index_size: and a positive max_context_window_tokens under context_window:.

The lint also re-checks a small set of literal terms the outcome requires directly (off, ephemeral, local, the default database path, SQLite, FTS5, no vector database, typed status, graph) and scans all three files for language that would make a vector or embedding database mandatory in the baseline, independent of whether the positive "no vector database" claim is still present.

docs.title: Contract
docs.text:
• tests/specs/AUR-020/alternatives.txt and tests/specs/AUR-020/allowed-source-domains.txt are the single source of truth for, respectively, the exact five alternative names the matrix and the ADR must resolve, and the hostnames a matrix Source link may cite. Both the shell acceptance test and tests/integration/AUR-020.go read these two files instead of duplicating the lists.
  • A matrix row's Version cell must match a semantic-version-like pattern (v0.86.0, 3.53.3) or, for a non-versioned artifact such as a social media post, an immutable post identifier (post 1937902205765607626) paired with its Date.
  • Every - Criterion: <name> — <text> line in the ADR must resolve to a criterion column present in the matrix; a name outside that set, a missing criterion in a Rejected/Decision section, an alternative missing from the matrix, an unversioned source, or a non-allowlisted source host all fail with the same typed code: AUR-020/AC-001/undecided-criterion.
  • Introducing a mandatory vector/embedding database anywhere in the three artifacts fails with AUR-020/AC-001/vector-database-mandated, regardless of whether the existing "no vector database" sentence is also removed.
  • This card produces no executable index, database, or CLI surface. The SQLite FTS5 plus graph baseline it fixes is implemented by dependent O10-memory/O02-index cards, not here.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
standards/memory/limits.yaml fixes the two bound families ADR-0001 (invariant 8) requires:

  • index_size: max_index_bytes (on-disk ceiling for .git/aurumcode/memory.sqlite3, including FTS5 shadow tables and the WAL file), max_entities, max_retained_snapshots, max_snippet_bytes.
  • context_window: max_augmentation_tokens (the slice of one provider call's context budget the memory augmenter may spend), max_context_window_tokens (the ceiling the augmenter plans against), and min_reserved_baseline_tokens (the unaugmented baseline the augmenter must never shrink).

A consumer repository may lower these through trusted base configuration; it may not raise them past the ceiling declared here without a separate, reviewed change to this file.

docs.title: Example (no secret)
docs.text:
Running the acceptance test directly, with no network access and no secret material of any kind:

$ ./.board/bin/oci-run --profile bootstrap-readonly-v1 --card AUR-020
{"card":"AUR-020","scenario":"AC-001","selector":"AC-001","required_alternatives":5,"criteria_columns":3,"result":"pass"}

A failing example — a matrix row missing a criterion cell for SCIP:

$ tests/acceptance/AUR-020.sh
AUR-020/AC-001/undecided-criterion: alternative SCIP has an empty criterion cell

docs.title: Diagnosis
docs.text:
• AUR-020/AC-001/undecided-criterion: required artifact absent: <path> — one of memory-design.md, the ADR, standards/memory/limits.yaml, or a tests/specs/AUR-020/* fixture is missing or empty. Restore it from the card's owned paths.
  • AUR-020/AC-001/undecided-criterion: alternative <name> ... — the matrix row for that alternative is missing, duplicated, has no versioned source, has a non-ISO date, cites a non-allowlisted source host, or has an empty criterion cell. Fix the offending cell in the "Alternatives matrix" table.
  • AUR-020/AC-001/undecided-criterion: ADR cites a criterion outside the matrix: <label> — a - Criterion: line in the ADR names something that is not one of the matrix's criterion columns. Either fix the label to match the matrix or add the criterion as a matrix column and give every required alternative a value for it.
  • AUR-020/AC-001/undecided-criterion: "<section>" section has no justification for criterion: <name> — a Rejected/Decision section is missing a - Criterion: <name> — ... line for one of the matrix's criteria.
  • AUR-020/AC-001/vector-database-mandated: <path> mandates a vector/ embedding database in the baseline — remove the mandate; the baseline must stay free of a required vector or embedding database.
  • AUR-020/AC-001/undecided-criterion: <limits path> has no positive max_index_bytes ... (or max_context_window_tokens) — the corresponding bound in standards/memory/limits.yaml is missing, zero, or unparsable.
  • AUR-020/AC-001/infrastructure: ... — a required host tool is missing or the repository root could not be resolved; this is never a behavioral result and never counts as RED evidence for this card.

docs.title: AUR-021: Fixar MCP conformance e segurança
docs.text:
Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

This is a research/decision card. It does not ship an executable feature or start any MCP server; it fixes a design contract a later O11-mcp card implements against. The observable behavior is the acceptance lint itself: tests/acceptance/AUR-021.sh deterministically resolves the artifacts below and either passes or names exactly which one is incomplete.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
tests/acceptance/AUR-021.sh (selector AC-001) reads six artifacts this card owns and checks that they resolve to one consistent, testable pin, without making any network request:

  1. .board/research/mcp.md — contains, case-insensitive, every term listed in tests/specs/AUR-021/required-terms.txt (stdio, read-only, OAuth, injection, capability at time of writing), and a ## Sources matrix table with at least 5 data rows, each citing a [label](url) source whose host is allowlisted (tests/specs/AUR-021/allowed-source-domains.txt), a parseable version, an ISO-8601 date, and a non-empty "what it fixes" cell.
  2. standards/mcp/protocol.yaml — declares protocol.version as an ISO-8601 date and go_sdk.module / go_sdk.version as a semantic version; both version strings must also appear verbatim in .board/research/mcp.md, so the pinned standard cannot silently diverge from the source that justifies it.
  3. standards/mcp/tools.yaml — every declared tool has class: read_only or class: mutable; every mutable tool sets requires_explicit_consent: true and no read_only tool sets it; every tool named in tests/specs/AUR-021/required-mutable-tools.txt (review.publish at time of writing) is present, classified mutable, and requires explicit consent.

docs.title: Contract
docs.text:
• tests/specs/AUR-021/required-terms.txt, tests/specs/AUR-021/allowed-source-domains.txt, and tests/specs/AUR-021/required-mutable-tools.txt are the single source of truth for, respectively, the literal terms the research document must contain, the hostnames a Sources matrix link may cite, and the tools that must be classified mutable with explicit consent. The shell acceptance test reads all three instead of duplicating the lists.
  • A Sources matrix row's Version cell must match a semantic-version-like pattern (v1.6.1) or an ISO-8601 date, optionally followed by free text (2026-07-28 (RC locked 2026-05-21)); its Date cell must be a plain ISO-8601 date.
  • standards/mcp/tools.yaml's tool classification does not trust any MCP server's own self-reported readOnlyHint/destructiveHint annotations (the MCP specification itself treats those as untrusted unless the server is already trusted); it is this project's own, independently fixed policy.
  • This card produces no executable MCP server, transport, or tool registry. The protocol/SDK pin and tool classification it fixes here are consumed by a dependent O11-mcp card, not built here.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
standards/mcp/protocol.yaml fixes the two pins this baseline requires:

  • protocol.version: the adopted MCP specification revision (2025-11-25); protocol.transports: the transports this baseline recognizes (stdio, streamable-http).
  • go_sdk.module / go_sdk.version: the adopted Go SDK (github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk v1.6.1).

standards/mcp/tools.yaml fixes, per tool, a class of read_only or mutable, and for every mutable tool a requires_explicit_consent: true flag that a future server implementation must enforce before invocation.

docs.title: Example (no secret)
docs.text:
Running the acceptance test directly, with no network access and no secret material of any kind:

$ ./.board/bin/oci-run --profile bootstrap-readonly-v1 --card AUR-021
{"card":"AUR-021","scenario":"AC-001","selector":"AC-001","required_terms":5,"source_rows":7,"result":"pass"}

A failing example — review.publish reclassified read_only in standards/mcp/tools.yaml:

$ tests/acceptance/AUR-021.sh
AUR-021/AC-001/tool-misclassified: required tool review.publish must be class: mutable with requires_explicit_consent: true, got class=read_only requires_explicit_consent=

docs.title: Diagnosis
docs.text:
• AUR-021/AC-001/behavior-missing: required artifact absent: <path> — one of .board/research/mcp.md, standards/mcp/protocol.yaml, standards/mcp/tools.yaml, or a tests/specs/AUR-021/* fixture is missing or empty. Restore it from the card's owned paths.
  • AUR-021/AC-001/behavior-missing: required term missing from .board/research/mcp.md: <term> — one of the five required terms was removed or renamed; restore it, case-insensitively.
  • AUR-021/AC-001/source-not-versioned: ... — a Sources matrix row is missing, cites a non-allowlisted host, has no versioned Version cell, has a non-ISO Date cell, or a pin's version string in standards/mcp/protocol.yaml no longer appears in the research document. Fix the offending cell or restore the citation.
  • AUR-021/AC-001/tool-misclassified: ... — a tool in standards/mcp/tools.yaml has an invalid class, a mutable tool is missing requires_explicit_consent: true, a read_only tool wrongly sets it, or a required mutable tool (review.publish) is missing or reclassified. Fix the tool's class/requires_explicit_consent fields.
  • AUR-021/AC-001/infrastructure: ... — a required host tool is missing or the repository root could not be resolved; this is never a behavioral result and never counts as RED evidence for this card.

docs.title: History: Integration proof path was escalated and resolved at v2
docs.text:
At version: 1, this card's declared paths entry and TDD-proof "Integration" line named tests/integration/AUR-021.go::IntegrationAUR021. A .go file without the _test.go suffix is invisible to go test's scanner by definition of the Go toolchain, and IntegrationAUR021 was not Test-prefixed either, so that path could never carry a real, discoverable Integration proof — the same defect AUR-020's card carried at version: 1 (tests/integration/AUR-020.go::IntegrationAUR020), which round 1 vetoed as dead code and round 2 vetoed as a working test delivered outside the card's declared paths, resolved only by a governance version bump (.board/cards/ready/AUR-020.md v2) retargeting the path to tests/integration/AUR-020_test.go::TestAUR020Boundary.

Because .board/cards is this card's own forbidden_paths entry, the builder could not make that same correction from inside the card. Per the board's rule that an unimplementable spec is escalated rather than silently worked around, no file was written at either the declared dead-code path or an undeclared _test.go path in that round.

Governance resolved the escalation the same way it resolved AUR-020's: a version bump to version: 2 (.board/cards/doing/AUR-021.md) retargeted the TDD-proof "Integration" line to tests/integration/AUR-021_test.go::TestAUR021Boundary. That file is now part of this card's delivered paths, is discovered by go test ./... with no external dispatcher, and is the Integration evidence this document and the acceptance test currently rely on.

docs.title: AUR-233 - Verify the bootstrap lockset
docs.text: Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

docs.title: Outcome
docs.text: BootstrapLocksetV1 accepts exactly AUR-359 through AUR-364 when every locked artifact exists, its content digest matches the index, and the aggregate identity recomputes from the sorted child/digest pairs.

docs.title: Contract
docs.text:
• The index is .board/bootstrap/locks.yml.
  • The index contains one schema, one aggregate identity, and exactly six child rows.
  • Each child is bound to its embedded artifact path; aliases are rejected.
  • Digests are recomputed from artifact bytes. A value written in the index is not trusted merely because it has the right shape.
  • The aggregate identity is sha256: plus the SHA-256 digest of sorted lines in the form <card-id> <recomputed-digest>.
  • Verdict words and hand-written outcome claims are not accepted in the index.
  • The index is non-empty and at most 64 KiB/512 lines; each artifact is non-empty and at most 4 MiB.

Typed failures are lock_domain_missing, child_duplicate, child_digest_mismatch, and candidate_identity_mismatch. Child execution failures are reported separately by the acceptance harness and are never converted into a successful aggregate.

docs.title: Child bindings
docs.text: Card Artifact AUR-359 locks/trust-root.yml AUR-360 locks/go.yml AUR-361 locks/actions.yml AUR-362 locks/scanners.yml AUR-363 locks/parsers.yml AUR-364 locks/docs.yml

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: tests/acceptance/AUR-233.sh consumes and validates the tab-separated case matrix, then exercises the nominal domain, missing and duplicate children, digest and identity tampering, self-reference, handwritten verdicts, aliasing, malformed index lines, symlink artifacts, and child re-execution. tests/gates/bootstrap/AUR-233/cases.tsv is the compact mutation matrix. For example, deleting the AUR-363 row returns lock_domain_missing, while changing one artifact's content returns child_digest_mismatch. bash .board/bootstrap/verify.sh performs the same deterministic index, bounds, artifact, and identity checks without executing a child.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text: This card does not produce or reinterpret child artifacts, install toolchains, resolve credentials, or publish external state. Child acceptance programs are re-executed by the acceptance harness and their raw exit status remains the source of the child observation.

docs.title: AUR-308: legacy documentation characterization
docs.text: Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

docs.title: Contract
docs.text:
AUR-308 executes the reachable behavior of every Go package in the closed legacy scope: the extractor core, eight language extractors, normalizer, incremental, and site. classification.tsv binds each package to one passing behavioral test and to exactly one disposition: keep, migrate, replace, or delete. A fresh go list inventory, the explicit manifest, and the executed-test ledger must agree exactly.

migrate means the observed behavior is useful but must move behind the reconstructed ownership boundaries. replace means the executed probe exposes a behavior that the new implementation must not preserve: repository-controlled build execution, non-docstring capture, or symlink-following cache output. This snapshot has no package whose complete implementation stays at the legacy path (keep) and no behaviorless package (delete).
