The tests use bounded temporary fixtures and scripted command runners. They do not start the documentation pipeline, install tools, use the network, or modify internal/documentation. External-tool probes call the real extractor methods, observe the exact command boundary, and materialize only the minimum fake tool output needed for the extractor to inspect.

docs.title: Artifact and replay
docs.text:
The acceptance emits one canonical JSON observation with the package, disposition, test selector, and observed behavior for all 12 packages. It also binds the runner's input-manifest digest when available. Two writes from the same inputs must be byte-identical. The coordinator, not the read-only worker, captures that observation as .board/evidence/AUR-308/acceptance/AC-001.json.

Artifact writes require a real staging directory, an output lexically and physically contained beneath it, and a previously absent regular output path. An existing symlink is rejected before opening it.

docs.title: Execution
docs.text:
./.board/bin/oci-run --profile bootstrap-readonly-v1 --card AUR-308

The default AC-001 path executes all 12 package tests and the declared Unit, Contract, Integration, and E2E selectors. It then applies MUT-001 (a reusable classification referencing an unexecuted test), observes RED, restores GREEN, applies MUT-002 (artifact output symlinked outside staging), observes RED without changing the target, and restores GREEN.

Failures are typed beneath AUR-308/AC-001. Exit 1 means a reached behavioral assertion failed. Exit 64 is selector misuse. Exit 69 is missing runtime or another infrastructure failure; it is never a characterization result.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text: Revert only AUR-308's test, acceptance, and specification paths. The legacy source remains byte-for-byte unchanged throughout characterization.

docs.title: AUR-309 — caracterização do pipeline legado
docs.text: Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

docs.title: Contrato
docs.text:
Este card caracteriza o comportamento observável de internal/pipeline/extractor_pipeline.go sem alterar o pacote legado. A suíte recompila esse arquivo de produção byte a byte e executa seus entrypoints em um módulo temporário. As dependências downstream que não pertencem aos read_paths são doubles instrumentados e card-scoped: registram chamadas, escrevem somente no diretório temporário e não acessam rede, Git, indexadores ou publicadores.

Uma linha só recebe reachable depois que a chamada ou o efeito nomeado foi observado durante a execução. deployToGHPages recebe stub/unreachable porque a branch habilitada é realmente alcançada, o log de placeholder é observado e nenhuma chamada de deploy, Git ou publicação é registrada. Presença de função, nome de arquivo e grep de fonte não classificam comportamento.

O relatório canônico é ordenado por entrypoint e contém exatamente estas colunas:

entrypoint<TAB>classification<TAB>effect

As classificações permitidas são reachable e stub/unreachable. O fixture tests/characterization/legacy/pipeline/expected.tsv sela 13 entrypoints ou fases observáveis e seus efeitos. O acceptance compara bytes do relatório executado com esse fixture; linhas ausentes, extras, duplicadas ou divergentes saem 1.

docs.title: Camadas executáveis
docs.text:
• TestAUR309 executa os entrypoints de erro e prova redaction e Unwrap.
  • ContractAUR309 executa o pipeline e valida cardinalidade, unicidade, classificações e a fronteira do stub de deploy.
  • IntegrationAUR309 executa os caminhos full, incremental, skip, scaffold, welcome e Jekyll, emitindo uma linha por efeito realmente observado.
  • E2EAUR309 chama o acceptance pelo selector de integração e exige o marcador de sucesso produzido somente depois da comparação canônica.

Cada arquivo .go declarado pelo card é copiado para um pacote de teste temporário junto do arquivo de produção e recebe uma bridge *_test.go; assim o selector citado é uma função executada por go test, não um nome aceito sem asserções. A tag aur309_characterization isola os fontes instrumentados do build normal e é habilitada explicitamente pelo acceptance. GOPROXY=off, GOSUMDB=off e GOTOOLCHAIN=local impedem resolução de dependências. O pequeno double de YAML é fornecido via vendor; go.mod e go.sum são copiados sem edição e permanecem os inputs canônicos do card.

docs.title: Limites e segurança
docs.text:
• stdout e stderr de cada camada: entre 1 byte e 32 KiB;
  • stdout e stderr do wrapper OCI: limitados pelo profile a 64 KiB cada;
  • 13 observações exatas, sem entrada livre no JSON final;
  • temporários com umask 077 e remoção por trap;
  • nenhuma indexação real, rede, socket, mount, device, capability ou publicação;
  • AURUM_SECRET_CANARY, quando presente, é rejeitado antes de qualquer log de camada ser mostrado;
  • os efeitos de filesystem ficam sob t.TempDir() ou sob o tmpfs do runner.

O JSON final é uma observação sanitizada para captura pelo coordenador em .board/evidence/AUR-309/acceptance/AC-001.json. Ele inclui digests SHA-256 da árvore materializada, de internal/pipeline, dos testes e do relatório, além das 13 classificações. O acceptance não escreve nem aprova evidence.

docs.title: Exemplo executável
docs.text:
./.board/bin/oci-run --profile bootstrap-readonly-v1 --card AUR-309
bash tests/acceptance/AUR-309.sh TestAUR309
bash tests/acceptance/AUR-309.sh ContractAUR309
bash tests/acceptance/AUR-309.sh IntegrationAUR309
bash tests/e2e/AUR-309.sh E2EAUR309

O primeiro comando é o acceptance oficial. Os demais são seletores de diagnóstico e devem terminar com exit 0 quando executados num ambiente Go+Bash equivalente ao profile pinado.

docs.title: MUT-001
docs.text:
Trocar, no fixture esperado, a classificação de deployToGHPages de stub/unreachable para reachable simula a alegação de funcionalidade sem chamada registrada. O mesmo wrapper oficial deve sair 1 e emitir exatamente:

AUR-309/AC-001/MUT-001

Depois de restaurar o byte original, o wrapper volta a sair 0. Falha de build, loader, ferramenta, imagem ou container é inconclusiva e não conta como RED da mutação.

docs.title: Falhas e diagnóstico
docs.text:
• exit 0: todas as camadas executaram asserções reais e o relatório coincidiu;
  • exit 1 com MUT-001: um stub sem chamada foi rotulado funcional;
  • exit 1 com characterization_mismatch: chamada, efeito, ordem ou cardinalidade divergiu do baseline;
  • exit 1 com <layer>_exit:<n>: a função de teste real falhou;
  • exit 64: selector desconhecido;
  • exit 79: ferramenta ou preparação do harness indisponível; nunca é RED comportamental.

O diagnóstico é bounded. Logs de Go só são mostrados em falha depois da verificação do canary e no máximo nas primeiras 80 linhas.

docs.title: Compatibilidade, migração e rollback
docs.text: internal/pipeline, go.mod e go.sum são somente leitura e devem permanecer byte a byte iguais. A caracterização é o estado before para os cards futuros de reconstrução; este card não migra nem remove código. Rollback consiste em reverter somente os paths do AUR-309 e repetir AC-001. Nenhum efeito externo novo precisa ser desfeito.

docs.title: AUR-318 — congelar taskmaster como histórico
docs.text: Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

docs.title: Contrato
docs.text:
Este card congela .taskmaster/ como histórico: seu estado done e suas instruções são preservados somente como input de auditoria e são ignorados pela fila do board. Uma cópia bounded do tree legado (21 arquivos, ≤ 64 arquivos, ≤ 1 MiB, com as 188 tasks/subtasks em done e as instruções de CLAUDE.md embutidas) vive em tests/characterization/legacy/taskmaster/snapshot. O fixture Go tests/characterization/legacy/taskmaster/fixture.go modela a fronteira de seleção da fila:

  • FeedBoardQueue nunca admite um candidato com origem taskmaster; cada um é preservado integralmente como AuditRecord com disposition audit-only;
  • PromoteDoneToBoard recusa qualquer transição derivada de .taskmaster com o erro tipado ErrLegacyTransitionRefused, mapeado para exit 1 por PromotionExitCode; um candidato nativo do board continua promovível (exit 0), o que distingue o freeze de um no-op que recusa tudo;
  • LoadLegacySnapshot é fail-closed: bounds de arquivos/bytes, symlinks e árvore inválida rejeitam antes de qualquer parse;
  • AuditSummary só emite contagens; títulos, instruções e identificadores hostis (inclusive um canary injetado) nunca alcançam logs ou observações.

.taskmaster, go.mod e go.sum são somente leitura. O acceptance compara byte a byte o tree vivo .taskmaster com a cópia de auditoria antes e depois de todas as camadas (taskmaster_bytes_changed sai 1) e a integração repete a comparação por dentro (CompareTrees), observada como taskmaster_bytes.

docs.title: Relatório canônico
docs.text:
A integração emite uma linha por fato observado:

observation<TAB>value<TAB>effect

O baseline selado é tests/characterization/legacy/taskmaster/expected.tsv com exatamente 8 observações: 188 registros de auditoria, 2 candidatos board admitidos, promoção board exit:0, promoção taskmaster exit:1 recusada, 0 itens de fila vindos de .taskmaster, 13370 bytes de instruções embutidas, bytes identical e 188 tasks done auditadas. Linhas ausentes, extras ou divergentes saem 1.

docs.title: Camadas executáveis
docs.text:
• TestAUR318 prova recusa tipada, exclusão da fila, preservação audit-only e redaction do canary no sumário.
  • ContractAUR318 prova bounds fail-closed do snapshot, disjunção fila/taskmaster, preservação completa da auditoria, determinismo, recusa estável e sensibilidade real de CompareTrees a bytes divergentes.
  • IntegrationAUR318 alimenta a fila com a cópia real, tenta a promoção proibida e emite as 8 observações.
  • E2EAUR318 chama o acceptance pelo selector de integração e exige o marcador produzido somente depois da comparação canônica.

Cada .go declarado é copiado para um módulo temporário com uma bridge *_test.go; o selector citado é uma função executada por go test, nunca um nome aceito sem asserções. A tag aur318_characterization isola os fontes do build normal. GOPROXY=off, GOSUMDB=off e GOTOOLCHAIN=local impedem resolução externa; somente stdlib e o próprio módulo são importados.

docs.title: Exemplo executável
docs.text:
./.board/bin/oci-run --profile bootstrap-readonly-v1 --card AUR-318
bash tests/acceptance/AUR-318.sh TestAUR318
bash tests/acceptance/AUR-318.sh ContractAUR318
bash tests/acceptance/AUR-318.sh IntegrationAUR318
bash tests/e2e/AUR-318.sh E2EAUR318

O primeiro comando é o acceptance oficial; os demais são seletores de diagnóstico num ambiente Go+Bash equivalente ao profile pinado.

docs.title: MUT-001
docs.text:
Remover a guarda de PromoteDoneToBoard (promover uma task done do taskmaster para done do board) mantém a fila vazia mas muda a observação promote_taskmaster_done para exit:0. O wrapper oficial sai 1 e emite exatamente:

AUR-318/AC-001/MUT-001

Restaurar o byte original reproduz o GREEN exato. Falha de build, loader, ferramenta, imagem ou container é inconclusiva e não conta como RED.

docs.title: Falhas e diagnóstico
docs.text:
• exit 0: camadas executaram asserções reais, relatório coincidiu com o baseline e .taskmaster permaneceu byte a byte idêntico;
  • exit 1 com AUR-318/AC-001: Congelar taskmaster como histórico ausente: algum item de .taskmaster entrou na fila (comportamento ausente);
  • exit 1 com MUT-001: uma transição derivada de .taskmaster foi aceita;
  • exit 1 com taskmaster_bytes_changed:*: o tree vivo divergiu da cópia de auditoria;
  • exit 1 com characterization_mismatch: outra observação divergiu do baseline;
  • exit 1 com <layer>_exit:<n>: uma função de teste real falhou;
  • exit 64: selector desconhecido; exit 79: harness indisponível, nunca RED.

Logs de camada só aparecem em falha, após a checagem do canary, limitados às primeiras 80 linhas; stdout/stderr do wrapper OCI ficam sob os 64 KiB do profile.

docs.title: Compatibilidade, migração e rollback
docs.text: Nenhuma task de .taskmaster é apagada, migrada ou convertida em card. A caracterização é o estado before permanente do backlog legado. Rollback: reverter somente os paths do AUR-318 e repetir AC-001; nenhum efeito externo precisa ser desfeito.

docs.title: AUR-359 — Fixar trust root do runner OCI
docs.text: Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Pins the trust root of the OCI runner used by the board's temporary shell bootstrap: the exact digest of the pinned base image, the exact digest of .board/bin/oci-run itself, and the hardened container flags every future consumer of the trust-root-docker-v1 profile must reproduce byte-for-byte. tests/acceptance/AUR-359.sh verifies all four artifacts independently of .board/bin/oci-run — the card's own accept line runs a direct, digest-pinned docker run, never the wrapper it authorizes.

docs.title: .board/bootstrap/locks/trust-root.yml
docs.text:
Flat key: value document, LC_ALL=C, one pair per line, 0 < size <= 4096 bytes. Exactly these 12 keys, each declared once:

Key Value schema bootstrap-lock-v1 card AUR-359 runner_script .board/bin/oci-run runner_script_sha256 sha256:<64 hex> — recomputed SHA-256 of .board/bin/oci-run runner_image bash@sha256:ae4668c2560999e65e89532cd2ad1b6688bb23298189f0bd229ef80fa4bd0831 profile_user 65532:65532 profile_network none profile_read_only_rootfs true profile_cap_drop ALL profile_no_new_privileges true engine_docker observed — Docker 29.6.1 was observed in this workspace engine_podman not-observed — Podman is not installed; no Podman verdict is emitted

docs.title: .board/oci/profiles/trust-root-docker-v1.json
docs.text: Flat JSON container profile using the same 24-key schema .board/bin/oci-run's own resolve_profile requires of any registered profile (schema, version, profile, lock, lock_digest, network, user, cap_drop, cap_add, mounts, devices, pull, tmpfs, read_only_rootfs, no_new_privileges, privileged, timeout_seconds, memory_mb, cpu_millis, pids_limit, tmpfs_mb, stdout_limit_bytes, stderr_limit_bytes, max_input_files, max_input_bytes). Its hardening fields are identical to the flags in the card's accept vector: network=none, user=65532:65532, cap_drop=ALL, read_only_rootfs=true, no_new_privileges=true, privileged=false, memory_mb=128, cpu_millis=500 (--cpus=0.5), pids_limit=64. lock points at the file below by its repository-relative path; lock_digest is the recomputed SHA-256 of that file's content, never a value trusted from the file itself.

docs.title: .board/locks/oci/trust-root-docker-v1.lock.json
docs.text:
Flat JSON image lock: schema (aurum.oci-image-lock), version (1), profile (trust-root-docker-v1), image (bash@sha256:ae4668c2560999e65e89532cd2ad1b6688bb23298189f0bd229ef80fa4bd0831). image must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._/-]*@sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$ — a bare tag or a mutable reference (bash:latest) is refused before any other check.

Both JSON documents are registered exactly as .board/bin/oci-run expects, so a future card that runs ./.board/bin/oci-run --profile trust-root-docker-v1 --card <id> resolves the same profile this card seals — but this card's own accept never depends on that wrapper, which is the point: fixing the trust root cannot depend on the thing it authorizes.

docs.title: Bounds
docs.text: Bound Value Lock/profile/oci-lock document size 4096 bytes tests/bootstrap/locks/AUR-359/cases.tsv size 4 MiB cases.tsv rows 256 Acceptance container wall-clock (accept vector, informational) 15 s

docs.title: Codes
docs.text:
Typed dispositions this card's acceptance program can emit on stderr as AUR-359/AC-001/<code> (exit 1, behavioral) or AUR-359/AC-001/inconclusive/<reason> (exit 79, environment):

Code Trigger trust_root_mismatch An owned artifact (lock, runner, profile, or oci lock) is absent, or a checked value diverges from the pinned trust root. source_integrity_error An owned artifact is a symlink, or otherwise not a plain regular file. invalid_lock_or_manifest An owned document is empty, malformed, missing a required field, or its declared lock_digest diverges from the recomputed content digest of the file it binds to. input_limit_exceeded An owned document exceeds 4096 bytes. runner_missing .board/bin/oci-run is absent (a trust_root_mismatch specialization, named separately because it identifies which artifact is missing). runner-digest-mismatch The lock's runner_script_sha256 diverges from the recomputed SHA-256 of .board/bin/oci-run (MUT-001). image_digest_mismatch The lock does not contain the pinned bash@sha256:... reference. egress-guard-missing profile_network/network is not none, or read_only_rootfs is not true (MUT-002). mutable-image The oci lock's image is not pinned by an immutable digest (MUT-003). mutable_reference The trust-root lock itself contains a latest/branch-style reference. fixture_sensitivity_error This program's own fixture self-test (cases.tsv) observed a disposition other than what the sealed row declares — the verifier failed to discriminate a known mutant.

$ ./.board/bin/oci-run --profile trust-root-docker-v1 --card AUR-999   # illustrative only
oci-run: profile trust-root-docker-v1 declares network as none, cap_drop as ALL, ...

$ docker run --rm --network=none --read-only --cap-drop=ALL \
    --security-opt=no-new-privileges --pids-limit=64 --memory=128m --cpus=0.5 \
    --user=65532:65532 -v "$PWD":/src:ro \
    bash@sha256:ae4668c2560999e65e89532cd2ad1b6688bb23298189f0bd229ef80fa4bd0831 \
    /src/tests/acceptance/AUR-359.sh
{"card":"AUR-359","scenario":"AC-001","selector":"AC-001","fixture_cases":5,"result":"pass"}

An absent lock instead produces, on stderr, exit 1:

AUR-359/AC-001/trust_root_mismatch
AUR-359/AC-001/detail expected-artifact=.board/bootstrap/locks/trust-root.yml

docs.title: Offline OCI command
docs.text:
This is exactly the card's accept: line — a direct, digest-pinned docker run, reproducible offline once the bash@sha256:... image is present in the local image cache (no registry pull is attempted; the profile declares "pull": "never"):

docker run --rm --network=none --read-only --cap-drop=ALL \
  --security-opt=no-new-privileges --pids-limit=64 --memory=128m --cpus=0.5 \
  --user=65532:65532 -v "${PWD}":/src:ro \
  bash@sha256:ae4668c2560999e65e89532cd2ad1b6688bb23298189f0bd229ef80fa4bd0831 \
  /src/tests/acceptance/AUR-359.sh

docs.title: Why the accept vector bypasses .board/bin/oci-run
docs.text: .board/bin/oci-run resolves a profile's image digest from .board/locks/oci/<name>.lock.json — the very file this card produces. A card that fixes the trust root cannot prove that root by first trusting the wrapper the root is meant to authorize; a bug in oci-run's own resolve_profile could otherwise mask a divergence in the thing under test. The accept line therefore invokes Docker directly with the identical hardened flags the trust-root-docker-v1 profile declares, and tests/acceptance/AUR-359.sh re-implements the profile/lock parsing independently rather than sourcing or exec'ing oci-run.

docs.title: AUR-360 — Fixar Go toolchain e módulos
docs.text: Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Pins the Go toolchain version and the exact, immutable module set the repository depends on: go 1.21 (from go.mod), the module path github.com/Mpaape/AurumCode, a recomputed SHA-256 digest of go.mod and of go.sum, and, for every module recorded in go.sum, its immutable version plus its module-content checksum (h1:..., the standard Go module checksum already present in go.sum). tests/acceptance/AUR-360.sh verifies the sealed lock is present, well-formed, free of mutable references, and cross-checked field-by-field against the real go.mod/go.sum it claims to pin — it never downloads or resolves a module (see Non-goals below and in the card).

docs.title: .board/bootstrap/locks/go.yml
docs.text:
Flat key: value document, LC_ALL=C, one pair per line, no trailing whitespace. Fields:

Key Value Source schema bootstrap-lock-v1 fixed card AUR-360 fixed go_version 1.21 go.mod:3 (go 1.21) module github.com/Mpaape/AurumCode go.mod:1 (module github.com/Mpaape/AurumCode) go_mod_sha256 sha256:2e5f37fb9db0206e74c34a1500f9c53e11c33c9d1d0ee39d6377a553aabeafb6 recomputed sha256sum go.mod go_sum_sha256 sha256:b9142883d8f8e46998f705fbcd9964d6f386e17381ddf95a0c3173c832ce25e8 recomputed sha256sum go.sum module_count 3 count of distinct modules in go.sum module_<n>_path e.g. github.com/gorilla/mux go.sum column 1 module_<n>_version e.g. v1.8.1 go.sum column 2 module_<n>_checksum e.g. h1:TuBL49tXwgrFYWhqrNgrUNEY92u81SPhu7sTdzQEiWY= go.sum column 3 (module content hash, the non-/go.mod row)

The three modules pinned, all taken verbatim from go.sum in this repository:

docs.title: Codes
docs.text:
Typed dispositions tests/acceptance/AUR-360.sh::AC-001 actually emits on stderr as AUR-360/AC-001/<code> (exit 1), each now produced by a go.mod/go.sum cross-check, not a structural check alone:

Code Trigger (as implemented) go_lock_mismatch .board/bootstrap/locks/go.yml is absent or not a regular file; go_version differs from go.mod's go directive; a module go.sum records is unpinned, version-drifted, or pinned with the wrong checksum; or the lock pins a module go.sum does not record. source_integrity_error .board/bootstrap/locks/go.yml is a symlink; or the recomputed SHA-256 of go.mod or of go.sum no longer matches the lock's own go_mod_sha256/go_sum_sha256 field (the lock's declared "source hash lock" no longer holds). invalid_lock_or_manifest Missing the exact line schema: bootstrap-lock-v1 or card: AUR-360; no sha256:[0-9a-f]{64} pattern anywhere; a required field (go_version, module, go_mod_sha256, go_sum_sha256, module_count) absent or empty; module_count non-numeric, zero, or not equal to the number of module_<n>_path: lines actually present; or a module_<n>_path/module_<n>_version pair missing or duplicated. mutable_reference The file contains a bare latest token or an @main/@master/@HEAD-style reference. input_limit_exceeded .board/bootstrap/locks/go.yml exceeds 4096 bytes, or module_count exceeds 256 — checked before any per-module parsing, so an over-limit module_count never requires fabricating that many module lines to observe. module-path-mismatch The lock's module: field differs from go.mod's module directive (MUT-001's exact scenario: the module path changed in the snapshot after the source hash was locked, while go_mod_sha256 still matches the untouched go.mod). module-checksum-missing A module go.sum records is pinned in the lock with the correct path and version but an empty/absent module_<n>_checksum (MUT-002's exact scenario: the checksum removed, the version kept).

unknown-selector (exit 64) is emitted for any first argument outside AC-001, ContractAUR360, IntegrationAUR360, E2EAUR360; all four accepted selectors currently run the identical body above.

docs.title: Known gap — round 2 closure
docs.text:
Round 1 sealed a structural-only oracle (three checks: schema line present, some sha256: pattern present, no mutable token) that never read go.mod or go.sum and could not observe MUT-001 or MUT-002 at all — both mutations left the script's exit at 0. Round 2 replaces the oracle body with verify_go_lock(), which parses .board/bootstrap/locks/go.yml field by field and cross-checks go_version, module, go_mod_sha256, go_sum_sha256, and every module_<n>_path/version/checksum triple against the real, materialized go.mod/go.sum (a bijection both ways: no go.sum module unpinned, no lock entry phantom), before any other consumer of the domain runs. This closes every gap round 1 recorded:

  • Module path / go_version drift, per-module version/checksum drift: now detected — module-path-mismatch, go_lock_mismatch (go_version), go_lock_mismatch (per-module version/checksum drift or an unpinned real module), module-checksum-missing (checksum removed but version kept). Reproduced live against the real lock for MUT-001 and MUT-002 (see the acceptance evidence for this round), plus one extra mutation of the same supply-chain class this round adds: a present-but-wrong module_1_checksum (as opposed to MUT-002's missing checksum), which is deliberately a distinct disposition (go_lock_mismatch, not module-checksum-missing) because the field is present and parseable — only its value is wrong.
  • input_limit_exceeded: now reachable — module_count over 256 (the overlimit fixture) or the lock document over 4096 bytes both short-circuit to this code before any per-module parsing.
  • Symlink vs source_integrity_error: a symlinked lock now reports source_integrity_error, not go_lock_mismatch; the same code now also covers a go.mod/go.sum whose recomputed digest no longer matches the lock's own go_mod_sha256/go_sum_sha256 ("tamper in the source" per the card's Then clause — go.mod/go.sum are the "source" MUT-001's own phrasing names, "...depois do source hash lock").

Residual, documented tension (not closed, by design): the card's Public contract line enumerates exactly four codes (go_lock_mismatch|source_integrity_error|invalid_lock_or_manifest| input_limit_exceeded), while Skeptical mutations MUT-001/MUT-002 name two further, more specific literal codes (module-path-mismatch, module-checksum-missing) for what is, read one way, the same underlying "module field drifted from go.mod/go.sum" condition the Public contract's go_lock_mismatch already covers. .board/cards is this card's own forbidden_paths entry, so round 2 cannot edit the card text to reconcile the two lists; instead it honors the more specific, literally quoted MUT-001/MUT-002 strings — the two mutations the skeptical approver actually replays and checks byte-for-byte — as the authoritative requirement for those two exact scenarios, and keeps go_lock_mismatch for every other drift the AC-001 Then clause groups under that name (whole go_version drift, per-module version/checksum drift not matching either MUT's exact shape, and phantom pins). A future card correcting the card text itself (not this one, and not this file) would need to either fold module-path-mismatch/module-checksum-missing into the four-code contract list explicitly, or drop the two literal strings from the Skeptical mutations prose.

docs.title: Non-goals (restated from the card)

docs.title: AUR-361 — bootstrap action lock (.board/bootstrap/locks/actions.yml)
docs.text: Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

docs.title: Why this is a derivation and not a declaration
docs.text:
Round 1 of this card shipped a lock whose Section 1 (whole-file digests) was the only thing the sealed gate consulted, while Section 3 (the entry_NNN_* records that claimed "every uses: site is registered and pinned") was hand-written and read only to pick a cosmetic label. An adversarial reviewer reproduced the consequence end-to-end in the real container: append a job with uses: some-untrusted-org/some-action@main to a real workflow, recompute only that file's Section-1 digest — exactly what a legitimate author updating the lock does — leave Section 3 untouched, and the sealed accept exits 0 with "result":"pass".

The defect was not "the scanner missed a spelling of uses:". The defect was structural: a field that nobody derives is a field an attacker can leave standing. Section 3 was an assertion, and an assertion about the material under test is worth nothing when the material is what the attacker edits.

The redesign removes the class rather than the instance:

  1. The whole lock is generated. tests/acceptance/AUR-361.sh --generate is a pure function of the bytes under action.yml and .github/workflows. Section 1 and Section 3 come out of the same single pass over the same bytes. There is no hand-written field left in the file.
  2. The gate regenerates and compares byte for byte. The acceptance program derives the complete lock into a temporary file and runs cmp against the committed lock. One byte of divergence is exit 1. There is no field the attacker can leave stale, because there is no field they can set: a new uses: site changes the derived entry list, therefore the derived bytes, therefore the comparison.
  3. The rules run on derived entries. Trusted source, ref type, and pinning are evaluated over the entries the derivation just produced, never over entries a human wrote. This is what stops --generate from becoming the new bypass: regenerating the lock after adding some-untrusted-org/some-action@main makes the byte comparison agree and then the derived-entry policy refuses the run anyway.
  4. Emptiness is failure. Zero input files, zero derived uses: sites, a missing action.yml, a missing .github/workflows, no uses: inside action.yml, or no uses: under .github/workflows each exit 1. An AUR-361 with no uses: site is a broken board, not a clean one.

docs.title: Round 3: killing "the check that never runs"
docs.text:
Round 2's derivation was honest but its policy still classified by branch, and two branches skipped a check. Both were reproduced end-to-end inside the sealed container with exit_code: 0 / "result":"pass":

  • B1 — the docker branch had no owner. owner_is_trusted was called only when entry_kind == remote. For entry_kind == docker the owner was the hard-coded literal string docker, compared against nothing. A uses: docker://evil-registry.example.com/malware@sha256:<64 hex> was recorded in the generated lock and accepted.
  • B2 — a local composite action was opaque. For uses: ./path the derivation hashed the target action.yml for integrity but never opened it, and the file enumeration only ever covered .github/workflows plus the root action.yml. A hidden-nested/action.yml containing uses: attacker-controlled-org/definitely-not-trusted@main raised active_sites from 29 to 30 and passed, with neither the owner nor the mutable ref appearing anywhere in the lock.

These are one defect wearing two hats: a policy expressed as a per-shape branch always has a shape whose branch forgot the check. Round 3 deletes the branches instead of adding a third one.

docs.title: 1. Transitive closure over uses:
docs.text:
derive_lock no longer enumerates a fixed file list. It seeds a worklist with .github/workflows/** plus the root action.yml, and every local uses: target discovered while scanning any file is enqueued into that same worklist, iterated to a fixed point. The scanner used for a nested action.yml is the same scan_file used for a workflow — there is no second, lighter pass.

Cycle handling is structural, not heuristic: a path already enqueued is never enqueued again, so A -> B -> A terminates; and a path being dequeued twice is a hard reject (closure-revisit). At the fixed point four counts must agree — head == |queue|, |visited| == |queue|, |visited| == |enqueued|, |visited| >= |seeds| — or the closure is declared a lie (closure-not-drained, closure-visit-drift, closure-fixpoint-drift, closure-below-seeds).

An independent second opinion runs after the entries are built: every entry whose resolved local target is non-empty must have that target inside the closed file set, or the run exits 1 with closure-incomplete. The two counters that guard that loop use two different predicates (non-empty resolved target vs kind == local) and must agree. So a closure that silently missed an edge fails rather than passes.

Each file in the lock carries file_NNN_origin: seed | closure, so which files entered by closure is visible in the reviewed artifact rather than implied.

docs.title: 2. One origin policy, zero branches
docs.text:
There is a single allowlist table keyed by (source, owner):

github-remote       actions
github-remote       ruby
github-remote       Mpaape
container-registry  docker.io/library
repository          in-tree

origin_is_trusted is called for every derived entry with no conditional whatsoever. entry_kind may change how the owner is extracted; it can never change whether the owner is judged. repository/in-tree is in the table so that an in-repo composite action is allowed by the rule rather than exempt from it — and its contents are then closed over by (1), so "in-tree" is a claim about provenance, not a licence to hide.

docker:// references are normalised to <registry>/<namespace…>/<image> before judgement: alpine becomes docker.io/library/alpine with owner docker.io/library; evil-registry.example.com/malware keeps owner evil-registry.example.com; docker.io/evilns/img gets owner docker.io/evilns. Neither of the latter two is in the table, so both exit 1 with source_integrity_error.

Unknown source, unknown owner, an empty argument, and an empty table all fail closed.

docs.title: 3. The gate proves the check ran
docs.text: Not running a check is itself a failure mode with a typed code. The policy loop counts its own applications and refuses unless origin_checked == reftype_checked == |entries| and origin_checked > 0. The count is emitted into the lock as origin_policy_checked:, and Phase 1b of the gate re-asserts origin_policy_checked == active_site_count > 0 from the committed bytes. Every passing fixture is held to the same equality. So "the policy silently did not happen" cannot look like a pass anywhere.

docs.title: What is scanned
docs.text:
The seed set is exactly the card's read_paths:

  • action.yml — the composite action manifest at the repository root
  • every regular file under .github/workflows, at any depth, with any extension or none (there is no *.yml filter, so EVIL.YML and a/b/c/deep.yml are scanned)

The scanned set is the transitive closure of that seed set under local uses: edges: every action.yml / action.yaml reachable through a chain of uses: ./… references is scanned by the same code, to any depth, cycles included.

Files are emitted in LC_ALL=C sorted order. The scan is byte-oriented and bounded: at most 256 input files (seeds and closure), at most 256 derived entries, at most 4 MiB in total. Crossing a bound exits 1 with input_limit_exceeded.

Local path resolution is component-by-component: .. anywhere refuses (local-action-path-escape), an empty or . segment refuses (local-action-path-malformed), any symlinked component — not only the last — refuses (local-action-path-symlink), a missing component refuses (local-action-missing), and a resolved target outside the scan root refuses (local-action-outside-root). The number of components walked is cross-checked against a separately computed segment count.

docs.title: Symlink behaviour (declared and proved)
docs.text:
find -type f silently omits symlinks, which is precisely how a symlinked workflow file would escape a naive digest sweep. The derivation therefore enumerates symlinks separately and refuses them:

  • any symlink anywhere under .github/workflows → exit 1 source_integrity_error
  • .github/workflows itself being a symlink → exit 1 source_integrity_error
  • action.yml being a symlink → exit 1 source_integrity_error
  • any declared card path (.board/bootstrap/locks/actions.yml, tests/bootstrap/locks/AUR-361, tests/acceptance/AUR-361.sh, docs/specs/AUR-361.md) being a symlink → exit 1 source_integrity_error

Fixtures adv_symlink and symlinked_action_manifest exercise both shapes. .board/bin/oci-run independently refuses a symlinked acceptance program and refuses any symlink whose target is outside the materialised allowlist, so the container path is covered twice.

docs.title: Byte hygiene
docs.text: A NUL byte cannot be detected with BusyBox awk/grep (they truncate) or with bash read (it drops the byte silently). The derivation counts NUL bytes with tr -cd '\000' | wc -c and refuses any input with a non-zero count (invalid_lock_or_manifest). Carriage returns are counted the same way and refused, so a CRLF rewrite of a workflow cannot shift the line numbers the lock records. Path names containing a newline are caught by a count assertion: the number of lines from find -type f must equal the number of NULs from find -type f -print0, and a disagreement exits 1.

docs.title: The uses: scanner
docs.text:
Derivation is line-based on purpose. A YAML object model — which the previous round used — loses every document after the first --- and attributes merge-key reuse to the wrong site. A line scan loses neither. Each line is processed in three stages:

  1. Full-line comment. If the first non-whitespace character is #, the line is inert by YAML's own rule. If it nonetheless carries the textual token uses: it is recorded as an inert_NNN_* witness so that even commented references are locked bytes.
  2. Unsupported construct. On a line that carries the token uses, an explicit key indicator (?), a merge key (<<:), or a YAML anchor/alias in key or value position exits 1 with invalid_lock_or_manifest. These are the constructs the scanner cannot reason about, so they are rejected rather than skipped — "no blind spot" is enforced, not claimed.
  3. Flow segmentation. The line is split at {, [ and ,. A segment is an active uses: key iff, after stripping leading whitespace and the structural characters -, ", ', it begins with uses, then an optional quote, then optional whitespace, then :.

Splitting cannot create a false negative: splitting only produces more segments, and a real uses: key always begins its own segment. It can produce a false positive (a uses: inside a quoted scalar that follows a comma); that direction is fail-closed and is the deliberate bias.

Forms proved by fixture: double-quoted value, single-quoted value, quoted key with space before the colon ("uses" : "…"), full-line comment, uses: inside a run: string, zero indentation, twenty-space indentation, no space after the colon, single-line flow mapping with uses first, single-line flow mapping with uses last, multi-line flow mapping, multi-document stream, uppercase filename, deep subdirectory, NUL byte, CRLF, alias value, merge-key reuse of an anchored uses:.

Known and declared residue: the merge site <<: *tpl is not counted as a separate site. It cannot smuggle anything, because the anchor's own uses: line is scanned and judged (fixture anchor_merge shows the anchored floating tag being refused), and any merge line is rejected outright when it carries the token uses.

docs.title: Reference classification and policy
docs.text:
Two independent gates apply to every entry, in this order: the origin gate (is this owner allowed to supply code to this repository at all?) and the ref gate (is this reference immutable?). Neither is conditional on the shape.

Origin gate — the (source, owner) allowlist above, applied to all entries:

shape source derived owner verdict actions/checkout@… github-remote actions allowed some-untrusted-org/x@… github-remote some-untrusted-org exit 1 source_integrity_error docker://alpine@… container-registry docker.io/library allowed docker://evil-registry.example.com/malware@… container-registry evil-registry.example.com exit 1 source_integrity_error docker://docker.io/evilns/img@… container-registry docker.io/evilns exit 1 source_integrity_error ./path repository in-tree allowed, and the target is then scanned by closure

Ref gate — applied to all entries after the origin gate:

shape ref_type requirement owner/repo@<40 hex> commit_sha accepted owner/repo@<7..39 hex> abbrev_sha exit 1 action_ref_mutable owner/repo@<anything else> mutable_tag frozen-debt register only ./path local_path resolves to a real action.yml/action.yaml; the lock binds its sha256 and its uses: lines are derived transitively; missing, escaping or symlinked → source_integrity_error docker://img@sha256:<64 hex> docker_digest accepted only if the normalised registry/namespace is in the origin allowlist docker://img:tag mutable_tag exit 1 action_ref_mutable anything else — exit 1 invalid_lock_or_manifest

An untrusted origin exits 1 with source_integrity_error even when the reference is perfectly pinned — fixture untrusted_owner pins some-untrusted-org/some-action@11bd7190…, fixture docker_untrusted_registry pins a full 64-hex manifest digest, and fixture nested_local_deep pins a full commit SHA two composite-action levels down. All three are refused. A sha256: digest proves which bytes; it never proves whose bytes, so pinning alone is not a substitute for provenance.

docs.title: The frozen floating-tag debt register
docs.text:
.github/workflows/ci.yml and .github/workflows/documentation.yml predate this card and reference trusted actions by mutable tag. The card's Non-goals forbid AUR-361 from rewriting a mutable uses:, and .github/workflows is a read_path here, so the debt cannot be repaid inside this card. It is frozen instead, as a hard-coded constant in tests/acceptance/AUR-361.sh:

actions/checkout@v4              3
actions/setup-go@v5              3
actions/upload-artifact@v4       2
actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3 1
actions/github-script@v7         1
actions/deploy-pages@v4          1
ruby/setup-ruby@v1               1

A floating reference is tolerated only if its identity@ref appears here and the derived count is less than or equal to the recorded count. Repaying debt is always allowed; growing it is not. actions/checkout@v4 at four sites exits 1 (debt_overflow), actions/checkout@main exits 1 (mutable_tag), actions/checkout@v9 exits 1 (uppercase_ext, deep_subdir). The register lives in the acceptance program, not in the lock, so widening it is a visible diff in a reviewed path and can never be done by regenerating the lock.

Closing this debt is .board/cards/backlog/AUR-306's job (it replaces those workflows with SHA-pinned ones); this card only stops it from growing.

docs.title: Lock schema
docs.text:
# GENERATED by tests/acceptance/AUR-361.sh --generate. Do not hand-edit.
# Every field below is derived from the bytes of the scanned inputs.
schema: bootstrap-lock-v1
card: AUR-361
derivation: uses-closure-derived-v2
seed_file_count: <s>
file_count: <n>                                         (n >= s: closure)
input_bytes: <total>
origin_policy_checked: <a>                              (must equal <a> below)
file_NNN_path / _origin / _bytes / _digest              (n quadruples)
active_site_count: <a>
inert_line_count: <i>
entry_NNN_file / _line / _kind / _source / _owner / _identity /
            _ref / _ref_type / _target / _line_digest   (a decuples)
inert_NNN_file / _line / _line_digest                   (i triples)

file_NNN_origin is seed or closure. entry_NNN_target is the closed-set path a local uses: resolved to, or - for a non-local entry; origin_policy_checked is the number of times the single origin gate fired and is re-asserted against active_site_count by the gate itself.

Ordering is total and deterministic: files in LC_ALL=C path order, entries in (file, line) order, inert witnesses likewise. --generate run five times in a row produces five identical sha256 digests.

Every section is derived. There is no section a human is expected to maintain, and therefore no section whose staleness can be exploited.

docs.title: Error codes
docs.text:
code meaning input_limit_exceeded more than 256 files (seeds plus closure), more than 256 entries, or more than 4 MiB invalid_lock_or_manifest NUL or CR byte, hostile path, unsupported YAML construct, unparseable uses: value or docker image, empty uses: value, zero derived sites, no input files, a closure/scan/policy count assertion failing (closure-*-drift, origin-policy-drift, reftype-policy-drift, origin-policy-never-ran, scan-*-drift), a declared card path missing or empty, or a fixture expectation not met source_integrity_error symlinked input, symlinked local path component, declared path symlink, non-regular input, untrusted origin of any kind (remote owner, container registry/namespace, or a shape whose source is unknown), missing or escaping local action manifest, a local target outside the closed set (closure-incomplete), or a lock/derivation divergence that is neither a site nor an identity nor a ref change action_ref_mutable abbreviated SHA, floating tag outside the frozen register, floating tag above its registered count, or docker:// without a digest action-identity-mismatch drift label: the derived identity at a committed (file, line) differs action-ref-mutable drift label: the derived ref at a committed (file, line) differs action-unlocked drift label: a derived site has no committed counterpart, or vice versa

The three hyphenated labels are the card's MUT-001..003 names. They are labels only: they are produced by classify_drift, which runs strictly after cmp has already decided the exit code is 1. classify_drift cannot select a pass, and the pass path never calls it. It keys on (file, line), so an identity that also occurs elsewhere in the same file — which the previous round's file-wide substring search confused — no longer blurs the label.

docs.title: What the sealed gate actually does
docs.text:
./.board/bin/oci-run --profile bootstrap-readonly-v1 --card AUR-361 runs bash tests/acceptance/AUR-361.sh inside bash@sha256:ae4668c2560999e65e89532cd2ad1b6688bb23298189f0bd229ef80fa4bd0831 (Alpine 3.22 + BusyBox, no Go toolchain), network none, read-only rootfs, all capabilities dropped, non-root, with only the card's paths and read_paths materialised. Consequently:

  • There is no Go engine in this design. Round 1 leaned on tests/integration/AUR-361_test.go for the semantic check; that file was outside the card's declared paths and was invoked by no gate that blocks a card transition, so it was decorative. All semantics now live in the single program the sealed gate actually executes.
  • --generate cannot run inside the container (read-only rootfs). It is an author-side command; the gate only ever re-derives into /tmp and compares.

Phases, in order:

  1. every declared card path exists, is not a symlink, is non-empty, and is actually read (byte counts accumulated, loop count asserted)
  2. re-derive the whole lock from the live tree — seed enumeration, transitive closure to a fixed point, entries, then the single origin+ref policy — and cmp against the committed lock; divergence → classify → exit 1 1b. assert from the committed bytes that origin_policy_checked equals active_site_count and that both are non-zero
  3. run all 37 fixture cases from tests/bootstrap/locks/AUR-361/cases.tsv, asserting exit, code, active count, inert count, identity list, the origin-gate count, and — for every refusing row — the named control that had to fire; the number of cases executed must equal the number of rows declared and must be at least 36, and the number of named controls asserted must equal the number of refusing rows and be non-zero
  4. emit one bounded JSON line on stdout carrying named_controls (how many refusing fixtures named the control that fired), seed_files, closure_files, active_sites and origin_checks

docs.title: Fixtures and reference truth
docs.text:
tests/bootstrap/locks/AUR-361/cases.tsv is hand-written from reading the fixture YAML. It is not generated by the acceptance program and it is not a copy of the lock. This is the point: the previous round's nominal fixture was documented as "an exact copy of the real lock", which made the nominal comparison a tautology. Here the reference truth for the live tree is the workflow files (the lock is the derivative), and the reference truth for the fixtures is a human claim in cases.tsv (the derivation is what is on trial).

Round 3 fixtures, one per blocker plus the controls that prove the mechanism rather than the instance:

fixture proves docker_untrusted_registry B1: a fully digest-pinned image from a foreign registry is refused docker_untrusted_namespace B1: docker.io alone is not trust; the namespace is judged nested_local_hostile B2: a uses: inside a local composite action is derived and is policed nested_local_deep B2: the closure is a fixed point, not one extra level — depth 2 is caught nested_local_cycle A -> B -> A terminates and passes, so cycle handling is not "reject anything recursive" nested_local_trusted positive control: a legitimate nested composite still passes, with both sites recorded zero_uses / no_inputs Law 12: an empty closure and an empty seed set are FAILURES, not clean runs

docs.title: The reason column, and why a typed code was not enough
docs.text:
Round 3 mutation-tested its own controls and found that asserting the typed code alone let two mutants live. Deleting the no-input-files refusal, or deleting the zero-uses-sites-derived refusal, kept the suite green: a different, redundant control (seed-duplicate, origin-policy-never-ran) refused with the same code invalid_lock_or_manifest, and no row could tell the two apart. Behaviour was still fail-closed, but the evidence could not observe a control that had stopped running — the surviving class one level up.

Every refusing row therefore carries a reason: the exact control that must fire. It is asserted as a colon-delimited field of the refusal detail, not as a substring (a substring test would match local-action-missing inside local-action-missing-manifest), and a count assertion requires one named control per refusing row, at least one overall. A refusing row without a reason, or a passing row with one, is itself a failure (fixture-reason-missing, fixture-reason-unexpected), so the column cannot be quietly emptied. Both mutants die on it:

detail fixture-reason:no_inputs:want=no-input-files:detail=seed-duplicate:0/1
detail fixture-reason:zero_uses:want=zero-uses-sites-derived:detail=origin-policy-never-ran

The 24 reasons were written by hand from the fixture YAML and the policy before the suite was run, and all 24 matched on the first execution.

docs.title: Reproducing offline
docs.text:
# regenerate the lock after a legitimate workflow change
bash tests/acceptance/AUR-361.sh --generate

# the card's declared acceptance, sealed
./.board/bin/oci-run --profile bootstrap-readonly-v1 --card AUR-361

docs.title: Diagnosis
docs.text:
Failures print two bounded lines on stderr and nothing else:

AUR-361/AC-001/<code>
AUR-361/AC-001/detail <file>:<line>:<reason>

No workflow content, no environment, no secret and no credential-shaped value is ever echoed — only paths, line numbers, counts and the typed reason.

docs.title: AUR-362 — Fixar scanners de segurança
docs.text: Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Pins the identity, version/digest, versioned rule base, finding format and offline/egress behavior of the four security scanner categories this reconstruction's security office intends to invoke in later cards: a secrets scanner, a dependency/vulnerability scanner, a static-application-security (SAST) scanner and a shell-script linter. tests/acceptance/AUR-362.sh verifies .board/bootstrap/locks/scanners.yml exists as a plain (non-symlink) file within its byte bound, declares the bootstrap-lock-v1 schema line, and parses each of its 46 fields against a ground-truth table — every pinned image digest, every rule-base identity, and every finding-format CLI contract — while also cross-checking .github/workflows, Dockerfile and .docker/docs.Dockerfile for a scanner tool the lock does not carry an entry for. It does all of this without running any scanner. Thirty-four of the 46 fields' ground truth is carried directly in the acceptance script, resolved live against each tool's release API / registry digest as recorded below; the twelve *_finding_format_* fields' ground truth is instead read from a separately-versioned, separately-hashed fixture, tests/bootstrap/locks/AUR-362/ground-truth/cli-format-fields.tsv, mechanically extracted from live pinned-digest CLI transcripts captured in tests/bootstrap/locks/AUR-362/ground-truth/RAW_CAPTURE.txt (see "Ground truth for the finding-format fields" below) — this split exists because a round-2 adversarial review found three of those twelve values wrong in both the lock and the script's own hand-typed literal at once, which a single-file, single-author "independently carried" table cannot catch by construction: a lock value and its own oracle can go wrong together when both are typed by the same hand from the same mistaken belief.

At the time this card was authored, none of .github/workflows/, Dockerfile or .docker/docs.Dockerfile (this card's read_paths) invoke any security scanner: this repository does not yet run secrets, vulnerability, SAST or shell-lint scanning anywhere. This card therefore does not derive its pins from an existing in-repo invocation (there is none to derive from); it fixes, from each tool's own primary source (its GitHub release and its Docker Hub / GHCR image, resolved live against the network available in this workspace), the exact identity every later card that actually wires a scanner into a workflow must reproduce byte-for-byte. Non-goal, restated from the card: this lock does not execute a scanner, produce a finding, or triage a vulnerability.

docs.title: .board/bootstrap/locks/scanners.yml
docs.text:
Flat key: value document, LC_ALL=C, one pair per line, no comments. First line is exactly schema: bootstrap-lock-v1. Four scanner blocks, one per category, sharing the same 11-field shape (scanner_name, scanner_role, scanner_version, scanner_image, rulebase_id, a rule base identity field, finding_format_flag, finding_format_default, finding_format_values, offline_mode [+ offline_flag where the tool needs one], egress), each under a category prefix (secrets_, vuln_, sast_, shell_).

Field (per prefix) Meaning <prefix>_scanner_name The tool's canonical name. <prefix>_scanner_role One of secrets, vulnerabilities, sast, shell. <prefix>_scanner_version The tool's own release tag. <prefix>_scanner_image <registry>/<repo>@sha256:<64 hex> — the OCI image reference this card resolved for that release tag, pinned by digest, never by tag alone. <prefix>_rulebase_id A human identity for the rule base bound to this exact scanner release. rule base identity field <prefix>_rulebase_sha256 (secrets, shell) or <prefix>_rulebase_image (vuln) or <prefix>_rulebase_ref (sast) — the concrete, recomputed-or-resolved identity of the rule base itself, never a value trusted from a floating pointer. <prefix>_finding_format_flag The tool's real CLI flag that selects a machine-readable finding output. <prefix>_finding_format_default The format the tool emits with no flag. <prefix>_finding_format_values The full comma-separated set of formats the flag accepts, as documented by the tool. <prefix>_offline_mode How the tool behaves without network: fully-offline (never calls out), pre-cached-db-required (needs a rule base fetched ahead of time, then runs offline), or local-config-required (needs a local, non-registry rule path). <prefix>_offline_flag The concrete flag that selects the offline behavior, where the tool has one. <prefix>_egress Always denied — every later card that runs one of these scanners inside the board's network: none container profiles must supply the rule base/config locally; none of the four tools is invoked with network available.

docs.title: Per-scanner pins and their primary source
docs.text:
All four were resolved live against each tool's own GitHub release API and Docker Hub / GHCR registry from this workspace on 2026-08-05; the network access itself is evidence, not an assumption — curl -sI https://github.com returned HTTP/2 200 in this session before any pin below was resolved.

secrets — gitleaks v8.30.1 - Release tag: https://api.github.com/repos/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases/latest → tag_name: v8.30.1. - Image digest: docker buildx imagetools inspect zricethezav/gitleaks:v8.30.1 → index digest sha256:c00b6bd0aeb3071cbcb79009cb16a60dd9e0a7c60e2be9ab65d25e6bc8abbb7f. - Rule base: gitleaks' own bundled default config at that same tag, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/v8.30.1/config/gitleaks.toml, fetched and hashed in this session: sha256:e163e53b9e7e8a8511e77271e2b323ed057759542a6d988258afe3a1fa329caf (97731 bytes). - Finding format: -f/--report-format, values json,csv,junit,sarif,template (confirmed live against the pinned digest's own --help, round 3). Default: none — corrected in round 3. Running the pinned digest with no --report-path emits no report at all (log lines only); running it with --report-path but no --report-format fails fatally (Unknown report format:, exit 1) rather than falling back to json. Raw transcript: tests/bootstrap/locks/AUR-362/ground-truth/RAW_CAPTURE.txt, section 4. - Offline: gitleaks scans local git history/files with its bundled config; it never calls out. fully-offline.

vulnerabilities — trivy 0.73.0 - Release tag: https://api.github.com/repos/aquasecurity/trivy/releases/latest → tag_name: v0.73.0. - Image digest: docker buildx imagetools inspect aquasec/trivy:0.73.0 → index digest sha256:7cced7cae583819fc7806d4cbc0dbbc7cad18b99f7d3e235192e6da8c091045c. - Rule base: trivy's vulnerability DB is a separate, versioned OCI artifact, schema 2: docker buildx imagetools inspect ghcr.io/aquasecurity/trivy-db:2 → digest sha256:cce7b2ad966d6fe3789d65879579b8b24fce9d31052ed3ff73b1c5224f049142. - Finding format: --format, default table (Cobra's own (default "table") flag annotation, confirmed live). Values: table,json,template,sarif,cyclonedx,spdx,spdx-json,github,cosign-vuln — corrected in round 3. A round-2 adversarial review ran trivy image --help against the exact pinned digest and found the enum this card previously carried (table,json,sarif,template,sbom,github) both missing four real values (cyclonedx, spdx, spdx-json, cosign-vuln) and inventing one that does not exist (sbom — trivy's SBOM output is a shape selected via cyclonedx/spdx/spdx-json, never a literal sbom token). Raw transcript: tests/bootstrap/locks/AUR-362/ground-truth/RAW_CAPTURE.txt, section 1. - Offline: trivy's own air-gap documentation states --offline-scan "prevent[s] Trivy from trying to connect" during scanning; it still requires the DB artifact above to be present locally first. pre-cached-db-required.

sast — semgrep 1.172.0 - Release tag: https://api.github.com/repos/semgrep/semgrep/releases/latest → tag_name: v1.172.0. - Image digest: docker buildx imagetools inspect semgrep/semgrep:1.172.0 → index digest sha256:65dcd4408adda7c183a6b4550cb1e9b19f7f627a6fbb7e0559bd466bedc44d7b. - Rule base: the community semgrep/semgrep-rules repository ships no version tags (.../releases and .../tags both return empty at the time of writing); this card therefore pins the repository's own commit identity instead of an unpinned branch pointer — the branch tip resolved via the GitHub API in this session, commit 311ca4e9ba59d700624539bf658e3d29b134ee77. A later card that adopts this rule base must clone or fetch that exact commit, never a branch name. - Finding format: --json (also --sarif, --text, --junit-xml, --emacs, --vim, --gitlab-sast, --gitlab-secrets) (confirmed live against the pinned digest's own semgrep scan --help, round 3). Default: text — corrected in round 3. A round-2 adversarial review ran the pinned digest with --config=auto and no format flag and found the actual default output is semgrep's own colored "Scan Status"/"Scan Summary" table, never json; round 3 confirmed this transcript is byte-identical to an explicit --text run of the same input, establishing text (not merely "not json") as the correct value. Raw transcript: tests/bootstrap/locks/AUR-362/ground-truth/RAW_CAPTURE.txt, section 3. - Offline: semgrep's --config accepts a local YAML file or directory instead of a registry entry name, which the docs confirm avoids any registry network call. local-config-required.

shell — shellcheck v0.11.0 - Release tag: https://api.github.com/repos/koalaman/shellcheck/releases/latest → tag_name: v0.11.0. - Image digest: docker buildx imagetools inspect koalaman/shellcheck:v0.11.0 → index digest sha256:61862eba1fcf09a484ebcc6feea46f1782532571a34ed51fedf90dd25f925a8d. - Rule base: shellcheck's SC-code checks are compiled into the binary itself; there is no separate rule artifact to pin, so this card uses the same image digest as the rule base identity, on the basis that the two are inseparable for this tool. - Finding format: --format / -f, default tty (confirmed live: the pinned digest's default-invocation transcript is byte-identical to an explicit --format=tty run). Values: checkstyle,diff,gcc,json,json1,quiet,tty — corrected in round 3. A round-2 adversarial review ran the pinned digest with --format=xml and found it rejected (Unknown format xml, exit 4) with the tool's own Supported formats: list matching its --help text exactly — seven values, none named xml. Raw transcript: tests/bootstrap/locks/AUR-362/ground-truth/RAW_CAPTURE.txt, section 2. - Offline: a pure static analyzer over shell script text; it makes no network calls during a scan (this is separate from the unrelated shellcheck.net web front end). fully-offline.

docs.title: Ground truth for the finding-format fields
docs.text:
A round-2 adversarial review (/tmp/aurum-reviews/AUR-362-r2-reviewB.md) found vuln_finding_format_values, shell_finding_format_values and sast_finding_format_default wrong by running the exact pinned scanner digests directly, and identified the structural cause: the round-2 acceptance script's expected ground-truth table was a static bash literal typed by the same author, at the same time, from the same belief as the lock's own values — its comment claimed the table was carried "independently of the lock file it checks," but nothing forced that independence, so a wrong belief could and did land in both places at once, and the "independent" check could never catch its own author's mistake.

Round 3 fixes this for the twelve *_finding_format_* fields specifically (the class where the defect was found), without altering the design for the other 34 fields (each of which round 2 confirmed correct against its own live primary source — GitHub release API, registry digest — a check that already does not depend on the lock's own text):

  1. Every pinned scanner digest in .board/bootstrap/locks/scanners.yml was run live in this session (docker run --rm <pinned digest> ...), for real, against network access confirmed available (docker version succeeded). The complete, verbatim stdout/stderr and exit code of every such invocation is captured in tests/bootstrap/locks/AUR-362/ground-truth/RAW_CAPTURE.txt, timestamped 2026-08-05T14:45:36Z.
  2. tests/bootstrap/locks/AUR-362/ground-truth/cli-format-fields.tsv mechanically extracts the twelve *_finding_format_* values from that raw transcript — a key<TAB>value file, following the same parse discipline tests/acceptance/AUR-362.sh already applies to .board/bootstrap/locks/scanners.yml itself (bounded, non-symlink, duplicate/unknown-key detection, every declared key required present).
  3. tests/acceptance/AUR-362.sh reads this file into its expected map at run time instead of hand-typing these twelve values into its own source a second time. A value wrong in the lock is now only ever caught if it also happens to be wrong, independently, in a separately-versioned, separately-hashed fixture derived mechanically from a raw tool transcript — not merely wrong in the same author's second literal. Absence, corruption, or structural defect (duplicate key, unknown key, a declared field missing) in cli-format-fields.tsv is this program's own fixture machinery failing, not a verdict about the real lock: it fails inconclusive (exit 79), same discipline as cases.tsv.

While reproducing reviewer-b's method against all twelve fields (not only the three named), this round also found secrets_finding_format_default false under the identical test: gitleaks v8.30.1's --report-format flag has no default — omitting it never yields json (see the gitleaks entry above and RAW_CAPTURE.txt section 4). This field is corrected here too, disclosed separately since it fell outside reviewer-b's named blocker; it was found only because this round re-derived the ground truth for the entire *_finding_format_* field group from real tool output rather than touching only the three named fields and trusting the rest.

docs.title: Bounds
docs.text: Bound Value .board/bootstrap/locks/scanners.yml size 8 KiB (observed at 2350 bytes today; independently enforced by tests/acceptance/AUR-362.sh before any field is parsed — see the overlimit fixture below). tests/bootstrap/locks/AUR-362/cases.tsv size 4 MiB (card-declared bound; enforced by the sealed acceptance program). cases.tsv rows 256 (card-declared bound; enforced by the sealed acceptance program). tests/bootstrap/locks/AUR-362/ground-truth/cli-format-fields.tsv size 4 KiB (round-3 bound; enforced before any of its rows are parsed — absence or a bound violation is inconclusive, never a lock verdict). Acceptance container wall-clock (accept vector, informational) 15 s.

docs.title: Codes
docs.text:
Typed dispositions tests/acceptance/AUR-362.sh emits on stderr as AUR-362/AC-001/<code> (exit 1, behavioral). The script parses .board/bootstrap/locks/scanners.yml field by field against a ground-truth table (34 fields resolved live from each tool's own release API / registry digest and carried directly in the script; the twelve *_finding_format_* fields read at run time from the separately-versioned tests/bootstrap/locks/AUR-362/ground-truth/cli-format-fields.tsv — see "Ground truth for the finding-format fields" above), and cross-checks .github/workflows, Dockerfile and .docker/docs.Dockerfile for a scanner this card never locked:

Code Trigger scanner_lock_incomplete .board/bootstrap/locks/scanners.yml is absent (not a symlink; a symlink is source_integrity_error, below). source_integrity_error The lock is a symlink rather than a plain file, or a pinned identity field (a *_scanner_image, vuln_rulebase_image, *_rulebase_sha256/_digest/_ref) is well-formed but its value diverges from the ground-truth table — a supply-chain value tampered without breaking its own shape. invalid_lock_or_manifest The file is empty, misses the schema: bootstrap-lock-v1 or card: AUR-362 line, misses any sha256:<64 hex> digest, is missing one of the schema's 46 declared fields outright, or a non-identity, non-format field (name/role/version/rulebase_id/offline_mode/offline_flag/egress) has a well-formed but wrong value. input_limit_exceeded .board/bootstrap/locks/scanners.yml exceeds 8 KiB, or cases.tsv exceeds its own 4 MiB / 256-row bound. scanner-ref-mutable A pinned OCI image field (any *_scanner_image, or vuln_rulebase_image) does not match <registry>/<repo>@sha256:<64 hex> — a digest replaced by a floating tag or branch reference (MUT-003's class; vuln_rulebase_image is this card's own extra field in the same class). finding-schema-mismatch Any *_finding_format_flag/_default/_values field diverges from the ground-truth CLI contract for that scanner's pinned version (MUT-002's class). scanner-unlocked .github/workflows, Dockerfile or .docker/docs.Dockerfile reference a scanner tool this card's lock does not carry a prefix for (MUT-001's class).

docs.title: Known gap between this card's prose and the sealed acceptance program
docs.text:
This gap, as recorded by this card's round-1 builder, is now closed. The round-2 acceptance program (tests/acceptance/AUR-362.sh) parses .board/bootstrap/locks/scanners.yml field by field against an independently-carried ground-truth table (not merely three whole-file structural checks), and separately cross-checks this card's read_paths (.github/workflows, Dockerfile, .docker/docs.Dockerfile) for a scanner tool absent from the lock. Per gap item recorded by round 1:

  • MUT-001 (scanner-unlocked) is now produced: the script scans the three read_paths for a fixed set of scanner-tool keywords disjoint from the four this card locks (bandit, snyk, codeql, checkov, trufflehog, grype, syft, gosec) and fails scanner-unlocked on any match. This still never writes to .github/workflows, Dockerfile or .docker/docs.Dockerfile in the repository proper (read_paths, not paths) — the two new fixtures below (unlocked-workflow, unlocked-dockerfile) each materialize their own private copy of the affected read_path under this card's own paths (tests/bootstrap/locks/AUR-362/fixtures/<case>/...), and the live round-2 proof mutated .github/workflows/ci.yml only transiently, restoring it via git checkout and a matching SHA-256 before the patch was cut.
  • MUT-002 (finding-schema-mismatch) is now produced: the script parses all twelve *_finding_format_* fields and fails finding-schema-mismatch on any divergence from the ground-truth CLI contract, independent of the selector (AC-001, ContractAUR362, IntegrationAUR362, E2EAUR362 all run the identical check; the selector remains a passthrough label).
  • MUT-003 (scanner-ref-mutable) now emits the card's own literal code instead of the structurally-similar mutable_reference round 1 used: any of the five pinned-image fields (secrets_scanner_image, vuln_scanner_image, vuln_rulebase_image, sast_scanner_image, shell_scanner_image) failing the @sha256:<64 hex> shape now fails exactly scanner-ref-mutable.
  • The byte-size bound is now implemented directly on .board/bootstrap/locks/scanners.yml (8 KiB, checked before any field is parsed) and exercised by the overlimit fixture, closing the input_limit_exceeded gap; cases.tsv's own 4 MiB / 256-row bound was already enforced by the sealed program and remains so.

A round-2 adversarial review (/tmp/aurum-reviews/AUR-362-r2-reviewB.md) blocked that round on exactly this design: it ran the pinned scanner digests directly and found vuln_finding_format_values, shell_finding_format_values and sast_finding_format_default wrong in both the lock and the script's own "independently carried" literal at once — because both were typed by the same author from the same belief, the round-2 script's own comment claiming independence was false for these three fields. Round 3 closes this:

  • The three named fields are corrected to what the pinned digests actually do, confirmed live in this round (see "Ground truth for the finding-format fields" and the per-scanner entries above, each citing its RAW_CAPTURE.txt section).
  • secrets_finding_format_default is also corrected (json → none), found false under the identical live-digest test while this round re-derived ground truth for the whole *_finding_format_* field group rather than only the three named fields — disclosed separately since it was not part of reviewer-b's blocker.
  • The twelve *_finding_format_* fields' ground truth moved out of the script's own hand-typed literal into tests/bootstrap/locks/AUR-362/ground-truth/cli-format-fields.tsv, a separately-versioned, separately-hashed fixture mechanically extracted from RAW_CAPTURE.txt's live pinned-digest transcripts — so this class of defect (one author's same wrong belief landing in the lock and its own oracle at once) requires tampering two independently-versioned artifacts, not editing one file twice. The nominal, unlocked-workflow and unlocked-dockerfile fixtures (byte-identical copies of the real lock) and cases.tsv's SHA-256 for all three were updated to match the corrected lock; every other fixture (tamper, invalid, mutable, mutable-rulebase, format-mismatch, digest-tamper, overlimit) triggers its disposition on a field checked earlier than the *_finding_format_* group in verify_scanners_dir and needed no change.

No open item remains from round 1's list. One judgment call this round adds, recorded here for the next reviewer: a pinned-format-but-wrong-value mismatch on vuln_rulebase_image and the four *_rulebase_sha256/_ref/ _digest content-hash fields is classified source_integrity_error rather than a new code, on the basis that the card's own "Acceptance scenarios" prose groups "tamper" and "symlink" under that single code — this digest-tamper fixture demonstrates a non-symlink instance of the same disposition, and the tamper fixture (a symlink) was re-pointed from scanner_lock_incomplete to source_integrity_error to match, since the card text assigns absence and tamper/symlink two different codes and the round-1 script had collapsed them into one.

tests/bootstrap/locks/AUR-362/cases.tsv and its fixtures/ (11 cases: nominal, absence, tamper, invalid, mutable, mutable-rulebase, format-mismatch, digest-tamper, unlocked-workflow, unlocked-dockerfile, overlimit) reproduce every disposition tests/acceptance/AUR-362.sh can now produce, each fixture's .board/bootstrap/locks/scanners.yml (or, for the two unlocked-* cases, its accompanying materialized read_path file) hashed by SHA-256 in cases.tsv so a byte-identical replay is independently verifiable.
