The verdict says why: BROWSERPROOF_TARGET_ABSENT (no home page), BROWSERPROOF_UNREACHABLE_ROUTE (the index links to nothing), BROWSERPROOF_TEXT_MISMATCH (a page without the expected content), BROWSERPROOF_EMPTY_RENDER 64 Usage: missing/unknown flags, --docs not a readable directory 69 Inconclusive: the environment could not judge (invalid request, unusable pinned driver, uncorroborated driver observation, server fault). Never read as pass or fail

docs.title: The driver
docs.text: Without AURUM_BROWSERPROOF_DRIVER the run navigates through the in-process scripted driver and says so on stderr; the driver identity (kind + digest) is part of the embedded proof, and the scripted double can never satisfy a lock that pins a real browser. Setting AURUM_BROWSERPROOF_DRIVER to a pinned headless-browser driver executable upgrades the same command to a real browser without changing the output contract.

docs.title: Offline by design
docs.text: The acceptance sandbox denies network, so the verification proves the exact built artifact by serving it on loopback - the simulated-driver instrument AUR-428's acceptance already names for this card. --url names the published location the verdict is about and is recorded verbatim in published_url; watching the live deploy at that URL is the human action AUR-428 documents, not something this hermetic command pretends to do.

docs.title: Failure diagnostic
docs.text:
The verdict on stdout carries outcome, code and a bounded sanitized detail naming the route that broke; stderr repeats the code. A refusal is a statement about the site (fix the generated pages or the publication); an inconclusive is a statement about the environment (fix the driver, the request or the sandbox) and never a statement about the site.

Example refusal, symbol page published without the promised content:

docsverify: refused: BROWSERPROOF_TEXT_MISMATCH: none of the 1 links the index carries shows "func NewGreeting"

docs.title: Security
docs.text: The verification reaches only the loopback server it starts; the scripted driver refuses non-loopback addresses and an external driver inherits no environment (no AURUM_SECRET_CANARY, tokens or proxy settings). Verdicts carry sanitized bounded text only - never raw HTML, screenshots or secrets.

docs.title: AUR-430: aurumcode review
docs.text:
Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

Restores AurumCode's local code-review engine (deleted 2025-11-03, commit c12d7ab is the last commit before deletion) and wires it behind a new CLI entrypoint, cmd/aurumcode.

docs.title: Command
docs.text:
aurumcode review --base <ref>

Run from inside the git repository you want reviewed — a normal working tree, a linked worktree (git worktree add), or a bare repository, with loose or packed objects. It diffs <ref> against HEAD in that repository, sends the diff to a model, and prints every finding the model reports as one line per finding:

<file>:<line>: [<severity>] <message>

sorted by (file, line) so the same input always prints in the same order. If the model reports no findings, it prints No issues found.. Running the command twice against the same input always produces byte-identical output.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Flag Required Meaning --base <ref> yes The ref to diff against HEAD. Accepts a 40-hex commit SHA, a branch name (resolved under refs/heads/), HEAD, or any of those with a ~N parent-walk suffix (HEAD~1, main~2, ...).

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 The command ran and printed its findings (including zero findings). 1 A real failure: not a git repository, the ref does not resolve, the LLM call failed, or the model's response could not be understood at all (see "Parser fallback" below). 2 Usage error: unknown subcommand, or review invoked without --base.

docs.title: Provider configuration
docs.text:
aurumcode review never hardcodes a vendor. It selects a provider from the environment, in this order:

  1. AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE=<path> — read that file's content and return it verbatim as the model's response. This is how the acceptance test and the example below run fully offline and deterministically; it is not a special case in the review engine, just an llm.Provider implementation (internal/review.FakeProvider) like any other.
  2. LLM_API_KEY and LLM_BASE_URL — use the existing OpenAI-compatible LiteLLM proxy provider (internal/llm/provider/litellm), the same one cmd/regenerate-docs already uses, naming a model via LLM_MODEL (default gpt-4).
  3. Neither set: the command fails with a clear error naming both options, never a panic or a silent no-op provider.

docs.title: Example (no secrets)
docs.text:
$ cd tests/fixtures/repos/git-demo/repo.git   # a deterministic fixture repo
$ AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE=../../review/known-problem-response.json \
    go run ../../../../../cmd/aurumcode review --base HEAD~1
config/demo-tokens.txt:4: [error] A credential-shaped value was committed in plain text (DEMO_API_TOKEN).

The fixture response and the values it describes (AURUM-FAKE-TOKEN-0000-0001 and friends) are synthetic; see tests/fixtures/repos/git-demo/content/03/config/demo-tokens.txt.

docs.title: Limits on what gets diffed
docs.text:
Not every changed file can be line-diffed safely, so aurumcode review refuses some of them before reading their content into lines. A refused file is left out of the diff entirely — no model call is made for it, and none of its content reaches a prompt — and is reported on stdout instead:

$ aurumcode review --base HEAD~1
diff too large: generated/schema.sql (12480 lines > limit 10000)
diff too large: dist/bundle.min.js (3145728 bytes > limit 1048576)
binary file, skipped: assets/logo.png
src/auth.go:88: [warning] Error from the token refresh path is discarded.

Skipping is a normal outcome, not a failure: the notices print before the findings, in the same sorted path order the diff uses, and the exit code is still 0.

Limit Value Applied to Lines per side 10000 The old and new content of one file, independently. Bytes per side 1 MiB Same. Catches minified or generated single-line files, which pass the line limit trivially. Binary a NUL byte in the first 8000 bytes Git's own heuristic and its own window.

The limits exist because the cost of a line diff is driven by the edit distance D, not by file size alone. The engine records the shortest-edit- script search trace, and that trace grows as D²; left unbounded it made reviewing a single 12674-line added file cost about 2.6 GB, and a ~22k-line file could exhaust a 31 GB host. Two independent bounds now prevent that:

  • This input cap, which rejects files outright, with the messages above.
  • A trace budget (maxTraceCells in internal/analyzer/textdiff.go, 4Mi cells ≈ 32 MiB). A file under the input cap can still have a large edit distance — two 10000-line versions sharing nothing — so the search itself is budgeted too. Past the budget the engine stops searching for the minimal script and renders the change as a whole-file replacement: every old line removed, every new line added. That output is correct, just coarser, and it costs O(N+M).

Budgeting the trace rather than pre-rejecting on worst-case size is what keeps the common case exact: a one-line change inside a 10000-line file has an edit distance of 2 no matter how long the file is, so it is diffed precisely and costs almost nothing. Peak memory for the differ is bounded by the trace budget regardless of input, and files within both bounds produce byte-for-byte the same diff they always did — internal/analyzer checks that against the previous full-width implementation over every pair of strings up to length 6, and textdiff_memory_test.go fails if the unbounded shape returns.

docs.title: Diagnosing a failure
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause aurumcode review: <dir> is not a git repository cwd is not a git repository: no git binary recognizes it, no .git directory, and it is not itself a bare repository (no HEAD/objects/refs). aurumcode review: computing diff <ref>..HEAD: ...object ... not found as a loose object (packed objects are not supported by this reader) No git binary was found on PATH, so the pure-Go fallback reader is in use, and it only reads loose objects; see "Reading a repository" below. aurumcode review: no LLM provider configured: ... Neither AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE nor LLM_API_KEY+LLM_BASE_URL is set. aurumcode review: could not understand the model's response (no_json_found\|invalid_json\|validation_failed\|no_findings_recovered) The model's response had neither valid JSON nor a recognizable degraded-mode finding line (see below).

docs.title: Reading a repository: two backends, selected once
docs.text:
aurumcode review must work both against a real, lived-in checkout — a linked worktree, where .git is a file, not a directory (this very card was built in one); a repository whose objects git gc has packed (this board's own AurumCode checkout is one) — and inside this card's sealed acceptance profile, bootstrap-readonly-v1, which carries a Go toolchain and bash but no git binary and no network. One implementation cannot satisfy both for free, so internal/analyzer/gitrepo.go's OpenRepo picks a backend once, and every other method (ResolveRef, Diff, the tree walk) is written against that single choice:

  • git binary present (the common case on a real machine): every read goes through git rev-parse and git cat-file, run with the reviewed repository's own directory as the subprocess's working directory and no other flags — this is exactly the os/exec approach this card's own text describes. Letting git itself discover the repository is what makes a linked worktree and a git gc'd repository work at all: git already understands .git-as-a-file indirection and packfiles; reimplementing either in this reader would just be a worse copy of git.
  • No git binary (this card's own acceptance sandbox — the same fact card AUR-011's acceptance program independently documents and relies on for the same fixture): a pure-Go reader inflates loose objects directly (zlib + the standard type size\0content header) and resolves refs by reading the loose ref files, then walks commit → tree → blob to build the diff itself, using a from-scratch Myers O(ND) line diff (internal/analyzer/textdiff.go) for each changed blob. This path is scoped to loose objects only — the shape every fresh commit, and the tests/fixtures/repos/git-demo fixture, uses — and returns a clear, typed error naming the object when it meets a packed one, never a silently empty diff.

Both backends return the same information through the same Repo methods, so Diff, the tree walk and the line diff are written and tested once. internal/analyzer/gitrepo_test.go runs entirely on the pure-Go path (this repository's own sandbox has no git); internal/analyzer/gitrepo_gitbinary_test.go builds a real repository — including a linked worktree and a git gc'd one — and runs the git-binary path against it whenever a git binary is available to run it with, skipping (never silently passing) when one is not.

docs.title: Prompt sourced from .aurumcode/prompts/review.md
docs.text: internal/prompt/templates/review.md is a build-time copy of the read-only .aurumcode/prompts/review.md. go:embed patterns cannot reach outside their own source file's directory tree, so a runtime read of the read-only path was the only alternative — but that would tie the binary's behavior to running with a particular working directory or a repo-relative env var, which a CLI meant to review an arbitrary target repository should not require. Baking the content in at build time keeps the binary self-contained regardless of where it runs, at the cost of the copy needing to be refreshed if .aurumcode/prompts/review.md changes (out of this card's scope to automate).

docs.title: Parser fallback
docs.text:
The restored internal/prompt.ResponseParser.ParseReviewResponse used to have exactly one path: parse the model's response as JSON, or fail the entire review with no output. That is a real usability problem for smaller or local models that cannot reliably follow a JSON schema.

ParseReviewResponse now has two paths:

  1. JSON (unchanged behavior for a well-formed response): extract JSON from a fenced code block or a bare {...}, repair common malformations (see repairJSON below), decode and validate it.
  2. Degraded fallback: if step 1 fails for any reason, scan the response line by line for the convention
[-*] <path>:<line>: [severity:] <message>

(severity defaults to warning when omitted) and turn every match into a types.ReviewIssue. If that recovers at least one finding, it is returned as a normal, successful result with Metadata["parse_mode"] == "degraded".

If neither path produces anything, ParseReviewResponse returns a typed *prompt.ParseError (with a Kind — no_json_found, invalid_json, validation_failed, or no_findings_recovered — and a bounded preview of the raw response) rather than an empty-but-successful result. This distinction matters: an empty []ReviewIssue must always mean "the model looked and found nothing," never "the engine gave up and said nothing."

docs.title: repairJSON: quotes are repaired, not blindly swapped
docs.text:
The restored repairJSON translated typographic ("smart") double quotes (“ ”) to straight ASCII quotes with a global string replace over the entire response, including inside already-open JSON string values. That is a real bug: substituting inside a string value inserts a bare, unescaped " that ends the string early and corrupts everything after it.

repairJSON now tracks, character by character, whether it is currently inside a JSON string. A quote character — straight or typographic — only closes the current string when it looks like a genuine boundary (the next non-whitespace character is one of , } ] :, or end of input); any other quote met inside a string is escaped in place instead. Typographic single quotes/apostrophes (‘ ’) are never JSON delimiters, so they are still normalized with a plain global replace. See TestRepairJSON/smart_quotes and TestRepairJSON_TypographicQuotesInsideStringsDoNotCorruptJSON in internal/prompt/parser_test.go.

docs.title: ISOScores is optional
docs.text: pkg/types.ReviewResult.ISOScores is *ISOScores today (the restored c12d7ab code treated it as a value field). This card's engine never asks a model to score ISO/IEC 25010 characteristics — that scoring pipeline (internal/review/rules.go, internal/review/iso25010) is explicitly out of scope here and belongs to dependent cards — so a response that omits iso_scores is valid and ISOScores stays nil; a block that is present is still validated to the 1–10 range.

docs.title: No vendor coupling
docs.text: internal/analyzer, internal/prompt and internal/review name no LLM vendor anywhere. The engine's only contact point with a model is internal/llm.Orchestrator.Complete(ctx, prompt, llm.Options), called with whatever llm.Provider cmd/aurumcode's selectProvider constructed — internal/review.FakeProvider for the offline/fixture path, or the existing vendor-neutral internal/llm/provider/litellm.Provider for a live one. internal/review/reviewer_test.go, tests/unit/AUR-430.go, tests/integration/AUR-430.go and the acceptance program all run the real review pipeline through FakeProvider and never touch a vendor package; that is the proof, not just the claim, that the pipeline is provider-agnostic.

docs.title: MUT-001 (the skeptical mutation) is applied to a staged copy, not to production
docs.text: tests/acceptance/AUR-430.sh's mutation_case proves the card's declared mutation — "return an empty issue list for a diff with a known problem" — by editing a writable, throwaway staged copy of reviewer.go with sed (nulling the issue slice right before GenerateReview's final return), rebuilding a second binary from that mutated copy, and asserting the known-problem diff then comes back with No issues found.. The committed source is never touched, so this is reversible by construction — there is nothing to "restore" afterward. An earlier draft of this card instead read an AURUM_A430_MUTATION environment variable inside GenerateReview itself; that shipped a runtime kill-switch in the production binary (set one env var, a security review tool reports zero findings, silently, exit 0) and was removed before this card's candidate was reviewed. Production internal/review/reviewer.go contains no mutation hook of any kind.

docs.title: Out of scope (see the card)
docs.text:
• Fetching a PR's diff from a Git host (GitHub, etc.) or publishing a review comment — future cards (AUR-437+).
  • Rule citation (internal/review/rules.go) and ISO/IEC 25010 scoring (internal/review/iso25010) — dependent cards.

docs.title: AUR-431 — aurumcode review --fail-on: break the build on a grave finding
docs.text:
Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

aurumcode review --base <ref> --fail-on <level> turns the AUR-430 review into a CI gate: the command exits with the distinct code 3 when the review reports at least one finding at the chosen severity or above, and 0 when no finding reaches the threshold. Without --fail-on, nothing changes: the command behaves exactly as documented in docs/specs/AUR-430.md, and findings never influence the exit code.

docs.title: Command
docs.text:
aurumcode review --base <ref> [--fail-on <level>]
Flag Required Meaning --base <ref> yes Unchanged from AUR-430: the ref to diff against HEAD. --fail-on <level> no Minimum severity that closes the gate. When any finding sits at this severity or above, the command exits 3 after printing its normal output.

docs.title: Levels
docs.text:
The review engine emits exactly three severities — error, warning, info (internal/prompt/parser.go rejects anything else). --fail-on accepts those names directly, plus the CI-conventional aliases high, medium and low. Matching is case-insensitive.

--fail-on value Gates on high or error error only medium or warning warning and error low or info info, warning and error

Any other value — including an explicitly empty one (--fail-on=, or --fail-on "$VAR" with VAR empty in CI) — is a usage error: the command exits 2 before reviewing anything, never a silently-open gate.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Code Meaning 0 The review ran; no finding reached the --fail-on threshold (or no --fail-on was given). 1 A real failure, unchanged from AUR-430: not a git repository, the ref does not resolve, the LLM call failed, or the response could not be understood. 2 Usage error, unchanged plus one case: unknown subcommand, review without --base, or an unknown --fail-on level. 3 The gate closed: the review ran fine and found at least one issue at or above the --fail-on severity.

3 is deliberately distinct from 1 so a pipeline can tell "the review found a grave problem" (block the merge, show the findings) apart from "the review tool itself broke" (fix the pipeline).

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
stdout is byte-identical with and without --fail-on: the same notices and findings, in the same sorted order, as specified by AUR-430. When the gate closes, one explanatory line goes to stderr:

aurumcode review: 1 finding(s) at severity error or above (--fail-on error)

The stderr note names the canonical engine severity (error, warning, info) regardless of which alias the user typed. Repeating the run over the same input produces the same output and the same exit code.

docs.title: Example (no secrets)
docs.text:
Fully offline, deterministic, no network and no credentials — the model response is pinned to a file via AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE (see AUR-430's provider selection):

$ cat /tmp/response.json
{
  "issues": [
    {
      "file": "config/demo-tokens.txt",
      "line": 4,
      "severity": "error",
      "message": "A credential-shaped value was committed in plain text (DEMO_API_TOKEN)."
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The change commits plaintext credential-shaped values."
}
$ cd tests/fixtures/repos/git-demo/repo.git
$ AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE=/tmp/response.json aurumcode review --base HEAD~1 --fail-on high
config/demo-tokens.txt:4: [error] A credential-shaped value was committed in plain text (DEMO_API_TOKEN).
aurumcode review: 1 finding(s) at severity error or above (--fail-on error)
$ echo $?
3
$ AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE=/tmp/response.json aurumcode review --base HEAD~1 --fail-on high; echo $?   # info-only response instead: exit 0

A typical CI step is then just:

aurumcode review --base "origin/${BASE_BRANCH}" --fail-on high

docs.title: Failure diagnosis
docs.text:
• Exit 3, findings printed — working as intended: a finding at or above the threshold closed the gate. Read the findings on stdout and the count on stderr.
  • Exit 2, --fail-on: unknown level ... — the level is not one of high|error, medium|warning, low|info. Fix the spelling; the gate never guesses.
  • Exit 1 — the review itself failed before any gating; diagnose it exactly as for AUR-430 (repository, ref, provider configuration, parser).
  • Exit 0 but you expected 3 — check the threshold: a warning finding does not close a --fail-on high gate. Rerun with --fail-on medium or low to gate on lower severities.

docs.title: MUT-001 note
docs.text: The skeptical mutation for this card downgrades the severity every finding presents to the gate (severityRank(issue.Severity) → severityRank(issue.Severity[:0]+"info") in cmd/aurumcode/main.go's countAtOrAbove — the slice keeps the mutant compiling): the gated command then exits 0 again and the acceptance fails. The mutation is applied only to a scratch staged copy inside tests/acceptance/AUR-431.sh::mutation_case; the committed source contains no mutation hook, and the unmutated binary reproduces the exact GREEN in the same run.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: This card changes only cmd/aurumcode (flag parsing, severity ranking and the exit-code gate). The review pipeline — analyzer, prompt, parser, reviewer, providers — is byte-untouched, and every contract published by AUR-430 (output format, existing exit codes, provider selection) holds verbatim.

docs.title: AUR-432 — Revisar código privado sem vazar segredo
docs.text:
Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

aurumcode review --base <ref> reviews private code that may contain credentials. This card wires the single AUR-009 redaction filter (internal/security/redaction) into every path a secret could take out of that command: a secret present in the reviewed diff never reaches the model, and a secret echoed back by the model never reaches stdout, stderr, the prompt capture, or the report. The finding that cites the secret's line still arrives, because the filter replaces values, not context.

docs.title: Command
docs.text:
aurumcode review --base <ref> [--fail-on <level>] [--modelo <nome>]

Flags, output format, and exit codes are exactly those published by AUR-430 (docs/specs/AUR-430.md), AUR-431 (--fail-on), and AUR-436 (--modelo). This card changes none of them: for a secret-free review, stdout and stderr are byte-identical to the previous behavior.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
• 0 — the review ran; findings (if any) printed.
  • 1 — the review itself failed (provider, parse, repository error).
  • 2 — usage error.
  • 3 — --fail-on gate closed (AUR-431).

Redaction never changes an exit code: it sanitizes content, it does not judge it.

docs.title: The three wiring points
docs.text:
1. Send path (internal/review/reviewer.go): the diff — the untrusted material — is redacted before the prompt is assembled (redactDiff). Composition matters, not just coverage: a diff line carries a +/-/space marker and the filter's header rule is anchored at line start, so redacting the assembled prompt would let +Authorization: Bearer x through verbatim. Each line's marker is stripped, the bodies are redacted together (anchored header rules and the multi-line private-key rule both apply), and the markers are re-attached; a collapsed multi-line secret fails closed without markers. Secret values become [REDACTED]; key names, header names, file paths and line structure survive, so the model still sees that a credential sits on a line and can report it usefully.
  2. Model output boundary (internal/review/reviewer.go): the parsed response — untrusted model output that may echo a secret — is redacted field by field (file, message, suggestion, summary, comments) at the boundary. Prose fields get the same marker-stripping treatment, because a model quoting the offending diff line echoes it marker and all. This runs before the AUR-434 rule-citation suffix is appended: the suffix (rule security/hardcoded-secret: <title>) comes from the trusted embedded catalog and would itself be rewritten by the filter's secret: value rule, so redacting first is what keeps the published output byte-stable for secret-free reviews.
  3. Process sinks (cmd/aurumcode/main.go): stderr writes through redaction.NewWriter (every canonical stderr line is filter-identity, pinned by TestStderrLinesSurviveTheRedactionWriter); diff-derived notices pass Filter.Redact before stdout. The --modelo selection note masks an LLM_BASE_URL userinfo password at the origin with url.Redacted() (redactedEndpoint), and the stderr writer replaces the whole userinfo component on top of that.

The AURUM_SECRET_CANARY environment value, when present, is registered as an exact-match secret (redaction.FromEnv) in both the reviewer's filter and the CLI's sink filter. There is no response cache in this path (llm.NewOrchestrator(provider, nil, nil)); the only persisted prompt artifact is the opt-in capture below, which is written after redaction.

docs.title: Observing the guarantee: AURUMCODE_PROMPT_CAPTURE
docs.text: With the deterministic offline provider (AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE), setting AURUMCODE_PROMPT_CAPTURE=<file> makes the provider write the exact prompt it received to <file> (mode 0600) before answering. That is the observability hook the acceptance uses to prove nothing secret leaves the process — with the wiring in place the captured prompt is already redacted. Live providers have no equivalent; the wire-level proof for them is tests/integration/AUR-432.go, which records the raw bytes a loopback endpoint receives.

docs.title: Offline, secret-free example
docs.text:
cd "$(mktemp -d)"
cat > response.json <<'EOF'
{
  "issues": [
    {
      "file": "config/demo-tokens.txt",
      "line": 4,
      "severity": "error",
      "rule_id": "security/hardcoded-secret",
      "message": "A hardcoded credential is committed in plain text at this line."
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The change commits a plaintext credential."
}
EOF
cd <repo-under-review>
AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE=$OLDPWD/response.json \
AURUMCODE_PROMPT_CAPTURE=$OLDPWD/prompt.txt \
aurumcode review --base HEAD~1
# prompt.txt now holds what the model was shown: values [REDACTED],
# context intact. Every value in this example is synthetic.

docs.title: Failure diagnosis
docs.text:
• A planted value found in prompt.txt, stdout, or stderr is the behavioral RED this card guards against (AUR-432/AC-001/behavior-missing in the acceptance vocabulary).
  • tests/acceptance/AUR-432.sh AC-001-MUT-001 proves the guard bites at both points: disabling the send-path diff redaction makes the planted secret appear in the capture, and disabling the output-boundary redaction makes the model-echoed secret appear on stdout; either way the accept fails, and restoring reproduces the GREEN.
  • The e2e (tests/e2e/AUR-432.sh) also pins that the AUR-437 fixture builder refuses credential-shaped content (git-demo/non-synthetic-secret), which is why credential shapes are exercised in-process by tests/unit/AUR-432.go with runtime-assembled values, never through tracked files.

docs.title: Known residual notes (review 2026-08-13, non-blocking)
docs.text:
• internal/llm/httpbase/client.go logs via log.Printf (default stderr), bypassing the CLI's stderr redaction writer. Today those lines carry only method/path/provider names, and httpbase's own RedactSecret truncates response bodies; wiring log.SetOutput to the redaction writer belongs to whichever card next touches httpbase.
  • AURUMCODE_PROMPT_CAPTURE is a truncating file write gated by an environment variable in shipped code. It is confined to the offline FakeProvider (live providers have no capture path) and, with the wiring in place, the captured prompt is already redacted.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
• Unit: tests/unit/AUR-432.go::TestAUR432 (send path, private-key block, output boundary, determinism — in process).
  • Integration: tests/integration/AUR-432.go::IntegrationAUR432 (real binary; offline capture and wire-level loopback proof; userinfo note).
  • E2E: tests/e2e/AUR-432.sh::E2EAUR432 (runtime-planted secrets in a rebuilt fixture repository, full user journey).
  • Acceptance: tests/acceptance/AUR-432.sh (AC-001, byte-pinned published formats, MUT-001).

docs.title: AUR-433 — aurumcode review --limite: know and cap what a review costs
docs.text:
Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

aurumcode review --base <ref> --limite <usd> gives the user a hard USD ceiling on what a single review run may spend calling the model. Before the model is ever called, the command estimates the cost and prints it; if that estimate exceeds --limite, the command refuses to call the model at all — exit 1, nothing spent — instead of running the review and finding out afterward. When the run proceeds, it also reports the actual cost once the review completes. Without --limite, nothing changes: output and exit codes are exactly as documented in docs/specs/AUR-430.md, AUR-431.md, AUR-435.md and AUR-436.md.

docs.title: Command
docs.text:
aurumcode review --base <ref> [--fail-on <level>] [--modelo <nome>] [--seguranca] [--limite <usd>]
Flag Required Meaning --base <ref> yes Unchanged from AUR-430: the ref to diff against HEAD. --fail-on <level> no Unchanged from AUR-431. Composes freely with --limite. --modelo <nome> no Unchanged from AUR-436. When set, cost is tracked against this model's key; the note and the cost lines both print. --seguranca no Unchanged from AUR-435. Composes freely with --limite. --limite <usd> no Maximum US dollars this run may spend. Must be a positive number; empty, non-numeric, zero or negative is a usage error (exit 2). Without it, no budget is enforced.

docs.title: How the estimate and the enforcement work
docs.text:
This card adds no cost-accounting logic of its own — it wires the already-existing, already-tested internal/llm/cost.Tracker into internal/llm.Orchestrator, which already checks a reservation against a configured ceiling atomically, before ever invoking the provider (cost.Tracker.Reserve, called inside Orchestrator.Complete ahead of executeWithTimeout). All the cost-control logic lives in one new file, cmd/aurumcode/cost.go; main.go only registers the flag and calls into it, and redaction_wiring_test.go gains the new stderr lines to its existing filter-identity pin (see Scope below):

  1. Pricing. $ per 1000 input/output tokens, from AURUMCODE_LLM_INPUT_USD_PER_1K and AURUMCODE_LLM_OUTPUT_USD_PER_1K (both or neither — half a price is not a price) or, when neither is set, a documented default ($0.01 / $0.03 per 1000 tokens).
  2. One model key. The chosen --modelo name, or "default" without it. A small wrapper (fixedModelProvider) forces the orchestrator to resolve every request to this exact key — the offline fixture provider (review.FakeProvider) reports none of its own, and cost.Tracker.Reserve fails closed on an unpriced key, so without this every --limite run would refuse regardless of the limit chosen.
  3. One tracker. cost.NewTracker(limite, limite, {key: price}), the single place --limite's parsed value reaches enforcement, passed into llm.NewOrchestrator as its budget tracker.
  4. One gate. That tracker, checked by the orchestrator before it ever calls the model. There is no second, independent check in this command: a redundant check would let the two disagree at the margin and let a defect in either hide behind the other.

The printed estimate is a pre-flight figure, not the number the enforcement decision is made against. It prices the diff text already available before the review starts, with the same $-per-1000-token arithmetic and the same output-token cap (review.DefaultConfig().MaxTokens - ReserveReply) the tracker itself uses — but the actual gate, inside Orchestrator.Complete, prices the final assembled prompt (system template plus the diff, redacted a second time — see internal/review.redactDiff — immediately before that prompt is built). This command deliberately never re-derives that prompt itself, so the printed estimate can differ slightly from what the enforced check sees; in the git-demo fixture the difference is a small fraction of the total, which is dominated by the fixed output-token cap both figures already share.

Both cost lines go to stderr, never stdout, exactly like the --modelo selection note and the --fail-on gate note:

aurumcode review: estimated cost $0.0914, diff-only pre-flight (--limite $0.5000)
aurumcode review: actual cost $0.0181 (--limite $0.5000)

An over-limit run prints only the estimate, plus the refusal:

aurumcode review: estimated cost $0.0914, diff-only pre-flight (--limite $0.0001)
aurumcode review: refusing to call the model: the request's cost would exceed --limite $0.0001; nothing was spent (...)

The refusal message deliberately does not repeat the printed estimate. Because the printed figure is diff-only and the enforced check prices the larger, fully assembled prompt, there is a margin where the two disagree: on the git-demo fixture with the default price, the diff-only estimate is $0.0914, but the run still refuses for any --limite up to $0.10 and only proceeds from $0.11 — a --limite $0.10 run prints estimated cost $0.0914, diff-only pre-flight (--limite $0.1000) and then refuses, which is correct even though $0.0914 < $0.10. Saying "the request's cost" rather than restating a dollar figure keeps the two lines from ever contradicting each other.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 The review ran (with or without --limite, as long as the estimate fit). 1 The review failed, unchanged from AUR-430/431/435/436, now including: the assembled request's cost would exceed --limite. The model was never called. 2 Usage error, unchanged plus: an empty, non-numeric, zero or negative --limite; a malformed AURUMCODE_LLM_*_USD_PER_1K pair. 3 Unchanged from AUR-431: the --fail-on gate closed. Cost is still reported.

docs.title: Example (no secrets, fully offline)
docs.text:
$ cat /tmp/response.json
{
  "issues": [
    {
      "file": "config/demo-tokens.txt",
      "line": 4,
      "severity": "warning",
      "rule_id": "security/hardcoded-secret",
      "message": "A credential-shaped value was committed in plain text (DEMO_API_TOKEN)."
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The change commits plaintext credential-shaped values."
}
$ cd tests/fixtures/repos/git-demo/repo.git
$ AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE=/tmp/response.json aurumcode review --base HEAD~1 --limite 0.50
aurumcode review: estimated cost $0.0914, diff-only pre-flight (--limite $0.5000)
aurumcode review: actual cost $0.0181 (--limite $0.5000)
config/demo-tokens.txt:4: [warning] A credential-shaped value was committed in plain text (DEMO_API_TOKEN). (rule security/hardcoded-secret: Hardcoded Secrets)
$ echo $?
0

A limit too small to afford this same review:

$ AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE=/tmp/response.json aurumcode review --base HEAD~1 --limite 0.0001
aurumcode review: estimated cost $0.0914, diff-only pre-flight (--limite $0.0001)
aurumcode review: refusing to call the model: the request's cost would exceed --limite $0.0001; nothing was spent (...)
$ echo $?
1

(Without --limite, both runs above print only the finding line, byte for byte the AUR-430 contract, on stdout — the cost lines and the refusal all go to stderr.)

docs.title: Failure diagnosis
docs.text:
• Exit 1, refusing to call the model: the request's cost would exceed --limite ... — the assembled request's cost is higher than the ceiling given (the printed "diff-only pre-flight" estimate can look smaller than --limite and the run still correctly refuses — see the margin note above). Raise --limite, or lower cost by pricing the actual model with AURUMCODE_LLM_INPUT_USD_PER_1K / AURUMCODE_LLM_OUTPUT_USD_PER_1K if the built-in default over-prices it.
  • Exit 2, --limite: must be a number of US dollars (got "...") / must be greater than zero / value must not be empty — the flag's value was missing, non-numeric, zero or negative. Give a positive number, or drop the flag entirely to run unmetered.
  • Exit 2, AURUMCODE_LLM_INPUT_USD_PER_1K is set but AURUMCODE_LLM_OUTPUT_USD_PER_1K is not (or vice versa) — only one half of a custom price pair was set; a missing half would price those tokens at $0. Set both, or neither to use the documented default.
  • No cost lines at all — --limite was not given. This is the unchanged, unmetered AUR-430 behavior, not a failure.

docs.title: MUT-001 note
docs.text: The skeptical mutation targets the one place --limite's parsed value reaches enforcement — cost.go's buildCostTracker, the single assignment ceilingUSD := limiteUSD that feeds cost.NewTracker — inflating it far past the ceiling the user actually gave. The mutant then admits an over-limit request straight through to the model: the offline fixture's call counter (AURUMCODE_PROMPT_CAPTURE's file, absent on a correct refusal) goes from absent to present for the exact same run tests/acceptance/AUR-433.sh::nominal_case proves refuses, and tests/integration/AUR-433.go proves the same defect with a literal numeric count of HTTP requests reaching a loopback endpoint (zero, correctly; nonzero, under the mutant). The mutation is applied only to a scratch staged copy inside mutation_case; the committed source carries no mutation hook, and the unmutated binary reproduces the exact GREEN — refusal, zero calls — in the same run.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: This card changes only cmd/aurumcode: one new file (cost.go) holding all cost-control logic, the minimum wiring into main.go (the flag, its validation, and the call sites into cost.go), and one extension to the existing redaction_wiring_test.go pin (the new stderr lines added to the list it already checks for filter-identity, per AUR-432). The review pipeline — analyzer, prompt, parser, reviewer, providers, and internal/llm/cost.Tracker itself — is byte-untouched, and every contract published by AUR-430, AUR-431, AUR-432, AUR-435 and AUR-436 holds verbatim without --limite.

docs.title: AUR-434 — Every finding cites the project review rule that sustains it
docs.text:
Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

Card AUR-434 makes aurumcode review follow the project's review standard: every problem the command prints cites the rule that sustains it, and a finding that cannot cite such a rule never reaches the user.

docs.title: Command
docs.text:
aurumcode review --base <ref>

Unchanged from AUR-430 (see docs/specs/AUR-430.md for the full command reference): diffs <ref> against HEAD in the git repository at the current working directory, sends the diff to the configured LLM provider, and prints the findings. No new flags.

docs.title: What this card changes in the output
docs.text:
Each printed finding now ends with the citation of the sustaining rule:

<file>:<line>: [<severity>] <message> (rule <rule-id>: <rule-title>)

Example (offline, no secret — the fixture is a canned model response):

cd tests/fixtures/repos/git-demo/repo.git
AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE=../../../review/known-problem-response.json \
  aurumcode review --base HEAD~1

prints

config/demo-tokens.txt:4: [error] A credential-shaped value was committed in plain text (DEMO_API_TOKEN). (rule security/hardcoded-secret: Hardcoded Secrets)

A model finding whose rule_id is missing, or names a rule that does not exist in the embedded catalog, is discarded before printing: it never reaches the user. A run where every finding is discarded prints the unchanged AUR-430 no-findings output:

No issues found.

The reviewer records how many findings it discarded in the review result's metadata (issues_rejected_without_rule); the CLI does not print metadata.

docs.title: The rule catalog
docs.text:
The catalog is embedded in the binary via go:embed from internal/review/rules/*.yml. The three files (security.yml, quality.yml, performance.yml) are the c12d7ab .aurumcode/rules catalog, restored by this card, with one id normalized: security/hardcoded-secrets is now security/hardcoded-secret, the singular form the engine's prompt contract and fixtures emit. Because the catalog is embedded, the binary carries its rules everywhere — the historical defect where running the binary outside the repository root found zero rules silently is structurally gone.

internal/review/rules.go is the restored c12d7ab RulesLoader (Get/GetAll/GetByCategory over rules indexed by id) re-pointed at the embedded catalog. Loading fails loudly — error, not an empty catalog — when:

  • no rules/*.yml file is embedded (also a compile-time error: the go:embed pattern refuses to match nothing);
  • the embedded files declare zero rules in total;
  • a rule has an empty id (an empty id would let findings with no rule_id resolve against it, silently defeating the gate);
  • two rules share an id (the winner would depend on file order);
  • a file is not valid YAML.

The rejection itself is NEW logic added by this card (enforceRuleCitations in internal/review/reviewer.go): the historical c12d7ab mapRulesToIssues only enriched issues (filling an empty Message/Severity from the rule, cleaning the file path) and let findings without a resolvable rule pass through. That enrichment is kept; the gate on top of it is what this card adds. ISO/IEC 25010 scoring (internal/review/iso25010) remains out of scope for this card.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Unchanged from AUR-430:

Exit Meaning 0 Review completed (with or without surviving findings). 1 Runtime failure: not a git repository, diff failure, no provider configured, unparseable model response — or, new with this card, a broken embedded rules catalog (review rules unavailable: ...). 2 Usage error (unknown command, missing --base).

docs.title: Diagnosing a failure
docs.text:
Symptom Likely cause A finding the model reported does not print It did not cite a rule of the project standard: rule_id was missing or unknown. This is the card's contract, not a bug. Degraded-mode parses (Metadata["parse_mode"] == "degraded") carry no rule_id, so their findings are always discarded. aurumcode review: review rules unavailable: ... The embedded catalog failed to load (see the loud failure list above). This indicates a broken build of the binary. No issues found. where findings were expected Either the model reported none, or every reported finding failed the rule gate.

For everything else (repository backends, provider selection, parser fallback, diff limits) see docs/specs/AUR-430.md.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
• Acceptance: tests/acceptance/AUR-434.sh (scenario AC-001; selectors TestAUR434, IntegrationAUR434, E2EAUR434, AC-001-MUT-001). Runs fully offline against deterministic fixtures; requires the engine packages and the git-demo fixture repository to be materialized, and reports exit 69 (inconclusive infrastructure), never a behavioral RED, when they are not.
  • MUT-001: the acceptance mutates a staged copy of reviewer.go so the gate stops discarding ungrounded findings, rebuilds, and proves the planted rule_id-less finding then reaches the output — i.e. accepting a finding without a cited rule makes the acceptance fail. The committed source contains no mutation hook.

docs.title: AUR-435 — aurumcode review --seguranca: find the vulnerability, not just the style
docs.text: Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

docs.title: Command
docs.text:
aurumcode review --base <ref> [--fail-on <level>] [--modelo <nome>] [--seguranca]

--seguranca additionally runs the project's security pass over the <ref>..HEAD diff and prints its findings in a section of their own, separate from the quality findings. Without the flag, stdout is byte-identical to the published contract of docs/specs/AUR-430.md (and the --fail-on / --modelo behaviors of AUR-431/AUR-436 are untouched).

docs.title: What the security pass is
docs.text:
The restored review rules (internal/review/rules/security.yml, embedded in the binary since AUR-434) historically were metadata without a matcher. AUR-435 restores the missing piece: a security-category rule may now carry a pattern — a Go regular expression compiled at load (a broken pattern fails the whole catalog loudly) — and a standard binding naming the rule of the enforced project security standard (standards/security-review/rules.md) that scopes it.

With --seguranca, the ADDED lines of the diff are matched against the patterns of the security-category rules — never the quality rules, never removed or context lines. The pass is deterministic and calls no model, so it works identically offline and online. Each match prints as:

<file>:<line>: [<severity>] <description> [standards/security-review <SCR-id>] (rule <id>: <title>)

The AUR-434 rule gate applies to this pass unchanged: every finding cites the security-category catalog rule that sustains it.

docs.title: Output shape
docs.text:
<notices and quality findings, exactly as without the flag>

Security findings (standards/security-review):
src/db.py:8: [error] Potential SQL injection vulnerability detected [standards/security-review SCR-001] (rule security/sql-injection: SQL Injection Vulnerability)

When the pass matches nothing the section reports the honest absence:

Security findings (standards/security-review):
No security findings.

The section always begins with one blank separator line and the header above; the bytes before it are exactly the no-flag output.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Review ran; gate (if any) open. 1 The review itself failed (no provider, unreadable repo, broken rules catalog). 2 Usage error (missing --base, unknown flag or level). 3 --fail-on gate closed. With --seguranca, security findings count toward the gate: a matched vulnerability (severity error) closes --fail-on high, even when every quality finding sits below the threshold.

docs.title: Offline, secret-free example
docs.text:
The repository ships a synthetic fixture whose HEAD~1..HEAD diff plants a SQL injection built by string concatenation (tests/fixtures/review/vuln, rebuildable deterministically with tests/fixtures/repos/git-demo/build-fixture.sh; nothing in it is a real application, credential, or database):

cd tests/fixtures/review/vuln/repo.git
AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE=../../known-problem-response.json \
  aurumcode review --base HEAD~1 --seguranca

prints the model-pass findings first, then:

Security findings (standards/security-review):
src/db.py:8: [error] Potential SQL injection vulnerability detected [standards/security-review SCR-001] (rule security/sql-injection: SQL Injection Vulnerability)

docs.title: Failure diagnosis
docs.text:
• flag provided but not defined: -seguranca — the binary predates AUR-435; rebuild from source.
  • aurumcode review: review rules unavailable: ... — the embedded rules catalog is broken (empty, duplicated id, or invalid pattern); the command fails loudly with exit 1 instead of silently scanning with no rules. Fix the catalog under internal/review/rules/ and rebuild.
  • The section says No security findings. but you expected a match — the pass scans only ADDED lines of the --base ..HEAD diff with the patterns carried by security-category rules; a vulnerability in untouched code, in a removed line, or in a rule without a pattern is out of its declared scope.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• The pass matches the raw diff in-process; it never echoes the matched line. Everything printed is trusted catalog text plus the diff-derived file path (redacted at the sink, AUR-432) and line number.
  • The AURUM_SECRET_CANARY value never reaches stdout, stderr, prompt, cache, or evidence; tests/acceptance/AUR-435.sh asserts this on every run.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: tests/acceptance/AUR-435.sh AC-001 (sealed: ./.board/bin/oci-run --profile bootstrap-readonly-v1 --card AUR-435), with selectors TestAUR435 (tests/unit/AUR-435.go), IntegrationAUR435 (tests/integration/AUR-435.go), E2EAUR435 (tests/e2e/AUR-435.sh) and AC-001-MUT-001 (the quality-rubric mutation, which must make the expected finding vanish).

docs.title: AUR-436 — aurumcode review --modelo: choose which AI reviews, including a local one
docs.text:
Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

aurumcode review --base <ref> --modelo <nome> lets the user choose which model performs the review — including a local model — instead of the selection being decided only by environment variables. When nothing is configured to serve the chosen model, the command fails loudly with a clear, actionable error on stderr and exit 1: which model, why it is unavailable, and how to configure a provider that serves it. It never degrades to an empty review with exit 0. Without --modelo, nothing changes: provider selection, output and exit codes are exactly as documented in docs/specs/AUR-430.md and docs/specs/AUR-431.md.

docs.title: Command
docs.text:
aurumcode review --base <ref> [--fail-on <level>] [--modelo <nome>]
Flag Required Meaning --base <ref> yes Unchanged from AUR-430: the ref to diff against HEAD. --fail-on <level> no Unchanged from AUR-431: the severity gate. Composes freely with --modelo. --modelo <nome> no The model that reviews, e.g. local, llama3, gpt-4. The flag commands the selection: with it set, LLM_MODEL is ignored.

docs.title: How the chosen model is served
docs.text:
--modelo adds no vendor. It reuses the two provider mechanisms AUR-430 already published (cmd/aurumcode/main.go, selectProvider):

  1. AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE=<path> — the deterministic offline provider (internal/review.FakeProvider) answers for the chosen model. This is how the sealed, network-denied acceptance exercises --modelo local.
  2. LLM_API_KEY + LLM_BASE_URL — the chosen model rides the existing OpenAI-compatible provider (internal/llm/provider/litellm), with the flag's name sent as the wire model, overriding LLM_MODEL. A local model is chosen by pointing LLM_BASE_URL at a local endpoint: an ollama server's OpenAI-compatible API (http://localhost:11434/v1), a llama.cpp server, or a litellm proxy in front of any local model. tests/integration/AUR-436.go proves with a loopback httptest endpoint that the name typed after --modelo is the name that reaches the wire.

Neither configured — or the configured endpoint unreachable / not serving the model — means the chosen model is unavailable (see below).

When --modelo is set, one deterministic note goes to stderr (never stdout) naming the selection:

aurumcode review: reviewing with model "local" (offline fixture provider)

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 The review ran with the chosen model (findings or No issues found. — an available model reporting nothing is a normal result). 1 The review failed, unchanged from AUR-430, now including: the chosen model is unavailable. The error names the model, the reason and the fix. 2 Usage error, unchanged plus one case: an explicitly empty model name (--modelo=, or --modelo "$VAR" with VAR empty). The command never silently falls back to a model the user did not choose. 3 Unchanged from AUR-431: the --fail-on gate closed. The chosen model's findings gate exactly like the default selection's.

docs.title: Unavailable model
docs.text:
The defect this card guards against (MUT-001): an unavailable model must never produce an empty review with exit 0. Instead, stderr carries two lines — which model, why, how to fix — and the command exits 1:

aurumcode review: model "local" is unavailable: no LLM provider is configured to serve it
aurumcode review: to serve model "local": set AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE=<response-file> for a deterministic offline run, or set LLM_API_KEY and LLM_BASE_URL to an OpenAI-compatible endpoint that serves it -- a local endpoint works, e.g. LLM_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434/v1 (ollama) or a litellm proxy in front of any local model -- then re-run with --modelo local

A configured-but-unreachable endpoint (local server not running, wrong URL, model not served there) reports the same shape with the transport error as the reason.

docs.title: Example (no secrets)
docs.text:
Fully offline, deterministic, no network and no credentials:

$ cat /tmp/response.json
{
  "issues": [
    {
      "file": "config/demo-tokens.txt",
      "line": 4,
      "severity": "warning",
      "rule_id": "security/hardcoded-secret",
      "message": "A credential-shaped value was committed in plain text (DEMO_API_TOKEN)."
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The change commits plaintext credential-shaped values."
}
$ cd tests/fixtures/repos/git-demo/repo.git
$ AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE=/tmp/response.json aurumcode review --base HEAD~1 --modelo local
aurumcode review: reviewing with model "local" (offline fixture provider)
config/demo-tokens.txt:4: [warning] A credential-shaped value was committed in plain text (DEMO_API_TOKEN). (rule security/hardcoded-secret: Hardcoded Secrets)
$ echo $?
0

(The finding cites an embedded rule — rule_id — because the AUR-434 rule-citation gate discards any finding that cannot cite one; see docs/specs/AUR-434.md.)

(The selection note is on stderr; stdout carries only the findings, byte for byte what the same run prints without --modelo.)

Against a genuinely local model:

# ollama serving llama3 on its OpenAI-compatible API:
LLM_API_KEY=ollama LLM_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434/v1 \
  aurumcode review --base HEAD~1 --modelo llama3

docs.title: Failure diagnosis
docs.text:
• Exit 1, model "..." is unavailable: no LLM provider is configured to serve it — neither AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE nor LLM_API_KEY+LLM_BASE_URL is set. Configure one of them as the message says.
  • Exit 1, model "..." is unavailable: LLM request failed: ... — the endpoint in LLM_BASE_URL refused or failed the request. For a local model: check the local server is running at that URL and actually serves the model name you typed.
  • Exit 2, --modelo: model name must not be empty — the flag was given without a value (typically --modelo "$VAR" with VAR unset in CI). Name a model or drop the flag.
  • No issues found., exit 0 — the chosen model was available and reported nothing. This is a healthy result, distinguishable from unavailability by the exit code and the absence of the error lines.

docs.title: MUT-001 note
docs.text: The skeptical mutation makes the unavailable-model path hand the engine a deterministic empty review instead of the error (selectProviderForModel's final return nil, "", errors.New(...) → returning a review.FakeProvider with {"issues":[],"summary":"ok"}): the command then prints No issues found. and exits 0 for a model nothing serves, and the acceptance fails. The mutation is applied only to a scratch staged copy inside tests/acceptance/AUR-436.sh::mutation_case; the committed source contains no mutation hook, and the unmutated binary reproduces the exact GREEN in the same run.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: This card changes only cmd/aurumcode (flag parsing, provider selection for the chosen model, the unavailability error). The review pipeline — analyzer, prompt, parser, reviewer, providers — is byte-untouched, and every contract published by AUR-430 and AUR-431 (output format, exit codes, no-flag provider selection) holds verbatim.

docs.title: AUR-437 — Comentar o review no pull request (cliente GitHub restaurado)
docs.text: Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

docs.title: O que este card entrega
docs.text: A biblioteca Go internal/git/githubclient: um cliente da API do GitHub que le as mudancas de um pull request e publica os problemas encontrados como comentario, recusando publicar quando o token nao tem permissao de escrita. O comando de usuario (aurumcode review --pr 42 --repo dono/projeto --publicar) pertence ao AUR-438, que depende deste card e e dono de cmd/aurumcode; aqui entra somente o cliente e seus fixtures httptest.

docs.title: Origem: restauracao, nao reescrita
docs.text:
O cliente existiu no repositorio e foi removido em 2025-11-03 pelo mesmo lote que apagou o motor de review. Ele foi restaurado do commit c12d7ab (internal/git/githubclient/client.go, 774 linhas, junto com seus dois arquivos de teste httptest historicos, client_test.go e integration_test.go), e nao reescrito.

Duas adaptacoes de restauracao, sem mudanca de comportamento:

  • Tipos de diff locais ao pacote (diff.go): o historico importava aurumcode/pkg/types, mas o aceite selado deste card materializa apenas os paths/read_paths declarados, entao o pacote precisa compilar sozinho. Diff, DiffFile e DiffHunk espelham campo a campo (com as mesmas tags) os tipos de pkg/types, para conversao trivial no AUR-438.
  • Module path: os imports usam github.com/Mpaape/AurumCode/..., o module path atual do go.mod (o historico usava aurumcode).

docs.title: Os quatro defeitos medidos, corrigidos
docs.text:
Cada um tem teste que falha na restauracao crua e passa com a correcao (seletor unit TestAUR437, subtests Defeito1..Defeito4; ha equivalentes no proprio pacote):

  1. Retry de POST reenviava corpo ja consumido. req.Clone compartilha o mesmo reader do corpo; a retentativa enviava corpo vazio. O resgate interno do net/http (rewindBody) so ocorre em conexao reutilizada, entao um rate-limiter que responde Connection: close expunha o defeito como http: ContentLength=N with Body length 0. Correcao: toda tentativa apos a primeira reobtem o corpo via req.GetBody; corpo nao-replayavel e erro explicito.
  2. 403 de rate-limit nao era retentado. So 429 contava como rate limit, mas o limitador primario do GitHub responde 403 com X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 (ou Retry-After). Correcao: isRateLimited403 trata esse 403 como rate limit retentavel; 403 simples (negacao real de permissao) continua retornando imediatamente, sem retry.
  3. time.Sleep no retry ignorava o contexto. Um chamador cancelado esperava o backoff inteiro. Correcao: sleepContext aborta a espera assim que ctx.Done() fecha, nos dois pontos de espera (backoff e retry-after).
  4. extractFilePath casava o primeiro literal b/. Em diff --git a/cmdb/settings.go b/cmdb/settings.go o primeiro b/ esta dentro de cmdb/, produzindo settings.go. Correcao: ancora no ultimo separador b/, que introduz o caminho do lado novo — resolve o caso medido (um segmento de diretorio terminado em b).

Caso residual, nao coberto por esta correcao: quando o proprio caminho do lado novo contem o literal b/, o ultimo separador b/ da linha cai DENTRO desse caminho, e extractFilePath ainda trunca o resultado. Reproduzido em internal/git/githubclient/client.go:795-802: a linha diff --git a/foo b/bar.go b/foo b/bar.go (caminho foo b/bar.go, que contem b/) retorna bar.go em vez de foo b/bar.go. Este card nao corrige esse caso.

docs.title: A verificacao de permissao antes de publicar
docs.text:
• HasWritePermission(ctx, owner, repo) le o objeto permissions de GET /repos/{owner}/{repo} (push || maintain || admin); resposta sem o objeto conta como sem escrita — a checagem falha fechada. O veredito e cacheado por owner/repo na vida do cliente.
  • PostIssueComment, PostReviewComment e SetStatus passam por requireWritePermission antes de montar qualquer POST e recusam com o erro sentinela ErrNoWritePermission (testavel com errors.Is). Nenhum POST sai do processo com token somente-leitura.
  • MUT-001: o aceite muta uma copia de trabalho de client.go fazendo requireWritePermission retornar nil sem checar nada, reconstroi e prova que o vetor de token somente-leitura entao falha (readonly_not_refused). O binario de producao nao tem gancho de mutacao algum.

docs.title: API publica
docs.text:
c := githubclient.NewClient(token)                  // api.github.com
c := githubclient.NewClientWithBaseURL(token, url)  // testes/fakes

diff, err := c.GetPullRequestDiff(ctx, owner, repo, numero) // Accept v3.diff, cache ETag/304
files, err := c.ListChangedFiles(ctx, owner, repo, numero)  // paginacao via Link rel="next"
ok, err := c.HasWritePermission(ctx, owner, repo)
err = c.PostReviewComment(ctx, owner, repo, numero, githubclient.ReviewComment{...}, chaveIdem)
err = c.PostIssueComment(ctx, owner, repo, numero, corpo)
err = c.SetStatus(ctx, owner, repo, sha, githubclient.CommitStatus{...})

Erros: HTTP nao-2xx vira HTTP <codigo>: <corpo>; recusa de publicacao embrulha ErrNoWritePermission; cancelamento devolve o erro do contexto. Retry: ate 3 retentativas para 5xx, 429 e 403 de rate-limit, com backoff exponencial (1s base, teto 30s, jitter) sensivel ao contexto.

docs.title: Exemplo executavel sem segredo
docs.text:
bash tests/e2e/AUR-437.sh E2EAUR437

Sobe um fake GitHub em loopback a partir de tests/fixtures/scm/github/ (diff do PR 42 — incluindo o diretorio cmdb/ que prova o defeito 4 —, paginas de arquivos, permissoes read-write/read-only, resposta de comentario criado), compila um harness que usa a biblioteca como o AUR-438 usara e imprime um transcript deterministico: ARQUIVO_DO_DIFF ..., COMENTARIO_PUBLICADO path=cmdb/settings.go line=3, POST_RECEBIDO=true no cenario de escrita; RECUSADO_SEM_PERMISSAO_DE_ESCRITA, POST_RECEBIDO=false no cenario somente-leitura. Tokens sao strings sinteticas montadas em runtime; nenhum shape de credencial existe em arquivo rastreado.

docs.title: Selectors e exit codes
docs.text:
• Aceite: tests/acceptance/AUR-437.sh — selectors AC-001 (tudo), TestAUR437, IntegrationAUR437, E2EAUR437, AC-001-MUT-001.
  • Exit codes (convencao do board): 0 comportamento provado; 1 RED comportamental; 64 selector desconhecido; 79 infraestrutura / inconclusivo (nunca evidencia de RED).

docs.title: Diagnostico de falha
docs.text:
• AUR-437/AC-001/behavior-missing: a biblioteca nao entrega o fluxo prometido (ver stderr do harness).
  • readonly_not_refused / readonly_post_leaked: a recusa de publicacao sem escrita foi violada — exatamente o que o MUT-001 provoca.
  • non_deterministic: duas execucoes identicas divergiram.
  • infrastructure/missing_go, infrastructure/mktemp, loopback indisponivel (exit 79): ambiente, nunca RED.
  • Compatibilidade: nenhum comando ou formato publicado por outro card muda; rollback = reverter somente os paths deste card; nenhum estado externo.

docs.title: AUR-438 — Comentar no arquivo e na linha exata (fiacao no cmd)
docs.text: Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

docs.title: O que este card entrega
docs.text:
O caminho de pull request de aurumcode review:

aurumcode review --pr <numero> --repo <dono>/<projeto> --publicar --na-linha

Le as mudancas de um pull request atraves do cliente GitHub restaurado (AUR-437, internal/git/githubclient), revisa o diff atraves do mesmo motor e da mesma selecao de provider que o caminho --base ja usa, e publica cada problema encontrado como comentario no pull request: na linha exata do arquivo quando o diff adicionou aquela linha, ou como comentario geral do pull request quando o problema esta fora das linhas alteradas -- nunca descartado em silencio. A publicacao recusa, antes de qualquer POST, quando o token nao tem permissao de escrita no repositorio.

Este card e fiacao, nao reescrita: o cliente GitHub (leitura de diff, listagem de arquivos, comentario inline, comentario geral, verificacao de permissao) e o motor de review ja existem e ja estao provados. O que falta, e o que este card adiciona, e a conversao do formato local de diff do cliente para pkg/types que o motor consome, a classificacao de cada achado em "linha exata" ou "geral", e o loop de publicacao -- tudo em cmd/aurumcode/pr.go.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
• --pr <numero>: numero do pull request. Ativa o caminho de PR; ausente, review continua exatamente como antes (--base, byte a byte).
  • --repo <dono>/<projeto>: obrigatorio com --pr. Qualquer outra forma (sem barra, dono ou projeto vazio, mais de uma barra) e erro de uso.
  • --publicar: obrigatorio com --pr (booleano). E o consentimento explicito do usuario para publicar; independente dele, a publicacao ainda recusa quando o token carecer de permissao de escrita (ver abaixo).
  • --na-linha: obrigatorio com --pr (booleano). Nomeia o comportamento que este card entrega -- comentar na linha exata quando possivel, geral quando nao.

--repo, --publicar e --na-linha sao obrigatorios com --pr pela mesma razao que --base ja e obrigatorio no caminho existente: este card constroi e testa exatamente o comando que ele declara (review --pr N --repo o/r --publicar --na-linha); nenhuma variante nao testada (por exemplo, --pr sem --publicar fazendo uma execucao seca) e um comportamento este card promete.

Deteccao de --pr usa fs.Visit (nomes canonicos de flag apos o parse), e o parser flag do Go ja trata -pr e --pr de forma identica -- um traco ou dois, tanto faz. Isso vale para toda flag deste comando, incluindo --base; nenhum guarda manual de string "--" foi escrito aqui (ver "Achado herdado" abaixo).

docs.title: Classificacao: linha exata vs. comentario geral
docs.text:
Para cada achado do motor, o arquivo e a linha sao comparados ao diff que o cliente GitHub leu: se a linha e uma linha que o diff ADICIONOU (marcador + no hunk que a cobre) naquele arquivo, o achado vira um comentario inline (PostReviewComment, ancorado em path+line). Qualquer outro caso -- uma linha de contexto, uma linha alem de todo hunk, ou um arquivo que o diff nem tocou -- vira um comentario geral do pull request (PostIssueComment, com o arquivo e a linha no corpo do texto), nunca e descartado.

Os achados sao publicados em ordem (arquivo, linha) -- deterministica, independente da ordem em que o modelo os listou -- entao repetir a mesma entrada produz a mesma sequencia de publicacao, nao so a mesma saida de tela.

docs.title: A conversao de tipos (achado herdado do revisor do AUR-437)
docs.text:
internal/git/githubclient define Diff/DiffFile/DiffHunk locais ao seu proprio pacote (seu aceite selado materializa so os paths/ read_paths daquele card, entao ele nao pode importar pkg/types). Os campos espelham pkg/types.Diff{,File,Hunk} um a um, de proposito, para que a conversao neste card seja trivial e sem perda -- e essa conversao (convertDiff em cmd/aurumcode/pr.go) e o que este card entrega: nao ha mais um espelhamento sem uso real, o motor de review consome o resultado convertido diretamente.

Nota deliberada: este documento nao repete a alegacao sobre extractFilePath e o separador " b/" que o spec do AUR-437 fez ao descrever a correcao do defeito 4 daquele card. extractFilePath pertence a internal/git/githubclient (read_path aqui, nao reescrito por este card), e este card nao caracteriza nem depende de nenhum comportamento alem do que esta unico teste ja prova: o path do lado novo do fixture pr-42.diff (cmdb/settings.go, cujo diretorio termina em "b") chega correto na conversao.

docs.title: Permissao de escrita: verificada antes de qualquer trabalho, nao so antes de postar
docs.text: runPRReview chama client.HasWritePermission uma vez, antes da busca do diff e antes de qualquer chamada ao motor/modelo, e recusa com uma mensagem clara, citando githubclient.ErrNoWritePermission, sem enviar nenhum POST, quando o token nao pode escrever. A ordem importa: um token somente-leitura nao deve pagar por uma chamada ao LLM cujo resultado ele nunca podera publicar. Isso e adicional, nao um substituto, ao guardiao que ja existe dentro de PostReviewComment/PostIssueComment (requireWritePermission, fail-closed) -- a checagem explicita aqui existe so para dar uma mensagem unica e clara em vez de uma falha por achado; a garantia de fail-closed em si pertence ao cliente e este card nao a reimplementa nem a enfraquece.

docs.title: O SHA do commit: recusa fail-closed, nunca um POST com commit_id vazio
docs.text:
PostReviewComment exige um commit_id. O formato de diff unificado que GetPullRequestDiff le (Accept: application/vnd.github.v3.diff) nao carrega o SHA do commit de topo do pull request, e este card nao estende internal/git/githubclient (e read_path aqui) para adicionar um endpoint que o buscasse. commit_id vem da variavel de ambiente GITHUB_SHA -- a mesma que o GitHub Actions ja expoe a um step (ver docs/specs/AUR-440.md).

Isto nao e uma alegacao de que o comentario inline fica ancorado no commit de topo do pull request em uso real; e uma limitacao documentada, nao uma capacidade reivindicada. E, ao contrario de uma versao anterior deste documento, nao e mais tratado como inofensivo publicar com commit_id vazio: a API real do GitHub responde 422 a um comentario inline sem commit_id, e uma primeira versao deste card deixava esse POST sair mesmo assim (bloqueador medido pelo revisor: o aceite so nao pegava porque seus proprios fakes aceitavam qualquer commit_id, um mock que sempre concordava).

A regra agora: depois de classificar os achados, se pelo menos um exige comentario inline (ver "Classificacao" acima) e GITHUB_SHA esta ausente, o comando recusa antes de qualquer POST -- inline ou geral -- com uma mensagem clara em stderr, o mesmo formato fail-closed da checagem de permissao. Um review cujos achados sao todos gerais nao precisa de SHA algum (PostIssueComment nao carrega commit_id), entao esse caso nao e bloqueado pela ausencia da variavel. tests/e2e/AUR-438.sh reproduz o 422 real: seu fake GitHub responde 422 a um commit_id vazio no endpoint de comentario inline, e o cenario "sem GITHUB_SHA" prova que zero POSTs chegam ao servidor -- a recusa e um guardiao deste comando, nao uma consequencia observada so depois de uma resposta de erro do servidor.

docs.title: Uma falha de publicacao isolada nao engole as demais
docs.text: O loop de publicacao agrega falhas em vez de abortar no primeiro erro: se um POST (inline ou geral) falha, o achado seguinte ainda e tentado. Ao final, cada achado que falhou aparece listado em stderr e o exit code e 1; todo achado que PODE ser publicado ainda e. Uma versao anterior deste card retornava no primeiro erro (return 1 dentro do loop), o que, dado que os achados sao publicados em ordem (arquivo, linha), fazia uma falha no primeiro comentario (tipicamente o inline) descartar silenciosamente todo achado geral que viria depois -- o mesmo bloqueador do revisor, pela mesma causa raiz de "nenhum POST empresta commit_id vazio a esta versao antiga do codigo". tests/integration/AUR-438.go e tests/e2e/AUR-438.sh provam isso injetando uma falha (400, nunca retentada pelo cliente) na primeira publicacao e checando que a segunda ainda chega ao servidor.

docs.title: Gap anotado, nao implementado: PostIssueComment sem chave de idempotencia
docs.text: PostReviewComment recebe uma chave de idempotencia (X-GitHub-Idempotency-Key); PostIssueComment, na assinatura de internal/git/githubclient (read_path aqui, fora de paths), nao recebe nenhuma. Isso significa que reexecutar aurumcode review --pr ... --publicar --na-linha sobre o mesmo pull request -- por exemplo, um retry de CI apos uma falha de rede no meio da execucao -- pode duplicar o comentario geral de um achado ja publicado; o comentario inline, por ter chave de idempotencia, nao duplica. Esta e uma limitacao real do cliente restaurado que este card nao corrige: uma correcao exigiria mudar a assinatura de PostIssueComment, fora do que este card pode escrever. Fica registrada aqui para quem assumir esse trabalho.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
• 0: os achados foram publicados (ou "No issues found." quando o motor nao encontrou nenhum), sem erro.
  • 1: falha em tempo de execucao -- busca do diff, chamada ao motor, recusa por falta de permissao de escrita, ou falha ao publicar um comentario especifico.
  • 2: erro de uso -- --repo/--publicar/--na-linha ausentes com --pr, --pr nao positivo, ou --repo fora do formato dono/projeto.

Nenhum destes e novo: e o mesmo vocabulario de exit code que --base ja usa (docs/specs/AUR-430.md).

docs.title: Exemplo executavel sem segredo
docs.text:
bash tests/e2e/AUR-438.sh E2EAUR438

Compila o binario real, sobe um fake GitHub em loopback (net/http/httptest sobre net.Listen) a partir de tests/fixtures/scm/github/ (o diff do PR 42, as permissoes de leitura-escrita e so-leitura, a resposta de comentario criado), escreve uma resposta de modelo deterministica com dois achados -- um na linha 3 de cmdb/settings.go (linha que o diff adicionou) e um na linha 99 de docs/notas.md (bem alem do unico hunk +1 daquele arquivo) -- e roda aurumcode review --pr 42 --repo dono/projeto --publicar --na-linha contra ele. O fake responde 422 a um comentario inline com commit_id vazio, exatamente como a API real -- nao e mais um mock que concorda com qualquer requisicao. Prova: o primeiro achado chega como comentario inline (path=cmdb/settings.go, line=3); o segundo chega como comentario geral citando docs/notas.md:99 em vez de desaparecer; repetir a execucao produz a mesma saida e a mesma sequencia de publicacao; com um token so-leitura nenhum POST alcanca o servidor -- o comando recusa antes; sem GITHUB_SHA (variavel genuinamente ausente, nao so vazia) o comando tambem recusa antes de qualquer POST, mesmo havendo um achado inline valido; e quando o fake falha deliberadamente a primeira publicacao (400, nunca retentado pelo cliente), a segunda ainda chega ao servidor -- uma falha isolada nao engole as demais. Tokens sao strings sinteticas montadas em tempo de execucao; nenhum shape de credencial existe em arquivo rastreado.

docs.title: Selectors e exit codes do aceite
docs.text:
• Aceite: tests/acceptance/AUR-438.sh -- selectors AC-001 (tudo), TestAUR438, IntegrationAUR438, E2EAUR438, AC-001-MUT-001.
  • Exit codes (convencao do board, tests/acceptance/EXIT_CODE_CONVENTION.md): 0 comportamento provado; 1 RED comportamental; 64 selector desconhecido; 79 infraestrutura / inconclusivo (nunca evidencia de RED).

docs.title: Diagnostico de falha
docs.text:
• AUR-438/AC-001/behavior-missing: o caminho de PR nao entrega o fluxo prometido (ver stderr do harness em tests/e2e/AUR-438.sh).
  • missing_general_finding / missing_general_marker / missing_general_comment: o achado fora das linhas alteradas nao foi publicado -- exatamente o que MUT-001 provoca ao mutar cmd/aurumcode/pr.go para descartar esse ramo em silencio.
  • readonly_not_refused / readonly_post_leaked: a recusa de publicacao sem permissao de escrita foi violada.
  • nosha_not_refused / nosha_post_leaked: a recusa fail-closed por SHA de commit ausente foi violada -- um POST (inline, com commit_id vazio) chegou ao servidor, ou o comando nao recusou.
  • onefail_swallowed_other_finding / onefail_missing_failure_summary / onefail_second_post_not_attempted: uma falha isolada de publicacao impediu outro achado de ser publicado -- a regressao que o bloqueador do revisor descreveu.
  • non_deterministic / non_deterministic_publish_count: duas execucoes identicas divergiram na saida ou na sequencia de publicacao.
  • infrastructure/missing_go, infrastructure/mktemp, infrastructure/fakegithub_did_not_start (exit 79): ambiente, nunca RED.

docs.title: Achado herdado do revisor do AUR-440
docs.text: O guarda de flags das lanes do AUR-440 so reconhecia tokens com prefixo "--", entao a grafia de traco unico ("-publish", que o pacote flag do Go trata identicamente) escapava da deteccao. Aquele guarda vive em tests/acceptance/AUR-440.sh/docs/specs/AUR-440.md, fora de paths e read_paths deste card -- nao foi tocado aqui. O que este card faz e nao repetir o erro na sua propria fiacao: nenhuma flag deste comando e detectada por um prefixo "--" escrito a mao; toda deteccao (--pr incluido) passa por fs.Visit sobre um flag.FlagSet comum, que ja trata -x e --x de forma identica para toda flag, nova ou preexistente (prova: TestReviewFlagsAcceptSingleOrDoubleDash em cmd/aurumcode/pr_test.go). A correcao do guarda das lanes do AUR-440 em si, e da frase correspondente em docs/specs/AUR-440.md:38-39, permanece um gap para um card com esses arquivos em paths.

docs.title: Compatibility, migration, rollback
docs.text:
• Compatibility: --base, --fail-on, --modelo e --seguranca mantem o contrato publicado byte a byte quando --pr esta ausente -- o dispatch para o caminho de PR acontece antes de qualquer verificacao do caminho --base, entao nenhum codigo existente e alterado, so contornado quando --pr e dado.
  • Migration: not-applicable.
  • Rollback: reverter somente os paths deste card; nenhum estado externo e publicado por ele fora do que o proprio usuario pediu ao rodar o comando.

docs.title: AUR-439 — Bloquear o merge quando o review reprova
docs.text: Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

docs.title: O que este card entrega
docs.text:
Uma nova flag no caminho de pull request de aurumcode review:

aurumcode review --pr <numero> --repo <dono>/<projeto> --publicar --check

Depois de publicar cada achado como comentario no pull request (o comportamento que o AUR-438 ja entrega, inalterado), publica um commit status no commit de topo do pull request atraves do cliente GitHub restaurado (AUR-437, internal/git/githubclient.SetStatus): "failure" quando pelo menos um achado e grave (severidade error, o mesmo patamar que --fail-on high|error ja nomeia), "success" caso contrario. Uma regra de branch protection que exige esse check bloqueia o merge do pull request ate a correcao.

Este card e fiacao, nao reescrita: SetStatus ja existe, ja esta provado (internal/git/githubclient/client_test.go) e ja e fail-closed em permissao de escrita (requireWritePermission, a mesma garantia que PostReviewComment/PostIssueComment ja usam). O que falta, e o que este card adiciona, e inteiramente em cmd/aurumcode/pr.go: a flag --check, a classificacao "grave" (reaproveitando severityRank/countAtOrAbove de cmd/aurumcode/main.go -- nenhuma segunda escala de severidade), e a funcao publishCheckStatus que monta e publica o githubclient.CommitStatus.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
• --check: opcional (booleano). Publica o commit status descrito acima. Com --pr, satisfaz sozinha a exigencia que --na-linha normalmente impoe -- o comando declarado por este card (review --pr N --repo o/r --publicar --check) nao leva --na-linha, e --check nomeia seu proprio comportamento com a mesma clareza que --na-linha nomeia o dela. Sem --check e sem --na-linha, o caminho de PR continua recusando exatamente como antes (aurumcode review: --na-linha is required with --pr, exit 2) -- nada nesse contrato pre-existente muda.
  • --repo e --publicar continuam obrigatorios com --pr, com ou sem --check, exatamente como o AUR-438 ja exige. --check nao substitui nem suprime a publicacao de comentarios que --publicar ja exige: os dois convivem na mesma execucao -- cada achado ainda vira comentario inline ou geral no pull request (AUR-438, inalterado), e o commit status e publicado depois, como um efeito adicional, nunca no lugar dos comentarios.

docs.title: O que conta como "grave"
