docs.text: Um achado e grave quando sua severidade e error -- o rank mais alto que o motor de review ja usa (internal/prompt's vocabulary: error, warning, info), o mesmo rank que --fail-on high|error ja nomeia no caminho --base. publishCheckStatus conta os achados grave com countAtOrAbove(issues, rankError), a mesma funcao que --fail-on ja usa em cmd/aurumcode/main.go -- nao existe uma segunda nocao de "grave" só para o --check.

docs.title: O commit status publicado
docs.text:
githubclient.CommitStatus{
    Context:     "aurumcode/review",
    State:       "failure" | "success",
    Description: "<N> achado(s) grave(s) no pull request #<numero>" |
                  "nenhum achado grave no pull request #<numero>",
}

Context e contrato publico: uma regra de branch protection identifica qual check e obrigatorio pelo context exato, entao renomea-lo em uma versao futura des-bloquearia silenciosamente todo merge que dependia dele em vez de continuar bloqueando. "aurumcode/review" e o valor fixo que este card publica e testa (tests/unit/AUR-439.go, tests/integration/AUR-439.go).

Zero achados ainda publica "success": um commit que corrigiu todo achado grave de uma execucao anterior precisa que o check anterior seja limpo, ou o merge continua bloqueado para sempre por um status que nunca mais e atualizado. "No issues found." continua imprimindo exatamente como antes; o commit status e adicional, nao um substituto.

docs.title: O SHA do commit: a mesma recusa fail-closed, agora tambem por --check
docs.text:
SetStatus publica em /repos/{owner}/{repo}/statuses/{sha} -- nao ha forma dessa chamada sem um SHA de commit, exatamente como uma chamada PostReviewComment inline nao existe sem um commit_id (AUR-438). Este card nao abre um segundo guardiao paralelo para essa exigencia: a mesma variavel needsCommitID que o AUR-438 ja usa para achados elegiveis a comentario inline agora tambem comeca em true quando --check foi dado. O efeito pratico: um review --pr ... --publicar --check sem GITHUB_SHA recusa antes de qualquer POST -- mesmo quando nenhum achado e elegivel a comentario inline, mesmo quando nao ha achado nenhum -- com a mesma mensagem de recusa que o AUR-438 ja publica em stderr (refusing to publish: an inline comment requires a commit SHA...). A mensagem e reaproveitada tal como esta, sem alteracao: o contrato pre-existente sem --check e byte a byte pinado, e mudar o texto so para --check exigiria dois textos condicionais em vez de um guardiao unico.

tests/integration/AUR-439.go prova especificamente o caso mais estreito: um achado so-geral (nenhum elegivel a inline) com --check e sem GITHUB_SHA ainda recusa -- a prova de que --check contribui sua propria exigencia ao guardiao em vez de depender de carona em um achado inline que por acaso esteja presente.

docs.title: Permissao de escrita: herdada, nao contornada
docs.text: A checagem explicita de HasWritePermission que o AUR-438 ja faz antes de qualquer trabalho (busca de diff, chamada ao modelo) cobre --check sem nenhuma mudanca: --check nunca chega a publishCheckStatus quando o token e so-leitura, porque a funcao inteira ja retornou. E mesmo que chegasse, SetStatus em si tambem chama requireWritePermission internamente (o mesmo guardiao fail-closed que PostReviewComment/ PostIssueComment ja usam) -- nao existe um caminho que contorne essa garantia so porque a chamada e para o endpoint de status em vez de comentario.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
• 0: os achados foram publicados (ou "No issues found."), sem erro; com --check, o commit status publicado foi "success" (nenhum achado grave).
  • 1: falha em tempo de execucao -- inclui agora a falha ao publicar o proprio commit status (uma falha de transporte/API do SetStatus, nao um achado grave).
  • 2: erro de uso -- --repo/--publicar ausentes com --pr, --na-linha ausente quando --check tambem esta ausente, --pr nao positivo, ou --repo fora do formato dono/projeto.
  • 3 (exitFindings, o mesmo codigo que --fail-on ja usa): com --check, pelo menos um achado grave foi encontrado e o commit status publicado foi "failure". Este codigo nunca pode ser confundido com sucesso -- é exatamente o que MUT-001 prova: uma versao que reportasse sucesso (codigo 0, ou um status "success") com um achado grave presente e o defeito que a mutacao introduz e que o aceite precisa pegar.

Uma falha ao publicar um comentario individual e a falha ao publicar o commit status sao independentes: se um achado falha ao publicar mas o commit status ainda publica com sucesso (ou vice-versa), o exit code permanece 1 (a falha de publicacao de comentario tem precedencia sobre o 3 do --check, porque 1 ja significa "algo na publicacao falhou" -- nenhuma das duas causas de falha e silenciada, ambas aparecem em stderr).

Nenhum destes codigos e novo: e o mesmo vocabulario que --base e --pr ... --na-linha ja usam (docs/specs/AUR-430.md, docs/specs/AUR-431.md, docs/specs/AUR-438.md).

docs.title: Exemplo executavel sem segredo
docs.text:
bash tests/e2e/AUR-439.sh E2EAUR439

Compila o binario real, sobe um fake GitHub em loopback a partir de tests/fixtures/scm/github/ (o diff do PR 42, as permissoes de leitura-escrita e so-leitura, a resposta de comentario criado) estendido com o endpoint de status (/repos/dono/projeto/statuses/<sha>, que responde 422 a um state ausente ou invalido, nunca um mock que concorda com qualquer corpo), escreve quatro respostas de modelo deterministicas -- uma com um achado grave (error) mais um achado geral, uma so com um achado nao-grave (warning), uma sem achado nenhum, e uma so-geral (para a prova mais estreita do SHA acima) -- e roda aurumcode review --pr 42 --repo dono/projeto --publicar --check contra cada uma. Prova: achado grave publica state=failure e um exit code que nunca e 0; achado so warning publica state=success e exit 0; zero achados ainda publica state=success; sem GITHUB_SHA o comando recusa antes de qualquer POST mesmo quando nada e elegivel a inline; um token so-leitura e recusado antes de qualquer POST; repetir a execucao produz a mesma saida e o mesmo status publicado; e o contrato pre-existente (--na-linha no lugar de --check) nunca contata o endpoint de status. Tokens sao strings sinteticas montadas em tempo de execucao; nenhum shape de credencial existe em arquivo rastreado.

docs.title: Selectors e exit codes do aceite
docs.text:
• Aceite: tests/acceptance/AUR-439.sh -- selectors AC-001 (tudo), TestAUR439, IntegrationAUR439, E2EAUR439, AC-001-MUT-001.
  • Exit codes (convencao do board, tests/acceptance/EXIT_CODE_CONVENTION.md): 0 comportamento provado; 1 RED comportamental; 64 selector desconhecido; 79 infraestrutura / inconclusivo (nunca evidencia de RED).

docs.title: Diagnostico de falha
docs.text:
• AUR-439/AC-001/behavior-missing: o caminho --check nao entrega o fluxo prometido (ver stderr do harness em tests/e2e/AUR-439.sh).
  • grave_wrong_exit: um achado grave nao produziu o exit code 3 esperado (ou produziu 0, o defeito exato que MUT-001 injeta).
  • wrong_state_reported_success: o state publicado no commit status foi "success" com um achado grave presente -- o outro rosto do mesmo defeito, visivel no corpo do POST em vez de so no exit code (a licao dos cards irmaos: o discriminador tem que ser o state publicado, nao so "nao deu erro").
  • clean_wrong_state / empty_missing_check_line: o caminho sem achado grave nao publicou "success".
  • nosha_not_refused / nosha_post_leaked: --check nao herdou a recusa fail-closed por SHA ausente.
  • readonly_not_refused / readonly_post_leaked: --check nao herdou a recusa fail-closed por falta de permissao de escrita.
  • nocheck_status_leaked / nocheck_check_line_leaked: o contrato pre-existente (--na-linha, sem --check) regrediu -- contatou o endpoint de status ou imprimiu a linha de check quando nao deveria.
  • non_deterministic / non_deterministic_status_count: duas execucoes identicas divergiram na saida ou no status publicado.
  • infrastructure/missing_go, infrastructure/mktemp, infrastructure/fakegithub_did_not_start (exit 79): ambiente, nunca RED.

docs.title: Compatibility, migration, rollback
docs.text:
• Compatibility: --base e review --pr ... --publicar (sem --check) mantem o contrato publicado byte a byte -- toda a logica nova de --check fica atras de if check { ... }, e o unico ramo pre-existente que muda de posicao (o calculo de commitID/needsCommitID, movido para antes do retorno antecipado de "No issues found.") e um no-op quando check e false: needsCommitID so passa a true ali pela mesma condicao que ja usava antes (um achado elegivel a inline), entao nenhuma saida observavel muda para quem nunca passa --check.
  • Migration: not-applicable.
  • Rollback: reverter somente os paths deste card; nenhum estado externo (alem do commit status publicado durante um teste real, nunca durante o aceite offline) e afetado.

docs.title: AUR-440 — A Action revisa pull requests automaticamente
docs.text: Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

docs.title: O que este card entrega
docs.text: Um workflow de exemplo, .github/workflows/examples/code-review.yml, que o usuario copia para o repositorio dele como .github/workflows/code-review.yml. A partir da copia, todo pull request aberto, sincronizado ou reaberto e revisado pelo AurumCode e recebe o resultado como comentario no proprio pull request, sem ninguem rodar comando.

docs.title: A arquitetura decidida: evento nativo, sem servidor proprio
docs.text:
O GitHub Actions dispara nativamente no evento pull_request e o job publica com o token da propria Action (github.token). Nao existe servidor de webhook self-hosted nem validacao HMAC neste desenho: esse segundo modelo de gatilho (internal/git/webhook, cmd/server) ficou fora do escopo desta rodada e permanece recuperavel do commit c12d7ab se um card futuro precisar dele. A decisao esta registrada no card AUR-440.

O binario de review e construido do checkout da release Mpaape/AurumCode na tag v1 — codigo confiavel e pinado. O codigo do pull request e apenas DADO para o job: e lido como diff git, nunca compilado nem executado. Um PR malicioso nao ganha execucao de build script sob um token com escrita.

docs.title: Divergencia registrada: --publish pertence ao AUR-438
docs.text:
O Escopo do card menciona chamar o binario "com --publish". Esse flag nao existe no binario da arvore que a tag v1 publica, nem em nenhum flag ja publicado por cmd/aurumcode — o nome em portugues e --publicar, nao --publish. A publicacao atraves do proprio binario (--publicar, com --pr/--repo) pertence ao card AUR-438, que depende do cliente GitHub restaurado pelo AUR-437. AUR-438 esta done: cmd/aurumcode ja publica --pr, --repo, --publicar e --na-linha (cmd/aurumcode/pr.go, cmd/aurumcode/main.go). Um workflow que passasse o flag inexistente --publish sairia com exit 2 (flag desconhecido) em todo run de usuario — um exemplo quebrado por construcao, independente do estado do AUR-438.

Por isso este workflow entrega o Outcome com o que existe em v1: o binario revisa (review --base) e a publicacao e feita pelo passo seguinte com gh pr comment, sob a permissao pull-requests: write do job. As tres lanes deste card travam o conjunto de flags da invocacao em {--base, --fail-on}: qualquer flag fora do conjunto — --publish incluido — reprova o aceite. AUR-438 ja entregou a publicacao nativa em cmd/aurumcode (--pr, --repo, --publicar, --na-linha), mas este workflow de exemplo ainda nao foi migrado para usa-la — code-review.yml continua chamando review --base e publicando com gh pr comment. Migrar o exemplo e afrouxar/ajustar esse conjunto de flags trancado continua sendo trabalho de um card proprio, distinto deste.

docs.title: Como usar
docs.text:
1. Copie .github/workflows/examples/code-review.yml para o seu repositorio como .github/workflows/code-review.yml, sem editar nada.
  2. Configure dois secrets de repositorio: LLM_API_KEY e LLM_BASE_URL (endpoint compativel com OpenAI). Opcionalmente a variavel de repositorio LLM_MODEL (default do binario: gpt-4).
  3. Abra um pull request. O job review roda sozinho e publica o comentario ### AurumCode code review com os findings (ou No issues found.).

Exemplo executavel sem segredo: sem LLM_API_KEY/LLM_BASE_URL configurados, o passo de review falha com ::error::LLM_API_KEY and LLM_BASE_URL must be configured as repository secrets e exit 1 — nunca um check verde para um review que nao rodou.

docs.title: Permissoes (privilegio minimo)
docs.text:
• Nivel do workflow: contents: read e nada mais. Nenhuma entrada pull-requests existe no topo.
  • Job review (o unico job, e o unico lugar com escrita):
  • contents: read — faz os dois checkouts;
  • pull-requests: write — e o que permite gh pr comment publicar o comentario. Remover essa permissao faz a validacao de manifesto deste repositorio falhar com AUR-440/AC-001/MUT-001 (mutacao cetica do card) e faz o GitHub recusar a publicacao em runtime.

Pull request de fork: o GitHub retem os secrets e rebaixa o token para somente leitura no evento pull_request. O passo de review entao falha com a mensagem de secret ausente — falha visivel, nunca check verde silencioso. O exemplo nao usa pull_request_target de proposito: aquele evento entrega token com escrita a codigo vindo de fork.

docs.title: Exit codes observaveis no job
docs.text:
O binario aurumcode review (ver docs/specs/AUR-430.md e docs/specs/AUR-431.md):

  • 0 — review rodou; findings (ou a linha No issues found.) impressos e publicados como comentario.
  • 1 — o review em si falhou (provider indisponivel, resposta invalida, diff ilegivel); o job falha e nada e publicado.
  • 2 — erro de uso; nao ocorre com a copia intacta do exemplo.

Passos do workflow: exit 1 quando os secrets faltam, quando o binario nao produz saida, ou quando gh pr comment e recusado (por exemplo sem pull-requests: write).

docs.title: Publicar a tag v1 e acao humana
docs.text: O workflow referencia Mpaape/AurumCode em ref: v1, a tag semver publicavel — nunca um SHA local de trabalho e nunca um branch mutavel. A publicacao da tag v1 e um ato humano do mantenedor, fora de qualquer run de CI e fora do aceite hermetico deste card (o sandbox nega rede). O aceite (tests/acceptance/AUR-440.sh) prova estaticamente, por parse YAML real (yaml.v3, arvore de nos), que o manifesto copiado entrega o contrato; ele nunca finge provar uma publicacao viva. Politica de pin imutavel? Troque a tag pelo SHA que ela resolve no momento da sua revisao.

docs.title: Diagnostico de falha
docs.text:
• LLM_API_KEY and LLM_BASE_URL must be configured... — configure os dois secrets no repositorio que copiou o workflow.
  • gh: ... (HTTP 403) no passo de publicacao — a permissao pull-requests: write foi removida do job, ou o PR vem de fork (token somente leitura). Restaure a permissao do exemplo.
  • aurumcode review: no LLM provider configured — o secret chegou vazio ao binario; verifique o nome exato dos secrets.
  • Job nem dispara — o arquivo precisa estar em .github/workflows/ do branch default, e o evento coberto e pull_request (opened, synchronize, reopened).

docs.title: Validacao deste card
docs.text:
• Unit: tests/unit/AUR-440.go::TestAUR440 — o documento do workflow, parseado de verdade, declara gatilho, permissoes, pins e passos.
  • Integration: tests/integration/AUR-440.go::IntegrationAUR440 — contrato cruzado com go.mod (owner/repo e diretiva go) e com action.yml (a composite raiz e o gerador de documentacao e nao revisa; nenhum passo pode delega-la).
  • E2E: tests/e2e/AUR-440.sh::E2EAUR440 — copia byte-identica para um repositorio de usuario de scratch, validador compilado rodado duas vezes com saida deterministica.
  • Accept: ./.board/bin/oci-run --profile bootstrap-readonly-v1 --card AUR-440.

docs.title: AUR-441 — aurumcode review --base <ref>: do not pay twice for the same file
docs.text: Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

docs.title: Command
docs.text:
aurumcode review --base <ref> [--fail-on <level>] [--modelo <nome>] [--seguranca]

No new flag. On the --base path, a second invocation against an unchanged file does not resend that file to the model, and the command reports how many files were reused. --pr's review path (AUR-438) is unaffected. Every other published behavior — output shape, exit codes, --fail-on, --modelo, --seguranca — is unchanged.

docs.title: Why this exists
docs.text: The review engine sends the entire reviewed diff to the model in one prompt, one Complete call per invocation (internal/review.Reviewer.GenerateReview, internal/prompt.PromptBuilder.BuildPrompt): there is no per-file send for a cache to intercept. cmd/aurumcode (cmd/aurumcode/review_cache.go) filters the diff down to the files internal/review/cache does not already hold an entry for before calling GenerateReview; when nothing missed, the call to the model is skipped entirely.

docs.title: Cache key and storage
docs.text:
Each changed file gets its own cache key: a content digest of that file's own diff (path, language tag, every hunk — the only bytes the engine bases a finding on), combined with the model identity and a prompt-version constant. Any change to what the model would see for that file — a byte in the diff, the model, or a manually-bumped prompt version — misses.

The digest is computed over the raw, unredacted diff content, not the redacted form actually sent to the model: redacting first would collapse two genuinely different file versions that differ only inside a redacted span (a rotated secret, for instance) into the same key, masking a real content change. A digest is one-way, so nothing recoverable is persisted by computing it this way.

"Model identity" is not simply the provider's name:

  • The offline fixture provider (AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE) reports the same name regardless of which canned response file is configured, but two different fixture files answer differently — so, for caching, they are two different models: the fixture file's own content digest is folded into the key whenever AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE is set.
  • --limite (AUR-433) wraps the provider to pin the cost tracker's accounting key; that wrapper's resolved model key (llm.ModelResolver) is folded in too, so a metered and an unmetered request against identical content never share an entry — a metered call is guarded by a budget check an unmetered one never has.

A live, unwrapped, unfixtured provider's answer is determined by provider.Name() alone, which is used verbatim.

Entries live one file per key under a cache directory:

  • AURUMCODE_CACHE_DIR, when set, names it exactly (even a relative path): two invocations that name the same directory reuse each other's entries.
  • Otherwise, a directory unique to this process invocation ($TMPDIR/aurumcode-review-cache-<pid>) — never a location a separate aurumcode run could land on by coincidence, so a bare, unconfigured second run behaves exactly as if caching were off. This was a deliberate reversal from a first design that scoped the default to the reviewed repository (so a bare second run would reuse it automatically): that design broke AUR-433's already-published --limite contract, whose own acceptance program runs the built binary several times in a row against one repository — once unmetered, twice at an identical --limite ceiling to prove byte-for-byte determinism, once refused — and asserts every call independently reaches the model and reports its own real, freshly-computed cost. A shared default would have served the second --limite invocation from the first's cache entry: no call, an "actual cost" of $0.0000 instead of the real figure the first invocation printed, and a determinism assertion that can never pass again by construction, because the two invocations would no longer be doing the same work. Persisted reuse across separate invocations is therefore something the caller always asks for explicitly, via AURUMCODE_CACHE_DIR — exactly what every proof of this card's own Outcome does.

A cache directory that cannot be created or used degrades the run to exactly the pre-AUR-441 behavior: every file sent, every run. Caching is a performance optimization, never a correctness gate — a write failure never fails an otherwise-successful review.

docs.title: Output shape
docs.text:
Stdout is byte-identical whether or not caching engaged, in a cold run or a fully-reused one: a cache hit's findings are merged back into the same printed result a fresh call would have produced. The one visible signal is on stderr, and only when at least one file was actually reused:

aurumcode review: reused <N> file(s) from cache (not resent to the model)

This mirrors --fail-on's and --modelo's existing stderr-only notes: the published stdout contract never grows a new line for a flag- or state-dependent behavior.

--fail-on composes correctly with a cache hit: the gate reads the merged result, so a reused finding still closes the gate exactly like a freshly produced one. --seguranca's deterministic pass is unaffected — it always scans the full diff and never consults the cache.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Unchanged from docs/specs/AUR-430.md, AUR-431.md, AUR-436.md:

Code Meaning 0 Review ran; gate (if any) open. 1 The review itself failed. 2 Usage error. 3 --fail-on gate closed (a cache-hit finding counts).

docs.title: Offline, secret-free example
docs.text:
cd tests/fixtures/repos/git-demo/repo.git
export AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE=../../review/known-problem-response.json
export AURUMCODE_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/example-aurumcode-cache

aurumcode review --base HEAD~1
# config/demo-tokens.txt:4: [error] ... (rule security/hardcoded-secret: Hardcoded Secrets)

aurumcode review --base HEAD~1
# config/demo-tokens.txt:4: [error] ... (rule security/hardcoded-secret: Hardcoded Secrets)
# stderr: aurumcode review: reused 2 file(s) from cache (not resent to the model)

The second run's stdout is byte-identical to the first; the reuse note appears only on stderr.

docs.title: Failure diagnosis
docs.text:
• A second run never reuses anything (stderr never shows reused ...) — without AURUMCODE_CACHE_DIR set, every invocation gets its own process-scoped cache and always behaves like a cold run; set AURUMCODE_CACHE_DIR to the same directory across invocations to observe reuse.
  • A reused file's finding is missing from the output — check that AURUMCODE_CACHE_DIR is actually writable and was not cleared between runs; a cache miss simply resends the file, it never drops a finding.
  • Two different AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE files against the same repository correctly produce two different results, never a stale answer from the other fixture: they are treated as two different models for caching.
  • A metered (--limite) and an unmetered run sharing an explicit AURUMCODE_CACHE_DIR correctly never serve one another's cached answer: they are treated as two different models for caching (see "Cache key and storage").
  • --base HEAD (nothing changed) still calls the model exactly like before AUR-441; a zero-file diff is not treated as a full cache hit.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Whatever is written to a cache file already passed internal/review.redactReviewResult (AUR-432) before this card's own code ever saw it; nothing model-authored reaches disk unredacted.
  • The cache key is a one-way digest of raw content, never the content itself, so nothing recoverable is persisted by key computation either.
  • AURUM_SECRET_CANARY never appears in stdout, stderr, prompt, or any cache file; tests/acceptance/AUR-441.sh and tests/integration/AUR-441.go assert this on every run, including walking every file the cache directory contains.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: tests/acceptance/AUR-441.sh AC-001 (sealed: ./.board/bin/oci-run --profile bootstrap-readonly-v1 --card AUR-441), with selectors TestAUR441 (tests/unit/AUR-441.go), IntegrationAUR441 (tests/integration/AUR-441.go), E2EAUR441 (tests/e2e/AUR-441.sh) and AC-001-MUT-001 (invalidating reuse on every execution, which must make the submission count stop dropping between runs).

docs.title: AUR-442 — aurumcode review --seguranca: the passage finds what the catalog promises
docs.text: Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

docs.title: Command
docs.text:
aurumcode review --base <ref> [--fail-on <level>] [--modelo <nome>] [--seguranca]

Same command AUR-435 published. This card does not add a flag or change the output shape; it repairs what --seguranca's deterministic pass actually matches, so the pass stops claiming coverage it never delivered.

docs.title: The measured defect (2026-08-13 dogfooding)
docs.text: Running the real binary against real repositories: --seguranca matched only 2 of the 8 catalog rules (security/sql-injection, security/command-injection), both requiring the narrow "..." + var string-concatenation shape. The other six (xss, path-traversal, hardcoded-secret, weak-crypto, insecure-random, missing-auth) were metadata with no pattern, so they never matched anything. The observable consequence: the project's own demo fixture, tests/fixtures/repos/git-demo — whose sole purpose is to plant a plaintext secret — reported No security findings. on every run.

docs.title: The decision: option (a), scoped to one rule
docs.text:
The card offered two legitimate fixes: give the missing rules a pattern with a fixture proving each one (a), or declare the covered subset honestly and stop promising the rest (b). This card takes (a), scoped to exactly one rule — security/hardcoded-secret, the card's named priority and the rule git-demo's fixture depends on — rather than (a) for several rules under the same review pass. The other five stay declared-only: each now carries an explicit code comment in internal/review/rules/security.yml recording that decision (not silence), and this file is the honest, spec-level declaration the card's option (b) requires for them. Two reasons narrowed scope to one rule instead of the card's own hardcoded-secret-plus-weak-crypto example:

  • Precision cost. A matcher shipped without a validated, tested false-positive boundary is exactly the failure mode this card exists to close (a rule that fires on the wrong things is not meaningfully better than a rule that never fires). hardcoded-secret alone required two regex branches, an explicit "letter mixed with a digit or hyphen" requirement to reject plain function calls (token := getToken()) and plain numeric constants (TOKEN_MAX_AGE_SECONDS = 31536000), and a dedicated benign-line test suite (see internal/review/rules/security.yml's rule comment and tests/unit/AUR-442.go's ScanRejectsBenignAssignments). A second matcher (weak-crypto, or any other) needs the same rigor, which this card's scope did not budget for without rushing it.
  • xss, path-traversal, and missing-auth are not line-shape questions at all — they turn on data flow (does untrusted input reach an unescaped sink / an unvalidated path / a handler that should require auth and does not), which a single added line cannot answer regardless of how carefully the regex is written.

Every undelivered rule remains citable by a model finding (AUR-434's rule-citation gate resolves any catalog id, pattern or not) — only the deterministic --seguranca pass is scoped. Nothing in --help, this document, or the command's printed output claims coverage beyond what is proven below.

docs.title: What security/hardcoded-secret now matches
docs.text:
Two shapes, both requiring a credential-named identifier (api key, secret, password, passwd, token, credential, access key, case-insensitive) assigned a value that mixes a letter with a digit or a hyphen:

  1. <keyword> (:=|:|=) "<value>" — a quoted assignment, the shape common in application source (api_key := "AURUM-FAKE-KEY-9000-2222").
  2. UPPER_SNAKE_KEYWORD = <value> unquoted — the env/config-file shape tests/fixtures/repos/git-demo/content/03/config/demo-tokens.txt uses (DEMO_API_TOKEN=AURUM-FAKE-TOKEN-0000-0001). The keyword may be the whole identifier with no prefix (TOKEN=..., SECRET=..., API_KEY=..., PASSWORD=...) or prefixed (DEMO_API_TOKEN=...); a review fix (2026-08-13) closed a gap where a mandatory leading uppercase letter silently consumed the keyword's own first character whenever the identifier had no prefix, so the four bare forms never matched despite this shape being documented without that exclusion (tests/unit/AUR-442.go's ScanFindsTheBareUnquotedEnvShape).

The letter-plus-(digit-or-hyphen) requirement is deliberate: it is what lets the matcher find password = "hunter2xyz123" and SERVICE_ACCESS_KEY=AURUM-FAKE-ACCESS-9000-3333 while passing over token := getAuthToken(), API_TOKEN = get_token_from_vault(), and TOKEN_MAX_AGE_SECONDS = 31536000 — a bare function call or a bare numeric constant, neither a hardcoded secret. Findings cite the rule and, new under this card, the project security standard SCR-003 (Cryptographic Failures / hardcoded credential, standards/security-review/rules.md).

Known limitation, same category as the SQL-injection pattern's own documented breadth (docs/specs/AUR-435.md, noted by the AUR-435 reviewer): a line-level regexp cannot see intent. A variable named secretary assigned an unrelated 16+ character token, or a comment line that happens to read secret: <8+ char word>, can still match. This is an accepted, bounded trade-off — the alternative (no matcher at all) is the defect this card fixes — not a promise of perfect precision.

docs.title: Output shape
docs.text:
Unchanged from AUR-435:

<notices and quality findings, exactly as without the flag>

Security findings (standards/security-review):
config/demo-tokens.txt:4: [error] Hardcoded credentials or API keys detected [standards/security-review SCR-003] (rule security/hardcoded-secret: Hardcoded Secrets)
config/demo-tokens.txt:5: [error] Hardcoded credentials or API keys detected [standards/security-review SCR-003] (rule security/hardcoded-secret: Hardcoded Secrets)
config/demo-tokens.txt:6: [error] Hardcoded credentials or API keys detected [standards/security-review SCR-003] (rule security/hardcoded-secret: Hardcoded Secrets)

The message is trusted catalog text (rule.Description), never the matched diff content: the secret VALUE never reaches this line, only the file, the line number, and the rule/standard citation. This is structural (internal/review/securitypass.go builds every message from the catalog, not from the matched body), proven in tests/unit/AUR-442.go's ScanNeverEchoesTheMatchedValue and exercised end to end in tests/integration/AUR-442.go and tests/e2e/AUR-442.sh.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Unchanged from AUR-435 (docs/specs/AUR-435.md):

Code Meaning 0 Review ran; gate (if any) open. 1 The review itself failed (no provider, unreadable repo, broken rules catalog). 2 Usage error (missing --base, unknown flag or level). 3 --fail-on gate closed. A matched hardcoded-secret finding is severity error and closes --fail-on high on its own.

docs.title: The card's central proof: git-demo
docs.text:
tests/fixtures/repos/git-demo plants three synthetic secrets specifically so a security pass has something to find. Before this card, --seguranca reported No security findings. here; it now reports all three:

cd tests/fixtures/repos/git-demo/repo.git
AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE=../../../review/known-problem-response.json \
  aurumcode review --base HEAD~1 --seguranca

docs.title: A dedicated fixture proving both matched shapes
docs.text:
tests/fixtures/review/vuln/hardcoded-secret (new under this card, rebuildable deterministically with tests/fixtures/repos/git-demo/build-fixture.sh; sibling to and never touching AUR-435's own tests/fixtures/review/vuln/repo.git, whose HEAD~1..HEAD diff AUR-435's frozen tests pin byte for byte) plants one secret of each shape beside one deliberately benign line each:

cd tests/fixtures/review/vuln/hardcoded-secret/repo.git
AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE=../../../known-problem-response.json \
  aurumcode review --base HEAD~1 --seguranca

prints, after the unchanged quality block:

Security findings (standards/security-review):
config/secrets.env:4: [error] Hardcoded credentials or API keys detected [standards/security-review SCR-003] (rule security/hardcoded-secret: Hardcoded Secrets)
src/config.py:4: [error] Hardcoded credentials or API keys detected [standards/security-review SCR-003] (rule security/hardcoded-secret: Hardcoded Secrets)

— and not the benign SERVICE_NAME=aurum-fixture or timeout_seconds = 30 lines beside them.

docs.title: Failure diagnosis
docs.text:
• flag provided but not defined: -seguranca — the binary predates AUR-435; rebuild from source.
  • aurumcode review: review rules unavailable: ... — the embedded rules catalog is broken; fix internal/review/rules/ and rebuild.
  • The section says No security findings. but you expected a hardcoded-secret match — check the letter-plus-(digit-or-hyphen) requirement above; a bare function call or a bare numeric constant next to a credential-named identifier is correctly out of scope.
  • The section is silent about XSS, path traversal, weak crypto, insecure randomness, or missing auth — those five rules are declared metadata only (see "The decision" above); they are never out of scope by accident, and a model finding (without --seguranca, or alongside it) may still cite them.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Structural: the finding message is trusted catalog text, never the matched diff body (see "Output shape" above); the secret value cannot reach stdout through this path.
  • The AURUM_SECRET_CANARY value never reaches stdout, stderr, prompt, cache, or evidence; tests/acceptance/AUR-442.sh asserts this on every run.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
• review --base without --seguranca is byte-identical to the published AUR-430 contract; --fail-on, --modelo, --limite, --pr, --check, and docs are unaffected (tests/acceptance/AUR-433.sh, tests/acceptance/AUR-441.sh pass unchanged against this card's tree).
  • security/sql-injection and security/command-injection (AUR-435) keep matching exactly what they matched before (tests/unit/AUR-442.go's OtherSecurityRulesUnaffected).
  • tests/acceptance/AUR-435.sh and tests/integration/AUR-435.go are updated by this card, not left as follow-up debt. Both originally hardcoded that git-demo's --seguranca run prints No security findings. — true only because no rule had a matcher for the plaintext secret that fixture exists to plant. AUR-442's write-set was extended (.board/cards/ready/AUR-442.md's paths, same precedent as AUR-424 in this reconstruction: the card that changes behavior updates the tests that pinned the old behavior) to include both files. nominal_case (AUR-435.sh) and IntegrationAUR435 (AUR-435.go) now assert the correct behavior instead — the security/hardcoded-secret rule citation, the SCR-003 standard citation, and each of the three planted lines (config/demo-tokens.txt:4-6) by name — and explicitly fail if No security findings. reappears, so the rebase cannot regress to a weaker check. AUR-435's own MUT-001 (mutation_case, which runs against the unrelated tests/fixtures/review/vuln/repo.git, not git-demo) is untouched and still rejects its mutant.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
tests/acceptance/AUR-442.sh AC-001 (sealed: ./.board/bin/oci-run --profile bootstrap-readonly-v1 --card AUR-442), with selectors TestAUR442 (tests/unit/AUR-442.go), IntegrationAUR442 (tests/integration/AUR-442.go), E2EAUR442 (tests/e2e/AUR-442.sh) and AC-001-MUT-001 (deleting security/hardcoded-secret's pattern line, which must make the expected git-demo finding vanish).

Selector naming note (same technique tests/unit/AUR-445.go and tests/integration/AUR-445.go document): the card text's TDD proof section names TestAUR435 / IntegrationAUR435, copy-paste artifacts from the AUR-435 card this one was drafted against. Both symbols already exist in their packages (tests/unit/AUR-435.go, tests/integration/AUR-435.go) and would collide, so this card's proofs are TestAUR442 / IntegrationAUR442 instead.

docs.title: AUR-443 — a first-time user discovers aurumcode without reading source
docs.text:
Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

Outcome: a user who has never read the source code discovers what aurumcode does and can run a first review. Dogfooding on 2026-08-13 measured a first-use score of 3/10 against the real binary and found seven concrete defects. This card fixes five of them, and investigates and records two as deliberately unchanged because fixing them would break a published, done card's contract. It changes only help/error/exit surfaces: aurumcode review --base's findings output and aurumcode docs's output are byte-for-byte unchanged (see "Compatibility" below).

docs.title: Command
docs.text:
aurumcode --help | -h | help
aurumcode --version | version
aurumcode review --help | -h
aurumcode docs --help | -h

docs.title: 1. Top-level help
docs.text:
Before this card, aurumcode --help and aurumcode -h both failed: aurumcode: unknown command "--help", exit 2 — there was no top-level help at all, only each subcommand's own --help, and a user had to already know review or docs existed to find those. aurumcode --help (-h, or the bare word help) now lists every subcommand with a one-line summary and one runnable example, on stdout, exit 0:

$ aurumcode --help
usage: aurumcode <command> [flags]

Commands:
  review   Review a git diff with an LLM (or the project's deterministic security rules) and print, gate on, or publish the findings.
  docs     Generate project documentation from source code.

Run "aurumcode <command> --help" for that command's own flags.

Example:
  aurumcode review --base HEAD~1
$ echo $?
0

aurumcode with no arguments at all is unchanged: still a usage error (usage: aurumcode <review|docs> [flags], stderr, exit 2) — the user asked for nothing, so nothing was fulfilled; --help must be explicitly requested to count as a fulfilled request (see "3." below). An unknown command (aurumcode frobnicate) is likewise unchanged: stderr, exit 2.

docs.title: 2. --version
docs.text:
Before this card there was no version and no --version; the only way to learn which build was running was to read go.mod/git log. aurumcode --version (or aurumcode version) now prints a build-stamped version string, on stdout, exit 0:

$ aurumcode --version
aurumcode dev
$ echo $?
0

dev is the default (cmd/aurumcode/main.go's var version = "dev") because this reconstruction publishes no numbered release yet. A future release pipeline injects a real value with no other code change, via Go's standard -ldflags -X mechanism:

$ go build -ldflags "-X main.version=1.2.3" -o aurumcode ./cmd/aurumcode
$ ./aurumcode --version
aurumcode 1.2.3

docs.title: 3. One --help convention for every subcommand
docs.text:
Before this card, the same binary disagreed with itself: review --help printed usage to stderr and exited 2 (the generic flag.Parse error path, unchanged since AUR-430); docs --help printed usage to stdout and exited 0 (AUR-426's deliberate choice, documented in docs/specs/AUR-426.md's "--help's own convention" as intentionally not retroactively applied to review). Both are Go conventions in active use; the two-mindedness inside one binary was the actual defect.

The convention is now the same everywhere in this binary, at the top level and both subcommands: an explicitly requested --help (or -h) is a fulfilled request — stdout, exit 0. A genuine usage error (an unrecognized flag, a value that will not parse) is a refusal — stderr, exit 2.

$ aurumcode review --help >/dev/null; echo $?
0
$ aurumcode review --help 2>&1 1>/dev/null | wc -c   # nothing on stderr
0
$ aurumcode review --bogus 1>/dev/null; echo $?
2

review's flag descriptions and every other published review behavior (--base, --fail-on, --modelo, --seguranca, --pr, --limite, --check) are untouched; only the channel and exit code --help itself produces changed (cmd/aurumcode/main.go's runReview, mirroring the buffered-then-dispatched pattern runDocs already established).

docs.title: 4. The provider-missing message shows the fixture's shape
docs.text:
Before this card, a first run without a configured provider (the common case for a user who has cloned the repository and typed the example command) failed with the correct diagnosis but no way to act on it without reading source:

aurumcode review: no LLM provider configured: set AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE for offline use, or LLM_API_KEY and LLM_BASE_URL for a live provider

— naming the environment variable, but not what a valid file at that path looks like. The message now shows the minimal JSON shape inline and points at a real, versioned, already-committed example the user can point AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE at directly, with no source reading required:

$ aurumcode review --base HEAD~1
aurumcode review: no LLM provider configured: set AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE=<path> to a JSON file shaped like {"issues":[{"file":"<path>","line":<n>,"severity":"error|warning|info","message":"<text>"}]} for offline use (see tests/fixtures/review/known-problem-response.json for a worked example), or set LLM_API_KEY and LLM_BASE_URL for a live provider
$ echo $?
1
$ AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE=tests/fixtures/review/known-problem-response.json aurumcode review --base HEAD~1
config/demo-tokens.txt:4: [error] A credential-shaped value was committed in plain text (DEMO_API_TOKEN).
$ echo $?
0

reportModelUnavailable (the --modelo-specific unavailable-model message) gets the identical pointer for the same reason. Both messages are printed through the AUR-432 redaction writer; cmd/aurumcode/redaction_wiring_test.go's TestStderrLinesSurviveTheRedactionWriter pins both as filter-identity — neither file/line/severity/message nor the fixture's path is a key/value shape the AUR-009 filter's secret-key-name rules ever match, so the example itself is never rewritten to [REDACTED] in front of the user.

docs.title: 5. --limite's refusal exit code: investigated, left unchanged
docs.text:
The dogfooding note observed that a --limite refusal exits 1, indistinguishable from "the tool broke," while --fail-on's gate has its own exit 3. This card investigated giving --limite's refusal a dedicated exit code and did not make the change, because AUR-433 is already done and its published contract pins exit 1 for exactly this outcome in three places:

  • tests/acceptance/AUR-433.sh's nominal_case, the over-limit case: [[ "$rc" -eq 1 ]] || fail over-limit-wrong-exit.
  • The same function's margin/boundary case: [[ "$rc" -eq 1 ]] || fail boundary-wrong-exit.
  • mutation_case's restoration check: [[ "$rc" -eq 1 ]] || fail 'MUT-001/restoration-broken', and the mutant assertion [[ "$rc" -ne 1 ]] || fail 'MUT-001/not-rejected'.

docs/specs/AUR-433.md's own exit-code table independently documents the same thing: "1 | The review failed, unchanged from AUR-430/431/435/436, now including: the assembled request's cost would exceed --limite. The model was never called." Any exit code other than 1 for this outcome fails all three assertions above and contradicts the published spec. Per this card's own instructions, that is a stop condition, not a defect to route around: cmd/aurumcode/cost.go is untouched by AUR-443. This card's own tests/unit/AUR-443.go re-asserts the exit code directly ("--limite refusal is still exit 1"), and the builder additionally ran tests/acceptance/AUR-433.sh against this candidate directly in the worktree and confirmed it still exits 0 (recorded in this card's evidence). tests/acceptance/AUR-433.sh itself is not a read_path for AUR-443, so tests/acceptance/AUR-443.sh cannot stage and re-run it inside the sealed acceptance profile; that check is done out of band, against the full checkout, not nested inside AUR-443's own sandboxed acceptance.

If a distinct exit code for a budget refusal is still wanted, it is a follow-up card's job: one that is allowed to touch AUR-433's own paths (tests/acceptance/AUR-433.sh, docs/specs/AUR-433.md) and re-publish that contract deliberately, not one that changes it as a side effect of a UX pass.

docs.title: 6. Git-repository and ref errors: one clean, actionable message
docs.text:
Before this card, a repository that could not be opened produced a literally duplicated phrase, because cmd/aurumcode's computeDiff wrapped internal/analyzer.OpenRepo's own already-complete message with another "is not a git repository" prefix:

aurumcode review: /tmp is not a git repository: not a git repository (no .git dir and /tmp is not bare): /tmp

and a ref that does not resolve leaked implementation detail that means nothing to a user who has not read internal/analyzer: a raw filesystem path on the pure-Go backend (the one this card's own sealed acceptance profile always exercises — no git binary in bootstrap-readonly-v1),

aurumcode review: computing diff does-not-exist..HEAD: resolving base ref "does-not-exist": resolving ref refs/heads/does-not-exist: open /path/to/repo/.git/refs/heads/does-not-exist: no such file or directory

or git's own "fatal: ..." wording on the git-binary backend (used when a git binary happens to be on PATH, e.g. an interactive developer shell):

aurumcode review: computing diff does-not-exist..HEAD: resolving base ref "does-not-exist": resolving ref "does-not-exist": git rev-parse --verify does-not-exist^{commit}: fatal: Needed a single revision

— two different leaks of internal detail for the same user mistake, depending on an implementation choice (OpenRepo's backend selection) the user cannot see. Both are now one clean, actionable sentence, identical regardless of which backend answered:

$ aurumcode review --base HEAD~1     # run outside any git repository
aurumcode review: /tmp is not a git repository (no .git directory here, and this path is not itself a bare repository)
$ echo $?
1
$ aurumcode review --base does-not-exist
aurumcode review: ref "does-not-exist" not found in this repository: expected a branch name, HEAD, a 40-character commit SHA, or a "<ref>~N" parent expression
$ echo $?
1

internal/analyzer is a read_path for this card (frozen, not owned by AUR-443), so the cleanup lives entirely in cmd/aurumcode/main.go: computeDiff no longer wraps OpenRepo's error with %w (its one error case is fully known — see internal/analyzer/gitrepo.go's OpenRepo), and a new cleanRefError helper recognizes the two prefixes analyzer.Repo.Diff always wraps with ("resolving base ref %q: " / "resolving head ref %q: ") together with the two concrete leaks measured above (a *fs.PathError in the chain, or git's own "Needed a single revision"/"unknown revision or path" wording) and replaces them with the single sentence shown above. Any other Diff failure (a corrupted tree, an ambiguous parent count, ref indirection too deep) is not concretely measured by this card's dogfooding and keeps its pre-existing, more verbose wrapped message — this card fixes the two measured leaks, it does not invent a new taxonomy of ref errors that was never observed.

docs.title: 6.1. Post-review correction: permission denied is not "not found"
docs.text:
Independent review found that the first cut of cleanRefError matched any *fs.PathError as "no such ref," which also matches a ref that exists but cannot be read — EACCES, not ENOENT. Reproduced by chmod 000 on a bare fixture's refs/heads/main and running as a non-root uid (the same shape a locked-down runtime like bootstrap-readonly-v1, or this reviewer's repro at uid 65534, naturally has): the command answered ref "main" not found, exit 1 — a confident, wrong diagnosis that directly contradicts this file's own "never silently hidden behind a guessed diagnosis" promise. The pre-AUR-443 binary's leaked, verbose message at least contained the words "permission denied"; this card's first cut regressed that to a clean but false answer.

Two separate defects, because the two backends leak differently:

  • Pure-Go backend: errors.As(err, &pathErr) alone cannot distinguish EACCES from ENOENT — both are *fs.PathError. Fixed by additionally requiring errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist).
  • git-binary backend: git rev-parse --verify <ref>^{commit} prints the byte-identical fatal: Needed a single revision for both causes — verified directly (git rev-parse --verify against an unreadable ref vs. a missing one produces the same stderr text). No string-matching fix on git's own output can ever tell them apart.

The fix that closes both: cleanRefError no longer infers "not found" from either backend's ambiguous text alone. It first calls a new, independent probe, refPathPermissionDenied(repoRoot, ref), which opens the exact physical ref location either backend would have consulted (.git/refs/heads/<ref>, or .git/HEAD for ref == "HEAD") directly from cmd/aurumcode and checks whether that open fails with errors.Is(err, fs.ErrPermission). This is independent of which backend actually answered — it reads the same file cmd/aurumcode already knows the location of, so it correctly classifies the failure for both backends with one code path, without editing internal/analyzer (a read_path). The probe is conservative: a raw 40-character SHA is skipped (no loose-ref file to check), and any outcome other than a confirmed permission error — the file does not exist, or it opens fine — falls through to the existing (now-corrected) "not found" heuristic, so the probe never manufactures a diagnosis it cannot back up.

$ chmod 000 .git/refs/heads/main   # as a non-root user
$ aurumcode review --base main
aurumcode review: permission denied resolving ref "main" in this repository: this process cannot read the ref's storage under .git (or the bare repository root) -- check its file permissions
$ echo $?
1

Verified identical on both backends (tests/integration/AUR-443.go's "git-binary backend: the same unreadable ref is also a permission message" subtest asserts the git-binary path's answer for this exact scenario, alongside the pure-Go path). tests/unit/AUR-443.go's biting test ("a ref that exists but is unreadable: permission message, never ref-not-found") additionally asserts the negative: the message must not contain "not found", and the genuinely-missing-ref test ("a ref that does not resolve") asserts the opposite negative — it must not contain "permission denied" — so the two outcomes cannot silently swap.

docs.title: 6.2. Post-review correction: a directory is not "not found" either
docs.text:
A second, independent review pass (vector 3: "try to fool the logic") found a third distinct cause that fell through §6.1's fix into the same raw-chain leak: --base feature against a repository whose only branch under that name is the hierarchical feature/sub — no literal feature ref exists, only the directory refs/heads/feature/ holding sub — resolves refs/heads/feature to a directory, not a ref file. On the pure-Go backend, os.ReadFile on a directory fails with EISDIR, which is neither fs.ErrNotExist nor fs.ErrPermission — so §6.1's two checks both correctly said no, and the code fell through to the one remaining raw %w wrap, reproducing exactly the leak this card exists to close:

aurumcode review: computing diff feature..HEAD: resolving base ref "feature": resolving ref refs/heads/feature: read /tmp/.../refs/heads/feature: is a directory

— containing the literal refs/heads/ path tests/acceptance/AUR-443.sh already treats as a leak everywhere else in this file, just not (before this fix) against this specific scenario. The git-binary backend, for the same input, already said a clean but imprecise ref "feature" not found (git's own rev-parse folds this case into the same generic "no single revision" outcome) — so the two backends disagreed, and only the pure-Go one (the one bootstrap-readonly-v1 actually exercises) leaked.

The structural defect: cleanRefError, once it has matched the "resolving base ref " / "resolving head ref " prefix, is already committed to explaining a specific, named ref's resolution failure — falling through to the raw wrap at that point was always going to leak something for whatever cause the two existing checks did not recognize, EISDIR was just the first one review found. The fix removes the fallthrough entirely: every branch past the prefix match now returns a clean, ref-scoped sentence, including a new fallback ("could not resolve ref %q in this repository") for a genuinely unclassified cause, and a new refPathIsDirectory(repoRoot, ref) probe — sharing refPathCandidate with refPathPermissionDenied, the same direct-filesystem-probe approach §6.1 already established — checked before the not-found heuristic:

$ aurumcode review --base feature   # only refs/heads/feature/sub exists
aurumcode review: ref "feature" is not a branch: a directory of refs by that name exists (a hierarchical branch namespace, e.g. "feature/...") -- name the exact branch, not a namespace prefix
$ echo $?
1

Probing first, rather than only patching the pure-Go backend's own error text, makes both backends agree on this more precise answer — the git-binary backend's previous "not found" is now also replaced by "is not a branch," not merely left alone, since the probe runs regardless of which backend answered. Verified identical on both backends (tests/unit/AUR-443.go and tests/integration/AUR-443.go each add a subtest asserting the pure-Go and git-binary messages match byte for byte). tests/acceptance/AUR-443.sh's nominal case re-runs its two existing leak greps (no such file or directory, refs/heads/) against this exact scenario, per the review's instruction, so a future regression here cannot pass unnoticed.

docs.title: 7. The model response's unused summary field: investigated, left unchanged
docs.text:
The dogfooding note observed that pkg/types.ReviewResult.Summary (parsed by internal/prompt.ResponseParser from the model's "summary" field, redacted by internal/review.redactReviewResult) reaches cmd/aurumcode's result and is never printed — silent dead code from this command's point of view. This card's own instructions require a decision: print it (and document it) or remove it from the parse; never leave it silently dead.

Neither branch is reachable within this card's paths. The evidence:

  • Printing it is blocked by a published, done card's byte-pinned contract. tests/acceptance/AUR-426.sh's review-contract-broken check and tests/unit/AUR-426.go's "aurumcode review's published contract is untouched" subtest (tests/unit/AUR-426.go:319) both run aurumcode review --base HEAD~1 against the fixture {"issues":[],"summary":"Nothing to report."} — a non-empty summary — and assert stdout is exactly "No issues found.\n", byte for byte. Printing Summary on a successful review, even conditionally on it being non-empty, changes that byte sequence and fails a done card's own acceptance the next time it runs. This card's own instructions independently forbid it a second way: review --base's findings output is pinned not to change content, and a summary line is neither a help, error, nor exit-code surface.
  • Removing it from the parse is outside paths. The field is parsed in internal/prompt/parser.go's ParseReviewResponse and populated in pkg/types.ReviewResult; both are read_paths for AUR-443, not paths — this card cannot edit either file.

The resolution: the decision is made and recorded, not silently re-deferred. cmd/aurumcode/main.go's runReview carries a comment at the exact site result is consumed, citing this section and the two acceptance assertions above, so the omission reads as a deliberate, investigated choice instead of an unexplained gap. No behavior changed.

2026-09-13 postscript (AUR-490): this decision is superseded, on purpose, for review --base specifically. AUR-490's own Acceptance required --base to carry the same summary and Mermaid diagram --pr already produced, "sem configuração" -- the exact promise this product's README and site make and --base did not keep. That cannot coexist with the byte-exact "No issues found." contract above: a run's stdout cannot both always include a rendered summary and, for the zero-issue case, consist of nothing but that one line. AUR-490 chose to keep the promise and retire the byte-exact contract, not the reverse -- the whole reason that card exists is that the local path was silently missing what the product already advertises.

Two things independently made this safe to decide without reopening this card's own investigation above:

  • The blocking test no longer runs. tests/acceptance/AUR-426.sh's review-contract-broken check depends on cmd/regenerate-docs and tests/unit/AUR-426.go, both removed by the later review-only pivot (670c7f6) -- before AUR-490 touched anything, this acceptance was already unable to execute past its own docs invocation. Retiring that now-dead script is tracked separately; it is not evidence either way about whether the summary should print, only about why nothing caught this sooner.
  • The reversal is recorded at the site it happens, not just here: cmd/aurumcode/main.go's runReview, at the same call site this section originally annotated, now explains why renderLocalReport (which includes the summary) prints unconditionally, citing this postscript.

The exit-code table below has the matching amendment for the "no provider configured" row.

docs.title: Exit codes (all subcommands)
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 --help/-h/help (top-level or either subcommand) or --version/version: the request was fulfilled. 0 review or docs ran and did what it promises (unchanged from AUR-430/431/435/436/438/439/433/441/426). 1 A real failure: not a git repository, a ref that does not resolve, the model call failed, the response could not be parsed, --limite's estimate exceeded the ceiling (see "5." above) — all unchanged in meaning, some reworded per "4." and "6." above. "No provider configured" is no longer unconditionally in this row for review --base (AUR-490, see "7."'s postscript): that case now runs deterministic analysis and exits per --fail-on/--check/--exigir-qualidade against what it found — 0 when nothing crosses the configured threshold, 3 when something does. It remains exit 1 for the PR path (--pr) and for --base whenever --modelo was explicitly given and the named provider could not be reached. 2 Usage error: an unrecognized flag, a required flag missing, a value that will not parse — including an explicitly requested --help that fails to parse for an unrelated reason (never for --help/-h itself, see "3." above). 3 Unchanged from AUR-431/AUR-439: the --fail-on or --check gate closed on a grave finding.

docs.title: Compatibility, migration, rollback
docs.text:
• Compatibility. aurumcode review --base's findings output (stdout content: notices, findings, the security section, the cache-reuse note, the cost lines) and aurumcode docs's output are byte-for-byte unchanged. This card touched only: (a) new top-level --help/-h/help and --version/version handling in run(), previously unreachable code paths (every one of those tokens previously fell through to "unknown command", exit 2); (b) review's own --help/-h channel and exit code (stderr+2 → stdout+0), which no published spec or test pinned before this card (verified: no acceptance, unit, integration or e2e file for AUR-430/431/433/435/436/438/439/441 exercises review --help at all); (c) two provider-missing stderr messages (extended, not shortened — every reader relying on strings.Contains(..., "no LLM provider configured"), e.g. tests/unit/AUR-436.go:198, still matches); (d) computeDiff's git-repository/ref-resolution error text (never asserted verbatim by any published spec or test — verified by the same search). tests/acceptance/AUR-433.sh, AUR-439.sh, AUR-441.sh and AUR-426.sh are not read_paths for AUR-443, so this card's own sandboxed tests/acceptance/AUR-443.sh cannot stage and re-run them; instead, tests/unit/AUR-443.go and tests/e2e/AUR-443.sh re-assert the specific published invariants those four cards pin (byte-identical review --base output including with a non-empty summary, the --limite exit code, the finding line shape), and the builder separately ran all four sibling acceptance scripts directly against this candidate in the worktree and confirmed exit 0 in each (recorded in this card's evidence, not nested inside the sealed acceptance run).
  • Migration. Not applicable — no data or state format changes.
  • Rollback. Revert only paths; no state external to this repository is published by this card.

docs.title: AUR-444: the Action's entrypoint invokes flags that exist
docs.text: Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
The GitHub Action published from this repository (scripts/action-entrypoint.sh, Dockerfile, action.yml) announced that it runs an automated code review, but three things made that announcement false:

  1. scripts/action-entrypoint.sh's review mode invoked "$AURUMCODE_CLI" review --provider= --model= --api-key= --github-token= --post-comments=. None of those five flags exist on cmd/aurumcode's review command; the binary would refuse the parse (usage exit 2) before reviewing a single line.
  2. The comments in scripts/action-entrypoint.sh and Dockerfile claimed there is no cmd/cli (or, in the Dockerfile's phrasing, no other main package) in the source tree, and the Dockerfile did not build or copy cmd/aurumcode into the image. Even with flag names fixed, the binary the entrypoint tried to invoke was never inside the image.
  3. action.yml claimed a gomarkdoc failure is fatal for Go documentation. False since AUR-424, which replaced that subprocess with go/parser + go/doc + go/printer; the same false claim, in paraphrased form, was also present in Dockerfile.

docs.title: 1. Real flags, mapped deliberately
docs.text:
cmd/aurumcode review's only required flag is --base <ref>: the ref this run diffs against HEAD. Everything else the review command reads (LLM_API_KEY, LLM_BASE_URL, LLM_MODEL, AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE, GITHUB_TOKEN) is read straight from the process environment by cmd/aurumcode itself (main.go's selectProvider, pr.go's newGitHubClient) -- none of it is a flag, so the entrypoint passes nothing extra for it; it inherits those variables from the container's own environment exactly as GitHub Actions (or docker run -e) sets them.

scripts/action-entrypoint.sh now sends exactly:

"$AURUMCODE_CLI" review --base="${AURUMCODE_BASE_REF}"

AURUMCODE_BASE_REF is this entrypoint's own new required input: the ref --base diffs against HEAD (for example, the pull request's base commit SHA -- github.event.pull_request.base.sha, the same value .github/workflows/examples/code-review.yml already wires into --base). It is a usage error (exit 64) when unset, never a silent no-op review.

Inputs mapped, and inputs dropped. The previous revision's LLM_PROVIDER and POST_PR_COMMENTS inputs had no real consumer at all: cmd/aurumcode has no notion of an LLM "provider" name (provider selection is entirely env-var driven) and no --post-comments concept on the --base path (publishing is --pr-only, behind --publicar). Both are removed rather than mapped to something they never meant.

cmd/aurumcode review's other real flags -- --fail-on, --modelo, --seguranca, --limite, and the --pr/--repo/--publicar/--na-linha family -- are not wired into this mode. Wiring the --pr family would mean inventing pull-request-number extraction from GITHUB_EVENT_PATH this entrypoint never had and this card never observed anyone running (Non-goals); .github/workflows/examples/code-review.yml's own canonical review invocation is review --base "${BASE_SHA}" -- the same flag, --base, though that example spells it space-separated where this fix uses --base=<ref>; Go's flag package parses both forms identically. A future card can wire the rest deliberately, against an observed need.

docs.title: 2. The --check discrepancy: measured twice, differently, and why it is still not wired in
docs.text:
This card's own "Achado medido" section names --check among "the real flags, today". First measurement, against this worktree's tip at the time: absent. go build ./cmd/aurumcode && ./aurumcode review --help printed no -check, and git merge-base --is-ancestor cf3273f HEAD (the AUR-439 commit that adds it) reported NOT ANCESTOR -- only a board bookkeeping commit (9e78890, "AUR-439 crosses to done with evidence and delivery record") had moved that card to done on this line of history without ever integrating its code. That was reported as a genuine board-integrity gap this card could not fix itself (.board/cards is a forbidden path for it).

The coordinator has since merged the approved AUR-439 SHA onto this card's base. Second measurement, against the corrected tip:

$ go build -o aurumcode ./cmd/aurumcode && ./aurumcode review --help
  -base string
  -check
        publish a commit status (AUR-439) that fails when a grave
        (error-severity) finding is present, blocking the pull request's
        merge; with --pr, satisfies the --na-linha requirement on its own
        (default: off)
  -fail-on string
  -limite string
  -modelo string
  -na-linha
  -pr int
  -publicar
  -repo string
  -seguranca

--check now exists. Per this card's own instruction -- verify every flag independently, never trust a hand-written list -- this second measurement governs, and tests/unit/AUR-444.go (go/parser over cmd/aurumcode's source) and tests/integration/AUR-444.go (the real built binary's own --help) both confirm it dynamically rather than by a note in this file.

Decision: --check is still not wired into scripts/action-entrypoint.sh. Reading cmd/aurumcode/main.go and pr.go on this tip: check := fs.Bool("check", ...) is registered on the shared review flag set, but it is only ever read inside runPRReview -- it is passed to that function and nowhere else, and runPRReview is reached only when --pr is given (cmd/aurumcode/main.go's prGiven dispatch). AUR-439's own doc comment states its declared command surface directly: review --pr N --repo o/r --publicar --check. So --check is not an independent capability this entrypoint could add on top of the --base path this card already wires; it is a fourth member of the --pr family this spec's Fix section 1 already named as out of scope, for the same three reasons, now confirmed against real code instead of inferred:

  1. Activating --check requires --pr (a pull request number), which this entrypoint has never extracted from GITHUB_EVENT_PATH. Doing so now would be new capability nobody asked for and this card never observed anyone running -- exactly what Non-goals rules out.
  2. --repo is required alongside it -- another input this entrypoint does not currently derive from anything.
  3. The --pr path calls client.HasWritePermission (a live GitHub API call) before anything else, and --check itself needs a commit status API call to publish. This card's own Preconditions state the acceptance sandbox denies network; a capability this card could not test at all inside its own declared acceptance is not one this card should ship as if proven.

If a future card wires the --pr family into this entrypoint (PR-number extraction, --repo derivation, a network-capable acceptance path or a fixture GitHub server as AUR-438's own acceptance already builds), --check is the natural, cheap addition alongside it: it needs no code of its own here, only --check="${AURUMCODE_CHECK:-false}" threaded next to --publicar. This card does not do that, because doing it without observing or testing any of it would be inventing behavior on top of already-fake flags -- the same defect this card exists to remove, one flag later.

docs.title: 3. The binary is in the image
docs.text:
Dockerfile now builds cmd/aurumcode alongside cmd/regenerate-docs and copies both into the final image:

RUN CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -ldflags="-s -w" -o aurumcode ./cmd/aurumcode
...
COPY --from=builder /build/aurumcode /app/aurumcode

scripts/action-entrypoint.sh's AURUMCODE_CLI now defaults to ${AURUMCODE_BIN_DIR}/aurumcode (was: ${AURUMCODE_BIN_DIR}/cli, a path nothing ever built). The image's test -x fail-fast check (Dockerfile) asserts /app/aurumcode exists so the script and the image cannot drift apart silently again.

docs.title: 4. qa mode regression, closed in the same pass
docs.text:
Before this fix, run_qa was unguarded: once a real aurumcode binary exists at AURUMCODE_CLI, require_binary's file-existence check passes, and "$AURUMCODE_CLI" qa ... would hit cmd/aurumcode's default: case ("unknown command") and exit 2 -- a code this file's own EXIT CODES table never documents -- killing the script under set -e instead of reporting one of the three documented outcomes. cmd/aurumcode publishes exactly two subcommands, review and docs; it has never had a qa subcommand. qa mode now fails closed, before the binary is ever invoked, with the documented environment-failure exit 3:

ERROR (environment): mode 'qa' requires a 'qa' subcommand that '.../aurumcode'
does not publish (it implements only review and docs; see
cmd/aurumcode/main.go). Select a mode this image supports (review,
documentation, qa, all).

AURUMCODE_MODE=all still runs review then documentation then qa (unchanged call order). Whenever review and documentation both succeed, all now reaches the qa stage and stops there with the same documented exit 3 -- never the undocumented 2. When review or documentation fails first, all still stops at that earlier stage exactly as before this card, with its own already-documented exit; this card changes nothing about that ordering, only what happens once execution does reach qa. Only the qa-alone path (AURUMCODE_MODE=qa) is exercised directly by this card's e2e proof; all reaching the same run_qa function is a consequence of the two functions being identical, not a separately re-verified path.

docs.title: 5. gomarkdoc prose, fixed where it actually appeared -- twice
docs.text: action.yml's "Install extractor toolchains" step no longer installs gomarkdoc unconditionally; the comment now says Go needs no external tool since AUR-424 and specifically still names the seven languages that do (python/pydoc-markdown, javascript/typedoc, csharp/dotnet+xmldocmd, cpp/doxygen, rust/cargo, bash/bash, powershell/pwsh) -- the same false claim, in paraphrased form ("the Go extractor shells out to gomarkdoc"), was also in Dockerfile's builder-stage comment and its now-removed tools build stage; both are corrected together, and the tools stage and its COPY --from=tools .../gomarkdoc are removed rather than left installed alongside a comment that says it is unnecessary.

docs.title: How this is proved: the read_paths closure
docs.text:
An earlier measurement of this card's own read_paths found it listing cmd/aurumcode but none of the internal/... packages that source imports (internal/analyzer, internal/prompt, internal/review, internal/llm, internal/security/redaction, internal/git/githubclient, pkg/types, and the internal/documentation/... + internal/pipeline packages the docs subcommand reuses). Confirmed empirically: staging only the then-declared read_paths and running go build ./cmd/aurumcode failed offline ("finding module for package .../internal/analyzer" et al.), because those packages were not on disk and the sealed acceptance denies network. That was a genuine gap this card could not repair itself (.board/cards is a forbidden path for it).

read_paths has since been corrected to carry the full closure. As a result:

  • tests/unit/AUR-444.go still proves criterion (a) with go/parser alone (no build needed) -- this did not change, and stays the fast, import-free, always-available proof.
  • tests/integration/AUR-444.go now ALSO builds the real cmd/aurumcode binary inside the staged acceptance root and confronts the entrypoint's argv against that binary's own --help output -- criterion (a) proved by running the artifact, not only by reading its source.
  • tests/e2e/AUR-444.sh builds and invokes the real binary as a required step (previously best-effort, gated on the closure happening to be present), asserting it does not reject the entrypoint's flags as unrecognized -- alongside its stand-in-binary scenarios, which remain the right tool for proving the entrypoint's OWN control flow (the AURUMCODE_BASE_REF gate, exact argv construction, determinism, the qa regression fix) independently of cmd/aurumcode's flag registration.

docs.title: Command
docs.text:
AURUMCODE_MODE=review \
AURUMCODE_BASE_REF=<ref> \
GITHUB_WORKSPACE=<git-repo-path> \
[AURUMCODE_CLI=<path-to-aurumcode>] \
[LLM_API_KEY=... LLM_BASE_URL=... LLM_MODEL=...] \
[AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE=<path>] \
[GITHUB_OUTPUT=<path>] \
bash scripts/action-entrypoint.sh

AURUMCODE_CLI defaults to ${AURUMCODE_BIN_DIR}/aurumcode (AURUMCODE_BIN_DIR defaults to /app, the path the Dockerfile builds).

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Unchanged from the file's own pre-existing, self-documented convention (scripts/action-entrypoint.sh's own header comment):

Code Meaning 0 The requested mode ran and produced what it promises. 1 Behavioral failure: the pipeline ran and the result is wrong or absent (includes the review binary reporting failure). 3 Environment failure: a binary, script or workspace this image cannot supply itself is missing -- includes the binary being absent at AURUMCODE_CLI, and now qa mode unconditionally (no qa subcommand exists to run). 64 Usage error: no mode, an unimplemented mode, or a mode invoked without configuration it requires -- includes review without AURUMCODE_BASE_REF.

docs.title: Executable example (offline, no secret)
docs.text:
cat > /tmp/fake-aurumcode <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
echo "reviewed: $*"
exit 0
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/fake-aurumcode

mkdir -p /tmp/workspace

AURUMCODE_MODE=review \
AURUMCODE_BASE_REF=deadbeef \
GITHUB_WORKSPACE=/tmp/workspace \
AURUMCODE_CLI=/tmp/fake-aurumcode \
bash scripts/action-entrypoint.sh

Expected output includes Review: passed and, along the way, reviewed: review --base=deadbeef -- proving the entrypoint invokes the binary with exactly review --base=<ref>, nothing else. Swap the stand-in for a real cmd/aurumcode build and this becomes a genuine review, given a real git workspace and a provider (LLM_API_KEY/LLM_BASE_URL, or AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE for a deterministic offline response).

docs.title: Diagnosis of failure
docs.text:
• ERROR (usage): AURUMCODE_MODE is not set... (exit 64) -- set AURUMCODE_MODE to review, documentation, qa or all.
  • ERROR (usage): mode 'review' requires AURUMCODE_BASE_REF... (exit 64) -- set AURUMCODE_BASE_REF to the ref --base should diff against HEAD.
  • ERROR (environment): mode 'review' requires the executable '.../aurumcode'... (exit 3) -- the image (or your override of AURUMCODE_CLI) does not actually carry the binary; build it from cmd/aurumcode.
  • ERROR (environment): mode 'qa' requires a 'qa' subcommand... (exit 3) -- qa is not implemented by cmd/aurumcode and is not this card's scope; select review, documentation or all (which itself still stops at the same qa message).
  • ERROR: review pipeline reported failures. (exit 1) -- the binary ran and returned non-zero; its own stderr (printed above this line) names the reason (missing provider configuration, a diff it could not read, etc.).

docs.title: Non-goals carried over from the card
docs.text:
• No behavior is added that nobody can observe by running the declared command above: the other real review flags stay unwired until a future card demonstrates an observed need for them.
  • internal/git/githubclient, internal/review, internal/llm and every other package cmd/aurumcode imports are unmodified; this card only integrates what already exists.

docs.title: Known gap this card does not close
docs.text: action.yml at the repository root is a composite action that generates documentation only (go build ./cmd/regenerate-docs, run directly in a step); it does not use Dockerfile or scripts/action-entrypoint.sh at all, so no shipped GitHub Action currently wires a container action's AURUMCODE_MODE=review inputs end to end. This predates this card (its own history shows action.yml has always been the documentation composite action) and is out of this card's declared paths/Outcome, which is specifically the three named false claims. Recorded here so the next card that touches Action wiring does not have to rediscover it.

docs.title: AUR-445 — A documentação de raiz diz a verdade sobre o que a ferramenta faz
docs.text: Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

docs.title: O que este card entrega
docs.text:
A auditoria de 2026-08-13 (.board/cards/ready/AUR-445.md, seção "Achados medidos") encontrou cinco famílias de afirmação falsa espalhadas pela documentação de raiz. Este card corrige cada uma, ancorada no código real:

  1. LICENSE existe. README.md, ACTION_USAGE.md e CHANGELOG.md afirmavam "No LICENSE file is present" / "no LICENSE file is present". LICENSE (MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Mateus Magnus Pimentel Paape) está na raiz do repositório desde o AUR-428. Os três arquivos agora apontam para [MIT](LICENSE).
  2. aurumcode review existe. CHANGELOG.md afirmava "No code-review or test-generation output". cmd/aurumcode é um segundo binário package main que implementa revisão de código local: aurumcode review --base <ref> [--fail-on <nível>] [--modelo <nome>] [--seguranca] [--limite <usd>] [--pr <n> --repo <owner/repo> --publicar --na-linha]. CHANGELOG.md agora documenta essa superfície sob "Present" e corrige "Not present" para nomear cmd/regenerate-docs explicitamente (é esse binário, não o repositório inteiro, que não faz revisão de código).
  3. As opções de aurumcode review são flags, não variáveis de ambiente. CHANGELOG.md:93 generalizava "Every knob is an environment variable" para o repositório inteiro. Isso continua verdadeiro para cmd/regenerate-docs (nenhum flag. no seu main.go; todas as chaves são os.Getenv/os.LookupEnv), mas é falso para cmd/aurumcode, cujas opções são exclusivamente flag.String/flag.Bool/flag.Int registradas em cmd/aurumcode/main.go. A correção separa os dois binários em vez de generalizar.
  4. Go não precisa de ferramenta externa. README.md:72,99, SETUP_GUIDE.md:86, ACTION_USAGE.md:49,56,265, docs/getting-started.md:53-54,75 e o texto correlato em RUN_DOCS_PIPELINE.md declaravam gomarkdoc obrigatório para Go. Desde o AUR-424, internal/documentation/extractors/go/extractor.go usa apenas go/parser + go/doc da biblioteca padrão — Validate() sempre retorna nil e nenhum arquivo do pacote importa os/exec ou referencia gomarkdoc. As outras 7 linguagens registradas (JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, C/C++, Bash, PowerShell, e — atrás de AURUMCODE_ALLOW_REPO_CODE_EXECUTION — Rust e C#) continuam dependendo de uma ferramenta externa; a correção é específica a Go, não uma generalização de "nenhuma linguagem precisa de ferramenta".
  5. Há dois comandos, não um. RUN_DOCS_PIPELINE.md:6-8 afirmava que cmd/regenerate-docs é "the only command in this repository". O repositório builda dois binários package main: cmd/regenerate-docs (gerador de documentação, tema deste arquivo) e cmd/aurumcode (aurumcode review, revisão de código). A correção nomeia o segundo e aponta para docs/specs/AUR-430.md sem transformar este arquivo em um tutorial de aurumcode review.

docs.title: Escopo não expandido (Non-goals do card)
docs.text:
• Rust e C# não são suportados por padrão hoje: ambos exigem AURUMCODE_ALLOW_REPO_CODE_EXECUTION porque seus toolchains (cargo doc, dotnet build) executam código do repositório documentado (internal/documentation/extractors/{rust,csharp}/extractor.go, constante ExecutesRepositoryCode).
