Nenhuma correção deste card afirma suporte pronto para uso a Rust ou C#.
  • --seguranca roda um subconjunto das regras do catálogo: internal/review/rules/security.yml declara 8 regras; apenas 2 carregam pattern (security/sql-injection, security/command-injection) e são de fato casadas contra as linhas adicionadas do diff. As outras 6 são metadado citável por um achado do modelo, não casadas pela passagem determinística. CHANGELOG.md agora declara esse escopo explicitamente em vez de deixar --seguranca implicar cobertura total. Essa contagem foi verificada por leitura direta do arquivo durante a construção deste card; internal/review/rules/security.yml está fora dos read_paths declarados no card, então o aceite sandboxed (tests/integration/AUR-445.go) deliberadamente NÃO relê esse arquivo em tempo de aceite — fazê-lo falharia com entrypoint_missing no perfil bootstrap-readonly-v1, que só materializa paths/read_paths, em vez de produzir um resultado de comportamento real.

docs.title: Comando (verificação estática do aceite)
docs.text:
O aceite roda offline, sem executar aurumcode nem regenerate-docs, e sem rede — é leitura e correspondência de texto sobre os seis arquivos de documentação de raiz declarados em paths, mais checagem cruzada documentação-vs-código sobre os read_paths declarados no card.

# Dentro do profile pinado, cwd no worktree do candidato:
ulimit -v 8388608
export GOMEMLIMIT=2GiB GOFLAGS='-mod=mod -p=1'
bash tests/acceptance/AUR-445.sh AC-001

oci-run não passa seletor, então AC-001 (o default do script) é exatamente o que o aceite selado executa. O script, nesse caminho:

  1. Normaliza o texto de cada um dos seis arquivos (README.md, CHANGELOG.md, ACTION_USAGE.md, SETUP_GUIDE.md, RUN_DOCS_PIPELINE.md, docs/getting-started.md) — remove crase, normaliza para minúsculas, colapsa espaços em branco e quebras de linha — e confirma a ausência de cada uma das cinco famílias de frase falsa listadas acima (Unit, tests/unit/AUR-445.go::TestAUR445).
  2. Confirma, por leitura direta do código (não por outro grep sobre a documentação), que as afirmações verdadeiras têm lastro: LICENSE começa com "MIT License"; cmd/aurumcode/main.go e cmd/regenerate-docs/main.go são ambos package main; nenhum arquivo em internal/documentation/extractors/go/ referencia gomarkdoc ou importa os/exec; toda flag citada na documentação (base, fail-on, modelo, seguranca, limite, pr, repo, publicar, na-linha) está registrada em cmd/aurumcode/main.go (Integration, tests/integration/AUR-445.go::IntegrationAUR445).
  3. Roda a mesma verificação a partir do binário de shell (tests/e2e/AUR-445.sh::E2EAUR445), no mesmo processo do AC-001.

AC-001 sozinho NÃO reproduz o MUT-001: essa mutação é uma invocação separada, bash tests/acceptance/AUR-445.sh MUT-001, que este card provou manualmente durante a construção (nunca automática dentro de oci-run, mesma convenção de AUR-428/AUR-440). Essa invocação estagia uma cópia descartável SEPARADA em /tmp (nunca o README.md rastreado), reintroduz a frase banida só nessa cópia, exporta AUR445_MUTATION=MUT-001 para que o Unit e o E2E distingam a mutação deliberada do RED natural (que produz o mesmo texto banido, mas sem o marcador — ver a nota de normalização em tests/unit/AUR-445.go), e confirma que a saída capturada de cada camada carrega o rótulo AUR-445/AC-001/MUT-001 antes de aceitar a falha como a mutação detectada. A cópia é descartada ao final; o README.md rastreado nunca é tocado.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Código Contexto Significado 0 AC-001 Todas as cinco famílias de frase falsa estão ausentes dos seis arquivos e todas as afirmações verdadeiras têm lastro no código. 0 MUT-001 A mutação de ceticismo (reintroduzir "No LICENSE file is present" só na cópia descartável) foi detectada corretamente pelas camadas Unit e E2E; o script de aceite reporta sucesso EM DETECTAR a mutação. 1 (rotulado AUR-445/AC-001/behavior-missing) AC-001 sobre uma árvore não corrigida (RED), ou MUT-001 sem o marcador AUR445_MUTATION Uma frase falsa sobrevive, ou uma afirmação verdadeira não tem lastro. 1 (rotulado AUR-445/AC-001/MUT-001) Dentro da invocação MUT-001 A camada (Unit ou E2E) recusou a cópia mutada, como esperado; capturado e verificado pelo próprio script de aceite antes de reportar sucesso. 64 Seletor desconhecido (erro de uso do script). 69 Falha de infraestrutura (ex.: go ausente do PATH), nunca contada como aceite.

docs.title: Exemplo executável, sem segredo
docs.text:
cd /caminho/para/AurumCode
ulimit -v 8388608
GOMEMLIMIT=2GiB GOFLAGS='-mod=mod -p=1' bash tests/acceptance/AUR-445.sh AC-001
echo "exit: $?"

Saída esperada em GREEN: uma linha JSON {"card":"AUR-445","scenario":"AC-001","result":"pass",...} e exit 0.

docs.title: Diagnóstico de falha
docs.text:
• AUR-445/AC-001/behavior-missing:<arquivo>:<família> — a família de frase falsa nomeada ainda aparece (após normalização) no arquivo nomeado; releia a seção correspondente deste spec e a auditoria original no card.
  • AUR-445/AC-001/behavior-missing:integration:<claim> — a checagem cruzada contra o código (LICENSE, package main, ausência de gomarkdoc/os/exec no extrator Go, ou uma flag citada mas não registrada) falhou; o código mudou sem a documentação acompanhar, ou vice-versa.
  • AUR-445/AC-001/MUT-001 — esperado apenas durante a própria execução da mutação de ceticismo; fora dela, indica que a frase banida voltou a aparecer em README.md, ACTION_USAGE.md ou CHANGELOG.md.
  • Exit 69 — infraestrutura (Go ausente, mktemp falhou); nunca conta como prova de comportamento.

docs.title: Nota sobre os nomes dos seletores no card
docs.text: A seção "TDD proof" do card nomeia os seletores TestAUR428, IntegrationAUR428 e E2EAUR428 — resíduo do template copiado de AUR-428 (mesmo office, mesmo formato de card). Esses símbolos já existem em tests/unit/AUR-428.go e tests/integration/AUR-428.go, no mesmo pacote (unit, integration); declará-los de novo em tests/unit/AUR-445.go / tests/integration/AUR-445.go colidiria e quebraria go build ./.... Este card usa os nomes correspondentes ao seu próprio ID — TestAUR445, IntegrationAUR445, E2EAUR445 — mantendo o mesmo padrão de nomenclatura (prefixo TestAUR<NNN>) que todo outro card do office já segue.

docs.title: AUR-446 — Os specs entregues descrevem o comportamento entregue
docs.text: Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

docs.title: Outcome
docs.text: Cada spec de card entregue descreve o que o codigo faz hoje, e nao o estado do dia em que foi escrito. Este card corrige seis afirmacoes desatualizadas medidas na auditoria de 2026-08-13 e entrega o mecanismo que prova que elas continuam corrigidas: uma verificacao estatica, offline, por grep -F sobre o texto literal dos specs corrigidos.

docs.title: O comando
docs.text:
bash tests/acceptance/AUR-446.sh AC-001

Dentro do profile pinado bootstrap-readonly-v1, o mesmo comando roda via:

./.board/bin/oci-run --profile bootstrap-readonly-v1 --card AUR-446

O comando nao aceita entrada de rede nem chamada de modelo: e uma verificacao puramente textual sobre arquivos ja materializados por paths/read_paths.

docs.title: O que o comando verifica
docs.text:
Para cada um dos seis specs corrigidos, o comando confirma, por grep -F (correspondencia literal, nao regex), que:

  1. A afirmacao desatualizada (ancora negativa) esta ausente do arquivo.
  2. A afirmacao corrigida (ancora positiva) esta presente no arquivo.
Spec Afirmacao desatualizada removida Afirmacao corrigida docs/specs/AUR-424.md "Dentro do sandbox ela sai 69" (E2E sempre sai 69 por paths fora do contrato) "O accept selado sai 0" (paths/read_paths foram ampliados; o card esta done) docs/specs/AUR-425.md "No aurumcode docs subcommand exists" "subcommand delivered by AUR-426 (cmd/aurumcode/docs.go...)" docs/specs/AUR-428.md "Os demais exemplos ... (code-review, qa-testing, all-pipelines) continuam pinados por SHA" "code-review.yml não está mais nesse grupo: o AUR-440 o repinou para a tag v1" docs/specs/AUR-429.md "No aurumcode docs subcommand exists" "docs subcommand from AUR-426 (cmd/aurumcode/docs.go)" docs/specs/AUR-437.md (nenhuma ancora negativa; a afirmacao original nao era falsa, so incompleta) "Reproduzido em internal/git/githubclient/client.go:795-802" (caso residual do ultimo " b/" documentado) docs/specs/AUR-440.md "pelo AUR-437 e ainda nao foi executado" "AUR-438 esta done: cmd/aurumcode ja publica --pr, --repo, --publicar e --na-linha"

A correcao de docs/specs/AUR-437.md nao remove nenhuma afirmacao (a descricao original do defeito 4 e da correcao continuam verdadeiras para o caso que ela cobre); ela acrescenta a divulgacao do caso residual que a correcao nao fecha. Por isso essa linha nao tem ancora negativa: o comando so verifica a presenca da ancora positiva para este spec.

O caso residual de AUR-437.md e verificado de duas formas independentes: por ancora textual (grep -F) e por comportamento real, atraves da API publica de internal/git/githubclient (TestAUR446 em tests/unit/AUR-446.go), que prova empiricamente que extractFilePath("diff --git a/foo b/bar.go b/foo b/bar.go") retorna "bar.go" em vez de "foo b/bar.go" — nao apenas que a prosa do spec diz isso.

docs.title: Sexto achado, incorporado apos reparo de paths: docs/specs/AUR-428.md
docs.text:
A auditoria original (achado 5) tambem cobre docs/specs/AUR-428.md:123-125, que afirmava que os "demais exemplos" (code-review.yml incluido) "continuam pinados por SHA" — falso para code-review.yml desde o AUR-440, que o repinou para a tag v1 (ref: v1 no passo "Checkout the AurumCode release" de .github/workflows/examples/code-review.yml); ainda verdadeiro para qa-testing.yml e all-pipelines.yml, que continuam pinados por SHA 6f584b5987c12399bc7a85571dad4a81e28005c8.

Na primeira passagem deste card, docs/specs/AUR-428.md ficou fora do escopo gravavel: nem paths nem read_paths do card AUR-446 (frontmatter em .board/cards/ready/AUR-446.md) listavam esse arquivo — paths listava docs/specs/AUR-446.md duas vezes em vez de uma vez AUR-428.md e uma vez AUR-446.md. Esse gap foi relatado em vez de contornado silenciosamente (o mesmo padrao que docs/specs/AUR-424.md documenta para o candidato original do AUR-424), o coordenador corrigiu o frontmatter do card para listar docs/specs/AUR-428.md e a duplicata sumiu, e a correcao real agora vive em docs/specs/AUR-428.md, seção "Fora de escopo / notas" — nao mais nesta seção.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Rotulos exatos, tal como os quatro arquivos (tests/acceptance/AUR-446.sh, tests/e2e/AUR-446.sh, tests/unit/AUR-446.go, tests/integration/AUR-446.go) realmente emitem — nao uma paráfrase:

Exit Significado Rotulo(s) exatos 0 As cinco verificacoes passam nas tres lanes (Unit, Integration, E2E). {"result":"pass",...} 1 Ancora positiva ausente (a afirmacao corrigida nao esta no spec). AUR-446/AC-001/behavior-missing:<spec>:missing:<ancora> (E2E e Go); AUR-446/AC-001/entrypoint_missing:<path> (arquivo deste card ausente, checado por tests/acceptance/AUR-446.sh antes de estagiar) 1 MUT-001: ancora negativa (afirmacao desatualizada) foi reintroduzida. AUR-446/AC-001/MUT-001/<spec>:stale-claim-present:<ancora> (E2E); AUR-446/AC-001/MUT-001:<spec>:stale-claim-present:<ancora> (Go, dois-pontos em vez de barra) 1 Saida nao-deterministica entre as duas passagens do E2E. AUR-446/AC-001/nondeterministic-output:<digest1>:<digest2> 1 Uma lane Go falhou por um motivo que o grep de detalhe do orquestrador nao capturou. AUR-446/AC-001/selector-exit:<pacote>:<rc> 64 Seletor desconhecido. AUR-446/AC-001/unknown-selector 79 Infraestrutura: go, tr, grep ou sha256sum ausente, ou um dos read_paths (cmd/aurumcode, internal/git/githubclient, .github/workflows/examples/code-review.yml) nao esta materializado — nunca uma aprovacao nem uma reprovacao comportamental. AUR-446/AC-001/infrastructure/<motivo> (missing_go, missing_tr, missing_grep, missing_sha256sum, read_path_not_materialized:<path>, repo_root)

docs.title: Exemplo executavel (sem segredo)
docs.text:
$ bash tests/acceptance/AUR-446.sh AC-001
...
{"card":"AUR-446","scenario":"AC-001","result":"pass","specs_checked":5,"anchors_verified":9}

Nenhuma variavel de ambiente com segredo e lida por este comando; ele nao abre socket nem faz chamada de rede.

docs.title: Diagnostico de falha
docs.text:
• AUR-446/AC-001/MUT-001/docs/specs/AUR-425.md:stale-claim-present:... (ou AUR-429.md): a ancora negativa No \aurumcode docs` subcommand exists:` voltou a aparecer no arquivo — este e exatamente o MUT-001 deste card.
  • AUR-446/AC-001/behavior-missing:docs/specs/AUR-424.md:missing:...: a ancora positiva O accept selado sai **0** sumiu do arquivo.
  • AUR-446/AC-001/MUT-001/docs/specs/AUR-424.md:...: a ancora negativa Dentro do sandbox ela sai 69 voltou.
  • AUR-446/AC-001/behavior-missing:docs/specs/AUR-437.md:missing:...: a ancora internal/git/githubclient/client.go:795-802 sumiu do spec.
  • A subtest Go AUR-437 residual...truncation is real code behaviour falha sem nenhum rotulo behavior-missing de spec: o proprio codigo parou de reproduzir o truncamento (extractFilePath foi corrigido para o caso residual) — nesse caso a divulgacao do caso residual em AUR-437.md passou a superclamar um bug que nao existe mais, e precisa ser corrigida na direcao oposta.
  • AUR-446/AC-001/behavior-missing:docs/specs/AUR-440.md:missing:...: a ancora positiva AUR-438 esta done: \cmd/aurumcode` ja publica` sumiu.
  • AUR-446/AC-001/MUT-001/docs/specs/AUR-440.md:...: a ancora negativa restaurado pelo AUR-437 e ainda nao foi executado voltou.
  • exit 79 com rotulo infrastructure/read_path_not_materialized:<dir>: cmd/aurumcode, internal/git/githubclient ou .github/workflows/examples/code-review.yml nao esta presente no checkout — nunca tratado como reprovacao comportamental.
  • exit 79 com rotulo infrastructure/missing_tr (ou missing_grep, missing_sha256sum, missing_go): uma ferramenta que o script depende esta ausente do PATH. Checado explicitamente antes de qualquer verificacao para nao colapsar em falso RED sob set -euo pipefail.
  • exit 1 com rotulo AUR-446/AC-001/nondeterministic-output:<d1>:<d2>: as duas passagens de tests/e2e/AUR-446.sh sobre os mesmos arquivos reais produziram transcritos diferentes — a clausula de repeticao do AC-001 falhou.

docs.title: TDD proof
docs.text:
• Test: tests/acceptance/AUR-446.sh::AC-001.
  • Red: antes das correcoes acima, docs/specs/AUR-425.md e docs/specs/AUR-429.md continham No \aurumcode docs` subcommand exists:(ancora negativa presente) e nenhum dos cinco specs continha sua ancora positiva correspondente; o aceite falhava emitindo, para cada spec, tantoAUR-446/AC-001/MUT-001/:stale-claim-present:...(ancora negativa presente) quantoAUR-446/AC-001/behavior-missing::missing:...(ancora positiva ausente) — reproduzido diretamente restaurandodocs/specs/AUR-425.mda partir degit show HEAD:docs/specs/AUR-425.md(a versao pre-correcao) e rodandotests/acceptance/AUR-446.sh AC-001` sobre ela antes deste card ser aceito. Falha de compilacao, imagem, loader ou rede nao conta como RED.
  • Green: as edicoes de prosa acima em docs/specs/AUR-424.md, docs/specs/AUR-425.md, docs/specs/AUR-429.md, docs/specs/AUR-437.md e docs/specs/AUR-440.md.
  • Refactor: preservar as ancoras exatas, os exit codes e o formato de saida.
  • Unit: tests/unit/AUR-446.go::TestAUR446.
  • Contract: not-applicable — nenhum port novo e publicado.
  • Integration: tests/integration/AUR-446.go::IntegrationAUR446.
  • E2E: tests/e2e/AUR-446.sh::E2EAUR446.

    • Nota de nomenclatura: o card .board/cards/ready/AUR-446.md cita os seletores TestAUR428/IntegrationAUR428/E2EAUR428 na clausula "TDD proof" — um residuo de copia do template de AUR-428 (a mesma origem do titulo duplicado de AC-001 e da duplicata docs/specs/AUR-446.md em paths). Todo tests/unit/AUR-*.go existente neste repositorio nomeia sua funcao apos o proprio numero do card, sem excecao (verificado por varredura completa de tests/unit/AUR-4*.go); este card segue essa convencao (TestAUR446/IntegrationAUR446/E2EAUR446) e tests/acceptance/AUR-446.sh aceita TestAUR428/IntegrationAUR428/E2EAUR428 como aliases do seletor para quem invocar com o nome literal do card.

docs.title: Security and privacy
docs.text:
• Data flow: repositorio -> grep -F sobre arquivos ja materializados -> saida sanitizada de uma linha.
  • Secrets: o canario AURUM_SECRET_CANARY nao aparece em stdout, stderr, cache ou evidencia; nenhum passo le variavel de ambiente com segredo.
  • Least privilege: nenhum processo externo e iniciado alem de go test (para as lanes Unit/Integration) e grep; rede, socket, mounts de host, devices e capabilities permanecem negados pelo profile.

docs.title: Compatibility, migration, rollback
docs.text:
• Compatibility: nenhum comando ou formato ja publicado por outro card muda.
  • Migration: not-applicable.
  • Rollback: reverter somente os arquivos em paths; nenhum estado externo e publicado por este card.

docs.title: AUR-447 — aurumcode docs documents Rust and C# like the pipeline already does
docs.text:
Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

aurumcode docs --source <projeto Rust ou C#> generates real documentation pages the same way cmd/regenerate-docs already does. Command syntax, flags, defaults and exit codes are unchanged from docs/specs/AUR-426.md; this card fixes what languages the CLI's copy of the registration list covers.

docs.title: Achado (revisao do AUR-427)
docs.text:
Before this card, cmd/aurumcode/docs.go carried its own registerDocsExtractors that predated AUR-427 and was never updated when AUR-427 gave cmd/regenerate-docs native, tool-free Rust and C# extractors. A reviewer reproduced the defect directly:

$ aurumcode docs --source ./tests/fixtures/docs/rustproject --output /tmp/site
aurumcode docs: documentation extraction produced no documentation: 1 source
files, 0 processed, 0 docs generated, 0 error(s), 1 language(s) skipped
{skipped: rust: no extractor registered [1 file(s)]}
$ echo $?
1

while cmd/regenerate-docs (AURUMCODE_SOURCE_DIR=... AURUMCODE_OUTPUT_DIR=... go run ./cmd/regenerate-docs) documented the same tree correctly, because its own registerLanguageExtractors already registered internal/documentation/extractors/rust.NewNativeExtractor() and .../csharp.NewNativeExtractor() by default (AUR-427).

docs.title: Fix
docs.text: cmd/aurumcode/docs.go's registerDocsExtractors now registers the same two native extractors, reused unmodified from internal/documentation/ extractors/rust and .../csharp — no extraction logic is reimplemented. The CLI's registered language set is now: Go, JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, C++, Rust, C#, Bash, PowerShell — the exact set cmd/regenerate-docs registers by default (its opt-in AURUMCODE_ALLOW_REPO_CODE_EXECUTION toolchain left off).

docs.title: Achado e desenho: por que isto nao virou um registro unico compartilhado
docs.text:
The ideal fix is a single function both cmd/aurumcode and cmd/regenerate-docs call, so a future new language extractor can never be added to one binary's list and forgotten in the other's — exactly the defect this card fixes. That requires two things neither of which fits inside this card's paths:

  1. A home for the shared function. cmd/regenerate-docs's registerLanguageExtractors and cmd/aurumcode's (former) registerDocsExtractors are each defined in a package main — Go does not allow importing a main package, from either direction. A shared function has to live in an importable package, which here means internal/pipeline or internal/documentation.
  2. cmd/regenerate-docs/main.go calling it. Creating the shared function alone does not unify anything: cmd/regenerate-docs would keep using its own inline list unless its main.go is rewritten to call the new function instead.

Both are outside this card's paths (cmd/aurumcode, the declared test files, and this document only; cmd/regenerate-docs and internal/pipeline are read_paths, not writable). Rewriting cmd/regenerate-docs is also explicitly out of scope on its own terms — this card's Non-goals state "Reescrever pacote existente que ja cumpre a funcao; este card integra o que existe em vez de recriar", and cmd/regenerate-docs already documents Rust and C# correctly; it is not the package with the defect.

What this card does instead: cmd/aurumcode/docs.go's registerDocsExtractors is written to register, extractor-for-extractor, the exact same default set cmd/regenerate-docs's registerLanguageExtractors registers (its second, opt-in AURUMCODE_ALLOW_REPO_CODE_EXECUTION path stays cmd/regenerate-docs-only, since that logic lives inside its unimportable main package and executes code from the documented repository — wiring it a second time here is outside what this card's --help promises, same boundary docs/specs/AUR-426.md already drew). Both functions now import and call the identical extractor constructors (rustExtractor.NewNativeExtractor(), csharpExtractor.NewNativeExtractor(), and every other extractor already shared before this card) from the single place those constructors are actually defined (internal/documentation/extractors/*) — no extraction logic is duplicated, only the two short registration call lists remain separately maintained. The residual risk is the literal one this card's own root cause demonstrates: a language added to one list in the future and not mirrored in the other. Closing that risk structurally is a follow-up card whose paths would need to include internal/pipeline (or internal/documentation) and cmd/regenerate-docs.

docs.title: What is intentionally out of scope
docs.text:
Unchanged from docs/specs/AUR-426.md, with the Rust/C# line corrected:

  • Welcome-page LLM generation and Jekyll-build validation are not wired into this subcommand.
  • The repository-code-executing Rust/C# toolchain (cmd/regenerate-docs's cargo/dotnet-backed RustExtractor/ CSharpExtractor, opt-in via AURUMCODE_ALLOW_REPO_CODE_EXECUTION) is not wired into this subcommand. Only the native, tool-free extractors are — see "Achado e desenho" above for why that boundary cannot move inside this card's paths.
  • --incremental, --docs-dir, --base-url and the other cmd/regenerate-docs knobs are not exposed as flags.

docs/specs/AUR-426.md's own "What is intentionally out of scope" section still says "Rust and C# extractors are not registered here" — that line is superseded by this card. docs/specs/AUR-426.md sits outside this card's paths, so it is not edited here; this document is the current, accurate statement of what aurumcode docs registers.

docs.title: Command and exit codes
docs.text:
Unchanged from docs/specs/AUR-426.md:

aurumcode docs [--source <dir>] [--output <dir>] [--languages <list>]
aurumcode docs --help
Code Meaning 0 --help was requested: usage printed to stdout. 0 Documentation was generated: at least one page exists on disk after the run. 1 --source does not exist or is not a directory. 1 The pipeline failed outright. 1 The run produced zero documentation pages — aurumcode docs: no documentation page was generated on stderr. 2 Usage error: an unknown flag or a value a flag cannot parse.

docs.title: Example (no secrets)
docs.text:
$ aurumcode docs --source ./tests/fixtures/docs/rustproject --output /tmp/rust-site
Generated 1 documentation page(s) in /tmp/rust-site:
  - /tmp/rust-site/rust/src__lib.md
$ echo $?
0
$ grep -F 'pub struct Entry' /tmp/rust-site/rust/src__lib.md
### struct pub struct Entry

The same fixture, run through cmd/regenerate-docs (AURUMCODE_SOURCE_DIR=./tests/fixtures/docs/rustproject AURUMCODE_OUTPUT_DIR=/tmp/rust-site2 go run ./cmd/regenerate-docs), writes the same rust/src__lib.md page with the same real symbols, because both callers now drive the same set of registered extractors against the same internal/pipeline engine.

No environment variable carrying a secret is read by this command path, same as before this card. A path derived from --source/--output (or from an extractor's underlying error) is passed through the AUR-009/AUR-432 redaction filter before it reaches stdout or stderr.

docs.title: Failure diagnosis
docs.text: Unchanged from docs/specs/AUR-426.md, except the "nothing any registered extractor recognizes" example: a Rust-only or C#-only project is now documented, not one of the causes of a zero-page run. The remaining causes (a --languages name with the wrong case or spelling; a filter matching nothing present in --source; a source tree with no file any registered extractor recognizes at all, e.g. Java-only) are unchanged.

docs.title: MUT-001 note
docs.text: The skeptical mutation flips cmd/aurumcode/docs.go's registerNativeRustAndCSharp constant from true to false, keeping both rustExtractor.NewNativeExtractor() and csharpExtractor.NewNativeExtractor() referenced in source (so the mutant still compiles — a compile break is explicitly disqualified as RED/mutation evidence by this card's TDD proof, the same constraint AUR-427's own MUT-001 solved this way) while skipping both registrations at runtime. Run against the card's own Rust fixture, the mutant reproduces the exact defect this card fixes: exit non-zero, "no extractor registered", zero Rust pages. tests/unit/AUR-447.go's Rust-generation subtest independently catches the same mutation when rebuilt against the mutated tree.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
• aurumcode review in every form AUR-430/431/435/436/438 published is byte-for-byte unchanged; this card's only edits are inside cmd/aurumcode/docs.go's extractor registration and its package documentation.
  • aurumcode docs's flags, defaults, --help text and exit codes (docs/specs/AUR-426.md) are unchanged. Only the set of languages a --source tree can be documented in grows, from seven to nine.
  • cmd/regenerate-docs is untouched by this card (outside paths) and keeps generating documentation exactly as before.

docs.title: AUR-448 — no discard is silent
docs.text:
Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

Card AUR-448 closes a confidently-wrong-answer defect in aurumcode review: a user who followed the no-provider-configured message literally could get No issues found. with exit 0 for a fixture that actually planted a finding, because the message's example shape omitted rule_id, which the AUR-434 rule gate (internal/review.enforceRuleCitations) requires. Two fixes, both required:

  1. The no-provider message now shows the complete fixture shape the engine accepts, rule_id included, with a real id from the embedded catalog as the example.
  2. When the rule gate discards one or more findings, the command names how many and why on stderr. It never happens silently again.

docs.title: Command
docs.text:
aurumcode review --base <ref>

Unchanged from AUR-430/AUR-434 (see docs/specs/AUR-430.md and docs/specs/AUR-434.md): diffs <ref> against HEAD, sends the diff to the configured LLM provider, prints the findings. No new flags.

docs.title: 1. The no-provider message shows the complete fixture shape
docs.text:
Before this card (selectProvider, cmd/aurumcode/main.go):

no LLM provider configured: set AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE=<path> to a JSON file
shaped like {"issues":[{"file":"<path>","line":<n>,"severity":"error|warning|info","message":"<text>"}]}
for offline use (see tests/fixtures/review/known-problem-response.json for
a worked example), or set LLM_API_KEY and LLM_BASE_URL for a live provider

A user who builds a fixture from exactly that shape gets a finding with no rule_id. The rule gate discards it, and — before this card's second fix — aurumcode review printed No issues found., exit 0: the code looked clean when it was not. The referenced example file also does not exist outside this repository's own checkout, so a user running the released binary elsewhere could not open it either.

After this card:

no LLM provider configured: set AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE=<path> to a JSON file
shaped like {"issues":[{"file":"<path>","line":<n>,"severity":"error|warning|info",
"rule_id":"<id from the embedded rule catalog, e.g. security/hardcoded-secret>",
"message":"<text>"}]} for offline use -- a finding whose rule_id is missing
or unknown is discarded, never shown, so rule_id is not optional -- if you
have the AurumCode source checked out, tests/fixtures/review/known-problem-
response.json is a worked example -- or set LLM_API_KEY and LLM_BASE_URL
for a live provider

(wrapped here for readability; the command prints it as one line).

  • rule_id is shown with a real id from the embedded catalog (security/hardcoded-secret, internal/review/rules/security.yml), not a placeholder, so copying it verbatim into a fixture works.
  • The message explains, inline, why rule_id matters: a finding without one is discarded, never shown. A reader does not need to already know about the rule gate to avoid the trap.
  • The example-file pointer is explicitly conditional ("if you have the AurumCode source checked out"): the message is self-sufficient without it, because the file it names is not guaranteed to exist in the environment where the released binary runs. This wording keeps the pointer (still useful to a contributor working in this checkout) without making it load-bearing for anyone else — see AUR-443's tests/acceptance/AUR-443.sh (no-provider-missing-fixture-pointer), which still asserts the literal path substring is present in this message and continues to pass unmodified.

reportModelUnavailable (the --modelo <name> unavailable message, cmd/aurumcode/main.go) is a distinct message, reachable only when --modelo is given. It already points at the same fixture file and was not part of this card's measured defect (the achado's repro is aurumcode review --base HEAD~1, no --modelo); this card's Non-goals excludes behavior the declared command cannot observe, so it is left unchanged. Recorded here, not silently skipped.

docs.title: 2. A discard is never silent
docs.text:
internal/review.enforceRuleCitations (AUR-434) already discarded a finding whose rule_id was missing or unknown before this card; that gate is unchanged. What is new is discardSummary and formatDiscardWarning (internal/review/reviewer.go): GenerateReview now tallies why each discard happened (a missing rule_id, an unknown one, or both, naming the distinct unknown ids) and stores the rendered one-line explanation in result.Metadata["discard_warning"], "" when nothing was discarded.

cmd/aurumcode's runReview prints that string to stderr, verbatim, prefixed like every other canonical stderr line here ("aurumcode review: %s\n"), immediately after the review runs and before any finding prints:

aurumcode review: 2 finding(s) discarded: 1 with no rule_id, 1 citing an unknown rule_id (security/definitely-not-a-rule)

Singular case:

aurumcode review: 1 finding(s) discarded: 1 with no rule_id

stdout is byte-identical to the published AUR-434/AUR-426 contract in every case. The discard already hid the finding from stdout before this card (that gate is unchanged); this card only adds the stderr explanation. When every reported finding is discarded, stdout is still exactly No issues found. — now with the reason on stderr instead of nothing.

When rejected == 0 (every finding the model reported cited a resolvable rule, or the model reported none), discard_warning is "" and the if warning != "" guard in runReview never executes: stderr receives zero additional bytes. This is the byte-identical happy path tests/acceptance/AUR-448.sh's nominal_case measures directly against the unmodified known-problem-response.json fixture (one grounded finding, zero discards) before asserting anything about the discard case.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Unchanged from AUR-430/AUR-434:

Exit Meaning 0 Review completed (with or without surviving findings, with or without a discard). 1 Runtime failure: not a git repository, diff failure, no provider configured, unparseable model response, broken embedded rules catalog. 2 Usage error (unknown command, missing --base).

Discarding a finding, with or without the new stderr warning, never changes the exit code by itself — exactly like AUR-434's own gate. (The independent --fail-on gate, AUR-431, still evaluates the surviving findings; a discarded finding never participates in it, unchanged.)

docs.title: Offline, secret-free example
docs.text:
cd tests/fixtures/repos/git-demo/repo.git
cat > /tmp/mixed.json <<'EOF'
{
  "issues": [
    {"file": "config/demo-tokens.txt", "line": 3, "severity": "error",
     "rule_id": "security/hardcoded-secret", "message": "grounded finding"},
    {"file": "config/demo-tokens.txt", "line": 4, "severity": "error",
     "message": "no rule_id at all"},
    {"file": "config/demo-tokens.txt", "line": 5, "severity": "warning",
     "rule_id": "security/definitely-not-a-rule", "message": "unknown rule_id"}
  ],
  "summary": "example for docs/specs/AUR-448.md"
}
EOF
AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE=/tmp/mixed.json aurumcode review --base HEAD~1

stdout:

config/demo-tokens.txt:3: [error] grounded finding (rule security/hardcoded-secret: Hardcoded Secrets)

stderr:

aurumcode review: 2 finding(s) discarded: 1 with no rule_id, 1 citing an unknown rule_id (security/definitely-not-a-rule)

docs.title: Diagnosing a failure
docs.text:
Symptom Likely cause No issues found. with a stderr line starting aurumcode review: N finding(s) discarded: ... The model reported N finding(s) this run, and every one of them failed the rule gate (missing or unknown rule_id). This is the exact case that used to be indistinguishable from "the code is clean" — read the stderr line, then either fix the fixture/model output's rule_id or, for a real provider, check that it is following the review prompt's schema. No issues found. with no stderr discard line The model genuinely reported zero findings this run. Nothing was discarded. A finding you expected does not print, but stderr names it discarded Same cause as AUR-434's own table: the rule_id it cited is missing or not in the embedded catalog (internal/review/rules/*.yml). no LLM provider configured: ... No AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE, LLM_API_KEY+LLM_BASE_URL configured. The message shows the complete fixture shape, rule_id included, with a real catalog id as the example.

For everything else (repository backends, provider selection, parser fallback, diff limits, --modelo, --limite, --seguranca, --pr, --check, the review cache) see docs/specs/AUR-430.md and the other cards' specs it and this file cross-reference.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• result.Metadata["discard_warning"] is built entirely from data already redacted at the model boundary: enforceRuleCitations runs strictly after redactReviewResult in GenerateReview (see reviewer.go's own ordering note), so every RuleID the discard message can quote was already passed through the single AUR-009 redaction filter before this card's code ever reads it. The discard warning line also passes through cmd/aurumcode's errW (the AUR-432 redaction writer wrapping stderr) like every other canonical stderr line.
  • The AURUM_SECRET_CANARY value never appears in the discard warning: it is built only from counts and already-redacted rule ids, never from a finding's Message, File, or Suggestion.

docs.title: A note on this card's own TDD-proof identifiers
docs.text: The card's TDD proof section names the unit/integration/e2e selectors TestAUR435 / IntegrationAUR435 / E2EAUR435. tests/unit/AUR-435.go and tests/integration/AUR-435.go already declare functions with exactly those names, in the same unit/integration packages every card's bridge test shares — reusing them here would be a duplicate-symbol compile error, not a naming preference. This is a numeral copy artifact in the card text, not an instruction this card can satisfy literally without breaking the build. tests/unit/AUR-448.go, tests/integration/AUR-448.go, and tests/e2e/AUR-448.sh instead declare TestAUR448 / IntegrationAUR448 / E2EAUR448, following the same numeral-matches-file convention every sibling card in this office already uses (TestAUR434, TestAUR443, ...). The acceptance program (tests/acceptance/AUR-448.sh) still answers to the selectors AC-001, TestAUR448, IntegrationAUR448, E2EAUR448, and AC-001-MUT-001, and still proves exactly what the TDD proof section describes in prose (Unit/Integration/E2E layers plus the mutation).

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
ulimit -v 8388608
GOMEMLIMIT=2GiB GOFLAGS='-mod=mod -p=1' bash tests/acceptance/AUR-448.sh

./.board/bin/oci-run --profile bootstrap-readonly-v1 --card AUR-448 runs the same program inside the sealed, read-only, network-denied profile.

docs.title: AUR-449 — aurumcode review --seguranca: the deterministic pass runs without a provider
docs.text: Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

docs.title: Command
docs.text:
aurumcode review --base <ref> [--fail-on <level>] [--modelo <nome>] [--seguranca]

Same command AUR-435/AUR-442 published. This card does not add a flag or change the output shape of any path that already had a provider; it removes an artificial requirement from exactly one path: --seguranca alone, with no provider configured at all.

docs.title: The measured defect (2026-08-14 re-test)
docs.text: aurumcode review --base HEAD~1 --seguranca with no AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE and no LLM_API_KEY/LLM_BASE_URL exits 1 with no LLM provider configured — before the security pass ever runs. But that pass (internal/review.SecurityScan, restored by AUR-442) is a deterministic regex matcher over the diff's ADDED lines: it never calls a model. Requiring a provider for it was a barrier the pass's own implementation does not need — the product's only free, offline, deterministic path was locked behind the one thing that needs a credential.

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
When all three of the following hold, aurumcode review --base <ref> --seguranca now runs the security pass alone and reports its findings, instead of refusing outright:

  1. --seguranca was given.
  2. --modelo was not given. An explicit model choice is a specific request; the caller who makes it must still be told loudly when it cannot be served (reportModelUnavailable, unchanged — see docs/specs/AUR-436.md). Composing --modelo with --seguranca and no provider that serves the model is untouched: exit 1, the AUR-436 error.
  3. Provider selection failed with exactly "nothing is configured at all" — selectProvider's errNoProviderConfigured sentinel, not any other provider failure. A caller who attempted configuration and got it wrong (an AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE path that does not exist, for example) is still told the review failed; that is a different, more specific defect than "nothing was configured," and silently downgrading it into "just run the security pass" would hide a real misconfiguration from the caller.

Combined with the quality review (no --seguranca, or a provider that IS configured), the provider requirement is completely untouched: this card changes nothing about the path that talks to a model.

When the skip engages, runReview (cmd/aurumcode/main.go) never constructs the orchestrator, the cost tracker, or the review cache — none of that machinery has anything to do when no call is ever made. The result carries no quality issues, and the quality section is not printed at all (see "Output shape" below): printing "No issues found." would assert something the tool never checked.

docs.title: Output shape
docs.text:
Without a provider, --seguranca given:

Security findings (standards/security-review):
config/demo-tokens.txt:4: [error] Hardcoded credentials or API keys detected [standards/security-review SCR-003] (rule security/hardcoded-secret: Hardcoded Secrets)
config/demo-tokens.txt:5: [error] Hardcoded credentials or API keys detected [standards/security-review SCR-003] (rule security/hardcoded-secret: Hardcoded Secrets)
config/demo-tokens.txt:6: [error] Hardcoded credentials or API keys detected [standards/security-review SCR-003] (rule security/hardcoded-secret: Hardcoded Secrets)

No quality block precedes it — not even "No issues found." — because no quality review ran. stderr carries the actionable explanation, printed before stdout, never silence:

aurumcode review: no LLM provider configured: quality review skipped, running --seguranca only (no LLM provider configured: set AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE=<path> to a JSON file shaped like {"issues":[{"file":"<path>","line":<n>,"severity":"error|warning|info","message":"<text>"}]} for offline use (see tests/fixtures/review/known-problem-response.json for a worked example), or set LLM_API_KEY and LLM_BASE_URL for a live provider)

Without a provider, --seguranca given, but nothing in the diff matches (e.g. --base HEAD against itself, an empty diff): the pass still ran and found nothing, so it prints the honest absence, not silence and not a claim it never ran:

Security findings (standards/security-review):
No security findings.

With a provider configured, --seguranca given: byte-identical to the AUR-442 contract — the quality block, then the security section, exactly as already published. Manually verified during this card's development: a binary built from the parent commit (before this card's change) and the candidate binary built from this card's tree both produce the exact same git-demo --seguranca stdout under AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE, sha256 63c649af1c90e38b473e1bd45b4152b1f96ecad17d5d9c05c17bb94df7b8240f (stderr empty on both sides). tests/acceptance/AUR-449.sh pins this exact hash as a regression guard.

Without --seguranca: byte-identical to the AUR-430 contract — this card touches nothing on that path; no LLM provider configured still refuses with exit 1 when no provider is set, exactly as before.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Unchanged from AUR-435/AUR-442 (docs/specs/AUR-435.md), with one addition:

Code Meaning 0 Review ran; gate (if any) open. New under this card: includes --seguranca alone with no provider configured — the security pass ran and its findings printed. 1 The review itself failed: no provider (when the quality review is actually needed — no --seguranca, or --seguranca with --modelo, or --seguranca with an attempted-but-broken provider configuration), unreadable repo, broken rules catalog, or an explicit --modelo that cannot be served. 2 Usage error (missing --base, unknown flag or level). 3 --fail-on gate closed. A matched security finding closes the gate even when no quality review ran at all — the gate composes with the skip exactly as it already composed with --seguranca (docs/specs/AUR-442.md).

docs.title: Offline, secret-free example
docs.text:
cd tests/fixtures/repos/git-demo/repo.git
unset AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE LLM_API_KEY LLM_BASE_URL
aurumcode review --base HEAD~1 --seguranca

prints, with exit 0:

Security findings (standards/security-review):
config/demo-tokens.txt:4: [error] Hardcoded credentials or API keys detected [standards/security-review SCR-003] (rule security/hardcoded-secret: Hardcoded Secrets)
config/demo-tokens.txt:5: [error] Hardcoded credentials or API keys detected [standards/security-review SCR-003] (rule security/hardcoded-secret: Hardcoded Secrets)
config/demo-tokens.txt:6: [error] Hardcoded credentials or API keys detected [standards/security-review SCR-003] (rule security/hardcoded-secret: Hardcoded Secrets)

and stderr says plainly why the quality block is absent — never silence:

aurumcode review: no LLM provider configured: quality review skipped, running --seguranca only (...)

docs.title: Failure diagnosis
docs.text:
• flag provided but not defined: -seguranca — the binary predates AUR-435; rebuild from source.
  • aurumcode review: no LLM provider configured: ... with exit 1 and no "quality review skipped" note — either --seguranca was not given, --modelo was given (an explicit model choice always fails loudly instead of falling back), or a provider WAS attempted and is broken (check the AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE path, or LLM_API_KEY / LLM_BASE_URL).
  • The security section says No security findings. but you expected a match — unrelated to this card: the pass's coverage is exactly what AUR-442 documents (docs/specs/AUR-442.md's "Failure diagnosis").
  • aurumcode review: review rules unavailable: ... — the embedded rules catalog is broken; fix internal/review/rules/ and rebuild.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• No new sink: the security pass's own output guarantees (trusted catalog text, never the matched diff body) are exactly AUR-442's; this card only changes when the pass is reached, not what it prints.
  • The AURUM_SECRET_CANARY value never reaches stdout, stderr, prompt, cache, or evidence on the skip path; tests/acceptance/AUR-449.sh asserts this.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
• review --base with a configured provider, with --modelo, or without --seguranca, is byte-identical to the already-published contract (tests/acceptance/AUR-442.sh, tests/acceptance/AUR-443.sh, tests/acceptance/AUR-433.sh, tests/acceptance/AUR-441.sh, tests/acceptance/AUR-436.sh all pass unchanged against this card's tree).
  • --fail-on's composition with security findings (docs/specs/AUR-442.md) is unaffected: it still gates on result.Issues plus securityFindings, and the latter is exactly what the skip path alone produces.
  • The review cache (AUR-441) is never consulted on the skip path — there is no model call for it to deduplicate.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
tests/acceptance/AUR-449.sh AC-001 (sealed: ./.board/bin/oci-run --profile bootstrap-readonly-v1 --card AUR-449), with selectors TestAUR449 (tests/unit/AUR-449.go), IntegrationAUR449 (tests/integration/AUR-449.go), E2EAUR449 (tests/e2e/AUR-449.sh) and AC-001-MUT-001 (reverting runReview's skip condition to always require a provider, which must make --seguranca alone fail again — the exact pre-AUR-449 defect).

Selector naming note (same technique tests/unit/AUR-442.go and tests/unit/AUR-445.go document): the card text's TDD proof section names TestAUR435 / IntegrationAUR435 / E2EAUR435, copy-paste artifacts from the AUR-435 card this one was drafted against. Those symbols already exist in their packages (tests/unit/AUR-435.go, tests/integration/AUR-435.go, and TestAUR442/IntegrationAUR442 already occupy the next-available names too) and would collide, so this card's proofs are TestAUR449 / IntegrationAUR449 / E2EAUR449 instead.

docs.title: AUR-450 — aurumcode review --seguranca: the pass names what it searched
docs.text: Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

docs.title: Command
docs.text:
aurumcode review --base <ref> [--fail-on <level>] [--modelo <nome>] [--seguranca]

Same command AUR-435/AUR-442/AUR-449 published. This card adds no flag and changes no byte of stdout; it adds one line to stderr, printed only when --seguranca runs.

docs.title: The measured defect (2026-08-14 re-test)
docs.text: Code carrying hashlib.md5(password) (security/weak-crypto) and "<b>" + name + "</b>" (security/xss) gets Security findings (standards/security-review): No security findings. with exit 0. Five of the embedded catalog's eight security-category rules are metadata only (internal/review/rules/security.yml) — AUR-442 gave three of them (sql-injection, command-injection, hardcoded-secret) a real matcher and documented, scoped reasons for leaving the other five patternless — but the CLI never says which rules ran. A user reads the silent No security findings. as full coverage. This is not a matcher false positive or false negative; it is the output omitting its own scope.

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
--seguranca now prints, on stderr, exactly one additional line: how many and which security-category rules of the embedded catalog actually carry a matcher, against how many the category declares in total. The figures are derived from the catalog at run time (internal/review.RulesLoader.AppliedInCategory, cmd/aurumcode/main.go's printSecurityCoverage), never a hand-written list — a list typed once into a doc or a stderr format string would silently go stale the next time a card adds, removes, or gives a rule a matcher (internal/review/rules/ security.yml's own pattern: field is the single source of truth; nothing here duplicates it). tests/acceptance/AUR-442.sh's own MUT-001 case (which removes security/hardcoded-secret's matcher) demonstrates the derivation empirically: rerun on this card's tree, the note recomputes to "2 of 8" without a single line of AUR-450 code changing.

The note prints before the findings are known and is catalog-derived, not diff-derived — it does not depend on what the reviewed diff contains. That is deliberate: the empty case ("No security findings.") and the non-empty case must carry the byte-identical note, because the defect this card fixes is specifically the empty case being misread as full coverage.

docs.title: Why stderr, not stdout
docs.text:
tests/acceptance/AUR-449.sh pins an exact sha256 of git-demo's --seguranca stdout with a configured provider (63c649af1c90e38b473e1bd45b4152b1f96ecad17d5d9c05c17bb94df7b8240f) as a regression guard. That pin is not this card's to break: internal/review and cmd/aurumcode are this card's paths, but the byte contract AUR-449 already published on that exact command is not a "format" this card is free to redefine — it is exactly the kind of already-published contract the card's own Compatibility section requires to stay inalterado. Any new byte on that pinned stdout — even a single trailing character — changes the hash and turns a passing sibling acceptance red for a reason unrelated to what AUR-449 actually tests.

This codebase already has an established idiom for exactly this situation — additive, caller-facing information that must not touch a byte-pinned stdout contract goes to stderr, prefixed aurumcode review:, the same sink and prefix AUR-433's cost lines, AUR-441's cache-reuse note, AUR-448's discard warning, and AUR-449's skip explanation already use. The coverage note follows that convention instead of inventing a new one. It is filter- identity under the AUR-432/AUR-009 redaction writer exactly like every other canonical stderr line this command publishes (pinned by cmd/aurumcode/redaction_wiring_test.go's TestStderrLinesSurviveTheRedactionWriter, which now includes this note verbatim) — the rule-id tokens it names (e.g. security/hardcoded-secret) never sit immediately before a bare :/= value, the shape the filter's secret-key rules require to trigger, so nothing in the note is ever rewritten or masked.

tests/acceptance/AUR-450.sh's nominal_case re-asserts the exact same AUR-449 stdout sha256, byte for byte, to prove this card's whole point: new information reaches the user without disturbing a single byte of a contract this card does not own.

docs.title: Output shape
docs.text:
--seguranca, no provider, findings present (git-demo, config/demo-tokens.txt plants three secrets AUR-442 already teaches the pass to find):

Security findings (standards/security-review):
config/demo-tokens.txt:4: [error] Hardcoded credentials or API keys detected [standards/security-review SCR-003] (rule security/hardcoded-secret: Hardcoded Secrets)
config/demo-tokens.txt:5: [error] Hardcoded credentials or API keys detected [standards/security-review SCR-003] (rule security/hardcoded-secret: Hardcoded Secrets)
config/demo-tokens.txt:6: [error] Hardcoded credentials or API keys detected [standards/security-review SCR-003] (rule security/hardcoded-secret: Hardcoded Secrets)

stderr (new under this card, printed before the findings are known):

aurumcode review: security pass applied 3 of 8 security rules (security/command-injection, security/hardcoded-secret, security/sql-injection); see internal/review/rules/security.yml for the full catalog

--seguranca, nothing matches (e.g. --base HEAD against itself, an empty diff): stdout prints the honest absence, exactly as AUR-449 already publishes it —

Security findings (standards/security-review):
No security findings.

— and stderr carries the byte-identical coverage note above: the figures are catalog-derived, not diff-derived, so the empty case can never be told apart from the non-empty case by looking at the note alone. That identity is exactly what stops "No security findings." from being misread as "the whole catalog ran."

--seguranca, a provider configured: stdout is unaffected — the exact AUR-442/AUR-449 contract, sha256-pinned by both tests/acceptance/AUR-449.sh and this card's own acceptance program — and the same coverage note appears on stderr.

Without --seguranca: no coverage note anywhere, on either stream — the note is scoped to the security pass, never printed on a plain quality review.

With --modelo unavailable: the command still fails loudly (reportModelUnavailable, AUR-436) before --seguranca is ever reached, so neither the security section nor the coverage note prints.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Unchanged from AUR-435/AUR-442/AUR-449 (docs/specs/AUR-449.md). This card adds no new exit code and changes no exit code's meaning; only stderr grows one line, and only when --seguranca runs.

docs.title: Offline, secret-free example
docs.text:
cd tests/fixtures/repos/git-demo/repo.git
unset AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE LLM_API_KEY LLM_BASE_URL
aurumcode review --base HEAD~1 --seguranca

prints, with exit 0, on stdout (unchanged from AUR-442/AUR-449):

Security findings (standards/security-review):
config/demo-tokens.txt:4: [error] Hardcoded credentials or API keys detected [standards/security-review SCR-003] (rule security/hardcoded-secret: Hardcoded Secrets)
config/demo-tokens.txt:5: [error] Hardcoded credentials or API keys detected [standards/security-review SCR-003] (rule security/hardcoded-secret: Hardcoded Secrets)
config/demo-tokens.txt:6: [error] Hardcoded credentials or API keys detected [standards/security-review SCR-003] (rule security/hardcoded-secret: Hardcoded Secrets)

and on stderr (the AUR-449 skip note, since no provider is configured, followed by this card's new coverage note):

aurumcode review: no LLM provider configured: quality review skipped, running --seguranca only (...)
aurumcode review: security pass applied 3 of 8 security rules (security/command-injection, security/hardcoded-secret, security/sql-injection); see internal/review/rules/security.yml for the full catalog

docs.title: Failure diagnosis
docs.text:
• The security section says No security findings. and you are unsure whether the pass actually looked for what you expected — check the coverage note on stderr: it names every rule the pass can match, by id, every single run. A rule not in that list is metadata only (internal/review/rules/security.yml has no pattern: for it) and will never fire regardless of what the diff contains — see docs/specs/AUR-442.md's "The decision" for why each of the five stayed patternless.
  • No coverage note anywhere — either --seguranca was not given, or an earlier failure (a broken rules catalog, an unavailable --modelo) stopped the command before the security pass was reached; check the exit code and the rest of stderr.
  • aurumcode review: review rules unavailable: ... — the embedded rules catalog is broken; fix internal/review/rules/ and rebuild. Both the findings and the coverage note come from the same catalog load, so this failure blocks both, before either prints anything.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• No new sink: the coverage note is trusted catalog text (rule ids, a literal count, a literal repository-relative path to the catalog file) — never diff content, never a matched value, never a secret. It is filter- identity under the redaction writer (see "Why stderr, not stdout" above).
  • The AURUM_SECRET_CANARY value never reaches stdout, stderr, prompt, cache, or evidence alongside the new note; tests/acceptance/AUR-450.sh asserts this.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
• review --base without --seguranca, with --modelo, or with a configured provider is byte-identical to the already-published contract on both stdout and stderr: tests/acceptance/AUR-442.sh, tests/acceptance/AUR-443.sh, tests/acceptance/AUR-448.sh, and tests/acceptance/AUR-449.sh all pass unchanged against this card's tree (re-verified, exit 0 each, as part of this card's own validation).
  • tests/acceptance/AUR-449.sh's exact stdout sha256 pin for --seguranca with a provider configured is re-asserted, unchanged, by this card's own tests/acceptance/AUR-450.sh.
  • --fail-on's gate composition (docs/specs/AUR-442.md) is unaffected: it still gates on result.Issues plus the security findings, which this card does not touch — only the coverage figures are new, and they never enter the gate.
  • The findings themselves — content and order — are exactly what securityScanWithRules already produced; SecurityScanWithCoverage (the new entry point cmd/aurumcode calls) computes them with the exact same unexported helper SecurityScan uses, so the two can never diverge. SecurityScan itself is untouched: tests/unit/AUR-435.go and tests/unit/AUR-442.go keep calling it with its original two-value signature.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
tests/acceptance/AUR-450.sh AC-001 (sealed: ./.board/bin/oci-run --profile bootstrap-readonly-v1 --card AUR-450), with selectors TestAUR450 (tests/unit/AUR-450.go), IntegrationAUR450 (tests/integration/AUR-450.go), E2EAUR450 (tests/e2e/AUR-450.sh) and AC-001-MUT-001 (silencing the coverage note's print call while leaving the security pass itself untouched, which must make the acceptance fail — internal/review.SecurityScanWithCoverage still returns the right figures; only cmd/aurumcode's print of them is suppressed).

Selector naming note (the same technique tests/unit/AUR-442.go and tests/unit/AUR-449.go document): the card text's TDD proof section names TestAUR435 / IntegrationAUR435 / E2EAUR435, copy-paste artifacts from the AUR-435 card this one was drafted against. Those symbols already exist in their packages (tests/unit/AUR-435.go, tests/integration/AUR-435.go) and TestAUR449/IntegrationAUR449 already occupy the next-available names too, so this card's proofs are TestAUR450 / IntegrationAUR450 / E2EAUR450 instead.

docs.title: AUR-451 — O review de pull request passa a usar o motor inteiro
docs.text: Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

docs.title: O defeito medido (revisao de produto 2026-08-14)
docs.text: cmd/aurumcode/pr.go nunca chamava SecurityScan, e das flags do comando so usava countAtOrAbove internamente para sustentar --check. No caminho de pull request -- o caso de uso principal do produto -- --seguranca/--fail-on/--limite/--modelo eram aceitas como flags mas nao faziam nada: sem varredura de seguranca, sem gate de severidade, sem teto de custo, sem escolha de modelo. O comentario do proprio pr.go declarava isso como Non-goal do card que o criou (AUR-438). Este card remove essa limitacao.

docs.title: O que este card entrega
docs.text:
aurumcode review --pr <numero> --repo <dono>/<projeto> --publicar --na-linha \
  [--seguranca] [--fail-on <nivel>] [--limite <usd>] [--modelo <nome>]

As quatro capacidades que ja funcionavam em --base agora valem em --pr, reutilizando exatamente as mesmas funcoes que o caminho --base ja chama (cmd/aurumcode/main.go, cmd/aurumcode/cost.go) -- nenhuma logica foi duplicada ou reimplementada:

  • --seguranca: roda review.SecurityScanWithCoverage sobre o diff do pull request -- o mesmo pacote/funcao que --base ja usa -- e imprime a mesma nota de cobertura do AUR-450 em stderr (security pass applied N of M security rules (...)). Cada achado de seguranca vira seu proprio comentario no pull request, publicado exatamente como um achado de qualidade: na linha exata quando o diff adicionou aquela linha, geral caso contrario (a classificacao do AUR-438, isInlineEligible, que este card nao altera). O comentario carrega a citacao da regra ((rule security/<id>: <titulo>)) porque Message ja chega assim de review.enforceRuleCitations -- nao ha uma secao separada como no relatorio stdout de --base, porque o formato de saida de --pr sempre foi "um comentario por achado", nao um relatorio de texto.
  • --fail-on <nivel>: apos a publicacao, o comando sai com o mesmo codigo distinto exitFindings (3) que --base ja usa quando algum achado publicado -- de qualidade ou de seguranca -- fica no limiar escolhido ou acima (severityRank/countAtOrAbove, inalterados). E independente do gate proprio de --check (grave-only, AUR-439): qualquer um dos dois fecha o portao sozinho.
  • --limite <usd>: o mesmo gate de custo do AUR-433 (internal/llm/cost.Tracker, buildCostTracker, fixedModelProvider) estima o custo antes de chamar o modelo e recusa -- sem gastar nada -- quando a estimativa excede o teto, reportando a estimativa e, em caso de sucesso, o custo real em stderr. A recusa acontece antes de qualquer comentario ser publicado.
  • --modelo <nome>: selectProviderForModel, o mesmo mecanismo de --base, escolhe o provider; quando o modelo pedido nao pode ser servido, reportModelUnavailable falha alto (exit 1), nunca um review vazio com exit 0.

Sem nenhuma das quatro flags novas, --pr e byte-identico ao contrato ja publicado pelo AUR-438/AUR-439 -- provado por sha256 contra um binario compilado do commit pai (antes deste card), nao so por leitura de codigo (ver "Prova de compatibilidade" abaixo).

docs.title: Ordem de validacao
docs.text: A validacao de --fail-on/--modelo/--limite acontece antes da checagem de permissao de escrita, da busca do diff e de qualquer chamada ao modelo -- a mesma ordem que --base ja segue, e pelo mesmo motivo: um nivel de --fail-on desconhecido, um --modelo vazio ou um --limite vazio/nao numerico e erro de uso (exit 2), nunca um gate silenciosamente desabilitado, e nunca vale a pena gastar uma chamada de rede para descobrir isso.

docs.title: Onde a seguranca entra na publicacao
docs.text: runPRReview combina result.Issues (achados de qualidade) com os achados de seguranca num unico slice antes de sortedIssues -- a mesma ordenacao (arquivo, linha) que ja rege a sequencia de publicacao do AUR-438. Um achado de qualidade e um achado de seguranca na mesma linha publicam dois comentarios distintos, nenhum e descartado nem mesclado no outro.

docs.title: Ordem de prioridade se o escopo precisasse ser cortado
docs.text:
O card declarou esta ordem de valor; todas as quatro foram entregues, mas fica registrada porque orientou o desenho:

  1. --seguranca com --pr (o caso de uso que vende o produto).
  2. --fail-on com --pr (o gate de CI passa a considerar severidade).
  3. --limite com --pr (nao gastar sem teto no caminho automatico).
  4. --modelo com --pr.

docs.title: Prova de compatibilidade (sha256 contra o binario do commit pai)
docs.text: Como parte da validacao deste card, o binario atual (cmd/aurumcode com este card integrado) e o binario compilado do commit pai (git show HEAD:cmd/aurumcode/{main,pr}.go, antes deste card) foram executados com o comando review --pr 42 --repo dono/projeto --publicar --na-linha -- sem nenhuma das quatro flags novas -- contra o mesmo fake GitHub e a mesma resposta de modelo deterministica. stdout e stderr sao byte a byte identicos entre os dois binarios (mesmo sha256), confirmando que o comando publicado antes deste card nao mudou nenhum byte.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Inalterados: o mesmo vocabulario que --base e --pr ja publicavam.

  • 0: os achados foram publicados (ou "No issues found."), sem erro, e (quando --fail-on foi dado) nenhum achado publicado atingiu o limiar.
  • 1: falha em tempo de execucao -- busca do diff, chamada ao modelo, recusa por falta de permissao de escrita, falha ao publicar um comentario especifico, --modelo indisponivel, ou --limite estourado (nada foi gasto).
  • 2: erro de uso -- inclui agora um --fail-on desconhecido, um --modelo vazio, ou um --limite vazio/nao numerico/nao positivo em --pr, exatamente como --base ja recusa.
  • 3 (exitFindings): pelo menos um achado publicado -- de qualidade ou de seguranca -- ficou no limiar de --fail-on ou acima. Novo neste card para o caminho de PR; o mesmo codigo que --check e --base ja usam para o mesmo significado.

docs.title: Exemplo executavel sem segredo
docs.text:
bash tests/e2e/AUR-451.sh E2EAUR451

Compila o binario real, sobe um fake GitHub em loopback a partir de tests/fixtures/scm/github/ (permissoes de leitura-escrita e so-leitura, resposta de comentario criado) servindo um diff que este script constroi -- tests/fixtures/scm/github/pr-42.diff e um read_path, nao editavel por este card, e nao contem nada que uma regra de seguranca do catalogo combine -- plantando API_KEY=AURUM-FAKE-KEY-9000-2222 (o mesmo valor sintetico que tests/unit/AUR-442.go ja prova bater com security/hardcoded-secret) na linha adicionada de cmdb/settings.go. Roda aurumcode review --pr 42 --repo dono/projeto --publicar --na-linha --seguranca --fail-on high contra ele. Prova: o achado plantado chega como comentario inline citando security/hardcoded-secret; o comando sai com 3; repetir a execucao produz a mesma saida; --seguranca sozinho (sem --fail-on) ainda publica o achado mas sai com 0; sem nenhuma flag nova o mesmo diff nao publica nada (No issues found., prova de que a correcao e aditiva); --limite 0.0001 recusa antes de qualquer publicacao; --modelo local sem provider configurado falha alto; um token so-leitura continua recusado antes de qualquer busca ou publicacao.

docs.title: Selectors e exit codes do aceite
docs.text:
• Aceite: tests/acceptance/AUR-451.sh -- selectors AC-001 (tudo), TestAUR451, IntegrationAUR451, E2EAUR451, AC-001-MUT-001.
  • Exit codes (convencao do board, tests/acceptance/EXIT_CODE_CONVENTION.md): 0 comportamento provado; 1 RED comportamental; 64 selector desconhecido; 79 infraestrutura / inconclusivo (nunca evidencia de RED).

Nota de nomenclatura de selector (a mesma tecnica que tests/unit/AUR-442.go, tests/unit/AUR-449.go e tests/unit/AUR-450.go ja documentam): o texto do card nomeia TestAUR435/IntegrationAUR435/E2EAUR435 na secao TDD proof, um artefato de copia-e-cola do card AUR-435 usado como base de redacao. Esses simbolos ja existem em seus pacotes (tests/unit/AUR-435.go, tests/integration/AUR-435.go), entao as provas deste card sao TestAUR451/IntegrationAUR451/E2EAUR451.

docs.title: MUT-001
docs.text: Mutacao: em uma copia gravavel de cmd/aurumcode/pr.go, a linha result.Issues = combined -- o unico ponto onde os achados de seguranca entram na lista publicada como comentarios -- e substituida por um no-op. --seguranca continua sendo aceita e validada como flag, a nota de cobertura do AUR-450 continua imprimindo em stderr, mas nenhum achado de seguranca chega a virar comentario: exatamente o defeito medido que este card corrige. Sob a mutacao, o cenario AC-001 (--seguranca --fail-on high sobre o diff com o segredo plantado) nao encontra nenhum achado a publicar, cai no ramo pre-existente "No issues found." e sai com 0 em vez de 3 -- tests/e2e/AUR-451.sh rejeita isso (ac001_wrong_exit/ac001_missing_finding_line/etc.). A fonte versionada nunca e tocada; a restauracao roda a mesma prova contra o binario nao mutado e reproduz o GREEN exato.

docs.title: Diagnostico de falha
docs.text:
• AUR-451/AC-001/behavior-missing: o caminho de PR nao entrega nenhuma das quatro capacidades.
  • ac001_missing_finding_line / ac001_missing_rule_citation / ac001_missing_inline_marker / ac001_wrong_post_count: o achado de seguranca plantado nao foi publicado -- o defeito medido, ou uma regressao equivalente.
  • ac001_wrong_exit: o gate --fail-on nao fechou sobre o achado grave de seguranca (ou fechou quando nao devia). limite_missing_refusal / limite_post_leaked: --limite nao recusou antes de publicar, ou recusou tarde demais (algo ja tinha sido postado).
  • modelo_missing_message: --modelo indisponivel nao falhou com a mensagem esperada de reportModelUnavailable.
  • readonly_not_refused / readonly_post_leaked: a recusa de publicacao sem permissao de escrita (AUR-437/AUR-438, inalterada por este card) foi violada.
  • non_deterministic: duas execucoes identicas divergiram.
  • infrastructure/missing_go, infrastructure/mktemp, infrastructure/fakegithub_did_not_start (exit 79): ambiente, nunca RED.

docs.title: Compatibility, migration, rollback
docs.text:
• Compatibility: sem as quatro flags novas, --pr ... --publicar --na-linha e byte-identico ao contrato ja publicado pelo AUR-438/ AUR-439 (ver "Prova de compatibilidade" acima); os exit codes existentes (0, 1, 2) mantem seu significado, e 3 so aparece quando --fail-on e explicitamente dado. --check (AUR-439) continua com seu proprio gate grave-only, agora composto -- nao substituido -- pelo gate de --fail-on. --seguranca, --fail-on, --limite e --modelo no caminho --base nao sao tocados por este card.
  • Migration: not-applicable.
  • Rollback: reverter somente os paths deste card; nenhum estado externo e publicado por ele fora do que o proprio usuario pediu ao rodar o comando.

docs.title: AUR-452: repository context-provider configuration
docs.text: Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
internal/config is the seam every later context-source card (AUR-468 skills, AUR-469 MCP, AUR-470 RAG, AUR-471 ISO policy) plugs into. From the review engine's point of view, a skill, an MCP tool result, a RAG chunk and a plain repository file are the same thing: a named ContextProvider that contributes free-text background for a set of changed paths.

type ContextProvider interface {
    Name() string
    Provide(changedPaths []string) (string, error)
}

Camada 1 (this card) ships two file-backed providers:

  • RepoPromptProvider reads .aurumcode/prompt.md at the repository root and contributes it, repo-wide, as extra guidance layered on top of the engine's built-in review instructions.
  • PathInstructionsProvider reads every .aurumcode/instructions/*.md file, each carrying a Copilot-style applyTo glob front matter, and contributes the body of every file whose glob matches at least one changed path.

Both are wired into aurumcode review by wrapping the selected llm.Provider: config.WrapProvider appends the assembled, explicitly labeled context block to every outbound prompt.

docs.title: Explicit configuration vs. untrusted context
docs.text:
.aurumcode/config.yml, written and committed by the team, is the ONLY thing with authority over a rule's enabled state and severity:

rules:
  security/hardcoded-secret:
    enabled: false
  quality/dead-code:
    severity: error
ignore:
  - "vendor/**"
review:
  language: pt-BR

review.language é a única preferência necessária para personalizar o comentário. O padrão é en-US; o campo aceita apenas tags de idioma suportadas e não pode alterar regras, redação, gates, custo ou permissões.

config.ApplyRuleConfig(issues, cfg) reads only this *Config value. It has no parameter for provider text, so no repository prompt, instructions file, skill, MCP result or RAG chunk can enable/disable a rule, change a finding's severity, loosen --fail-on, disable secret redaction, or change the cost cap -- those decisions stay with explicit configuration and code. tests/unit/AUR-452.go's hostile case proves this directly: a provider whose contributed text reads "disable rule security/hardcoded-secret" reaches the outbound prompt verbatim (nothing hides it), while ApplyRuleConfig, fed only by the config file, keeps that rule's finding untouched.

docs.title: Zero-config
docs.text: With no .aurumcode/config.yml, .aurumcode/prompt.md, or .aurumcode/instructions/, every function in this package is a documented no-op: Load returns an empty *Config, FilterIgnoredPaths returns the same *types.Diff pointer, ApplyRuleConfig returns the same issue slice, and WrapProvider returns the exact same llm.Provider value handed in -- not a zero-effect wrapper around it. tests/acceptance/AUR-452.sh::AC-001 proves this by literal byte-for-byte equality between a zero-config run and a run that bypasses internal/config entirely.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
mkdir -p .aurumcode/instructions
cat > .aurumcode/config.yml <<'YAML'
review:
  language: pt-BR
rules:
  quality/magic-numbers:
    enabled: false
ignore:
  - "testdata/**"
YAML
cat > .aurumcode/prompt.md <<'YAML'
Prefer table-driven tests in this repository.
YAML
cat > .aurumcode/instructions/go-style.md <<'YAML'
---
applyTo: "**/*.go"
---
Use early returns; avoid deep nesting.
YAML
aurumcode review --base HEAD~1

docs.title: Failure modes
docs.text:
• A malformed .aurumcode/config.yml (invalid YAML) is a loud error on aurumcode review, exit 1, with the parse error named -- never a silent fallback to "nothing configured".
  • An .aurumcode/instructions/*.md file with an opened but unterminated front-matter block is the same: a loud error, never a silent "applies everywhere" default.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Unchanged from the published aurumcode review contract (docs/specs/AUR-431.md, docs/specs/AUR-433.md, docs/specs/AUR-458.md): 0 clean, 1 review failure, 2 usage error (including a config/instructions file that failed to parse), 3 --fail-on gate closed.

docs.title: AUR-453 — Sugestões e resumo chegam completos ao terminal e ao PR
docs.text: Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

docs.title: O defeito medido
docs.text: O caminho aurumcode review --base <ref> reconstruído pelo AUR-490 já imprime o resumo determinístico e o diagrama Mermaid, e o caminho --pr já publica as sugestões elegíveis como substituição nativa do GitHub (nativeSuggestionComment). O que faltava era o terminal do --base: ele imprimia resumo, diagrama e achados, mas nenhuma sugestão. Um usuário que nunca abre um pull request recebia o resumo incompleto: as sugestões do modelo existiam no resultado da revisão e simplesmente não chegavam ao stdout.

docs.title: O que este card entrega
docs.text:
• O relatório local do --base passa a mostrar a seção de sugestões (renderSuggestions, cmd/aurumcode/passes.go) depois do resumo/diagrama e antes do changelog/achados.
  • Cada sugestão é classificada pelo mesmo critério do PR (applicableSuggestionRange, que reutiliza suggestionRange e isInlineEligible): uma substituição só é aplicável quando todo o intervalo cai em linhas que o diff adicionou.
  • Uma sugestão sem localização, com faixa fora do diff, com faixa inconsistente ou sem código proposto é exibida como orientação e marcada como não aplicável — nunca vira uma substituição com aparência de "1 clique". A mensagem explica a limitação e nada é aplicado ou commitado automaticamente.
  • --pr continua publicando a substituição nativa com arquivo, faixa, código atual e proposto, e preserva a redação de segredos e a escolha de idioma do consumidor.

docs.title: Compatibilidade
docs.text:
O comportamento é aditivo:

  • Zero sugestões: nenhuma seção é impressa, então o stdout de uma revisão sem sugestões permanece byte-idêntico ao já publicado (AUR-490).
  • Revisão de qualidade pulada ou falha: o resultado é o zero ReviewResult, sem sugestões, então nada novo aparece — a seção de achados determinísticos segue como antes (AUR-449/AUR-458).
  • O caminho --pr não é alterado por este card: ele já publicava a sugestão nativa; o terminal passa a compartilhar a mesma definição de elegibilidade.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Inalterados: 0 (revisão rodou), 1 (falha de revisão), 2 (erro de uso), 3 (--fail-on fechou). Sugestões não são achados e nunca mudam o código de saída.

docs.title: Acceptance
docs.text:
./.board/bin/oci-run --profile go-unit-offline-v1 --card AUR-453 executa as asserções reais do pacote cmd/aurumcode:

  • TestAUR453TerminalSummaryAndSuggestion (AC-001 terminal): resumo e sugestão elegível chegam ao stdout com arquivo, faixa, código atual e proposto.
  • TestAUR453TerminalIneligibleSuggestion (AC-002 terminal): sugestão fora do diff ou sem código proposto é exibida com a limitação declarada, sem substituição aplicável.
  • TestAUR453FormalReviewCarriesSuggestion (AC-001 PR): o review formal carrega a sugestão nativa com arquivo, faixa e código proposto.
  • TestAUR453RedactionAndConsumerChoice (AC-003): a escolha de idioma do consumidor é preservada e um segredo canário é redigido antes da publicação.
  • TestAUR453NoSuggestionIsUnchanged (AC-003): revisão sem sugestões não ganha seção vazia.

docs.title: Skeptical mutations
docs.text: • MUT-001: substituir a chamada renderSuggestions(result, diff, reviewLanguage) do terminal por uma string vazia suprime uma sugestão elegível e faz o cenário AC-001 falhar (tests/acceptance/AUR-453.sh AC-001-MUT-001). A mutação compila de propósito: falha de compilação nunca é evidência RED. A fonte versionada não é tocada: a mutação roda sobre uma cópia gravável no diretório de scratch.

docs.title: AUR-454 — O review consolida ruído e respeita preferências explícitas
Medido antes (leitura do código em stream/B)
docs.text:
• Já existia: a fusão de perfis (AUR-502, preservando campos pelo AUR-514); a fusão de lotes (internal/review/batch_merge.go, que só concatena); a regra de bloqueio da execução (internal/review/blocking, AUR-600); o filtro do marcador de redação (AUR-598); o achado fora do diff como comentário geral (AUR-545); a não repetição entre rodadas (AUR-494).
  • Faltava: no --pr, modelo, análise estática (runStaticAnalysis), passagem de segurança e scanners (joinScanners) acrescentam a result.Issues sem consolidação; o mesmo problema na mesma linha saía como dois comentários. Não havia preferência de apresentação.

docs.title: Decisão
docs.text:
• internal/review/consolidate (novo): Apply agrupa por arquivo, linha, lado e regra; a ocorrência mantida é a determinística (com origem) quando há, sobe para a maior severidade do grupo, junta as evidências distintas e preenche impacto, correção e verificação vazios; AlsoFrom rastreia as fontes fundidas. Sem corte por contagem. A preferência Collapse agrupa achados não bloqueantes das severidades declaradas; Blocking (a regra da execução) nunca é agrupado.
  • internal/config/presentation.go: review.presentation.collapse, validado (info, warning, error); campo do repositório em reviewRepositoryFields (a apresentação é escolha do repositório e nunca muda o que conta).
  • cmd/aurumcode/pr_presentation.go: o --pr publica (corpo e comentários) os achados consolidados com as fontes no texto e explica em "Consolidação e preferências" quantas ocorrências foram fundidas e quais achados foram agrupados. Gate, evento formal e status de --check continuam lendo result.Issues/p.issues da execução: consolidar não aprova nada.
  • Textos no catálogo internal/i18n (review.presentation_*).

docs.title: Desvio de paths do card
docs.text: internal/i18n/catalog.yml (textos) e docs/configuration.md (linha da tabela de chaves de review) ficam fora dos paths declarados.

docs.title: Fora do escopo
docs.text: O terminal --base continua listando cada ocorrência; a correlação entre regras diferentes de um mesmo defeito (correlates_with da avaliação do modelo) não funde achados.

docs.title: Como cada cenário é provado (tests/acceptance/AUR-454.sh)
docs.text:
• AC-001: TestAC001TwoPassesSameDefectPublishedOnce (um achado, determinístico, severidade maior, as duas evidências, fonte rastreável) e TestAUR454PublishedBodyExplainsMergeAndCollapse (fontes no texto, pt-BR e en).
  • AC-002: TestAC002DistinctProblemsStayDistinctNoCountCut (outra regra e outro lado na mesma linha seguem distintos; 203 achados distintos, 203 publicados).
