cmd/aurumcode/aur476_test.go (pacote main, o único que alcança a passagem não exportada) constrói fixtures Git soltas — sem binário git, sem subprocesso — com um arquivo de código e um arquivo de teste sob tests/, e exercita runReview (--base) e runPRReview (--pr) reais:

  • TestAUR476TerminalDeclaresIgnoredCoverage (AC-001/AC-003)
  • TestAUR476CompleteReviewHasNoNotice (AC-002)
  • TestAUR476NoticeIsPipelineDerivedNotModelDerived (AC-003)
  • TestAUR476PRDeclaresOmittedTests (AC-004)

tests/acceptance/AUR-476.sh executa esses seletores no perfil selado go-unit-offline-v1. A mutação declarada (MUT-001) insere um retorno vazio no topo de coverageNotice; o candidato continua compilando e o teste de comportamento correspondente falha (RED).

docs.title: Compatibilidade e rollback
docs.text: Zero-config: sem ignore e com diff que caiba no orçamento, coverageNotice retorna "" e nenhuma saída nova aparece — os bytes publicados permanecem idênticos. Nenhuma escrita no repositório consumidor. Nenhum segredo ou resposta bruta de provider entra na saída. O rollback é limitado a cmd/aurumcode.

docs.title: AUR-477 — Diff grande não vira review zero
Problema
docs.text:
Acima de certo tamanho, um pull request recebia review nenhuma. A reserva de pior caso que o AUR-467 introduziu (necessária — antes a declaração de cobertura era anexada fora do orçamento e estourava o teto) era proporcional ao total de arquivos de código do diff, não ao que a declaração de cobertura efetivamente lista.

Medido: com 200 arquivos e MaxTokens entre 1500 e 3000, a reserva sozinha (~1674 tokens) somada ao prompt base e à reserva de resposta excedia o orçamento, BuildPrompt retornava erro, e o reviewer propagava isso como falha dura com review zero.

docs.title: Causa raiz
docs.text: renderCoverageDeclaration listava todos os arquivos omitidos, um por linha. O pior caso (todos omitidos) era reservado inteiro antes do TrimToFit (maxCoverageDeclarationTokens), então o teto era consumido pela própria declaração antes de sobrar espaço para qualquer código.

docs.title: Correção (duas partes)
docs.text:
1. Lista de omitidos limitada (maxOmittedBullets = 20): a declaração lista até 20 arquivos omitidos e, além disso, troca para a contagem exata (... and N more code files not reviewed). A contagem de "quantos ficaram de fora" nunca é limitada — a lista de nomes é que tem tamanho fixo e orçável. Arquivos parciais continuam listados na íntegra, porque cobertura parcial é exatamente o silêncio que o AUR-467 existe para matar.

  2. Reserva pelo que é declarado, não pelo total: a reserva da declaração converge medindo o texto real montado (System + User), e não uma soma de estimativas por parte. Isso também fecha o arredondamento do estimator (len/4 arredonda cada parte para baixo, então a soma subestimava a concatenação em até um token por parte).

docs.title: Critérios de aceite
docs.text:
• AC-001 (nominal): 200 arquivos de código e MaxTokens=1500 → prompt válido dentro do orçamento, pelo menos um arquivo revisado, e a declaração informa quantos ficaram de fora.
  • AC-002 (o teto continua sendo teto): o prompt montado nunca excede MaxTokens, medido sobre o texto final incluindo a declaração.
  • AC-003 (recusa quando é mesmo impossível): se nem um único arquivo cabe depois da reserva mínima, a montagem recusa em alto e bom som.

docs.title: Mutações
docs.text:
• MUT-001: desfazer o limite da lista de omitidos (reserva volta a ser dimensionada pelo total de arquivos) → AC-001 cai.
  • MUT-002: excluir a declaração de cobertura da medição do teto (a reserva não cresce para cobri-la) → AC-002 cai.

docs.title: AUR-479 -- Split secrets across context providers
Outcome
docs.text: A registered secret does not reach the model by being divided between two context contributions. Before this card, filter.Redact ran per contribution (internal/config/provider.go) before the contributions were concatenated, and never over the assembled block. Two providers whose texts each contained half of a secret therefore produced a final prompt holding the whole secret verbatim. This is reachable today with two file providers (.aurumcode/prompt.md plus a configured docs/skill file); AUR-470's RAG slicing can also cut a secret in half by accident.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text:
BuildContextBlockWithWarnings now redacts twice:

  1. each non-empty contribution is passed through the AUR-009 *redaction.Filter before it is appended, keeping defense in depth at the source; and
  2. the newline-joined contributions are redacted once more as a single block, which is what makes a secret split across two contributions visible.

The assembled block is redacted exactly once, not on every partial concatenation, so the cost stays proportional to the final block. The AUR-009 filter itself is unchanged; it simply sees the assembled block too. Provider names are rendered separately so the redaction input preserves a plain newline boundary between contributions -- a joined pair of halves is still a contiguous match for the filter's line-break-tolerant registered secret rule.

docs.title: Acceptance
docs.text:
tests/acceptance/AUR-479.sh is the program. The container profile is bootstrap-readonly-v1 (Go + Bash image, network none).

  • AC-001 -- a secret split across two contributions does not appear verbatim in the final prompt.
  • AC-002 -- a whole secret confined to one contribution is still redacted, and the per-contribution pass is load-bearing.
  • AC-003 -- a secret-shaped span that only exists across the boundary is redacted without destroying the legitimate prose around it.

Selectors: AC-001, AC-002, AC-003, TestAUR479, IntegrationAUR479, E2EAUR479, MUT-001, MUT-002, all (runs every lane). An unknown selector exits 64.

docs.title: Skeptical mutations
docs.text:
• MUT-001: remove the assembled-block redaction (redact only per contribution). AC-001 goes RED because the split secret is reconstituted.
  • MUT-002: remove the per-contribution redaction (trust only the assembled block). AC-002 goes RED on the overlapping-registered-value case, where containing the whole value inside its own contribution before the join is what preserves abc\n[REDACTED].

Both mutation selectors apply the change to a staged copy of the source and restore nothing in the repository; the nominal run is the GREEN.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: 0 property holds; 1 behavioral RED (including a surviving mutant); 64 unknown selector; 79 infrastructure/inconclusive.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text: Revert internal/config/provider.go and the AUR-479 test/spec files. No external state is published.

docs.title: AUR-480 - Fonte opcional de contexto falha com aviso sem apagar o review
Medido antes
docs.text:
O comportamento ja existe no codigo e nao foi alterado. Este card entrega apenas a caracterizacao.

  • internal/config/provider.go callProviderBounded: cada provider roda sob ProviderTimeout (10s) e MaxProviderContributionBytes; trava, erro e estouro de prazo viram erro nomeado (context provider "<nome>" ...).
  • BuildContextBlockWithWarnings: falha de provider vira ProviderWarning{Provider, Reason}, ambos passam por filter.Redact, o provider e omitido e os demais continuam. So o estouro de tamanho (contributionLimitError) continua erro duro.
  • internal/config/provider_files.go: ConfiguredProviders trata .aurumcode/prompt.md ausente como opcional ("", sem aviso); toda fonte escrita explicitamente (ContextFile.Optional == false) devolve erro quando ausente, e esse erro aparece como aviso nomeado.
  • Parse/Load: YAML malformado, chave desconhecida (decodeStrict) e path de contexto fora do repo continuam erro; arquivo escrito e invalido nunca vira config vazia.
  • O texto do provider so entra no prompt (prompt.RenderRepositoryContext); nenhuma API de decisao (gate, regras, severidade, redacao) recebe texto de provider.
  • Teste existente: TestAUR480ProviderFailureWarnsAndContinues (provider_pending_test.go).

docs.title: O que mudou
docs.text:
• tests/acceptance/AUR-480.sh: copia cmd internal pkg go.mod go.sum inteiros para uma raiz temporaria, grava ali internal/config/aur480_acceptance_test.go e roda go test do pacote. O repositorio nao e tocado.
  • docs/specs/AUR-480.md: este documento. Nenhum arquivo de cmd/, internal/ ou pkg/ foi editado.

docs.title: Prova por AC
docs.text:
Comando geral (container, cwd no worktree): go-shared exec -w <worktree> bash -c 'bash tests/acceptance/AUR-480.sh <seletor>'.

AC Seletor Testes AC-001 AC-001 AC001HangingProviderIsOmittedWithinDeadline (provider que ignora ctx; aviso did not answer, review roda, retorno antes de 15s), AC001ErroringProviderWarnsAndReviewContinues (aviso com nome e motivo, resposta do modelo intacta, contexto saudavel preservado), AC001OnlyFailingProviderStillReviewsUnwrapped, mais o TestAUR480ProviderFailureWarnsAndContinues existente AC-002 AC-002 AC002MalformedConfigStillFails (YAML malformado, chave desconhecida, path escapando, idioma invalido, secao escalar, Load de arquivo invalido), AC002RequiredSourceMissingStillFails (fonte explicita ausente falha e aparece como aviso nomeado), AC002OptionalDefaultPromptAbsentIsSilent AC-003 AC-003 AC003ContextTextCannotChangeDecisions (texto hostil so como fundo; resposta/severidade do modelo e Gate/Rules inalterados), AC003WarningsDoNotLeakSecrets (segredo no nome e no motivo e redigido; nao chega ao prompt)

all roda os nove testes e exige --- PASS de cada um. Ultima linha real: AUR-480/all/pass; AC-001, AC-002 e AC-003 terminam em AUR-480/<AC>/pass. Seletor desconhecido: exit 64.

docs.title: Mutacoes (compilam e ficam vermelhas por comportamento)
docs.text:
Aplicadas na copia temporaria; o script recusa mutacao que nao compila ou que sobrevive.

Mutacao Alteracao Testes vermelhos (saida real) MUT-001 falha de provider aborta (return "", warnings, err no lugar do append) erroring optional source aborted the review: context provider "broken-rag": index unreachable; tambem hanging, only-failing, AC003 x2 e o teste existente MUT-002 aviso suprimido (_ = warning) warning must name the source and the reason, got []; hanging, only-failing, required-missing e existente MUT-003 ProviderTimeout = 24 * time.Hour a hanging provider held the review past 15s MUT-004 Reason sem Redact warning leaked the secret: {Provider:src-[REDACTED] Reason:... AURUM-480-canary-secret} MUT-005 fonte obrigatoria ausente vira "", nil missing required docs/missing.md must fail MUT-006 decodeStrict ignora erro de decode malformed yaml: Parse must fail, got nil

Cada uma termina em AUR-480/MUT-00N/pass (mutation produced RED).

docs.title: Fora de escopo
docs.text: Converter falha do modelo de review em sucesso ou inventar contexto substituto: nao ha teste nem codigo nesse sentido.

docs.title: AUR-481: Rust idiomatic security coverage
docs.text: Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

docs.title: The measurement
docs.text:
The 2026-08-26 measurement planted the same four defects (hardcoded secret, SQL injection, command injection, XSS) in eight languages and ran the deterministic --seguranca pass. Rust was the worst cell in the table: zero of three applicable rules fired, for a language the tool has a native documentation extractor for (AUR-427) and no external toolchain dependency. Three causes, each in security.yml's existing patterns:

  1. security/hardcoded-secret never matched const ACCESS_KEY: &str = "AKIA..."; -- the pattern expects a quote immediately after :=/:/=, and Rust's typed declarations put a TYPE (&str, String) between the identifier and =.
  2. security/sql-injection never matched conn.query(&("SELECT ... '".to_owned() + name)); -- the pattern requires ["']\s*\+ and Rust's idiomatic concatenation puts a method call (.to_owned()/.to_string()) between the closing quote and the +. Rust's more common shape, format!("SELECT ...{}", name), has no + at all.
  3. security/command-injection never matched Command::new("sh").arg("-c").arg("ping ".to_owned() + h).spawn(); -- none of the existing branches (exec[lv]p?e?, exec(Sync)?, spawn(...shell:true)) recognize Command::new.

docs.title: What this card delivers
docs.text:
internal/review/rules/security.yml:

  • security/hardcoded-secret gains two new alternatives: a typed const/static/let declaration (IDENT: &str|String = "value") assigned a quoted literal directly, and the String::from("value") wrapper (type annotation optional there). Both reuse the same case-insensitive keyword group and the same digit+letter VALUE class the existing quoted branch uses -- no weakening, same false-positive guard.
  • security/sql-injection gains two new alternatives: the .to_owned()/.to_string()-then-+ concatenation shape, and a format!(...) call whose format string carries a SQL verb and a {} placeholder followed by a comma-separated identifier argument.
  • security/command-injection gains one new alternative: Command::new("sh"|"bash") plus a .arg("-c") call, flagged on that combination alone (the same "dangerous regardless of what follows" reasoning the existing spawn(...shell:true) branch already uses), regardless of whether the later .arg(...) carries .to_owned() + h concatenation or a format!(...) call.

Both extensions were probed against every positive and negative shape (see tests/unit/AUR-481.go) with a throwaway regex harness before touching the catalog, then proven against the real loader (internal/review.SecurityScan) and the real CLI (aurumcode review --seguranca).

docs.title: Rust command-injection: first reverted, now restored
docs.text:
A branch analogous to the existing spawn(...shell:true) one -- Command::new("sh"|"bash") plus a .arg("-c") call, flagged on that combination alone regardless of what a later .arg(...) carries (.to_owned() + h concatenation or a format!(...) call) -- was written and proven correct (matches both vulnerable forms, excludes Command::new("ping").arg(host)). It was first reverted: extending security/command-injection's pattern broke tests/acceptance/AUR-462.sh's own MUT-001, which hardcoded that pattern's exact bytes, verbatim, as a literal grep-and-rewrite anchor (AUR-462.sh:266), and AUR-462.sh was not in this card's paths at the time. Measured directly: tests/acceptance/AUR-462.sh AC-001 produced AUR-462/AC-001/MUT-001/anchor-not-found, exit 1.

tests/acceptance/AUR-462.sh was then added to this card's paths (the coordinator's own call, after independently verifying the anchor-fragility claim), with instructions to reanchor MUT-001 stably rather than weaken its assertion. It now arms on the rule's - id: security/command-injection line -- a structurally stable, content-independent marker -- and rewrites the next pattern: line wholesale to an always-empty (pattern: ''), always-non-matching value, rather than string-replacing inside the pattern's own text. An awk END block makes the mutation impossible to silently no-op: if the anchor is never armed-and-matched, awk exits 1, mv never runs, and an explicit follow-up grep catches the untouched file and fails loudly. This is immune to any future card widening the pattern's text, which is exactly the failure this card hit (and the same failure mode AUR-448's own MUT-001 hit the same day, when AUR-467 added a second print of the same shape it anchored on). With that fix in place, the Rust command-injection branch is restored and shipped.

Go, C#, PowerShell, and bash command-injection coverage (also named by this card's own outcome measurement) remain out for the ordinary reason: this card's declared priority, set by the dispatcher, is Rust delivered completely and proven, over partial coverage of every language. Nothing in security.yml was touched for these four languages.

XSS was not in scope for any of the eight languages this card targeted (the outcome table shows XSS covered only for JavaScript, already fixed by AUR-462).

docs.title: Fixture
docs.text: tests/fixtures/review/vuln/rust-secret-sql-injection/ is a bare, loose-object git repository built by tests/fixtures/repos/git-demo/build-fixture.sh from that directory's history.spec (the sealed acceptance profile carries no git binary, so every fixture in this repository is committed pre-built rather than generated at test time). Its second commit adds src/main.rs carrying every AC-001 true-positive shape (typed const secret, String::from secret, .to_owned() SQL concat, format! SQL, Command::new("sh") with both a .to_owned() and a format! argument) beside every AC-002 safe form this card names (a numeric constant, a digit-free string constant, a $1-parametrized query, an argv-form Command with no shell).

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
• Unit: tests/unit/AUR-481.go::TestAUR481 -- package-boundary proof over synthetic diffs, including every AC-001 positive, every AC-002 negative, three AC-003 regression shapes, and a fixture-line-for-line end-to-end/determinism check.
  • Integration: tests/integration/AUR-481.go::IntegrationAUR481 -- CLI-boundary proof: builds the real binary, runs it against the committed Rust fixture and the pre-existing Python/secret/Node fixtures.
  • E2E: tests/e2e/AUR-481.sh::E2EAUR481 -- full-process proof, including the --fail-on high gate closing on the six real Rust findings.
  • Acceptance: tests/acceptance/AUR-481.sh -- runs all three selectors plus two mutations: MUT-001 removes both new SQL alternatives and proves the two Rust SQL true positives vanish; MUT-002 widens the format! branch past its SQL-verb requirement and proves the AC-002 safe form (format!("user {}", name)) is wrongly matched.
  • Regression: tests/acceptance/AUR-462.sh AC-001 and tests/acceptance/AUR-466.sh AC-001 were run before and after every edit in this card and both stayed exit 0.

docs.title: AUR-483: A documentacao gerada e do produto, nao dos testes dele
docs.text: Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: Measured on this repository: of the 613 code files internal/pipeline.ExtractorPipeline scanned, 489 (79%) were test or fixture code (tests/ alone: 399 files). shouldSkipPath (internal/pipeline/extractor_pipeline.go) already skipped node_modules, .git, .github, vendor, target, dist, build, _site, .taskmaster and .aurumcode, but never tests/, testdata/ or fixtures/. The published site (https://mpaape.github.io/AurumCode/) was therefore roughly 80% raw enumeration of the repository's own test scaffolding. Since the rule lives in the generator, not this repository, every user pointing AurumCode at their own repository inherited the same noise ratio.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text:
internal/pipeline/extractor_pipeline.go adds:

  • IsTestScopePath(path string) bool -- reports whether path is test or fixture scope: a directory component (not substring) equal to tests, testdata or fixtures, or a filename stem (not substring) ending in _test. Matching a whole path component/stem, never a substring, is what keeps internal/attestation, cmd/latest and a file named contest.go out of scope even though each contains the letters "test" (AC-003).
  • ExtractorPipelineConfig.IncludeTests bool and (*ExtractorPipeline).IncludeTests() bool -- the latter is true when either the config field is set or the process environment carries AURUMCODE_INCLUDE_TEST_DOCS (1/true/yes/on, case-insensitive). Default: false -- test/fixture scope is excluded unless explicitly turned back on (AC-002).
  • determineFilesToProcess excludes test/fixture-scope files from the file-discovery walk (both the full-extraction and incremental branches) when IncludeTests() is false, and its log always states the outcome: "scope: excluded N file(s) as test or fixture scope (...)" in the default case, or that the exclusion was disabled by config, in the opt-in case (AC-001's declaration requirement).
  • buildScopedSourceView / sourceDirForExtraction / Run -- why file-discovery filtering alone is not enough: every language extractor (ExtractRequest carries no file list) discovers its own files by independently walking SourceDir, so narrowing determineFilesToProcess's own file list changes only its accounting, never what an extractor actually reads. Run therefore builds a scoped copy (not a symlink tree -- some extractors' own walks may not treat a symlink DirEntry as a regular file) of SourceDir with test/fixture scope removed, and points every extractor at that copy instead, whenever !IncludeTests() and the run is not incremental. IncludeTests()==true (or incremental mode) leaves SourceDir completely untouched -- byte-for-byte the pre-AUR-483 code path.

No extractor and no page-rendering code was touched (out of scope per the card's Non-goals); internal/documentation/extractors/* and internal/documentation/site/welcome are read-only context for this card.

docs.title: Measured result (this repository, this worktree)
docs.text:
cmd/regenerate-docs run against this repository's own root, no LLM provider configured:

pages generated before (pre-AUR-483) 236 after (AUR-483 default) 57

A 76% drop, consistent with the card's own 79%-noise measurement.

docs.title: Configuring test documentation back on
docs.text:
Set AURUMCODE_INCLUDE_TEST_DOCS=true in the process environment of whichever binary invokes internal/pipeline (cmd/regenerate-docs, aurumcode docs, or a direct caller of the Go API via ExtractorPipelineConfig.IncludeTests = true). The environment variable is read directly by internal/pipeline itself, not plumbed through either CLI's own flag/env parsing -- both of which are read_paths for this card, not paths, and were not modified -- so the opt-in reaches every entrypoint without any of them needing a code change.

One caveat, not introduced by this card: the Go extractor (internal/documentation/extractors/go) has always hardcoded testdata in its own, separate package-discovery skip list, unconditional on any flag. Setting AURUMCODE_INCLUDE_TEST_DOCS=true restores tests/ and fixtures/ Go packages; a testdata/ Go package stays excluded by that pre-existing, unrelated mechanism, which this card's paths do not include.

docs.title: Acceptance
docs.text:
• AC-001 (nominal): default generation excludes tests/, testdata/, fixtures/ and *_test files; the run declares how many files it excluded by scope; the number of generated pages drops.
  • AC-002 (configurable): AURUMCODE_INCLUDE_TEST_DOCS=true restores test documentation; the capability was not removed.
  • AC-003 (component, not substring): internal/attestation, cmd/latest and contest.go are always documented.

tests/unit/AUR-483.go::TestAUR483 proves IsTestScopePath/IncludeTests in isolation. tests/integration/AUR-483.go::IntegrationAUR483 runs the real ExtractorPipeline.Run against the committed fixture (tests/fixtures/docs/AUR-483) and inspects the markdown pages it writes. tests/e2e/AUR-483.sh::E2EAUR483 runs the real cmd/regenerate-docs binary end to end and inspects both the generated pages and the stderr declaration. tests/acceptance/AUR-483.sh orchestrates all of the above plus MUT-001 (neutralizes the default-exclusion gate in Run) and MUT-002 (rewrites IsTestScopePath to match by substring), each proving the mutant is rejected by the same accept command.

docs.title: AUR-484: a página inicial ensina a usar, em vez de listar arquivos
docs.text: Documento histórico do board. Pode descrever componentes removidos; para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

docs.title: Achado
docs.text: A página publicada em https://mpaape.github.io/AurumCode/ foi lida como visitante novo. O que ela oferecia: três frases sobre as áreas do produto, links para outros documentos, e então ~80% de enumeração crua de páginas geradas (internal/documentation/site/scaffold.go's renderPageBlock, inline no corpo do index.md). Não oferecia nenhum comando copiável, nenhum exemplo de uso, nenhuma indicação de instalação, e nenhuma declaração do que a ferramenta não faz.

docs.title: O que mudou
docs.text:
internal/documentation/site/scaffold.go ganhou um segundo bloco delimitado, escrito pelo próprio scaffold (determinístico, sem LLM), imediatamente antes do bloco de páginas geradas: <!-- aurumcode:quickstart:start --> / <!-- aurumcode:quickstart:end -->. Esse bloco é sempre reescrito em uma nova execução, exatamente como o bloco de páginas sempre foi — stripGeneratedBlock agora remove a região a partir do primeiro marcador presente (quickstart, com fallback para o marcador antigo em um index.md escrito antes deste card) até o marcador de fim do bloco de páginas.

O conteúdo do bloco é uma constante Go (renderQuickstartBlock), não geração de modelo: existe com ou sem provider de LLM configurado, porque o site publica sem credencial hoje (internal/documentation/welcome continua sendo o caminho opcional de enriquecimento por modelo, e nunca é o único lugar onde este conteúdo aparece).

O que o bloco contém, cada item citando de onde a afirmação sai:

  1. Comando copiável sem credencial — ./aurumcode review --base HEAD~1 --seguranca. Verificado ao vivo neste card (aurumcode review: security pass applied 4 of 8 security rules ..., exit 0) e é a mesma forma usada em docs/getting-started.md e em demo.sh.
  2. Um exemplo por feature: a mesma passagem de segurança para code review; aurumcode docs --source . --output ./site para documentação (forma exata de docs/getting-started.md); e o snippet mínimo de workflow (uses: Mpaape/AurumCode@v1) para páginas — pinado em @v1, nunca @main, coerente com o que AUR-465/AUR-472 exigem.
  3. Limitações declaradas (AC-003):
  4. a passagem de segurança cobre 4 das 8 regras do catálogo: internal/review/rules/security.yml tem 8 regras; apenas 4 carregam pattern hoje (sql-injection, command-injection, hardcoded-secret, xss — confirmado lendo o arquivo diretamente nesta execução). path-traversal, weak-crypto, insecure-random e missing-auth continuam metadado-apenas, citável só por um modelo com provider.
  5. Cobertura por linguagem desigual: .board/cards/ready/AUR-481.md mede que Go, C#, PowerShell, Bash e Rust têm lacunas na regra de command injection (Bash e Rust também na de SQL injection); o exemplo exec.Command(...) do Go e Process.Start(...) do C# não casam com o pattern atual de command-injection, confirmado lendo o próprio regexp em security.yml.
  6. Sem provider de LLM, a review de qualidade não roda — só a passagem determinística executa (mesmo texto de aviso que o binário já imprime).

docs.title: AC-002: a enumeração deixa de ser o corpo do index
docs.text: Scaffold.Generate() escreve um segundo arquivo, reference.md, no DocsDir, contendo a listagem completa por linguagem e símbolo (renderPageBlock, inalterado no conteúdo, só realocado) -- mas apenas quando há MAIS DE UMA página gerada (ver decisão de desenho abaixo). index.md recebe renderPageSummaryBlock: para 0 páginas, o texto "No documentation pages were generated"; para 2+, contagem + link [full reference](reference.html); para exatamente 1 página, o link direto para essa página, inline, sem arquivo de referência algum. collectListedPages/collectWalkedPages excluem reference.md da própria varredura, para que uma segunda execução não indexe o arquivo de referência como se fosse uma página gerada.

docs.title: Decisão de desenho: reference.md não existe para um projeto de 1 página
docs.text:
Medido nesta execução: tests/e2e/browser_chain_test.go e tests/e2e/smoke_test.go andam pelo diretório do site gerado contando páginas de símbolo, e cmd/regenerate-docs/main.go's collectMarkdown (fora de paths/read_paths deste card) faz o mesmo de forma independente para compor a linha aurumcode: result=ok docs=N ... que o CLI imprime de verdade em produção -- ambos excluíam apenas index.md por nome. Um reference.md sempre emitido, mesmo para 1 página, era contado por essas varreduras como uma SEGUNDA página de documentação inventada: o CLI chegou a imprimir docs=2 para um projeto com uma única página real.

Havia duas saídas legítimas: (a) cada varredura passa a excluir reference.md também; (b) o gerador não emite reference.md quando há uma página só. (a) exigiria editar cmd/regenerate-docs/main.go, que este card não pode escrever -- só ler. (b) resolve os três lugares de uma vez, inclusive o que (a) não alcançaria, e é correto por si: uma página de referência cujo único papel é indexar várias páginas por linguagem não tem o que acrescentar quando existe exatamente uma. O custo aceito: a estrutura do site publicado varia com o tamanho do projeto (um projeto de 1 página não tem /reference/; um de 2+ tem). Quem automatiza sobre a estrutura do site precisa checar a existência do arquivo antes de linkar para ele.

docs.title: Non-goals respeitados
docs.text:
• O guia completo continua em docs/getting-started.md; o bloco novo é propositalmente curto.
  • Nenhuma prosa gerada por modelo entrou neste bloco.
  • A documentação de API gerada continua acessível (reference.md), só não é mais o corpo da página inicial.
  • Nenhuma limitação foi inventada: as três acima saem de arquivo lido nesta mesma execução (security.yml) ou de medição já registrada (AUR-481).

docs.title: Fora de escopo deste card
docs.text:
• internal/pipeline (AUR-483, em paralelo) não foi tocado.
  • .aurumcode/index.md (o arquivo realmente publicado hoje) não está em paths/read_paths deste card e não foi editado à mão; a correção vive no gerador (internal/documentation/site), que o próximo cmd/regenerate-docs volta a escrever por cima da mesma forma.

docs.title: AUR-486 -- Go, C#, PowerShell and bash in their idiomatic spelling
Outcome
docs.text: Command injection is found in the idiomatic spelling of Go, C#, PowerShell and bash, and SQL injection built by shell interpolation is found too. This is the remainder of AUR-481, which delivered Rust and was reduced in scope to what it proved.

docs.title: Measured finding (2026-08-26)
docs.text:
The same four defects (secret, sql, cmd, xss) were planted in eight languages and the deterministic security pass was run over them. The command-injection cell was missed in all four languages this card covers:

Language secret sql cmd Go sim sim NAO C# sim sim NAO PowerShell sim sim NAO Bash sim NAO NAO

Causes, read from the pattern at the time:

  • Go: exec.Command("sh", "-c", "ping "+host). The branch was exec[lv]p?e?, which needs an l or v right after exec (the C spellings execl/execv/execve); the dot in exec.Command also breaks the sequence. Go is this project's own primary language.
  • C#: Process.Start(...) was not in the pattern at all.
  • PowerShell: Invoke-Expression was not in the pattern at all.
  • Bash: eval "ping $1" and sh -c "ping $1" were not in the pattern; and SQL assembled by shell interpolation (query="... WHERE name = '$1'") has no + for the SQL rule to anchor on.

docs.title: The fix
docs.text:
internal/review/rules/security.yml gains branches, all of them deterministic (no LLM, no AST):

  • security/command-injection:
  • Go: exec.Command("sh"|"bash"|"cmd"|"powershell", "-c"|"/c"|"-Command", ...). The safe argv form exec.Command("ping", host) names no shell and is excluded structurally.
  • C#: Process.Start(...) reaching a shell by quote-then-+ concatenation, or a literal cmd/powershell file name. Process.Start("ping", host) and a ProcessStartInfo with separated ArgumentList are excluded.
  • PowerShell: Invoke-Expression / iex.
  • bash: sh -c / bash -c, and eval anchored at the start of the line (^\s*eval) so the word inside a # comment or a string literal does not fire.
  • security/sql-injection: a SQL verb followed later by a quote immediately before a shell sigil ('$1', "$name", '${ID}'). The quote/$ adjacency is what separates shell interpolation from a database placeholder ("SELECT ... = $1" in Rust, ? in Python), so AUR-481's parametrized-query AC-002 stays green.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text:
• No existing pattern is loosened. False positives in a merge gate teach the team to disable the gate (AUR-462, AUR-466).
  • No semantic analysis or AST: the pass stays a deterministic matcher over added lines.
  • No full language parity is promised; what is not covered is declared here.

docs.title: Acceptance
docs.text:
• AC-001: over a fixture with Go exec.Command(..., "sh","-c", ...), C# Process.Start, PowerShell Invoke-Expression, bash eval/sh -c and SQL-by-shell, the pass reports each with the correct rule citation.
  • AC-002: the Go argv form, C# separated arguments, eval inside a comment or a string literal, and parametrized SQL produce no finding.
  • AC-003 (regression): the Rust (AUR-481), Node (AUR-462), Python (AUR-435) and C++ (AUR-442/AUR-461) shapes still produce exactly the findings they produced before. C++ is asserted at the unit boundary: the system("ping " + host) true positive still fires and its benign neighbour system("ping example.com") does not. The Rust/Node/Python fixtures are additionally counted at the CLI boundary, scoped to the security section so the separate deterministic-analysis section cannot skew the count.

Selectors: unit tests/unit/AUR-486.go::TestAUR486; integration tests/integration/AUR-486.go::IntegrationAUR486; acceptance tests/acceptance/AUR-486.sh; e2e tests/e2e/AUR-486.sh::E2EAUR486.

docs.title: Mutations
docs.text:
• MUT-001: remove the Go branch (exec\.Command -> non-matching). The Go command-injection finding must vanish while C#/bash stay; AC-001 RED.
  • MUT-002: widen the Go branch to a bare exec\.Command\s*\(. The safe argv form must wrongly match; AC-002 RED.

docs.title: Runtime note
docs.text: The sealed profile bootstrap-readonly-v1 has bash and Go but no git, and this card's paths do not include tests/fixtures. The e2e script and the integration test therefore write a bare repository in the loose-object format tests/fixtures/repos/git-demo/build-fixture.sh emits; nothing shells out to git.

docs.title: Known limitation, accepted deliberately
docs.text: The bash eval anchor is the start of the line, so an eval reached through a command substitution or a wrapper on the same line (foo; eval "...") is not matched. This is the trade that keeps eval in a comment or inside a string literal from firing, which is this card's AC-002.

docs.title: AUR-492: real linters complement the review with a verifiable origin
Measured before (base 20565f39)
docs.text:
• analysis.Vet (internal/analysis/vet.go) had no caller. It parsed the text form of go vet ./... and, when the run failed but some line looked like a diagnostic, returned those findings with a nil error. Measured on go1.27.1: a module with one package that does not type-check and one printf diagnostic exits 1, and a missing dependency prints p/a.go:3:8: no required module provides package ..., a line the text parser read as a finding. Both read as a (partial) clean result.
  • scanner.ExecCommand (internal/scanner/executor.go) ran every engine with cmd.Env == nil, i.e. the whole environment of the reviewing process (LLM_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, any other job secret) reached semgrep, gitleaks and git, which read content the pull request's author controls. Output was buffered without bound and a grandchild holding the pipes could keep Wait blocked past the 120 s timeout.

docs.title: What changed
docs.text:
• internal/scanner/environment.go: BaseEnvironment (PATH, HOME, TMPDIR, LANG, LC_ALL, SSL_CERT_FILE, SSL_CERT_DIR), Environment{Pass, Fixed, Extra} per engine, ChildEnvironment (never nil) and GitSafeDirectories (only the safe.directory entries of GIT_CONFIG_*, renumbered; an http.extraheader is dropped).
  • internal/scanner/executor.go: IsolatedCommand(env) is the production command: explicit cmd.Env, WaitDelay 5 s, 32 MiB per stream (ErrOutputTooLarge, an invalid output). The executor builds each engine's command from Engine.Environment; ExecCommand keeps its signature with the base environment only.
  • internal/scanner/govet (new engine govet, category lint, origin govet, no options): go env GOVERSION (identity go vet <version>), git diff --unified=0 <base>...<head> for the added lines, then analysis.Vet; only findings on added lines are kept. Empty range is an error (never a whole-tree scan). Environment: GOCACHE, GOPATH, GOMODCACHE, GOROOT passed; GOTOOLCHAIN=local, GOPROXY=off fixed; GOFLAGS never passed. Registered in internal/scanner/engines.
  • internal/analysis/vet.go: go vet -json ./...; any runner error is an error with no findings; the JSON report is decoded (never interpreted); a position outside the root, without a line or without an analyzer is ErrInvalidOutput. Rule id go-vet/<analyzer>, severity warning.
  • gitleaks declares Environment{Extra: GitSafeDirectories}; semgrep uses the base environment.
  • Docs: docs/configuration.md (govet section, child environment and limits, lint in the gate.sources table); docs/tutorials/sast.md Caso 5 and "Sem go no PATH"; demo cases govet-achado (a fake go that answers exactly what the real go vet -json printed for the fixture, and records whether LLM_API_KEY/GITHUB_TOKEN reached it) and govet-sem-go (the real image, without Go).

docs.title: Review follow-up
docs.text:
• CGO_ENABLED=0 is fixed in govet's environment: the pull request controls the #cgo directives, so vet never invokes the C toolchain (TestGoChildHasCgoDisabled; the all-engine leak test also requires it).
  • git diff --relative from the review root, and a root without go.mod is lint_execution_error (TestDiffIsRelativeToTheRoot, TestRootWithoutModuleIsInconclusive; TestRealGitSubdirectoryRoot with a real repository whose root is a subdirectory, where git exists).
  • A path git quotes in +++ "b/..." is ErrInvalidOutput, never dropped (TestParseAddedLinesRefusesQuotedPath).

docs.title: How each scenario is proved
docs.text:
tests/acceptance/AUR-492.sh (selectors all, AC-001..AC-004, MUT-001..MUT-004; unknown selector exits 64).

  • AC-001: TestRealVetFindingOnAddedLine runs the real go vet through the executor with the production command (git answered by a canned diff, so the sealed image without git can run it): one finding calc/calc.go:9, rule go-vet/printf, origin govet, category lint. TestRealVetCorrectedChangeIsClean: the fixed change has none. TestRealVetIgnoresUntouchedLines: a diagnostic in an untouched file is dropped. TestRealGitRangeEndToEnd repeats it with a real git repository where git exists (go-shared). Demo: govet-achado publishes only calc/calc.go:9, never legado/legado.go, exit 3.
  • AC-002: TestMissingGoIsUnavailable (lint_unavailable), TestRealVetFailureIsInconclusive (a broken package next to a real diagnostic: lint_execution_error, no findings), TestNoRangeIsInconclusive, TestVetRefusesUntrustedReport, TestRefusesOptions. Demo: govet-sem-go is inconclusivo (lint_unavailable), exit 1.
  • AC-003: TestNoEngineChildInheritsSecrets registers every engine, puts fake semgrep, gitleaks, git and go first in PATH, sets LLM_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, AURUMCODE_LLM_API_KEY, GOFLAGS and an http.extraheader in GIT_CONFIG_*, runs each engine through Executor{} and asserts for each binary that it ran (PATH present), no sentinel reached it, every variable is in the declared list and git kept safe.directory. TestIsolatedCommandUsesOnlyGivenEnvironment, TestChildEnvironmentIsExplicit, TestGitSafeDirectoriesDropsOtherKeys, TestIsolatedCommandBoundsOutput. Demo: both ausente lines.
  • AC-004: the five pre-existing sast cases, recorded without the entry, never mention govet or lint_; TestGovetRunsOnlyWhenDeclared (config.Parse) where internal/config's imports exist. In the sealed image they do not (the card's paths/read_paths lack internal/dtrack and other config imports), and the script prints AC-004/config/not-materialized.
  • MUT-001 (failed vet read as findings, if runErr != nil && stdout == ""): TestRealVetFailureIsInconclusive RED with the calc finding.
  • MUT-002 (findings outside the diff kept): TestRealVetIgnoresUntouchedLines RED with legado/legado.go:6.
  • MUT-003 (govet import removed from engines.go, engine ignored): TestNoEngineChildInheritsSecrets RED (govet is not registered).
  • MUT-004 (cmd.Env = nil, environment inherited): TestNoEngineChildInheritsSecrets RED (semgrep received a secret of the reviewing process) and TestIsolatedCommandUsesOnlyGivenEnvironment RED.

Last lines, go-shared (bash tests/acceptance/AUR-492.sh all) and sealed (oci-run --profile go-unit-offline-v1 --card AUR-492):

AUR-492/MUT-004/rejected
AUR-492/all/pass

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• The engine vets the module at the review root (./...); nested modules are outside its coverage. Proxy variables are not passed to any engine.
  • The product image does not carry Go; govet in CI needs a runner image with Go on PATH. Nothing is installed by the review.

docs.title: AUR-494 — Novas rodadas preservam findings válidos sem repetir comentários
Medido antes (leitura do código em stream/B)
docs.text:
• Já existia: o histórico do PR (reviews, comentários inline e gerais) é lido a cada --pr e entra no prompt como contexto não confiável (pr_history.go); a identidade canônica de achado (render.FindingIdentityFor + render.FindingFingerprint, AUR-521) lê o código da linha no diff, nunca o texto do modelo; o cache de revisão (AUR-513) e o de veredito mudam de chave com prompt, configuração, perfis e contexto; o achado fora do diff vira comentário geral (AUR-545); o evento formal segue o gate (AUR-600).
  • Faltava: cada rodada republicava todo comentário de achado (inline e geral); nada ligava um comentário anterior ao achado atual. A identidade canônica inclui o número da linha, então mover o mesmo código mudaria a impressão. O parecer não registrava o que deixou de ser reportado.
  • docs/review-quality.md e README.md diziam "sem garantia de deduplicação" e "não atualiza comentários anteriores"; corrigidos.

docs.title: Decisão
docs.text:
• internal/review/rounds (novo): Marker escreve o marcador oculto <!-- aurumcode:finding <sha256> <regra> -->; Published lê os marcadores do histórico (respostas em thread não contam); PlanRound casa as impressões da rodada com as anteriores por contagem (duas ocorrências do mesmo defeito precisam de dois comentários) e lista as anteriores não reencontradas.
  • cmd/aurumcode/pr_rounds.go: roundFingerprint reaproveita a identidade canônica do AUR-521 com a linha zerada quando há código na linha (mover o trecho mantém a identidade; outra regra na mesma linha é outro achado). planRound usa as entradas do histórico já lidas para o prompt (pullRequestHistoryContext passa a devolvê-las; nenhuma requisição a mais). Sem histórico legível, tudo é comentado.
  • review_pr_publish.go: revisão formal e modo de comentários pulam o comentário de achado já comentado e anexam o marcador aos novos; o corpo ganha "Rodadas anteriores" com a contagem do não repetido e a lista do não reencontrado (review.round_* no catálogo internal/i18n).
  • O achado pulado continua em result.Issues: parecer, gate, evento formal e status não mudam; marcador forjado só evita um comentário repetido, nunca desliga regra. Resposta de pessoa só entra no prompt.

docs.title: Desvio de paths do card
docs.text: Os textos novos ficam em internal/i18n/catalog.yml (regra do catálogo: toda interface por idioma vem dele) e o README.md foi corrigido pela regra de documentação desatualizada; os demais arquivos estão em cmd/aurumcode, internal/review e docs/review-quality.md.

docs.title: Fora do escopo
docs.text: Dispensar uma revisão REQUEST_CHANGES de rodada anterior exige um método novo em internal/git/githubclient (fora dos paths): o evento e os status da rodada atual já deixam de bloquear; a dispensa fica documentada como limitação. O achado fora do diff (AUR-545) não leva marcador.

docs.title: Como cada cenário é provado (tests/acceptance/AUR-494.sh)
docs.text:
Os testes de cmd/aurumcode/aur494_test.go rodam rodadas reais de --pr contra um GitHub falso que guarda a conversa (o que uma rodada publica é o que a próxima lê).

  • AC-001: TestAUR494AC001SameDiffTwiceNoDuplicateComment (segunda rodada: zero comentários, mesmo evento, contagem no corpo) e os testes de internal/review/rounds.
  • AC-002: TestAUR494AC002MovedCodeKeepsIdentityNewDefectStays.
  • AC-003: TestAUR494AC003FixRemovesBlockAndTextDisablesNothing (resposta "falso positivo" chega ao prompt e o evento continua REQUEST_CHANGES; depois da correção o evento deixa de ser REQUEST_CHANGES e o corpo registra a resolução) e TestPublishedIgnoresReplies.
  • AC-004: TestAUR494AC004NewContextFindsNewDefectWithoutRepeating.
  • MUT-001: roundPlan.posts passa a devolver sempre true; compila e o AC-001 fica vermelho com AUR-494 duplicate comment.

docs.title: Correções da revisão estática
docs.text:
• Um achado agrupado por review.presentation.collapse (AUR-454) entrava em "não se repetem" embora continuasse reportado. PlanRound recebe também os achados agrupados (stillReported): nunca comentados, nunca resolvidos. Prova: TestPlanRoundCondensedIsNeverResolved.
  • Execução inconclusiva (falha do modelo ou gate inconclusivo) não lista nada como resolvido (conclusiveForRounds). Prova: TestAUR494InconclusiveRunNamesNothingResolved.
  • O marcador era aceito de qualquer autor: o autor do PR podia forjá-lo, calar o comentário de um achado e injetar um "corrigido". Agora só conta marcador de comentário cujo autor é AURUMCODE_PUBLISHER_LOGIN; o workflow reutilizável o define como github-actions[bot] (autor do github.token). Sem esse login, nenhum marcador é lido e tudo é comentado de novo (falha fechada). O cliente GitHub não tem leitura do usuário autenticado e GET /user não responde a token de instalação, por isso o login vem do ambiente da borda. Risco residual: outro workflow do mesmo repositório que publique com github.token escreve como o mesmo login. Prova: TestAUR494ForgedMarkerFromAnotherAuthorIsIgnored.
  • O texto "já comentado em rodada anterior" do stdout vem do catálogo (review.round_repeated_line).

docs.title: AUR-495 — Dependência alterada no PR checada contra o OSV em qualquer ecossistema
Medido antes (pela leitura)
docs.text:
• Nenhum código lia dependências de um diff. A única menção a OSV era o artefato de dados de análise (AUR-533, internal/artifacts), que publica uma cópia OSV mas não tinha consumidor ("quando um consumidor a usar (AUR-495)", docs/configuration.md).
  • O registro de scanners (internal/scanner) é feito para engines determinísticas sobre a árvore, sem acesso ao modelo; o card pede que o modelo extraia os pacotes e que o scanner seja só conferência.
  • O card cita internal/analysis nos paths; a lógica nova ficou no pacote novo internal/dependencies (citado em docs/architecture.md, exigência do teste estrutural), com o contribuidor em internal/gate e a ligação em cmd/aurumcode, a pedido do coordenador do stream (reaproveitar a arquitetura de fontes e gate).

docs.title: Decisão
docs.text:
• internal/dependencies:
  • extract.go: duas perguntas ao modelo (templates Markdown embutidos em prompts/): quais arquivos alterados são manifestos/lockfiles (só paths do diff são aceitos) e quais pacotes mudaram neles (ecossistema, nome, versões ou faixas, explicação, unresolved). Resposta em JSON validada.
  • ground.go: aterra a resposta no diff (AC-008): manifesto dado ao modelo, nome presente no diff do arquivo, cada versão/faixa presente nas linhas alteradas do lado certo; o resto é descartado e declarado.
  • conference.go: Extractor sobre todos os paths alterados; produção OSVScanner roda uma vez osv-scanner scan source --format json --all-packages --recursive <checkout> pelo scanner.Command (ambiente mínimo, scanner.Timeout) e guarda os pacotes dos arquivos alterados. Arquivo reconhecido que o modelo não apontou entra nos manifestos e a omissão é declarada (o modelo nunca remove evidência determinística); versão nova que o scanner não lista é divergência declarada; pacote que o scanner extrai das linhas adicionadas e o modelo omitiu é inconclusivo (dependencies_extraction_gap). Binário ausente ou saída ilegível = inconclusivo (exit 128, "nenhum pacote", é vazio).
  • osv.go: cliente da API OSV (POST /v1/query, paginação limitada, corpo limitado, advisories retirados ignorados). Severidade da fonte (database_specific.severity), versões corrigidas do pacote consultado, link ADVISORY/WEB ou o registro da fonte. Frescor opcional pelo Date+Age da resposta (max_source_age_hours); sem Date com limite declarado = vencida.
  • classify.go: os dois lados consultados (cache por execução); advisory só no head = introduzido, nos dois = pré-existente, só na base = corrigido; identidade por id ou alias. Faixa sem versão consulta o pacote inteiro. Qualquer falha descarta todos os achados e põe o motivo.
  • internal/config/dependencies.go: seção dependencies (ponteiro; nil = não declarada, nada muda), validada no parse e governada pela política central (governedSections). Declarada, o padrão de gate.inconclusive passa a block (scannerEnabled).
  • internal/gate/dependencies.go: DependenciesContributor, nono do pipeline; inconclusivo segue ApplyInconclusiveMode; achados são informativos neste card (o gate é o AUR-527).
  • cmd/aurumcode/dependency_check.go: roda no fechamento da evidência (joinEvidence de --base e --pr), depois da seleção do provedor, sobre o mesmo checkout e recusa dos scanners (scanRoot/scanBlocked). Seção declarada e verificação que não rodou = dependencies_not_run.
  • Dockerfile: estágio que instala osv-scanner v2.0.0 por go install (verificado pelo checksum database do Go) e confere a versão.
  • Docs: seção nova em docs/configuration.md com link em docs/index.md; corrigida a frase velha da seção analysis_data que dizia que o AUR-495 consumiria a cópia OSV (a verificação usa a API ao vivo).

docs.title: Como cada AC/MUT é provado
docs.text:
tests/acceptance/AUR-495.sh (pacotes internal/dependencies, internal/gate, internal/config; base OSV = httptest servindo internal/dependencies/testdata/osv-fake.json; modelo e scanner falsos):

  • AC-001 TestAUR495AC001IntroducedAdvisory, TestAUR495AC001FindingLine (+ parse/governança da seção).
  • AC-002 TestAUR495AC002Preexisting.
  • AC-003 TestAUR495AC003Fixed.
  • AC-004 TestAUR495AC004UnknownFormatAndDivergence, TestAUR495AC004ScannerEvidenceKept (arquivo reconhecido e não apontado é lido; pacote omitido pelo modelo é inconclusivo).
  • AC-005 TestAUR495AC005Range.
  • AC-006 TestAUR495AC006SourceFailures (HTTP 503, scanner ausente, Date velho, sem modelo, modelo falhando), TestAUR495AC006InconclusiveFollowsPolicy.
  • AC-007 TestAUR495AC007Monorepo.
  • AC-008 TestAUR495AC008InventedDependencyDiscarded.
  • MUT-001: return nil, err da consulta vira return nil, nil (falha lida como lista vazia): AC-006 fica vermelho.
  • MUT-002: status = StatusPreexisting vira StatusIntroduced: AC-002 fica vermelho.

docs.title: Riscos e fora do escopo
docs.text:
• Código escrito sem compilar (regra do stream); a prova roda no fluxo único.
  • A severidade vem só da palavra da fonte; advisory sem ela é unknown e o gate (AUR-527) a conta no topo (falha fechada). Cálculo CVSS próprio fora.
  • Os flags do osv-scanner v2.0.0 (--all-packages, --recursive) e o source.path absoluto da saída JSON não foram executados aqui.
  • Arquivos fora dos paths do card: internal/dependencies (pacote novo), internal/gate (contribuidor), docs/architecture.md (pacote e pipeline), docs/index.md (link da seção nova).
  • Os avisos de cmd/aurumcode/dependency_check.go são só em pt-BR, fora do catálogo internal/i18n.
  • Inconclusivos esperados em PRs reais (falha fechada, documentados em docs/configuration.md): diff de manifestos acima de 256 KiB (dependencies_manifests_omitted) e osv-scanner --recursive acima de 120 s num repositório grande (dependencies_scanner_failed).

docs.title: Correções da revisão estática
docs.text:
• Saída do osv-scanner: só 0 e 1 trazem relatório; 128 ("no packages found", códigos de retorno documentados do osv-scanner) é extração vazia; qualquer outro código, tempo esgotado ou processo morto é dependencies_scanner_failed, mesmo com JSON (exitCode, TestScannerExitCodesAndRelativeRoot).
  • Raiz relativa (--repo .): filepath.Abs antes de casar os caminhos do relatório.
  • Quando o scanner lista o pacote, a versão e o ecossistema dele são os consultados (alignWithScanner, TestScannerVersionAndEcosystemWin).
  • Severidade pelo vetor CVSS v3 quando o banco não traz uma (cvss.go, fórmula da especificação FIRST; v4 fica unknown, TestCVSSSeverity).
  • Registros do mesmo advisory em bancos diferentes viram um (mergeAliases, TestAliasesMerged).
  • dependencies.scanner só nome no PATH ou caminho absoluto; osv_url e deps_dev_url só https (http em loopback) (TestDependenciesSourcesAndScannerValidated).
  • Linhas do gate e avisos da revisão no catálogo internal/i18n (pt-BR e en), detalhe do inconclusivo redigido (TestDependencyLinesFollowLanguage, TestDependencyNoticesRedactDetail).
  • Dockerfile: o estágio do osv-scanner fixa GOPROXY, GOSUMDB, GOFLAGS=-mod=readonly e GOTOOLCHAIN=local; a integridade é a do checksum database do Go sobre as fontes, em vez de um sha256 de binário de release.

docs.title: AUR-498 - Deterministic changelog and semver engine
docs.text: Status: implemented for the reconstruction. Package: internal/changelog. Profile owner: AUR-006. Upstream: AUR-490.

docs.title: Purpose and contract
docs.text:
internal/changelog turns the reviewed commit messages of a range into (a) the next semantic version and (b) a Markdown changelog entry. It is:

  • pure - only the standard library, no clocks, no random, no I/O;
  • offline - no network, no LLM, no git invocation, no shell-out;
  • deterministic - the same []Commit always renders byte-identical output;
  • read-only - it never writes the repository, never edits CHANGELOG.md, never creates a tag or release;
  • untrusted-input safe - commit text is data, not instructions. It is escaped before rendering, bounded in count and length, and can never change the computed bump or authorize publication.

The rendered entry is advisory. Publication (PR/CI/tag) is AUR-499.

docs.title: Public API
docs.text: Symbol Meaning type Commit struct { Subject, Body, Hash string } one reviewed commit; all fields untrusted type Kind string recognized Conventional Commit type, or KindUnknown type Classification struct { Kind, Scope, Description, Breaking, Conventional, Subject, Hash } parse result func Classify(Commit) Classification parse one commit func ClassifyCommits([]Commit) []Classification parse at most MaxCommits type Bump int BumpNone, BumpPatch, BumpMinor, BumpMajor func (Bump) String() string "none" | "patch" | "minor" | "major" type Version struct { Major, Minor, Patch int } release-line version func ParseVersion(string) (Version, error) strict [v]major.minor.patch func (Version) String() string major.minor.patch func NextVersion(Version, []Commit) (Version, Bump) bump table func Render(Version, []Commit) string deterministic Markdown entry

docs.title: Classification table (AC-001)
docs.text:
Subject grammar: type(scope)!: description.

  • type is one of the recognized kinds below; anything else (or a subject that does not match the grammar) is residual: KindUnknown, Conventional == false, and the subject on its own is never breaking.
  • scope is optional and may not contain parentheses.
  • ! immediately after the type or closing parenthesis marks breaking.
  • A body line beginning BREAKING CHANGE: or BREAKING-CHANGE: marks breaking, including on a residual subject, because it is a deliberate machine-readable declaration.
Type Kind Breaking-capable feat KindFeat yes fix KindFix yes perf KindPerf yes refactor KindRefactor yes docs KindDocs yes chore KindChore yes test KindTest yes build KindBuild yes ci KindCI yes style KindStyle yes anything else KindUnknown footer only

docs.title: Semver bump table (AC-002)
docs.text:
Let current = major.minor.patch. The highest applicable rule wins.

Condition New version Bump any breaking, major > 0 (major+1).0.0 major any breaking, major == 0 0.(minor+1).0 minor else any feat major.(minor+1).0 minor else any fix or perf major.minor.(patch+1) patch else unchanged none

The 0.x exception keeps an unstable line from jumping to 1.0.0 on a breaking change; it rises the minor instead. docs, chore, test, build, ci, style and residual subjects do not bump. Prose such as chore: release v9.0.0 does not bump: only the parsed commit structure counts.

docs.title: Section mapping and ordering (AC-003)
docs.text:
The section set and order are fixed:

Section Source ### Added feat ### Changed perf, refactor, and every residual subject ### Fixed fix ### Removed reserved; no current type maps to it

Removed has no mapped Conventional type in this card's catalog; its heading is still emitted so the structure is stable. Types that neither bump nor map (docs, chore, test, build, ci, style) are omitted from the body.

Inside a section, bullets keep input order; the same input always yields the same bytes. Example:

## 1.3.0

### Added

- feat(api): add endpoint (abc1234)

### Changed

- perf: speed up parser

- totally non conventional subject

### Fixed

- fix: correct off-by-one

### Removed

docs.title: Escaping and bounds (AC-004)
docs.text:
Commit text is untrusted. Before rendering:

  • <, >, & become <, >, &;
  • backticks, *, _, [, ] are backslash-escaped.

A subject like feat: <script>alert(1)</script> therefore renders as feat: <script>alert(1)</script> and cannot inject markup. The engine never executes or shells out to commit text.

Bounds:

Constant Value Effect MaxCommits 256 commits beyond the cap are ignored MaxSubjectLen 500 runes subject/hash clipped with ... MaxOutputLen 65536 bytes entry hard cap, with a truncation marker

Empty or nil input never panics: ClassifyCommits(nil) is empty, NextVersion returns BumpNone, and Render emits the version heading plus the four fixed section headings.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text: Publishing to a PR, writing CHANGELOG.md, creating tags or releases, calling an LLM, reading .git at runtime inside the sandbox. Those belong to AUR-499.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
tests/acceptance/AUR-498.sh runs the four behavioral selectors plus three mutations (all exits 0 and prints AUR-498/<selector>/pass), rejects an unknown selector with exit 64, and reports missing Go as infrastructure (exit 79). The mutation scenarios edit a writable staging copy of the package, never the repository.

  • MUT-001 neutralizes the fix/perf -> patch rule; AC-002 (semver) fails.
  • MUT-002 stops marking breaking; AC-002 fails.
  • MUT-003 removes renderer escaping; AC-004 (untrusted text) fails.

docs.title: AUR-499 - Publishing the suggested version and changelog entry
docs.text: Status: implemented for the reconstruction. Profile owner: AUR-006. Upstream: AUR-498 (engine), AUR-490 (shared review passes).

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
The review uses the AUR-498 internal/changelog engine over the reviewed commit messages to show the suggested next version and a Markdown changelog entry in the review report and, when publishing, in the pull request's review body. The GitHub Action also exposes the suggested version/entry as outputs so a consumer workflow can read them.

Nothing is tagged, written to CHANGELOG.md, or released by this card. Text from commits and pull requests is untrusted data: it is redacted through the same sink pr_history.go uses, escaped by the engine, bounded, never executed, and never authorizes a publication on its own. Publication stays behind the existing authorization gate.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
internal/config adds two review settings, both read from the base branch when reviewing a pull request (authoritative like every other review setting):

Setting Values Default Meaning review.changelog off/absent, on off Publish the suggested version and changelog entry. review.version [v]major.minor.patch 0.0.0 Current release line the engine bumps from. A published tag is never read (AUR-472/AUR-478 own that decision).

An unrecognized review.changelog value is a parse error, never a silent fallback. --changelog forces the feature on for a single run.

docs.title: Commit sources (AC-001)
docs.text:
• --pr reads the pull request title and body (githubclient.GetPullRequestMetadata) plus every page of the pull request's commit messages (githubclient.GetPullRequestCommits), all read-only. The title/body is folded into a synthetic first commit so the engine sees the whole narrative.
  • --base reads the local range base..HEAD through the read-only analyzer (analyzer.Repo.Commits), which uses git log when a git binary is present and a first-parent object walk otherwise.
  • A missing source (no metadata, no commits, an unreadable range, or a base version that does not parse) omits the section, appends a declared limitation to the report, and never crashes the review.

docs.title: Surfaces (AC-002)
docs.text: The shared pass buildChangelogSection (cmd/aurumcode/passes.go) redacts every commit field, runs changelog.NextVersion and changelog.Render, and render.ChangelogSection (internal/render) formats the block. Both --pr (published review body) and --base (stdout report) call that one function. The engine's entry is escaped, so a subject like <script>alert(1)</script> renders as <script>... and cannot inject markup.

docs.title: Action output (AC-003)
docs.text: action.yml declares a changelog input and version, changelog_bump and changelog outputs. When enabled, the entrypoint passes --changelog and points AURUMCODE_OUTPUT_FILE at a temporary file; the CLI writes the output in GitHub Actions' key=value/heredoc format, and the entrypoint appends it to $GITHUB_OUTPUT (never the deprecated ::set-output). .github/workflows/review.yml mounts that file and re-exports the keys as job outputs.

docs.title: Trust boundary (AC-004)
docs.text: Commit and pull request text is data. Every field passes through redaction.Filter.Redact before the engine sees it, so a registered canary in a subject is replaced with the sink marker. An injection-style subject is escaped by the engine and only ever classifies as its Conventional Commit type; it cannot change a rule, a severity, --fail-on, or the publication gate.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text: Creating a tag or release, writing CHANGELOG.md in the consumer repository, choosing the bump from a published tag, and any new provider.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
tests/acceptance/AUR-499.sh runs four behavioral selectors and three mutations, rejects an unknown selector with exit 64, and reports missing Go as infrastructure (exit 79). Mutations run on a writable staging copy, never the repository.

  • AC-001 PR metadata/commits yield the section; missing metadata omits it with a limitation; --base reads the local range.
  • AC-002 the published body and --base report contain the version and entry, and both paths call the shared pass.
  • AC-003 action.yml declares the outputs and the entrypoint fills $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
  • AC-004 a canary secret is redacted; an injection subject is escaped and does not alter the bump or classification.
  • MUT-001 makes the body append a no-op -> AC-001/AC-002 fail.
  • MUT-002 deletes the Action outputs -> AC-003 fails.
  • MUT-003 echoes the raw subject -> AC-004 fails.

docs.title: AUR-500: perfis de revisor prontos
docs.text: Documento histórico do board. Para uso atual, consulte o guia do produto.

docs.title: O que é
docs.text: internal/reviewprofile é o sistema de perfis de revisor embutidos e versionados: solid, seguranca e performance. Um perfil é um preset determinístico, nunca um plugin: ele declara apenas o enfoque da review e as famílias de regra habilitadas, e é resolvido em processo. Nada no pacote lê arquivo de perfil, abre socket, executa conteúdo de perfil ou deixa um perfil carregar uma instrução.

docs.title: Seleção
docs.text:
Um perfil é escolhido por configuração do repositório ou pela flag da review. A flag vence a configuração; uma seleção vazia é o caso zero-config:

res, err := reviewprofile.Resolve(reviewprofile.Selection{
    Config: "performance", // .aurumcode/config.yml
    Flag:   "seguranca",   // --perfil / flag da review
})
// res.Profile.Name == "seguranca"
// res.Declared     == "profile: seguranca (v1)"

A resolução declara qual perfil entrou (Result.Declared). Um nome desconhecido é um erro nomeado (ErrUnknownProfile) retornado antes de qualquer chamada ao modelo. Uma seleção ausente devolve Applied=false e o chamador mantém o comportamento atual byte a byte.

docs.title: A fronteira que o perfil nunca cruza
docs.text:
Um perfil pode definir somente enfoque e famílias habilitadas. Ele nunca pode:

  1. mudar severidade de achado;
  2. afrouxar o gate de --fail-on;
  3. desligar a redação de segredos;
  4. mudar o teto de custo;
  5. desligar a passagem de segurança determinística.

Uma definição (Spec) que nomeie qualquer uma dessas cláusulas é recusada em Compile com um ErrRefusedClause que cita a cláusula recusada. O preset resolvido (Effective) fixa essas fronteiras para todo perfil embutido: passagem de segurança ligada, redação ligada, severidade/--fail-on intocados, teto de custo inalterado.

_, err := reviewprofile.Compile([]byte("name: evil\nsecurity_pass: false\n"))
// errors.Is(err, reviewprofile.ErrRefusedClause) == true
// err.Error() cita "security_pass"

A recusa é fail-closed: Compile percorre a árvore YAML crua antes de ligar a Spec, normaliza cada chave (minúsculas; sem -, _, .) e recusa qualquer grafia alternativa (security-pass, Security_Pass, security.pass, redact-secrets, no_redaction, disable_redaction, failOn, cost-cap, Severity, …), inclusive aliases YAML, security: <desligado> e chaves de merge (<<: &m {security_pass: false}), que o yaml.v3 resolveria depois do scan. A ligação usa KnownFields(true), então uma chave desconhecida restante também falha. O preset global é imutável: Builtin e Resolve devolvem uma cópia independente de Effective.Families, de modo que mutar a fatia devolvida não corrompe o embutido.

Os três embutidos são Specs de código compilados no init: um embutido que carregasse uma cláusula proibida derrubaria o binário no start (mustBuiltins), de modo que o programa não inicia com um preset que viole a fronteira.

docs.title: Determinismo e versão
docs.text: Cada perfil embutido declara um identificador de versão. Profile.Signature() cobre nome, versão, enfoque, famílias e instruções: a mesma entrada produz a mesma assinatura e a mesma lista de regras/instruções habilitadas.

docs.title: Não-objetivos
docs.text: Perfis remotos ou baixados, perfis como plugin executável, e perfis que alterem o vocabulário de severidade (isso é AUR-471).

docs.title: AUR-501 — Cada capacidade entregue tem tutorial e demonstração reproduzível
Medido antes (auditoria por leitura)
docs.text:
Capacidades de docs/configuration.md e de docs/index.md contra demo/tutoriais/*/run.sh (casos CASOS) e docs/tutorials/*.md:

Capacidade Tutorial antes Revisão, prompts/skills, provedores, opções públicas, PR grande revisao, skills, provedores Política central, gate, gate.sources, gate.triage, exceções, auditoria/SARIF politica-central, gate, excecoes, auditoria-sarif SAST, segredos, SBOM/Dependency-Track, assinatura, xBOM, analysis_data sast, segredos, sbom-dependency-track, assinatura, xbom, dados-de-analise Deliberação, qualquer linguagem, reaproveitamento, agente (MCP), extensão, benchmark, operação um tutorial cada Changelog obrigatório (AUR-509) e sugestão de changelog nenhum Realimentação da política (AUR-532) nenhum Memória de revisão (review.memory) nenhum Status do CI no parecer nenhum Release oficial (AUR-510) capacidade não entregue

Invariante medida em todos os 21 tutoriais: o conjunto CASOS do run.sh é igual ao conjunto expected/<caso>.txt. A frase de RESULTADO: nem sempre é literal no run.sh (53 de 204 vêm de variáveis ou helpers), por isso a evidência rastreada é a linha do expected/.

docs.title: Decisão
docs.text:
• Tutorial novo changelog (pt-BR, padrão existente: run.sh com _lib/tutorial.sh, repo-exemplo/ com base e overlays, fixture-llm.json, expected/, docs/tutorials/changelog.md com blocos arquivo/saida, "Quando falha" e "Problemas comuns"). Casos: entrada-valida, consolidar-release, sugestao-separada, pr-desliga-o-modo, log-de-agente, falha-entrada-ausente. Não executado: o expected/ foi escrito pela leitura de internal/changelog e cmd/aurumcode/cmd_changelog.go; o fluxo final grava out/ e a seção "Como fica" (gerada por scripts/docs/capturas.sh).
  • Tutorial novo realimentacao (mesmo padrão), com GitHub falso próprio (demo/tutoriais/realimentacao/github-falso.py, subindo dentro do container por dentro.sh com rede none, estado do caso em .estado/) e o provedor falso (fixture-propostas.json). Casos: plano-sem-publicar, publica-uma-pr, rodada-sem-novidade, medir-melhora, medir-regressao, falha-sem-modelo. Os ids dos sinais no expected/ foram calculados pela regra de internal/feedback/signal.go (sha256 de tipo, repo e id da fonte).
  • Tutorial novo memoria (review.memory): a memória local guarda a observação (cache apontado por XDG_CACHE_HOME para dentro do repositório do caso), a segunda rodada a recebe no prompt (AURUMCODE_PROMPT_CAPTURE), off não grava, modo desconhecido é relatado e a revisão segue.
  • Mapa rastreado tests/fixtures/tutorials/mapa.tsv: uma linha por caso público (capacidade, tutorial, caso, comando, fixture, expected/, a linha RESULTADO: prometida, jornada do AC-003, estado). Capacidades sem tutorial aparecem como planejado com o card ou a pendência: release (AUR-510) e status do CI.
  • docs/index.md liga o tutorial; docs/tutorials/README.md e demo/tutoriais/README.md ganham a linha do tutorial.
  • docs/site/index.html (legado) não foi alterado: o site publicado é o MkDocs, que já injeta docs/tutorials/*.md no nav (scripts/docs/hooks.py).

docs.title: Fora dos paths do card
docs.text: demo/tutoriais/changelog/, demo/tutoriais/realimentacao/, demo/tutoriais/memoria/ e demo/tutoriais/README.md (pedido explícito do coordenador: os tutoriais seguem o padrão demo/tutoriais), docs/index.md (link do tutorial).

docs.title: Como cada cenário é provado (tests/acceptance/AUR-501.sh, só bash)
docs.text:
• AC-001: todo caso de todo run.sh está no mapa como entregue; cada linha entregue aponta para doc, run.sh, caso em CASOS, expected/ com a linha prometida e comando que existe no registro de subcomandos; planejado sem tutorial traz o motivo.
  • AC-002: cada caso entregue afirma exit_code= e RESULTADO:; o caso sem provedor (TUT_FIXTURE=none) existe e o texto explica a análise determinística; tutorial que roda review identifica a fixture do modelo.
  • AC-003: as jornadas review, contexto, memória, sugestão/fix, publicação, changelog e release estão no mapa; as entregues têm "Quando falha" ou "Problemas comuns".
  • AC-004: nenhuma forma de credencial em docs/tutorials e demo/tutoriais; nenhum go build/test/run em bloco bash dos tutoriais; o job de documentação roda em pull_request.
  • MUT-001: tirar revisao/fix do mapa → case-missing-from-map:revisao/fix; trocar a promessa de changelog/entrada-valida → promised-output-changed.

docs.title: Limites
docs.text:
• O expected/ do tutorial novo é uma previsão por leitura; o fluxo final roda run.sh all, grava out/ e corrige divergência, se houver.
  • Status do CI e release ficam como planejados no mapa: não há tutorial deles nesta entrega (release depende de uma versão publicada).

docs.title: AUR-502: team-defined reviewer profiles and multi-agent review
Outcome
docs.text: The team declares its own reviewer profiles in a versioned repository file, .aurumcode/profiles.yml, and can run more than one profile in the same review. Findings from every profile merge deterministically, each one naming the profile that produced it, and the output declares which profiles entered. Profiles remain presets over review emphasis and enabled rule families.

docs.title: AC-001 Team definition
docs.text:
.aurumcode/profiles.yml is a profiles: sequence. Each entry declares:

profiles:
  - name: release
    version: "2"                # optional, defaults to "1"
    emphasis: upstream compatibility
    families: [quality, performance]
    instructions: Confira contrato e custo de rollout.

A missing file is the zero-config case. A file that exists must fail closed: an entry without a name, without emphasis/families/instructions, a repeated name, a name that shadows a built-in, or an unknown key is an error naming the problem. A selected name that resolves to neither a built-in nor a team profile is ErrUnknownProfile, returned before any model call.

docs.title: AC-002 Multi-agent
docs.text:
ResolveAll(Selection{Names: [...]}, team) resolves every name in order and declares them. Findings are represented by reviewprofile.Finding; each carry a Profile. MergeFindings collapses duplicates to the first profile in declaration order, keeps the source profile on every finding, and sorts by a stable content key (file, line, rule, message), so the same input always yields the same bytes.

At the CLI seam, --perfis a,b (or its --profile single alias) selects profiles for aurumcode review --base; the repository review.profiles list is the default and the flag wins. When more than one profile is selected each profile gets its own model pass, with its emphasis and instructions prepended to the prompt, and the findings merge. --perfis/--profile are refused with --pr rather than silently ignored.

docs.title: AC-003 Frontier
docs.text: A profile -- built-in or team -- can never change finding severity, relax --fail-on, disable secret redaction, change the cost cap or disable the deterministic security pass. Compile/LoadTeam refuse a definition that names any such clause (ErrRefusedClause, naming the clause), including through YAML merge keys and aliases, using the same fail-closed raw scan AUR-500 introduced. The cost tracker is shared across profile passes, so adding a profile cannot raise the ceiling, and the security pass still runs after the model.

docs.title: AC-004 Compatibility
docs.text: No team file, no review.profiles, no flag: behavior is byte-for-byte AUR-500/today. A single selected profile resolves to the exact same Profile.Signature() AUR-500's Resolve produced. product_owner joins solid, seguranca and performance as a built-in.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text: Remote or downloaded profiles, executable profile plugins, and any profile that changes the severity vocabulary (AUR-471).

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
bash tests/acceptance/AUR-502.sh all

Selectors: all, AC-001, AC-002, AC-003, AC-004, MUT-001, MUT-002. An unknown selector exits 64; a missing Go runtime exits 79.

MUT-001 ignores the selection and always adds profiles (AC-002/AC-004 go RED). MUT-002 neutralizes the raw clause scan so a team profile can disable a boundary (AC-003 goes RED).

docs.title: AUR-503 -- Command injection does not accuse a comment or prose
Outcome
docs.text: The command-injection branches AUR-486 delivered no longer accuse a textual mention. A exec.Command, Process.Start, Invoke-Expression/iex or eval written inside a comment (//, #, /* */, --) or a string literal produces no finding, and eval := ... / eval = ... (a declaration or assignment) produces none either -- while the real invocation of each branch is still found.

docs.title: Measured finding (2026-09-15)
docs.text:
AUR-486's reviewer reproduced, in the branches AUR-486 added, the same false-positive class AUR-486's round 2 fixed only in sh -c/SQL. These lines all produced a security/command-injection finding before this card:

// exec.Command("sh","-c","ping "+host)
// Process.Start("cmd.exe","/c ping "+host)
# Invoke-Expression "ping $host"
Write-Host "Invoke-Expression is unsafe"
# iex is dangerous
eval := compute()

The AUR-462 rule applies: a false positive in a merge gate teaches the team to disable the gate.

docs.title: The fix
docs.text:
A line regexp alone cannot decide whether a token sits inside a comment or a string literal. The naive anchor -- start of line or a ;/|/& separator -- both misses real invocations embedded in expressions and still fires on // foo; exec.Command(...), whose ; is inside the comment. The shipped fix therefore splits the decision in two:

  1. internal/review/rules/security.yml keeps every AUR-486 branch's token and argument shape unanchored (the exact bodies AUR-486 shipped). The Go exec.Command shell branch, both C# Process.Start branches and PowerShell Invoke-Expression/iex match the token anywhere on the added line. This is what keeps a real invocation reachable in every expression context: x := exec.Command(...), if err := exec.Command(...), out, err := exec.Command(...), return exec.Command(...), cmd := exec.Command(...), var p = Process.Start(...), if (x) { Process.Start(...) }, $r = Invoke-Expression $payload, $r = iex $payload. The two branches AUR-486's round 2 already anchored (^\s*(?:ba)?sh\s+-c and the SQL-by-shell branch) are untouched.

  2. internal/review/securitypass.go adds the context filter. The match test is re.FindStringIndex(body) instead of re.MatchString(body), and a security/command-injection match whose first byte is not marked CODE by codeMask is dropped. codeMask is a line-local lexical state machine that marks the bytes of # comments, // comments, -- comments (only after whitespace, so x-- is not one), /* */ spans, and "/'/backtick spans as non-code; both the opening marker byte and the whole span are marked, so a match starting on the marker is dropped too. The filter is scoped to security/command-injection only, so security/hardcoded-secret -- whose true positives are legitimately inside string literals -- is unchanged.

bash eval additionally distinguishes invocation from declaration: the branch requires a whitespace-separated argument that is neither : nor = (\beval\s+[^:=\s]), so eval "ping $1" and eval $cmd still fire while eval := compute() and eval = compute() do not.

docs.title: Acceptance
docs.text:
• AC-001: each branch (exec.Command, Process.Start, Invoke-Expression/iex, eval) mentioned inside a comment (//, #, /* */, --) or a string literal produces no finding, including // foo; exec.Command(...).
  • AC-002: the real invocation of each branch is still found (Go exec.Command("sh","-c",...) as a bare statement and in expression context, C# Process.Start concatenation and shell file name, PowerShell Invoke-Expression/iex, sh -c/bash -c, and SQL by shell interpolation).
  • AC-003: eval := ... / eval = ... produce no finding; eval "ping $1" / eval $cmd do.

Selectors: unit tests/unit/AUR-503.go::TestAUR503; integration tests/integration/AUR-503.go::IntegrationAUR503; acceptance tests/acceptance/AUR-503.sh, which also runs the unit and integration bridges under all.

docs.title: Mutations
docs.text:
• MUT-001: remove the command-injection context guard in internal/review/securitypass.go (rule.ID == "security/command-injection" && !codeMask(body)[loc[0]] -> ... && false). The comment mentions -- including // foo; exec.Command(...) -- are re-accused; if they are not, the mutation did not take effect and AC-001 would be a false green.
  • MUT-002: over-restrict the Go branch to column zero (\bexec\.Command -> ^exec\.Command). The real, tab-indented statement and every expression-context invocation are lost; if they survive, the restriction did not take effect and AC-002 would be a false green.

Both are exercised by tests/acceptance/AUR-503.sh, each asserting a sibling branch (bash eval, C# Process.Start) is untouched so the mutant is proven specific rather than a blanket disablement.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text:
• No AST and no semantic analysis: the pass stays a deterministic matcher over the added lines plus a line-local lexical mask.
  • No existing pattern is loosened; the AUR-462/AUR-481 true positives stay unchanged.

docs.title: Known limitations, accepted deliberately
docs.text:
