Sem eles, o Go tenta resolve-los como modulo e o GOPROXY=off recusa. Nao ha modulo externo faltando; go.mod/go.sum nao mudam.

Corrigido o build, IntegrationAUR439 mostrou uma segunda camada de defasagem, so em tests/integration/AUR-439.go (o e2e ja estava alinhado):

  • O fake respondia o DIFF em GET /repos/dono/projeto/pulls/42 para qualquer Accept. Desde o AUR-504, --check ancora o status no head.sha dos metadados JSON desse endpoint; sem ele o produto falha fechado (decoding pull request metadata, 0 status POST).
  • As respostas de modelo sinteticas nao traziam impact, evidence e verification; o gate de escopo e evidencia descarta o achado (grave virava sucesso).
  • O contrato de zero achados no --pr e a linha 0 comentario(s) publicado(s) mais o status; No issues found. e do --base (AUR-490), e o comentario-resumo sempre e postado (1 status + 1 resumo).

docs.title: Correcao
docs.text:
tests/acceptance/AUR-439.sh: copy "$root" cmd internal pkg (inteiros, nunca lista enumerada) e GOCACHE respeitado quando ja exportado. Nenhuma asserção, mutação, selector ou exit code mudou.

tests/integration/AUR-439.go: o fake devolve o diff quando o Accept pede diff e, senao, {"number":42,"title":"t","body":"b","head":{"sha":...}} com o head definido por subteste (o mesmo valor do GITHUB_SHA que o teste ja afirmava no caminho do status); fixtures com impact/evidence/verification; o subteste sem SHA espera a recusa head SHA (AUR-504, igual ao e2e); zero achados espera a linha de resumo e 2 POSTs. As mesmas propriedades continuam afirmadas (grave nunca sai 0, estado failure/success, um unico status, token somente-leitura sem POST, determinismo).

docs.title: Prova
docs.text: tests/acceptance/AUR-544.sh: AC-001 roda AUR-439.sh all e exige exit 0; AC-002 confere esta spec; AC-001-MUT-001 reverte a copia inteira para a lista antiga numa copia de trabalho e exige exit 1 com build_failed e cannot find module providing package. Selector desconhecido sai com 64.

docs.title: AUR-545: achado com evidencia fora das linhas alteradas tem destino definido
O que foi medido antes
docs.text:
• internal/review/scope.go (filterModelIssues) checava o escopo antes de qualquer prova: todo achado do modelo fora das linhas adicionadas ou removidas era descartado e contado em OutsideAddedLines (issues_rejected_by_scope, scope_discard_warning), mesmo com evidencia, impacto e verificacao completos.
  • Consequencia: o comentario geral de PR prometido pelo AUR-438 era inalcancavel para achados do modelo. bash tests/e2e/AUR-438.sh no container terminava com AUR-438/AC-001/missing_general_finding (exit 1), e tests/acceptance/AUR-542.sh fixava esse vermelho em red_scripts.
  • scope_test.go fixava o comportamento oposto ao AUR-438: um achado em other.go e os casos "wrong coordinate space", "unrelated file" etc. so podiam ser "nao mantidos", sem distinguir descarte de destino geral.
  • O gate da politica le apenas Review.Issues mais Extra (internal/gate, IssuesForGate); --fail-on, o veredito, o status --check, o SARIF e a auditoria derivam da mesma lista.

docs.title: Decisao
docs.text: Um achado do modelo fora das linhas alteradas que traz a prova completa (evidencia, impacto e verificacao nao vazios), um caminho relativo valido e uma regra do catalogo citada vira comentario geral: nunca inline, nunca entra em result.Issues, logo nunca conta para o gate da politica, nunca conta para --fail-on, nunca muda o veredito para reprovar, nunca entra no SARIF nem na auditoria. Achado fora do diff sem essa prova continua descartado e contado em issues_rejected_by_scope / scope_discard_warning, com o mesmo texto de antes. Um comentario geral fora do diff nunca conta para o gate.

docs.title: Motivo
docs.text:
• O modelo le contexto do repositorio de proposito; um defeito real em codigo nao tocado mas afetado pela mudanca (um chamador que quebra) e informacao util ao revisor humano. Descartar com prova completa perdia essa informacao sem ganho de precisao.
  • O risco que o filtro de escopo existe para evitar e o achado ganhar autoridade sobre codigo nao tocado. Essa autoridade so existe quando o achado conta para o gate, o veredito ou e ancorado na linha. Como o achado geral fica fora de result.Issues, ele nao tem nenhuma das tres.
  • O requisito de evidencia nao foi afrouxado: a prova exigida e a mesma do achado inline, a citacao de regra passa pelo mesmo gate de regras (rejeicao soma em issues_rejected_without_rule), e o filtro do marcador de redacao (AUR-598) continua rodando antes do escopo.

docs.title: O que mudou
docs.text:
• internal/review/scope.go: filterModelIssues devolve kept, outside e o resumo de descarte; so roteia para outside com prova completa e caminho normalizado valido.
  • internal/review/outside_diff.go: canal outside_diff_findings (chave de metadado do motor, JSON de types.ReviewIssue), OutsideDiffFindings para os consumidores. O motor sempre reescreve ou remove a chave depois dos gates, entao um valor forjado na resposta do modelo nao sobrevive.
  • internal/review/reviewer.go: applyGates separa o canal e passa os achados gerais pelo gate de regras (citedOutsideDiff); annotateResult grava o canal.
  • internal/review/batch_merge.go: lotes concatenam o canal.
  • cmd/aurumcode/outside_diff_output.go: --pr publica cada achado geral como comentario de PR (corpo com arquivo:linha), nos modos separado e review; --base lista o achado com o marcador -- fora das linhas alteradas (comentario geral; nao conta para o gate).
  • tests/e2e/AUR-438.sh: fixture ganha um terceiro achado fora do diff sem evidencia que nunca pode ser publicado; contagens de POST atualizadas para o comentario de resumo (que o produto passou a publicar depois que o script foi escrito) e ordem de publicacao checada entre execucoes.
  • tests/acceptance/AUR-542.sh: AUR-438 saiu de red_scripts para fixed_scripts; nao resta script "vermelho esperado".

Limitacao conhecida: o cache de revisao por arquivo guarda apenas result.Issues; num acerto de cache o comentario geral nao e republicado (comportamento conservador: nunca adiciona achado que conte).

docs.title: Como cada AC/MUT foi provado
docs.text:
tests/acceptance/AUR-545.sh (selectors all, AC-001, AC-002, AC-003, MUT-001; seletor desconhecido sai 64):

  • AC-001: esta spec tem Decisao e Motivo; scope_test.go (TestFilterModelIssuesRoutesProvedOutsideFindingsAndRejectsUnproved, TestDeletionRegressionUsesOldSideWithoutAdmittingUntouchedCode) e tests/e2e/AUR-438.sh (AUR-438/AC-001/E2EAUR438/ok) passam.
  • AC-002: TestOutsideDiffAC002UnprovedFindingStillDiscarded (issues_rejected_by_scope=1, warning presente), TestFilterModelIssuesNeverRoutesOutsideFindingWithoutFullProof e a checagem unproved_outside_finding_published do e2e.
  • AC-003: TestOutsideDiffAC003ProvedFindingNeverCountsForTheGate (o motor nunca poe o achado em result.Issues) e TestOutsideDiffFindingNeverCountsForTheGate (cmd/aurumcode): a sessao --pr real, contra um GitHub falso em processo, com um achado error provado em app.go:1 (linha nao alterada) e --fail-on error, sai 0, publica o achado como comentario geral com app.go:1 no corpo, nunca inline, e o parecer fica **Verdict:** Approve. (O selado nao tem git, por isso a prova usa o caminho --pr, nao --base.)
  • MUT-001: a mutacao result.Issues = append(result.Issues, outcome.outsideDiff...) faz o teste do motor falhar ("a finding outside the diff reached result.Issues") e a sessao --pr sair 3 sob --fail-on error.

Ultimas linhas reais (container go-shared):

MUT-001 red: an outside-diff finding counted for the gate: exit=3
AUR-545/all/pass

docs.title: Medido antes
docs.text:
• internal/prompt/templates/review.md nao ensina line_comments: o unico exemplo JSON tem issues como lista de achados, e a palavra so aparecia como parte de inline_comments (configuracao de publicacao). grep -rnw line_comments fora de internal/prompt, specs e tests/e2e/AUR-459.sh so acha o campo legado LineComments de pkg/types.ReviewResult.
  • Nenhum provedor (internal/llm), fixture (tests/fixtures), tutorial (demo/tutoriais, docs/tutorials) ou workflow depende de line_comments. O unico produtor era a fixture do proprio tests/e2e/AUR-459.sh, e tests/acceptance/AUR-459.sh ja estava aposentado (exit 69, AUR-586).
  • adoptLineComments (parser) convertia cada entrada em types.ReviewIssue sem evidence, impact nem verification; o gate de evidencia descartava todas (AUR-541/AUR-542). hasFindingsList aceitava line_comments como lista de achados, entao {"line_comments":[...]} parecia uma resposta valida.
  • O campo pkg/types.ReviewResult.LineComments (fora dos paths do card) continuava sendo preenchido pelo json.Unmarshal, e internal/render e o merge de lotes ainda o liam.

docs.title: Decisao
docs.text:
line_comments sai do parser. Ensinar o formato com evidencia criaria uma segunda forma de achado ao lado de issues, que e exatamente o defeito do AUR-459 (duas formas, o modelo escolhe a errada). Remover e mais simples e mantem a falha fechada:

  • internal/prompt/parser_line_comments.go foi reescrito: a conversao saiu; discardLineComments limpa result.LineComments e anuncia o descarte em Metadata["parse_discard_warning"], que o CLI ja imprime no stderr.
  • parser_validate.go::hasFindingsList so aceita issues (findingsListKey). Resposta so com line_comments vira erro de validacao missing_issues (revisao inconclusiva), nunca "No issues found.".
  • parser.go::acceptedReviewFields == canonicalReviewFields (sem line_comments); template e parser concordam.
  • tests/e2e/AUR-459.sh aposentado: imprime a justificativa e sai 69 (seletor desconhecido continua 64).
  • Observacao do AUR-543: ReviewChangeScope virou funcao exportada que delega para a var nao exportada reviewChangeScope (seam so dos testes do pacote); aur543_test.go troca a var nao exportada.

docs.title: Prova
docs.text:
• AC-001 (bash tests/acceptance/AUR-546.sh AC-001): spec com a decisao, template sem line_comments, nenhum adoptLineComments em internal/, e2e 459 sai 69 citando esta spec e 64 em seletor desconhecido, e os testes TestLineCommentsIsNeitherTaughtNorAccepted, TestReviewTemplateMatchesParser, TestAcceptedReviewFieldsAreConsumed verdes.
  • AC-002 (... AC-002): testes de unidade (resposta so com line_comments, com e sem rule_id, e missing_issues; ao lado de issues nada chega a Issues nem LineComments e o aviso e gravado) e o binario real contra tests/fixtures/repos/git-demo: so line_comments -> exit != 0 com validation_failed, sem "No issues found." nem o achado; misto -> exit 0, sem o achado no stdout, 1 line comment(s) ignored no stderr.
  • MUT-001 (... MUT-001): numa copia, hasFindingsList volta a aceitar line_comments e discardLineComments volta a converter as entradas em achados sem evidencia; compila e AC-002 fica vermelho (TestLineCommentsOnlyReplyIsInconclusive, TestLineCommentsBesideIssuesAreDroppedAndAnnounced).

docs.title: Execucao real
docs.text:
Container compartilhado (.board/bin/go-shared):

  • bash tests/acceptance/AUR-546.sh AC-001 -> AUR-546/AC-001/pass (rc 0)
  • bash tests/acceptance/AUR-546.sh AC-002 -> AUR-546/AC-002/pass (rc 0)
  • bash tests/acceptance/AUR-546.sh MUT-001 -> --- FAIL: TestLineCommentsOnlyReplyIsInconclusive, --- FAIL: TestLineCommentsBesideIssuesAreDroppedAndAnnounced (e TestAnswerWithoutFindingsListIsInconclusive), depois AUR-546/MUT-001/pass (rc 0: a mutacao compilou e ficou vermelha)
  • bash tests/acceptance/AUR-546.sh bogus -> AUR-546/bogus/unknown-selector (rc 64)
  • bash tests/acceptance/AUR-543.sh AC-001 e AC-002 -> pass (rc 0) com o seam reviewChangeScope nao exportado
  • go vet ./... && go test -p 1 ./... -> rc 0; gofmt -l vazio
  • ./.board/bin/oci-run --profile go-unit-offline-v1 --card AUR-546 -> AUR-546/all/pass, exit_code: 0
  • Tutoriais: run.sh all nos 21 diretorios com a imagem aurum-tutoriais:aur546 (construida desta arvore), todos rc 0, e run.sh --check rc 0 em todos; scripts/docs/capturas.sh regravou docs/assets/capturas (251 imagens).
  • bash tests/acceptance/AUR-542.sh AC-001 -> AUR-542/AC-001/infrastructure/e2e-infra:AUR-459:69 (rc 79), ver pendencia.

docs.title: Pendencia fora dos paths
docs.text: tests/acceptance/AUR-542.sh AC-001 fixa tests/e2e/AUR-459.sh como vermelho com a tag gate-open-on-converted-finding e trata exit 69 como infra. Com o e2e aposentado ele passa a sair 79 (e2e-infra:AUR-459:69). O script nao e path deste card; precisa de um card de acompanhamento que tire o AUR-459 da lista red_scripts (o AUR-573 executa o AUR-542 no grupo slow).

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text: Reverter os commits do card nos paths internal/prompt, tests/e2e/AUR-459.sh, tests/acceptance/AUR-546.sh e esta spec.

docs.title: AUR-547: aceites de cards done nao copiam pacotes removidos do produto
O que foi medido
docs.text:
AUR-542 (done) ja tinha medido, para tests/e2e/*.sh, que cmd/regenerate-docs, internal/pipeline e internal/documentation/* foram removidos do produto pelo commit 670c7f6 ("Focus AurumCode on code review", 2026-09-12) -- um pivo de produto deliberado e anterior, que o registro de entrega do AUR-490 (done) ja trata como fato assentado. Este card estende a mesma auditoria e a mesma correcao para tests/acceptance/AUR-443.sh, AUR-448.sh, AUR-449.sh, AUR-458.sh, AUR-466.sh e AUR-481.sh, e para tests/integration/AUR-449.go e tests/unit/AUR-449.go (AC-003).

Metodo: para cada script, a lista de pacotes copiados em stage_source() foi substituida pela resposta real de go list -deps ./cmd/aurumcode (rodado no container go-shared contra este worktree), filtrada aos pacotes github.com/Mpaape/AurumCode/internal/* e arredondada ao diretorio dono -- a mesma tecnica e a mesma lista final que o AUR-542 ja usou em tests/e2e/AUR-459.sh:

internal/analysis internal/analyzer internal/apply internal/changelog
internal/config internal/context internal/git internal/llm internal/memory
internal/prompt internal/render internal/review internal/reviewprofile
internal/security internal/testgen

Isso remove cmd/regenerate-docs, internal/documentation/* e internal/pipeline (que nao existem mais -- ls internal neste worktree confirma) e acrescenta pacotes que faltavam na lista original de cada script (internal/analysis, internal/apply, internal/changelog, internal/context, internal/memory, internal/render, internal/reviewprofile, internal/testgen), que o binario de hoje tambem importa e que a lista antiga, escrita antes desses pacotes existirem, nunca cobriu -- a materializacao estava incompleta nos dois sentidos, nao só excedente.

Cada script foi executado isolado, sem edicao, para medir a causa antes de qualquer correcao; depois de cada candidata, reexecutado para confirmar o novo resultado -- nunca inferido.

docs.title: AUR-443: infraestrutura corrigida; AC-001 fica vermelho por tests/unit/AUR-443.go e tests/integration/AUR-443.go, fora dos paths deste card
docs.text:
Causa. Teste desatualizado contra o AUR-490 e o pivo 670c7f6, exatamente como o AUR-542 ja decidiu para o tests/e2e/AUR-443.sh irmao -- mas os dois arquivos que ainda falham (tests/unit/AUR-443.go, tests/integration/AUR-443.go) ficam fora dos paths deste card. docs.title: AUR-448: infraestrutura corrigida; AC-001 fica vermelho por um gate de evidencia mais novo que a propria fixture do script nao satisfaz
docs.text:
Causa. Depois de corrigir a materializacao e o cenario 1 (mesma causa do AUR-443/AUR-490: "sem provedor" agora exit 0, stdout nao mais vazio -- a mensagem completa continua presente, impressa como segunda linha pelo conserto do AUR-542 em cmd/aurumcode/main.go) e os cenarios 2 e 4 (a comparacao exata de stdout precisa ser so da ULTIMA linha, pelo mesmo motivo do AUR-443), o script avanca e falha no cenario 3 (mixed.json, descarte misto): medido diretamente, a resposta do motor hoje e aurumcode review: 3 finding(s) descartado(s) pelo gate de escopo e evidencia: 3 sem evidencia concreta -- em portugues, descartando TODOS os 3 achados, inclusive o grounded com rule_id valido -- em vez de aurumcode review: 2 finding(s) discarded: 1 with no rule_id, 1 citing an unknown rule_id (security/definitely-not-a-rule). O gate que o AUR-448 testava (so citacao de rule_id, em internal/review.enforceRuleCitations) foi superado por um gate mais novo e mais estrito (internal/review/scope.go, "gate de escopo e evidencia", que exige Evidence/Impact/Verification em todo achado -- o mesmo gate que o AUR-542 ja documentou investigando tests/e2e/AUR-459.sh). Fica vermelho, com a causa medida acima, nao mascarado.

AC-001 para hoje em AUR-448/AC-001/s3-grounded-finding-missing no cenario 3 -- o gate de evidencia descarta ate o achado fundamentado antes mesmo do cenario 4 ser alcancado.

Correcao da secao anterior desta mesma spec (revisao independente, B2): a frase "cenarios 1, 2 e 4 corrigidos" estava errada -- o cenario 4 nunca chega a rodar dentro de AC-001 porque o cenario 3 falha primeiro. docs.title: AUR-548 — Semgrep entra no gate como SAST multilinguagem
Status
docs.text:
Implemented in internal/analysis/semgrep.go (the Semgrep adapter), internal/config/sast.go (quality_gates.sast), internal/config/central.go (central-policy precedence) and cmd/aurumcode/aur548.go (runSASTPass, applySASTGate), wired into both cmd/aurumcode/main.go's runReview (--base) and cmd/aurumcode/pr.go's runPRReview (--pr). Behavior proof: cmd/aurumcode/aur548_test.go::TestAUR548* (including the --pr cases, driven through runPRReview with the same httptest GitHub mock pattern aur537_test.go/aur515_test.go already use); acceptance: tests/acceptance/AUR-548.sh.

--pr's own scan target is the verified checkout, never the wrong tree. runPRReview reuses AUR-515/536's own verification exactly as computed for the codebase-context pass (codebaseContextMismatch + verifiedCleanCheckoutReason, mismatch/verifiedDir in pr.go): when the local checkout is confirmed to be the pull request's own head commit (same repository, same HEAD, clean tree), Semgrep scans that exact, verified directory. When it is not — a different repository, a divergent HEAD, an unclean tree, or simply unverifiable — Semgrep is never invoked at all, and the SAST pass reports its own inconclusive reason (sast_unverified_checkout) instead, following gate.inconclusive the same way every other Semgrep failure mode does.

Product image: verified. docker build -t aurumcode-aur548-check:tmp -f Dockerfile . builds successfully, and docker run --rm --entrypoint semgrep aurumcode-aur548-check:tmp --version reports 1.172.0 from inside the built image — Alpine/musl was a real theoretical risk (Semgrep's PyPI wheels have historically targeted glibc) but semgrep 1.172.0 ships a musllinux_1_2_x86_64 wheel, so the straightforward pip install on the existing Alpine final stage works with no base-image change needed. The temporary image was removed (docker rmi) after verification.

docs.title: Independent review follow-up (B1/B2/B3)
docs.text:
A review of the first --pr-wiring commit found three blocking gaps, closed in a follow-up commit, each with its own regression test:

  • B1 — a fatal Semgrep-side failure could pass as a clean scan. The original Semgrep() only ever looked at the runner's own exit code together with whether stdout parsed as JSON; it never read Semgrep's own top-level "errors" array, and it treated ANY non-zero exit whose stdout still parsed as "findings were reported" (true for some other CI integrations that pass --error, but this command never does). A rule-pack download failure prints exactly {"errors":[{...}],"results": []} — a decodable, zero-finding report — at an exit code that can be non-zero OR 0. decodeSemgrepReport now reads Errors explicitly (ErrSemgrepReportedErrors), checked BEFORE the runner's own exit code, and any remaining non-zero exit (no errors array, otherwise a clean report) is ALSO now a failure (AUR-548-MUT-001-ANCHOR in internal/analysis/semgrep.go), since --error is never passed. Tests: TestSemgrepReportedErrorsNeverReadAsClean/ TestSemgrepNonZeroExitWithoutErrorFlagIsFailure (internal/analysis/semgrep_test.go, unit level) and TestAUR548SemgrepReportedErrorsAreInconclusive/ TestAUR548NonZeroExitCleanReportIsInconclusive (cmd/aurumcode/aur548_test.go, end-to-end via runReview).
  • B2 — Semgrep 1.x's real severity vocabulary was unmapped. normalizeSemgrepSeverity only recognized the historical ERROR/WARNING/ INFO spelling; Semgrep 1.x's own documented extra.severity values are CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW/INFO (plus INVENTORY/EXPERIMENT for non-gating rules), so a real HIGH finding fell through to the "unrecognized" default — which happened to still be "error" today, but was unverified and one careless edit away from silently becoming "info". Now mapped explicitly: CRITICAL/HIGH→error, MEDIUM→warning, LOW/INFO→info, anything else→error. Tests: TestNormalizeSemgrepSeverity (table test, every input) and TestAUR548HighSeverityFailsAtErrorThreshold (end-to-end: a real HIGH finding fails the default fail_on_severity: ERROR threshold).
  • B3 — the scanned tree on --pr is the pull request author's own content. A # nosemgrep comment or a committed .semgrepignore let the author suppress a finding even under a central policy that is supposed to be authoritative over them. analysis.Runner.Semgrep now takes a policyOrigin parameter and, when true, passes TWO flags: --disable-nosem (so a # nosemgrep comment cannot suppress a finding) and --x-ignore-semgrepignore-files (so a committed .semgrepignore, at ANY depth in the tree, cannot hide a file from the scan either). A repository's own, policy-free opt-in never adds either flag: there is no author/policy trust boundary to defend when the repository configured SAST on itself. Tests: TestSemgrepPolicyOriginFlags (unit level) and TestAUR548PolicyOriginDisablesNosem (end-to-end, cmd/aurumcode/aur548_test.go).

Revision history for B3. The first fix (committed, then re-reviewed) instead scanned a sanitized filesystem COPY of the checkout with .semgrepignore stripped (sastScanRoot/copyTreeExcluding). A second review found that copy bypassable and unsafe: copyTreeExcluding used os.ReadFile, which follows symlinks, so a .semgrepignore containing * plus one dangling or tree-escaping symlink restored the original bypass (reproduced: scan == root) and could read arbitrary host paths (/etc/hostname, /proc/self/environ) into the scan tree or hang on a device file (/dev/zero); runSASTPass also silently fell back to scanning the unsanitized root on any copy error, which is itself a fail-OPEN path under a trust boundary. docker run --rm docker.io/semgrep/semgrep@sha256:65dcd4408adda7c183a6b4550cb1e9b19f7f627a6fbb7e0559bd466bedc44d7b semgrep scan --help (the exact digest .board/bootstrap/locks/ scanners.yml pins, confirmed at version 1.172.0, matching the product image's pip-installed version) was then checked for a native flag, per the second review's own suggestion, and found one: --x-ignore-semgrepignore-files ("[INTERNAL] Ignore all '.semgrepignore' files found in the project tree ... THIS OPTION IS NOT PART OF THE SEMGREP API AND MAY CHANGE OR DISAPPEAR WITHOUT NOTICE"). Using Semgrep's own, already-audited target-selection code instead of a second, hand-rolled filesystem copy removes the entire symlink attack surface outright; sastScanRoot/copyTreeExcluding and their tests were deleted. Should this internal flag ever disappear in a future Semgrep version, the invocation simply errors on an unrecognized flag, which this adapter already turns into a non-nil, fail-closed error (B1's own handling) -- never a silent, unprotected scan.

Also from that review: SastConfig.Validate now rejects a rule_packs entry starting with - (would otherwise read as a CLI flag); every Semgrep-sourced Message passes through the redaction filter before publication (runSASTPass's new filter parameter), matching every other publication sink in this codebase; and QualityGatesConfig precedence under ApplyCentralPolicy changed from "any central policy wins the WHOLE quality_gates block" to per-section — a policy that declares quality_gates.sast says nothing about quality_gates.ssor_dtrack or quality_gates.supply_chain, and a repository's own, undeclared sections survive untouched (internal/config/qualitygates.go, internal/config/central.go). TestAUR548PolicyWinsOverRepoDisable still passes under this narrower precedence rule, since that test's policy explicitly declares its own quality_gates.sast.

Per-section precedence surfaced one more gap the second review caught: sastOrigin in main.go/pr.go was derived from centralCfg != nil alone -- true for ANY central policy, even one that governs other sections entirely and never declares quality_gates.sast at all. Under per-section precedence that leaves repoCfg.QualityGates.Sast as the REPOSITORY's own value, which must be labeled "repo" (and must never receive the two policy-only hardening flags above); it was being labeled "policy" instead, just because some unrelated policy happened to exist. Fixed to centralCfg != nil && centralCfg.QualityGates.Sast != nil in both files. Test: TestAUR548PolicyOriginWithoutSastSectionIsRepo.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: The RFC behind this corporate-adoption office (.board/cards/backlog/AUR-549.md .. AUR-551.md's own "Origem" section) asks for multi-language SAST with Semgrep as one of four adoption gates (SAST, SBOM, Dependency-Track inventory, Sigstore/Cosign signing). AurumCode's own go vet-shaped deterministic-tool adapter (internal/analysis.Runner.Vet) already existed but was never wired into either review path (AUR-492's own "linter adapter" card, still ready, not done, at the time this card started) — there was no established pattern for "run an external security scanner over the WHOLE reviewed tree and gate on its findings" in this codebase, only "run a linter over the diff and anchor findings to changed lines" (AUR-492's own scope, explicitly a different problem: internal/analysis.Runner.Analyze's embedded catalog and .Vet are both diff-anchored; Semgrep's own report is not, by design — a SAST pass must see the resulting code, not only the lines that changed).

docs.title: Why not through evaluateGate
docs.text:
AUR-519's evaluateGate (cmd/aurumcode/policygate.go) is gated behind GateConfig.Declared() (no gate: key at all ⇒ Active=false, no-op) and, inside that, behind gate.fail_on being non-empty before its severity loop ever runs. quality_gates.sast is a separate, independently-configured gate: the RFC's own example config declares quality_gates.sast with no gate: section at all, and AC-001 requires that alone to be enough to fail the check on an ERROR-severity finding. Overloading evaluateGate's own signature to also carry a SAST threshold would have meant changing a function every one of AUR-519/520/521/537/538/543's existing tests calls directly, for a condition (quality_gates.sast) those tests know nothing about — and two sibling cards (AUR-549/550) touch cmd/aurumcode concurrently, in their own worktrees, so a wide signature change here is exactly the kind of edit that turns "additive" into "a guaranteed merge conflict".

Instead, applySASTGate (cmd/aurumcode/aur548.go) computes its own, independent decision from quality_gates.sast, Semgrep's own findings, and the Semgrep execution outcome, and folds it in place into the very same gateDecision struct evaluateGate already returned for this run. Every downstream consumer of that struct — publishPolicyGateStatus, writeComplianceArtifacts (AUR-521's audit record and SARIF document), and runReview's own exit-code section — needed zero changes to also honor a SAST breach or a SAST-inconclusive scan: from their point of view there is exactly one gate decision per run, now possibly informed by two independent, additive sources.

docs.title: The adapter
docs.text:
internal/analysis.Runner.Semgrep (internal/analysis/semgrep.go) mirrors Runner.Vet's own injected-commandRunner seam: production code (cmd/aurumcode/aur548.go's realSemgrepRunner) execs the semgrep binary from PATH; tests inject a fake executable on PATH instead (no network, no real Semgrep). It runs semgrep scan --json --quiet --metrics=off --disable-version-check --config <pack>... . in the reviewed root and parses the report's results array into analysis.Findings, each carrying RuleID = "semgrep:" + check_id, severity mapped ERROR→error, WARNING→warning, INFO/anything else→error (an unrecognized severity from an external tool must never silently fail open to a lower rank, hence the one asymmetric default), and the file/line Semgrep itself reported. Message is Semgrep's own fixed rule message (extra.message); the matched source line (extra.lines) is never read, so a Semgrep finding can never leak reviewed source text through this adapter.

Three failure modes all become a non-nil error, never an empty finding list: the runner itself failing with nothing parseable afterward (ErrNotFound ⇒ sast_unavailable; any other runner error ⇒ sast_execution_error), invalid JSON output, and valid JSON missing the "results" key entirely ({}) — ErrSemgrepNoResults ⇒ sast_invalid_output. That last case is this card's own guarded-against defect (MUT-001): a naive implementation that read "no results key" the same as "an empty results array" would treat a truncated or wrong-shaped response as a clean, zero-finding pass.

docs.title: The config
docs.text:
QualityGatesConfig (internal/config/sast.go) is the shared quality_gates: shape this office's four cards agree on: Sast (this card), SsorDtrack (AUR-549/550, SBOM + Dependency-Track — defined here as an empty placeholder struct only, pending those cards), SupplyChain (AUR-551, signing — likewise empty for now). Each is a pointer so an entirely absent section (nil) is distinct from one written with every field at its zero value, and *SastConfig's own methods (IsEnabled, Packs, Threshold, Validate) are nil-safe, so a nil Sast behaves exactly like a declared, disabled one everywhere it is read.

ApplyCentralPolicy (internal/config/central.go) governs QualityGates exactly like Gate/Rules/Ignore/Exceptions: under any central policy, effective.QualityGates = central.QualityGates unconditionally — a repository's own quality_gates.sast is always discarded (with a named warning when it declared one), regardless of whether the policy's own section is present. This is what makes "a repository cannot disable a policy-enabled SAST" (CR-TRUST-001) trivially true: under a policy, the repository's section never has any effect at all, in either direction.

docs.title: AC-005 by construction, not just by ordering
docs.text: applySASTGate is handed runSASTPass's own Semgrep-sourced issue slice directly — never result.Issues, the slice the model's parsed JSON response populates. A model reply that recites, contradicts or claims to have removed a Semgrep finding (in its summary field, the only channel available to it) has no code path by which it could reach applySASTGate's input at all. TestAUR548ModelCannotRemoveOrDowngradeFinding proves this with a fixture response that explicitly claims the finding was "removed as a false positive".

docs.title: Reproducible Semgrep availability
docs.text:
.board/bootstrap/locks/scanners.yml already pins sast_scanner_image: docker.io/semgrep/semgrep@sha256:... at version 1.172.0. The product image installs that same pinned version so aurumcode review can exec semgrep from its own container without a second, separately-orchestrated scanner container (the reusable workflow, .github/workflows/review.yml, runs exactly one container — the AurumCode image itself — mounting the reviewed checkout read-only; there is no docker-in-docker step for a second scanner image today).

Network requirement: semgrep scan --config p/<name> downloads that named pack from Semgrep's own rule registry on every invocation. In a CI runner with outbound network, this is transparent. In a fully network-isolated runner, point quality_gates.sast.rule_packs at local rule files already present in the image or checkout instead of a registry name — the adapter passes whatever string is configured straight to --config, so a local path works identically to a registry pack name.

docs.title: Acceptance scenarios
docs.text:
• AC-001: a fake Semgrep returning one ERROR finding fails the gate, naming the check_id and line in the published output, the audit record and the SARIF document.
  • AC-002: a finding below fail_on_severity is produced but does not fail.
  • AC-003: Semgrep absent, erroring, or returning invalid JSON all become inconclusive, following gate.inconclusive — never a silent clean pass.
  • AC-004: rule packs come from the yml, or the RFC's own documented defaults; with no quality_gates.sast section, Semgrep is never invoked.
  • AC-005: a model reply that claims to have removed or downgraded the Semgrep finding has no effect on the gate.

docs.title: Skeptical mutation
docs.text: • MUT-001: treating a Semgrep execution error as zero findings (the exact defect ErrSemgrepNoResults/the runner-error branch in internal/analysis/semgrep.go guards against) must turn AC-003's own tests red. tests/acceptance/AUR-548.sh AC-003-MUT-001 applies this mutation mechanically and checks for the red result.

docs.title: AUR-549 — SBOM CycloneDX 1.6 gerado com Trivy
Status
docs.text: Implementado em internal/sbom (gerador, validador, pipeline, configuração) e na wiring cmd/aurumcode/aur549.go (subcomando aurumcode sbom, aditivo a review/fix). Prova de comportamento: cmd/aurumcode/aur549_test.go:: TestAUR549*; aceite: tests/acceptance/AUR-549.sh.

docs.title: Problema
docs.text: A adoção corporativa (RFC do dono, fora deste repositório público) pede um SBOM OWASP CycloneDX gerado com Trivy para o repositório e, quando houver, para uma imagem de container — nunca um SBOM vazio ou de outro formato/versão aceito silenciosamente. Esta é a base que o AUR-550 (envio ao Dependency-Track) consome; este card cobre só a geração e a validação.

docs.title: v3: spec_version é um MÍNIMO, não um valor exato
docs.text:
A v2 (33253a0) validava specVersion por igualdade exata contra o configurado ("1.6"). Na revisão, o Trivy fixado por digest em .board/bootstrap/locks/scanners.yml (vuln_scanner_image, 0.73.0) emite CycloneDX 1.7, e não existe flag do Trivy para pedir uma versão de especificação mais antiga (Trivy CHANGELOG da 0.71.0, PR #10715) — ou seja, a igualdade exata reprovava TODO SBOM real que esse binário gerasse, não só uma entrada malformada.

A correção (internal/sbom/validator.go, specVersionAtLeast): aceitar quando a saída tem a MESMA major do configurado e minor ≥ ao configurado. Uma major diferente ("2.0" contra um configurado "1.6") continua recusada mesmo sendo numericamente "maior" — mudança de major é incompatibilidade, não avanço. Ambos os lados (a saída do Trivy e o spec_version configurado) são exigidos no formato estrito major.minor; internal/config.SBOMGeneratorConfig.Validate já recusa um spec_version fora desse formato na CARGA da configuração, antes de qualquer chamada ao Trivy — uma falha de "o que isso quer dizer" nunca vira uma falha de "o Trivy devolveu algo estranho" mais tarde.

Downstream: o OWASP Dependency-Track só ingere CycloneDX 1.7 a partir da versão 5.1.0 do servidor (ou do backport 4.14.4) — o AUR-550 (ou quem configurar o servidor) precisa dessa versão mínima.

docs.title: Decisão de arquitetura (v2): quality_gates dentro de internal/config
docs.text:
A v1 deste card não listava internal/config em seus paths e por isso lia sua própria seção de um arquivo separado, .aurumcode/quality_gates.yml. A v2 do card corrigiu esse defeito: internal/config passou a constar nos paths, e a diretriz do dono é uma só configuração simples — um .aurumcode/config.yml (mais Markdown) — nunca um segundo arquivo yml.

quality_gates agora é um campo de internal/config.Config (QualityGates QualityGatesConfig, qualitygates.go), lido do MESMO .aurumcode/config.yml que review/rules/ignore/gate/exceptions já usam. QualityGatesConfig é a seção COMPARTILHADA por três cards de adoção corporativa — Sast *SastConfig (AUR-548), SsorDtrack *SsorDtrackConfig (este card, campo SBOMGenerator, mais o AUR-550) e SupplyChain *SupplyChainConfig (reservado) — cada um um PONTEIRO: nil significa "nunca declarado", distinto de "declarado, mesmo vazio". Isso é o que permite a ApplyCentralPolicy (central.go) decidir a precedência POR SEÇÃO: diferente de Gate/Exceptions (que uma política sempre decide por completo, declarados ou não), aqui uma política que só declara sast não arrasta ssor_dtrack com ela — o repositório continua livre para configurar ssor_dtrack.sbom_generator por conta própria, porque a política nunca opinou sobre essa chave especificamente. Só quando a política declara ssor_dtrack (mesmo vazio) é que ela vale sozinha, com a seção do repositório descartada e um aviso (internal/config/central_test.go/qualitygates_test.go prova os três casos: política muda, política não fala do assunto, política fala de outra seção).

Como Config agora TEM o campo quality_gates, o decode estrito de LoadCentralPolicy (yaml.Decoder.KnownFields(true)) reconhece a chave normalmente — nenhuma política que declare quality_gates quebra mais a decodificação, ao contrário da v1.

aurumcode sbom lê Gate E quality_gates.ssor_dtrack.sbom_generator numa ÚNICA resolução efetiva (loadEffectiveConfig, cmd/aurumcode/aur549.go: config.Load e, com --politica, ValidatePolicyOutsideReviewedTree + LoadCentralPolicy + ApplyCentralPolicy) — a mesma sequência que runReview/runPRReview já usam, agora também compartilhando a mesma leitura de arquivo.

docs.title: Comportamento
docs.text:
aurumcode sbom [--repo dir] [--imagem referencia] [--politica dir] [--trivy-bin caminho]:

  1. Resolve o Config efetivo (loadEffectiveConfig) e, dentro dele, QualityGates.SsorDtrack.SBOMGenerator. Sem seção declarada (nem no repositório, nem na política quando há uma): não faz nada, sai 0 (Documentation and compatibility do card).
  2. Valida a seção (SBOMGeneratorConfig.Validate, internal/config/ qualitygates.go): tool só aceita trivy, format só aceita cyclonedx; qualquer outro valor é erro de configuração (exit 2), antes de qualquer chamada externa.
  3. Resolve output_file contra o repositório, recusando qualquer caminho que escape dele — absoluto, .., OU um link simbólico que resolva para fora da raiz (sbom.ResolveOutputPath, que roda EvalSymlinks sobre o prefixo já existente do caminho).
  4. Roda trivy fs --format cyclonedx --output <tmp> <repo> (sbom.TrivyGenerator.GenerateFilesystem) para um arquivo temporário no mesmo diretório do destino, valida esse arquivo (sbom.Validate: JSON, bomFormat=CycloneDX, specVersion igual ao configurado) e só então o renomeia para output_file (sbom.GenerateAndValidate) — AC-001. Uma falha em qualquer etapa (trivy ausente/erro, saída vazia, saída que não valida) nunca deixa um arquivo no caminho final — AC-002, AC-003.
  5. Com --imagem/--image, repete o mesmo pipeline com trivy image --format cyclonedx --output <tmp> <imagem>, escrevendo em um segundo arquivo derivado deterministicamente (sbom.ImageOutputPath: <nome>-image<ext>) — AC-004.
  6. Qualquer falha de geração/validação é reportada e roteada pelo MESMO gate AUR-519 que a revisão usa (evaluateGate, cmd/aurumcode/policygate.go), com o motivo próprio sbom_generation_failure (gateReasonSBOMFailure): gate.inconclusive: block, ou nenhum gate declarado (este comando é novo — não há comportamento legado a preservar, e o Outcome do card exige "nunca SBOM vazio aceito") → exitQualityNotReviewed; gate.inconclusive: warn → publica o motivo em stderr e sai 0, nunca bloqueando.

docs.title: Testes
docs.text:
cmd/aurumcode/aur549_test.go usa um executável trivy falso (um script sh) num diretório temporário colocado em PATH — nunca a rede, nunca o binário real:

  • TestAUR549TrivyGeneratesValidatedSBOM (AC-001): trivy falso que grava CycloneDX 1.6 válido produz o arquivo configurado, com o argv (fs, --format cyclonedx, --output, o repositório) registrado e verificado.
  • TestAUR549NonCycloneDXOutputRejected (AC-002): quatro subtestes — specVersion errado, bomFormat errado, saída que não é JSON, saída vazia — todos recusados, com o arquivo final confirmado ausente em cada caso.
  • TestAUR549MissingTrivyIsInconclusive (AC-003): trivy ausente do PATH sob nenhum gate/block (falha fechado) e sob warn (publica o motivo, sai 0).
  • TestAUR549ImageProducesSeparateFile (AC-004): com --imagem, duas invocações de trivy (fs e image) produzem dois arquivos distintos.

tests/acceptance/AUR-549.sh roda os quatro testes acima dentro de uma árvore semeada (go.mod go.sum cmd internal pkg) sem rede, e aplica AC-002-MUT-001: substitui a única linha de decisão em internal/sbom/validator.go (formatAndVersionOK, a comparação de bomFormat/specVersion) por return true e confirma que o subteste badversion de AC-002 vira RED — provando que o teste realmente depende da validação, e não passaria mesmo aceitando qualquer saída.

docs.title: Trivy como processo externo
docs.text:
internal/sbom.TrivyGenerator nunca embute um binário: resolve trivy via PATH, ou via --trivy-bin apontando a outro executável (usado pelos testes para apontar ao script falso, e, em CI, para o wrapper abaixo).

.github/workflows/review.yml ganhou a etapa "Generate SBOM (Trivy, AUR-549)", que roda SEMPRE (revisão desta rodada: um grep de texto que só decidia a mesma coisa que aurumcode sbom já decide, com o risco real de discordar dela, foi removido) — o custo de rodar sem nada configurado é só extrair o binário e gerar o wrapper; o docker run do Trivy em si só acontece quando aurumcode sbom decide gerar. A etapa extrai o binário aurumcode já compilado na imagem aurumcode-review (docker create/ docker cp — nenhum segundo build), gera (via heredoc com delimitador citado, sem interpolação, mais um sed para injetar o valor pinado) um wrapper trivy-docker.sh que reproduz o argv que TrivyGenerator já constrói (fs --format <f> --output <p> <raiz> / image --format <f> --output <p> <imagem>) dentro de docker run contra vuln_scanner_image (hoje docker.io/aquasec/trivy@sha256:7cced7cae583819fc7806d4cbc0dbbc7cad18b99f7d3e235192e6da8c091045c, de .board/bootstrap/locks/scanners.yml), e então chama aurumcode sbom --repo . --trivy-bin trivy-docker.sh DIRETO NO RUNNER (nunca de dentro de outro container): rodar docker run de dentro de um container através de um socket do Docker montado criaria um container IRMÃO que precisa de caminhos do HOST para seus próprios -v, e nada dentro daquele container sabe genericamente o caminho do host atrás do seu próprio /github/workspace — por isso esta etapa evita se aninhar desde o início, chamando docker run apenas do processo do job no runner.

Revisão desta rodada, segunda correção: o wrapper NÃO monta mais .aurumcode-target (a árvore checked-out) como gravável dentro do container do Trivy. A saída do Trivy dentro do container sempre aponta para um diretório descartável criado em $RUNNER_TEMP (mktemp -d), montado leitura-e-escrita; o próprio wrapper, já de volta no runner (nunca dentro do container), move (mv) o arquivo pronto para o caminho que aurumcode sbom pediu, só depois que o docker run termina, e limpa o diretório descartável (trap ... EXIT). A montagem da árvore escaneada (trivy fs, modo fs) continua só leitura, inalterada.

A sintaxe YAML+heredoc foi verificada localmente: python3 -c "import yaml..." confirma o parse do review.yml e extrai a string do run: inalterada; bash -n confirma a sintaxe do script extraído e do wrapper gerado; uma simulação com um docker falso no PATH confirma que o wrapper reconstrói exatamente os dois docker run esperados (fs e image) com os mounts corretos. NÃO foi validado contra uma execução real do GitHub Actions (sem acesso a CI neste ambiente) — um reviewer deveria considerar isso antes do primeiro merge que dependa desta etapa.

action.yml (a action standalone, using: docker) NÃO roda aurumcode sbom: seu próprio container não tem como traduzir seu /github/workspace para o caminho equivalente no HOST, que um docker run aninhado através do socket do Docker precisaria. Documentado como comentário no próprio action.yml.

docs.title: Lacunas conhecidas (reportadas, não resolvidas por este card)
docs.text:
• A etapa de CI em review.yml não foi exercitada contra uma execução real do GitHub Actions (ver seção acima) — validada por inspeção, YAML/bash sintático e uma simulação local com docker/aurumcode falsos.
  • action.yml continua sem gerar SBOM (limitação estrutural documentada, não um lapso) — um card futuro teria que resolver a tradução de caminho host/container para viabilizar isso de dentro de uma action standalone.
  • Dockerfile não foi alterado: a geração de SBOM em CI não depende de nada instalado na imagem do produto, só do docker do próprio runner.

docs.title: AUR-550 — SBOM submitted to Dependency-Track, gated by project metrics
Status
docs.text: Implemented in internal/dtrack (the Dependency-Track v5 REST client), internal/config/dtrack.go (quality_gates.ssor_dtrack config, central-policy precedence) and cmd/aurumcode/aur550.go (the gate hook, wired into runReview/runPRReview right after evaluateGate). Behavior proof: internal/dtrack/client_test.go and cmd/aurumcode/aur550_test.go::TestAUR550*. Acceptance: tests/acceptance/AUR-550.sh.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: AurumCode had no way to enforce a corporate "single source of record" inventory policy: upload the already-generated SBOM (AUR-549's own output) to a central OWASP Dependency-Track v5 server, and fail the review when that project's own open vulnerabilities/policy violations cross an operator's threshold. Without it, a repository's SBOM could exist on disk and never reach the inventory system at all, or reach it without any gate ever reading the result back.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
internal/dtrack is a thin REST client with three calls, mirroring Dependency-Track v5's own API exactly:

  • Upload — POST {host}/api/v1/bom, multipart fields project (the Dependency-Track project UUID) and bom (the SBOM bytes), header X-Api-Key. Returns the processing token from the JSON response.
  • PollUntilProcessed — GET {host}/api/v1/bom/token/{token} on an injectable interval, until the response's processing field (Dependency- Track's own BomProcessingResponse) is false, or an injectable clock decides the configured timeout elapsed first (ErrTimeout).
  • ProjectMetrics — GET {host}/api/v1/metrics/project/{project}/current, decoded into Dependency-Track v5's own ProjectMetrics fields critical, high and policyViolationsTotal (every open, unsuppressed finding/ violation in that scope — see internal/dtrack/client.go's own package doc for the exact semantics of each field).

Every one of those three metrics fields decodes as *int, never int: a response Dependency-Track did not fully populate (a metrics snapshot not yet computed right after processing finishes, or a differently-versioned server) must read as unknown, never as the silent zero that would make an unscanned project look clean. EvaluateMetrics/dtrack.Run refuse to grade an incomplete response at all — the caller's gate turns that refusal into inconclusive, never an approval. The same fail-closed rule applies to the processing field during polling (missing/null is read as "still processing", so a server that never finishes still times out instead of silently reading as done).

dtrack.Run composes the three calls end to end and returns a single Outcome{Active, Breach, Inconclusive, InconclusiveReason, Reasons, ...} — Reasons and InconclusiveReason are always this package's own stable, non-server-authored tokens (dtrack_timeout, dtrack_http_error, dtrack_unreachable, dtrack_metrics_incomplete) plus the bare integers read from the metrics response, never a response body or a raw Go error string — so a caller can publish Outcome verbatim to a review body, an audit record or SARIF without a second redaction pass over free text it does not control.

docs.title: HTTPS-only, no credential-forwarding redirect
docs.text: dtrack.ValidateHost (called once by NewClient, and again at config Validate() time so a misconfigured host is a loud parse-time error) accepts an absolute https:// URL, or http:// only when the host is a loopback IP literal (127.0.0.0/8 or ::1 — never the name localhost, which depends on a resolver/hosts file this rule refuses to trust). That one exception exists only so this package's own tests, and the card's own acceptance script, can point it at an httptest.Server; it is never a production escape hatch. Userinfo and a query string in server_api_host are refused outright. Client's own http.Client never follows a redirect (CheckRedirect returns http.ErrUseLastResponse): Go's HTTP client strips Authorization/Cookie on a cross-host redirect but not a custom header such as X-Api-Key, so the only safe rule is to never follow one at all — a 3xx response surfaces as its own HTTP status instead.

docs.title: Config and central-policy precedence
docs.text:
quality_gates.ssor_dtrack (internal/config/dtrack.go, SsorDtrackConfig) is a pointer field on the shared QualityGatesConfig struct (alongside Sast/SupplyChain, AUR-548/AUR-551's own sections — coordinated so the three cards' concurrent edits to internal/config converge on one struct). SsorDtrack is nil exactly when the section is absent from the yaml; every method on it has a pointer receiver and is nil-safe, so a caller never has to special-case "section absent" before calling Declared(). enabled: true is the single opt-in switch — a config that sets server_api_host/secrets ahead of flipping enabled changes nothing yet (a staged rollout stays inert).

ApplyCentralPolicy (internal/config/central.go) governs QualityGates exactly like Gate/Rules/Ignore/Exceptions already do: under a central policy, effective.QualityGates = central.QualityGates unconditionally, and a repository-declared ssor_dtrack is dropped wholesale with its own named warning. This is what makes "a repository cannot disable a policy-enabled ssor_dtrack" true: it is the general "only the policy decides" rule applied to one more field, not a special case.

sbom_generator.output_file (SsorDtrackConfig.SbomGenerator, AUR-549's own sub-section, nested here per AUR-549's own documented example) names the path to the already-generated CycloneDX document this card uploads as-is. Generating that file is explicitly AUR-549's job and this card's own Non-goal; SBOMOutputFile() is the one nil-safe accessor the gate hook uses, so an ssor_dtrack section enabled ahead of sbom_generator being declared reads as a (nil-safe) misconfiguration, not a panic.

docs.title: Gate wiring
docs.text:
cmd/aurumcode/aur550.go's applyDTrackGate runs once, immediately after evaluateGate in both runReview (main.go) and runPRReview (pr.go), and mergeDTrackGate folds its gateDecision-shaped result into the SAME gateResult/gateInconclusiveReason those two functions already publish through gateResult.Lines, writeComplianceArtifacts and publishPolicyGateStatus (policygate.go, AUR-519/521/538, all untouched). This card adds no second gate and no second writer:

  • Breach (a metric over its threshold): Breach/Fail are set unconditionally — exactly like evaluateGate's own severity threshold loop — with the metric numbers in Lines (e.g. ssor_dtrack: critical 3 > max_critical 0) and a synthetic render.AuditFinding{RuleID: "ssor_dtrack", ...} in BlockingFindings, so the audit record and SARIF carry the same breach the review body does.
  • Inconclusive (unreachable server, HTTP error, polling timeout, an incomplete metrics response, a missing secret, or an unreadable SBOM): sets Inconclusive with a stable reason token; Fail is set only when the SAME gate.inconclusive mode evaluateGate already reads is block — a run with warn or no gate: key at all only gets a visible, non-blocking alert, mirroring AUR-519's own warn/"" semantics exactly. A breach is never downgraded by this mode.
  • No-op: cfg.Declared() == false (no ssor_dtrack section, or enabled left at its default false) makes applyDTrackGate return a zero gateDecision and the SAME filter pointer — zero HTTP calls, nothing published, byte-identical to this card never existing.

gateInconclusiveReason (the single string writeComplianceArtifacts reads) is combined by joining with a comma, never overwritten — AUR-537's own single -reason assertions (e.g. "provider_failure") stay intact on a run that never declares ssor_dtrack, and a run where both a model-side and a dtrack-side reason fire publishes both.

docs.title: The API key never leaks (AC-004)
docs.text:
redaction.Filter is an immutable value built once by NewFilter/FromEnv (no mutator exists, and internal/security/redaction is read-only to this card). applyDTrackGate resolves the key from the environment variable named by api_key_secret and, the instant it is non-empty, builds a new filter (redaction.NewFilter(os.Getenv(redaction.CanaryEnv), apiKey)) carrying it as an exact-value secret, before constructing the HTTP client or doing anything else that could write a byte. The caller (main.go/pr.go) then wraps its own stdout/stderr with a second redaction.Writer layer built from that new filter (wrapWriterWithFilter) — a second layer on top of whatever writer was already there, flushed via defer before the function returns — so every subsequent write on those two sinks is redacted by the new filter as well, and filter itself (the value writeComplianceArtifacts uses for the audit record and SARIF) is reassigned to the new one. The key is also never put into an error string this package returns: StatusError carries only the operation name and the HTTP status code, the response body is read and discarded (io.Copy(io.Discard, io.LimitReader(...))) on every non-2xx response, and dtrack.Outcome's own Reasons/InconclusiveReason are stable tokens plus integers only.

cmd/aurumcode/aur550_test.go::TestAUR550APIKeyNeverLeaks is the canary: the fake server deliberately echoes the key back in its own 401 body (as a real Dependency-Track error page could), confirms the server genuinely received it in X-Api-Key (so the test cannot pass vacuously), and then asserts its absence from stdout, stderr, the audit record and the SARIF document alike.

docs.title: Minimum Dependency-Track server version
docs.text: AUR-549's pinned Trivy emits CycloneDX 1.7 (it has no option to emit an older spec version). Dependency-Track only accepts a 1.7 BOM upload starting at server version 5.1.0 (or 4.14.4 on the 4.x line) — dependencytrack.org/news/dependency-track-5-1, releases/tag/5.1.0, releases/tag/4.14.4. An older server answers the upload with a 4xx (an unsupported-specVersion body). That rejection is handled by the exact same path as any other non-2xx response on Upload (StatusError/ErrHTTPStatus -> ReasonHTTPError): the gate reads dtrack_http_error and goes inconclusive per policy, never approved, and PollUntilProcessed/ ProjectMetrics are never even called (there is no token to poll and no project to grade from a BOM the server never accepted). See cmd/aurumcode/aur550_test.go::TestAUR550UploadRejectedBySpecVersionIsInconclusive. This card does not itself validate the server's own version ahead of time -- it is a precondition for the operator to meet, documented here and in docs/configuration.md, not something this client can discover safely without an extra, undocumented API call.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text: Generating the SBOM (AUR-549's own job — this card only reads sbom_generator.output_file); administering Dependency-Track projects on the server (creating, renaming, deleting one is a human operation).

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• internal/dtrack/client_test.go exercises ValidateHost, and Run end-to-end against an httptest fake Dependency-Track server: approval within thresholds, a breach with the right numbers, a polling timeout, an HTTP error, an unreachable (closed) server, and an incomplete metrics response — all with an injected fake clock/sleeper, so a 180s configured timeout costs a test nothing.
  • cmd/aurumcode/aur550_test.go drives the same scenarios through the real runReview command (AC-001/AC-002/AC-003), the API-key canary (AC-004), a custom secret-variable-name run and a disabled-by-default no-op run (AC-005).
  • tests/acceptance/AUR-550.sh (selectors AC-001..AC-005, all, AC-003-MUT-001) runs the same Go tests inside a sealed, offline copy of the tree, and verifies the AC-003-MUT-001 mutation (treating a polling timeout as approved — the exact defect this card refuses to allow) turns TestAUR550PollingTimeoutIsInconclusive red.

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text:
• .github/workflows/review.yml and action.yml are untouched: AUR-548 and AUR-549 are editing both concurrently in parallel worktrees, and wiring a real Dependency-Track upload step into CI belongs with whichever card lands the actual SBOM-generation step it depends on. quality_gates.ssor_dtrack works today through .aurumcode/config.yml alone; exposing it as reusable workflow inputs is a follow-up, not implemented here.
  • Dependency-Track's own GET .../metrics/project/{project}/current can return a stale snapshot immediately after processing finishes (the server's own metrics recomputation is asynchronous to BOM processing). This card polls processing to completion but does not add a second wait for a fresh metrics snapshot; documented here as a known limitation, not implemented.

docs.title: AUR-551 — SBOM e imagem assinados com Sigstore/Cosign
Status
docs.text: Implemented in internal/supplychain (the Cosign-invoking signer, digest-ref validation), internal/config/qualitygates.go (quality_gates.supply_chain config, closed engine vocabulary, central-policy precedence already carried by ApplyCentralPolicy) and cmd/aurumcode/aur551.go (the aurumcode sign subcommand, additive to review/fix/sbom). Behavior proof: internal/supplychain/signer_test.go and cmd/aurumcode/aur551_test.go::TestAUR551*; central-policy precedence proof: internal/config/qualitygates_test.go::TestApplyCentralPolicySupplyChainPrecedence. Acceptance: tests/acceptance/AUR-551.sh.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: AUR-549 generates a CycloneDX SBOM and AUR-550 uploads it to Dependency-Track, but neither card signs anything: a tampered SBOM, or an image pushed under the same digest-pinned reference by someone other than this pipeline, would be indistinguishable from the genuine artifact downstream. The corporate adoption RFC (kept out of this public repository) asks for Sigstore/Cosign signatures on both the SBOM and the artifact image, verifiable afterwards, with signing failure never silently treated as "signed".

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
internal/supplychain.Signer shells out to an external cosign binary (never a crypto library this project links, never a key AurumCode manages) for exactly three calls: cosign sign-blob (the SBOM), cosign verify-blob (used by tests and the real proof below, never by production signing itself) and cosign sign (the image). Every failure is wrapped naming the artifact being signed/verified — internal/supplychain/signer.go's own doc comment spells out why (AC-002: "o parecer diz qual artefato ficou sem assinatura"). ValidateArtifactRef refuses any image reference that is not pinned by a full 64-hex-character sha256 digest; the same check is duplicated (not imported, to avoid a package cycle with internal/config) as validateImageDigestRef in internal/config/qualitygates.go, so a bad reference is refused both at config-load time (quality_gates.supply_chain. artifacts) and again if a caller bypasses config entirely and calls internal/supplychain directly with a CLI-supplied --image.

quality_gates.supply_chain (internal/config.SupplyChainConfig) is a pointer field on the existing QualityGatesConfig, exactly like Sast and SsorDtrack: nil means "not declared at all", and ApplyCentralPolicy (central.go) already governed it per-section before this card — the pointer and the three independent per-subsection if central.QualityGates.X != nil blocks pre-existed in central.go; this card only added the struct's fields (Engine, SignSBOM, SignArtifacts, Artifacts) and its own Validate(). Validate rejects a declared section whose engine is anything other than the literal "cosign" (including the empty string), and any artifacts entry that is not digest-pinned — both fail closed at config-load time, before any cosign call.

aurumcode sign (cmd/aurumcode/aur551.go) resolves the effective config the same way aurumcode sbom does (loadEffectiveConfig, reused from aur549.go), then:

  • exits 0 immediately, before resolving --cosign-bin or touching a file, if quality_gates.supply_chain is not declared at all (AC-003);
  • validates the section, then signs the SBOM (--sbom, falling back to quality_gates.ssor_dtrack.sbom_generator.output_file when sign_sbom is on and no --sbom was given) and/or the image(s) (--image, repeatable, falling back to quality_gates.supply_chain.artifacts when sign_artifacts is on);
  • fails unconditionally, naming the artifact, on any signing error — no gate.inconclusive softening. This is deliberately different from aurumcode sbom's own reportSBOMFailure: the card's own AC-002 names no warn mode ("falha de assinatura reprova a etapa"), so a signing failure is always a non-zero exit.

Keyless signing (no --key) relies on cosign's own ambient OIDC flow (Fulcio/Rekor); production CI never manages a private key for this. Tests and the real proof below always supply a local ephemeral key instead, so they run offline with no cosign network dependency at all.

docs.title: CI wiring
docs.text: .github/workflows/review.yml installs cosign via sigstore/cosign-installer, pinned by commit SHA (6f9f17788090df1f26f669e9d70d6ae9567deba6, tag v4.1.2 as of this card), with cosign-release: 'v3.1.3' — a fixed Cosign release, never latest, matching the version used for the real proof below so the pinned CI binary and the one this proof exercises are the same. The "Sign SBOM and image (Cosign, AUR-551)" step runs unconditionally right after the SBOM step and reuses aurumcode sign's own no-op decision, exactly like the SBOM step already reuses aurumcode sbom's. Signing in CI is keyless (GitHub Actions' own OIDC identity); this reusable workflow never declares a permissions: block (the same workflow_call constraint already documented for security-events: write), so a caller that wants sign_sbom/sign_artifacts must itself grant id-token: write to the job that calls this workflow. action.yml (the standalone Docker action) does not run aurumcode sign, for the same docker run-from-inside-a-container path-translation reason AUR-549 already documents for aurumcode sbom, plus the missing OIDC id-token a container-only action has no step to request.

docs.title: Real proof (AC-001): cosign, pinned by digest, signing and verifying a SBOM offline
docs.text:
Image resolved via gh api repos/sigstore/cosign/releases/latest (tag v3.1.3, not a draft/prerelease) and pulled to resolve its digest:

$ docker pull ghcr.io/sigstore/cosign/cosign:v3.1.3
...
Digest: sha256:9e5c2f2edc34351160407ca3416c61855bdf9403c3c5936e0f0be7fc261611b8
Status: Downloaded newer image for ghcr.io/sigstore/cosign/cosign:v3.1.3

cosign sign-blob --help was run against this exact digest first, because cosign v3 changed flag defaults from the version the card's own prose ("--tlog-upload=false") assumed: --tlog-upload is deprecated (warns, but still works) and --use-signing-config=true is now the default, which requires --bundle and a writable $HOME for a TUF client that still tries to reach the network even with a local key. The commands below were adjusted to what the pinned binary's own --help confirmed works offline.

Ephemeral key pair, generated fully offline, no network:

$ docker run --rm --network none -e COSIGN_PASSWORD= \
    -v "$SCRATCH":/w -w /w --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
    ghcr.io/sigstore/cosign/cosign@sha256:9e5c2f2edc34351160407ca3416c61855bdf9403c3c5936e0f0be7fc261611b8 \
    generate-key-pair
Private key written to cosign.key
Public key written to cosign.pub

Sign the example SBOM (sbom.json, a minimal CycloneDX document), with --tlog-upload=false and --use-signing-config=false so no Rekor upload or TUF fetch is attempted — --network none on the container proves it:

$ docker run --rm --network none -e COSIGN_PASSWORD= -e HOME=/w/home \
    -v "$SCRATCH":/w -w /w --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
    ghcr.io/sigstore/cosign/cosign@sha256:9e5c2f2edc34351160407ca3416c61855bdf9403c3c5936e0f0be7fc261611b8 \
    sign-blob --key cosign.key --yes --tlog-upload=false --use-signing-config=false \
    --bundle sbom.json.bundle sbom.json
Flag --tlog-upload has been deprecated, prefer using a --signing-config file with no transparency log services
Using payload from: sbom.json
Signing artifact...
Wrote bundle to file sbom.json.bundle
$ echo "EXIT:$?"
EXIT:0

Verify the bundle offline, with no tlog/SCT check (the exact offline counterpart of the card's own --insecure-ignore-tlog):

$ docker run --rm --network none -e HOME=/w/home \
    -v "$SCRATCH":/w -w /w --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
    ghcr.io/sigstore/cosign/cosign@sha256:9e5c2f2edc34351160407ca3416c61855bdf9403c3c5936e0f0be7fc261611b8 \
    verify-blob --key cosign.pub --bundle sbom.json.bundle \
    --insecure-ignore-tlog --insecure-ignore-sct sbom.json
WARNING: Skipping tlog verification is an insecure practice that lacks transparency and auditability verification for the blob.
Verified OK
$ echo "EXIT:$?"
EXIT:0

internal/supplychain.Signer (SignBlob/VerifyBlob) builds exactly this argv shape (--key, --bundle, --tlog-upload=false --use-signing-config=false when Options.SkipTransparencyLog is set for signing, --insecure-ignore-tlog --insecure-ignore-sct for verifying) — see signer_test.go's fake-cosign tests for the argv assertions that pin this shape in code.

The downloaded image was removed after this proof (docker rmi ghcr.io/sigstore/cosign/cosign@sha256:9e5c2f2edc34351160407ca3416c61855bdf9403c3c5936e0f0be7fc261611b8), and the ephemeral key pair and scratch files used for this run were discarded (never committed) — this project manages no Cosign key.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text: Managing keys outside Cosign's own mechanism; signing third-party artifacts; keyless (OIDC) verification (the real proof above only covers the key-based path, which is what this card's own acceptance script can run with no network and no GitHub Actions identity token).

docs.title: Known gap
docs.text: .board/bootstrap/locks/scanners.yml has no Cosign entry (it currently locks only gitleaks/trivy/semgrep/shellcheck). That file is in this card's read_paths, not its paths, so it was not edited here; the CI pin lives instead in .github/workflows/review.yml itself (cosign-installer's commit SHA plus a fixed cosign-release). A follow-up card should add a supplychain_scanner_* entry to scanners.yml for consistency with how every other externally-pinned tool in this project is locked.

docs.title: AUR-552: tipos de xBOM além do SBOM
Escopo entregue
docs.text:
• aurumcode xbom --type build|cbom: Build BOM e CBOM em CycloneDX 1.6, com evidência verificada (internal/xbom, cmd/aurumcode/aur552.go).
  • aibom, saasbom e netbom: formato e envio definidos e documentados em docs/configuration.md (âncoras xbom-aibom, xbom-saasbom, xbom-netbom); o comando recusa com exit 2 apontando a âncora (AC-003).
  • O envio ao servidor é o do AUR-550 (POST /api/v1/bom); xbom só gera o arquivo. Enviar o BOM pelo próprio xbom não faz parte deste card.

docs.title: Arquitetura
docs.text:
1. LoadCatalog resolve o catálogo do tipo: política central, repositório, embutido (catalog/<tipo>.yml, go:embed). Validação estrita (ParseCatalog).
  2. Extract percorre o repositório (sem seguir links simbólicos, ignorando binários e arquivos acima de 1 MiB) e aplica cada entrada cujo files casa o caminho: regex por linha, grupos nomeados, template do componente.
  3. Com provedor (selectProvider, incluindo AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE), o modelo recebe os candidatos (linha já redigida) e responde JSON: candidates[] (id, keep, description, properties) e additional[] (componentes novos com occurrences[] que ele cita). Id inexistente ou tipo inválido é rejeitado e contado (aurumcode:xbom:llm_rejected).
  4. verifyEvidence reabre cada ocorrência (caminho dentro do repositório, links simbólicos que saem são recusados) e exige que a linha contenha o token (lineCitesToken, a âncora de MUT-001). Falhou: descartado e contado em aurumcode:xbom:dropped_without_evidence.
  5. Serialização e ValidateBOM: internal/sbom.Validate (formato e specVersion mínimo) mais a regra própria (toda ocorrência com caminho relativo e linha positiva; todo cryptographic-asset com assetType).
  6. Escrita em temporário e rename.

docs.title: Formato do catálogo
docs.text:
Ver "Catálogos" em docs/configuration.md. Campos: version (1), type, file_sets, exclude, entries[] (id, files, pattern, token, component{type,name,version,purl,description,properties,crypto}).

Fora do escopo desta versão: consulta estrutural (AST) como alternativa à regex por linha; o catálogo só expressa padrões de linha. Referências a estágios anteriores de um Dockerfile (FROM build) viram candidato e cabe ao modelo (keep: false) ou a um catálogo próprio excluí-las.

docs.title: Metadados registrados
docs.text: aurumcode:xbom:type, catalog (embedded, repository, policy), llm (absent, present, failed), candidates, dropped_without_evidence, dropped_occurrences, e com provedor llm_excluded e llm_rejected.

docs.title: Aceite
docs.text: bash tests/acceptance/AUR-552.sh all|AC-001|AC-002|AC-003|AC-002-MUT-001. MUT-001 troca o corpo de lineCitesToken por return true numa cópia e exige que os testes de AC-002 caiam.

docs.title: AUR-553: provas do reaproveitamento do veredito cobrem cada termo da chave
O que foi medido antes
docs.text:
Pendencias da revisao do AUR-524, confirmadas no codigo de origin/dev (bef0f3c0):

  • Defeito de seguranca. O cache de revisao (AURUMCODE_CACHE_DIR) e entrada nao confiavel: em CI pode ser compartilhado com outros workflows do mesmo escopo. Dois leitores devolviam achados do disco sem redacao: gate.ReuseOrStoreGateVerdict (veredito do gate, --base e --pr) e partitionByCache (cache por arquivo do --base). Um verbete forjado com um segredo ou texto arbitrario chegava inteiro ao review publicado no pull request, ao stdout, ao SARIF e a auditoria. A redacao so era aplicada na fronteira da resposta do modelo (internal/review.redactReviewResult).
  • Os testes de versao do prompt e de modelo do AUR-524 trocavam tambem a fixture (AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE), cujo conteudo ja entra na chave por modelCacheKey; nao provavam o termo que diziam provar. O de versao do prompt usava NewPromptBuilderWithoutTemplates, cujo digest falha e desliga o reaproveitamento inteiro: com o termo removido da chave o teste continuava verde (medido: mutacao sobreviveu).
  • Digest do diff, identidade do repo, identidade do binario e armazenamento bruto no --pr nao tinham teste.

docs.title: O que mudou
docs.text:
• cmd/aurumcode/cache_redaction.go: redactCachedIssues aplica a cada achado lido do cache a mesma redacao campo a campo da fronteira do modelo (prosa com o marcador +/-/espaco preservado, como redactLinesKeepingMarkers). redactedVerdictReuse envolve o passo de reaproveitamento do pipeline do gate: o que ele acrescenta do cache (sufixo da uniao monotonica) e redigido com o filtro da execucao antes de qualquer passo seguinte ou sink; um achado que, redigido, iguala um ja existente e descartado.
  • cmd/aurumcode/review_gate.go: o pipeline monta o passo de reaproveitamento dentro de redactedVerdictReuse.
  • cmd/aurumcode/review_cache.go e main.go: partitionByCache recebe o filtro e redige cada achado de cache por arquivo.
  • cmd/aurumcode/aur524_test.go: os testes de modelo e de versao do prompt usam o servidor alternante (mesma identidade de provider); o de versao do prompt usa um builder com digest valido e diferente (um item de catalogo a menos) e afirma essa diferenca.
  • cmd/aurumcode/aur553_test.go: testes novos (abaixo).
  • tests/acceptance/AUR-553.sh: seletores all, AC-001..AC-004, MUT-001; cada mutacao e aplicada numa raiz temporaria nova e precisa compilar e deixar o teste correspondente vermelho.

A semantica monotonica do AUR-524 nao mudou: o reaproveitamento so acrescenta achados.

docs.title: Como cada AC/MUT foi provado
docs.text:
Comando: bash tests/acceptance/AUR-553.sh all no container compartilhado.

AC/MUT Teste Mutacao (vermelha) AC-001 TestAUR524AC002PromptVersionChangeInvalidatesReuse prompt_version: PromptVersionDigest vira "" na chave AC-001 TestAUR524AC002ModelChangeInvalidatesReuse model_name: modelCacheKey ignora Name() e o modelo resolvido AC-002 TestAUR553AC002DiffChangeWithoutSHAInvalidatesReuse (--pr, sem GITHUB_SHA) diff_digest: DiffDigest vira "" AC-003 TestAUR553AC003RepoIdentityChangeInvalidatesReuse (remote origin muda) repo_identity AC-003 TestAUR553AC003BinaryIdentityChangeInvalidatesReuse (main.version muda) binary_identity AC-003 TestAUR553AC003PRStoresRawIssues (regra desligada, depois religada) raw_storage: guarda os achados ja filtrados pela config AC-004 / MUT-001 TestAUR553AC004PRCachedFindingRedacted (review publicado no GitHub falso) unredacted_verdict: pipeline sem redactedVerdictReuse AC-004 / MUT-001 TestAUR553AC004BaseCachedFileFindingRedacted (stdout do --base) unredacted_file_cache: partitionByCache sem redacao

O teste do --pr forja o verbete do veredito com um segredo registrado no filtro, um token com forma de credencial e um cabecalho Authorization citado como linha de diff; exige que o achado forjado chegue ao review publicado (prova nao vazia), que nenhum canario apareca no corpo publicado, no stdout ou no stderr, e que o marcador de redacao apareca.

Ultimas linhas reais:

mutation prompt_version -> RED: aur524_test.go:411: round2 exit=3, want 0: a changed prompt-version digest must never reuse round1's stored breach
mutation model_name -> RED: aur524_test.go:375: round2 must call the provider again, got 1 calls
mutation diff_digest -> RED: aur553_test.go:314: round2 exit=3, want 0: a changed diff must never reuse round1's stored breach
mutation repo_identity -> RED: aur553_test.go:281: round2 exit=3, want 0: a changed repository identity must never reuse round1's stored breach
mutation binary_identity -> RED: aur553_test.go:297: round2 exit=3, want 0: a changed binary identity must never reuse round1's stored breach
mutation raw_storage -> RED: aur553_test.go:337: round2 (rule enabled) exit=0, want exitFindings(3): the raw finding stored by round1 must fire under the enabled rule
mutation unredacted_verdict -> RED: aur553_test.go:232: published PR review leaked the cached canary "aur553-registered-canary-7f3e1d"
mutation unredacted_file_cache -> RED: aur553_test.go:258: stdout leaked the cached canary "aur553-registered-canary-7f3e1d"
AUR-553/all/pass

bash tests/acceptance/AUR-524.sh all continua AUR-524/all/pass.

docs.title: Limites
docs.text:
• redactCachedIssues repete a regra de prosa de internal/review.redactLinesKeepingMarkers, que e privada e fica fora dos paths deste card; unificar exige exportar a funcao de internal/review num card que possua o pacote.
  • A redacao mascara valores com forma de segredo; ela nao torna confiavel o restante do texto de um verbete forjado (por exemplo um Origin forjado de achado deterministico). O reaproveitamento continua so podendo acrescentar achados, nunca aprovar.
  • No teste de modelo a mutacao cai primeiro pelo cache por arquivo (que usa a mesma modelCacheKey), antes do veredito.

Rollback: reverter os commits do card (paths do card apenas).

docs.title: AUR-554 — Guia e demonstração do gate corporativo
Status
docs.text: Entregue: docs/gate-corporativo.md (guia), demo/gate-corporativo/ (demonstração executável em containers), tests/acceptance/AUR-554.sh (aceite selado, sem rede) e este registro. O aceite selado confere o guia contra a demonstração e compara o out/ versionado com expected/; a execução completa roda fora do sandbox (containers e imagens públicas fixadas) e seu log está abaixo.

docs.title: Execução real
docs.text:
• Data: 2026-10-02, run.sh all (build, up, fail, fix, pass, verify, down), cerca de 67 s com as imagens já baixadas, a partir de um estado limpo (nenhum container, rede ou volume da demonstração).
  • Comando: demo/gate-corporativo/run.sh all, depois demo/gate-corporativo/run.sh --check (saída CHECK OK).

docs.title: Decisões
docs.text:
• Determinismo do inventário. Um Dependency-Track recém-criado não tem espelhos de vulnerabilidade, então a fase up cria pela API uma política de violação (demo-componente-proibido, condição de coordenadas sobre lodash 4.17.15, estado FAIL). O limiar policy_violations: 0 reprova; em produção critical/high vêm dos espelhos do servidor.
  • Métricas assíncronas no v5. O gate espera o token de processamento do BOM (processing: false) e só então lê as métricas: no v5 o fluxo de processamento inclui avaliação de política e atualização de métricas, e todas as execuções reais (várias, durante o desenvolvimento e a gravada) leram métricas consistentes com o BOM enviado, sem espera extra. A chave do time (BOM_UPLOAD, VIEW_PORTFOLIO, VIEW_POLICY_VIOLATION) não tem permissão de refresh de métricas (HTTP 403 observado), por isso run.sh não o chama; ele apenas relê as métricas e as violações pela API para nomear a política e o componente no log.
  • Sem provedor de modelo. AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE aponta para {"issues":[]} e --seguranca liga o passe determinístico. Sem fixture, o review ficaria quality_skipped (inconclusivo) e gate.inconclusive: block reprovaria o pass.
  • Aprovação exige o inventário "aprovado". Com inconclusive: warn, um servidor ou segredo ausente sairia com código 0; o aceite exige a linha ssor_dtrack: aprovado (...) no pass.
  • Rede. O container do produto usa --network host porque o gate só aceita https:// ou http:// com IP de loopback, e o servidor publica a porta em 127.0.0.1:8081.

docs.title: Achados para quem integra
docs.text:
• Na criação desta spec, review.yml gerava o SBOM e assinava depois da revisão e não repassava os secrets do Dependency-Track. O AUR-555 (main, c2ebe75) corrigiu: SBOM antes da revisão, DTRACK_API_KEY/DTRACK_PROJECT_ID opcionais (required: false) expostos só ao passo da revisão, assinatura só depois de a revisão terminar com sucesso, bundle .sigstore.json como artefato. O guia e workflow-obrigatorio.yml descrevem isso (o chamador repassa os secrets; code-review.yml usa secrets: inherit). A prova do AUR-555 é estrutural (YAML); continua sem execução em runner real, e esta demonstração reproduz a ordem em containers locais.
  • aurumcode sign não tem --key: a chave efêmera da demonstração entra pelo wrapper do Cosign.
