docs.title: Fora do escopo desta entrega
docs.text:
• Assinatura keyless (OIDC do GitHub Actions): só a chave efêmera foi exercitada na demonstração; o fluxo keyless segue documentado em docs/configuration.md.
  • Assinatura de imagem de artefato (sign_artifacts): desligada na demonstração.
  • Execução do workflow reutilizável em um runner real do GitHub (a integração em review.yml é do AUR-555, provada só estruturalmente).

docs.title: AUR-555 — Workflow liga o SBOM ao Dependency-Track com secrets opcionais
Status
docs.text: Implementado em .github/workflows/review.yml (ordem dos passos, secrets opcionais). code-review.yml já usa secrets: inherit e continua válido sem mudança; action.yml não é afetado (não declara secrets nem o gate). Prova: cmd/aurumcode/aur555_test.go::TestAUR555*, que lê o workflow como YAML. Aceite: tests/acceptance/AUR-555.sh.

docs.title: Ordem final e justificativa
docs.text:
1. SBOM (AUR-549): precisa existir antes do review porque o gate ssor_dtrack (AUR-550) lê o arquivo de quality_gates.ssor_dtrack.sbom_generator.output_file durante o review. O passo roda aurumcode sbom --repo . com cwd no checkout do PR, que resolve output_file dentro desse checkout; o container do review monta o mesmo checkout em /github/workspace (seu cwd), onde SBOMOutputFile() é lido. Nenhuma flag nova.
  2. Review (gate): envia o SBOM ao Dependency-Track e compara métricas. É o único passo com DTRACK_API_KEY/DTRACK_PROJECT_ID no env.
  3. Assinatura (AUR-551): só quando o review terminou com sucesso (success() && steps.review.outcome == 'success') — não se assina um artefato reprovado. Antes (always()) ela rodava mesmo com review reprovado.
  4. Upload do bundle de assinatura (inalterado; if-no-files-found: ignore).

Consequência aceita: o passo de SBOM não é mais always() e sem dependência do review; se ele falhar (digest do Trivy inválido, falha de geração com gate.inconclusive: block), o job falha antes do review. Sem sbom_generator declarado, o comando sai com 0 sem fazer nada e o fluxo é o de antes.

docs.text: DTRACK_API_KEY e DTRACK_PROJECT_ID em workflow_call.secrets, com required: false: os nomes padrão de api_key_secret/project_id_secret. Repasse ao container do review via -e. Sem ssor_dtrack, nada é exigido (AC-004). Com ssor_dtrack e secret ausente, o gate é inconclusivo (dtrack_secret_missing) segundo gate.inconclusive, nunca aprovado (AC-003).

docs.title: Cobertura
docs.text:
• AC-001 TestAUR555SBOMStepPrecedesReview
  • AC-002 TestAUR555SecretsOptionalAndScopedToReview
  • AC-003 TestAUR555MissingSecretIsInconclusiveNeverApproved (block e warn; o caso warn também existe em TestAUR550SecretMissingWarnsNeverBlocks, o caso block é novo)
  • AC-004 TestAUR555WorkflowValidWithoutDTrackAndSignsOnlyAfterReview
  • MUT-001: o script move o passo de SBOM para depois do review numa cópia do workflow (AUR555_WORKFLOW) e exige que o teste de AC-001 caia.

docs.title: Limites
docs.text: Os testes provam a estrutura do YAML, não a execução no runner do GitHub. Se api_key_secret/project_id_secret forem renomeados, o workflow não repassa os novos nomes (ver docs/configuration.md).

docs.title: AUR-556: analysis findings count toward the policy gate
Design
docs.text:
• internal/config.GateConfig.Sources is the closed list (skills, analysis, sast); ValidateSources runs in Validate at load time and SourceEnabled answers which origins count (empty = all).
  • Precedence is the existing one for gate: the central policy's Gate replaces the repository's wholesale, so repository sources never apply under a policy.
  • cmd/aurumcode/gate_sources.go holds the adapter: foldGateSources, called once by runReview and runPRReview right after evaluateGate, folds the SAST decision (applySASTGate, unchanged, SAST issues withheld when sast is excluded) and applyAnalysisGate. evaluateGate skips skill rules when skills is excluded; its signature is unchanged.
  • Analysis findings come from a fresh analysis.Runner.Analyze(diff) plus config.ApplyRuleConfig, not from result.Issues, so a model reply can neither forge nor drop them. They honor AUR-520 exceptions.
  • Origin is named in the gate line (origem analysis), therefore in the parecer, stderr and the audit record's reason. It is also a typed field: each render.AuditFinding counted by the gate carries Origin (skills|analysis|sast, JSON origin, omitted when empty), set where the finding is counted. The SARIF writer derives each result's origin from BlockingFindings and writes it as properties.origin; the message has no origin suffix. gateDecision.FindingOrigins no longer exists.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: No gate: no behavior change. Existing tests that declare a gate over a fixture containing a hardcoded secret now pin sources: [skills] to keep isolating the skill origin.

docs.title: Corpus
docs.text: tests/benchmark/out/multilang-report.* regenerated with -update-aur523: approved-with-defect total 3 -> 1 (java 1 -> 0, python 1 -> 0); the remaining one is the php case no rule detects; recall unchanged.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text: properties.origin and blocking_findings[].origin exist only for findings the gate counted; non-blocking findings carry no origin.

docs.title: AUR-557 -- Gate as one pipeline of contributors shared by --base and --pr
docs.text: A refactor with no change of behavior. runReview (--base) and runPRReview (--pr) each wired every gate source by hand, in two places, in the right order, inside functions of 1203 and 1033 lines. This card gives the gate one pipeline, and gives each path explicit phases.

docs.title: internal/gate
docs.text:
Type Role Result One run's gate outcome: what gateDecision was (Active, Fail, Inconclusive, Breach, Lines, BlockingFindings, AppliedExceptions), plus the analysis-data audit, Reason (the machine-readable inconclusive motive, comma-joined) and Trail (what each contributor added; never published). cmd/aurumcode keeps type gateDecision = gate.Result. Run The inputs every contributor shares: context, effective config, diff, the review result, Extra deterministic findings that count toward the gate but stay out of Review.Issues (the --base security pass), language, redaction filter and writers, verified repo identity, clock. Contributor Name(), Origin(), Apply(ctx, *Run, *Result) error. Pipeline NewPipeline, Names, Contributors, Run. Applies contributors in declared order and records each one's footprint in Result.Trail.

The failure rule lives in Pipeline.Run, once. A contributor that returns an ordinary error does not abort and is never read as "no findings": the result becomes Active and Inconclusive, Reason gains contributor_error:<name>, a line names the failure, and under gate.inconclusive: block the result Fails (exit 1, never approved). Later contributors still run. An error wrapped with gate.Fatal aborts the pipeline and is returned unchanged: configuration errors keep their historical exit 2 (aurumcode review: gate: ...).

docs.title: Contributors and their order (cmd/aurumcode/review_gate*.go)
docs.text:
assembleGatePipeline is the only place the pipeline is declared:

  1. exceptions -- declares that no exception can match when the repository identity could not be verified (AUR-520). The matching itself is applied by contributors 3 and 5, where a finding is judged.
  2. verdict-reuse -- reuses or stores a concluded verdict (AUR-524).
  3. policy-skills -- evaluateGate: the policy's skill sections (AUR-519, AUR-556 gate.sources).
  4. sast -- applySASTGate (AUR-548).
  5. embedded-analysis -- applyAnalysisGate (AUR-556).
  6. analysis-data -- applyAnalysisDataGate (AUR-533).
  7. dependency-track -- applyDTrackGate (AUR-550); it may replace the redaction filter and wrap the writers, which the path reads back from the Run.

This is exactly the order the two functions used. A new gate source is one Contributor in its own file and one line in assembleGatePipeline.

docs.title: Phases
docs.text:
Both paths run: resolve inputs, run analyses, run the gate pipeline, publish and exit. A phase returns (exit, done) so every early return N of the original keeps its code.

--base --pr entry runReview (review_base.go) runPRReview (review_pr.go) resolve inputs review_base_inputs.go review_pr_inputs.go analyses review_base_analysis.go, review_base_quality.go review_pr_model.go, review_pr_analysis.go, generateReview in pr.go gate review_base_gate.go review_pr_gate.go publish and exit review_base_publish.go review_pr_publish.go

They differ only in where the diff comes from and how the review is published (stdout report / exit code versus comments, formal review and commit statuses).

docs.title: Before / after
docs.text:
Function Before After runReview 1203 lines 27 lines runPRReview 1033 lines 20 lines largest function in cmd/aurumcode 1203 128 (runSign, untouched)

TestAUR557NoFunctionExceedsLineLimit (go/ast) fails if any production function of cmd/aurumcode exceeds 150 lines.

docs.title: What stayed in cmd/aurumcode, and why
docs.text:
The decision logic of each source (evaluateGate, applySASTGate, applyAnalysisGate, matchException, applyAnalysisDataGate, applyDTrackGate, reuseOrStoreGateVerdict, applyStructuralCoverage) still lives in its original file (policygate.go, aur548.go, gate_sources.go, aur520.go, aur533.go, aur550.go, aur524.go, structural_coverage.go). The contributors are thin adapters that call it. Moving those functions into internal/gate would change the signature of every one of them, and the existing tests (package main) call them directly; the card forbids editing those tests. Moving them is a follow-up (together with the file renames of AUR-558). Structural coverage is not a contributor: it runs before the inconclusive reason is ranked and its notice must keep its place in Limitations ahead of the changelog and policy notices, so moving it into the pipeline would reorder the published output.

Source-anchored acceptance mutations: AUR-519.sh, AUR-537.sh, AUR-538.sh and AUR-543.sh apply sed mutations anchored on exact statements of main.go/pr.go, and may not be edited. Those statements stay where the scripts look for them, with unchanged semantics: gateInconclusiveReason = "provider_failure", cacheErr = promptDigestErr and the three-tab result.Metadata[prompt.PolicyGateWithheldKey] = "true" (shared applyGateOutcome) in main.go; the transport-failure and budget branches (rc = 1, rc := reportBudgetExceeded(stderr, limiteUSD, err) followed by if !gateDeclared {) in generateReview in pr.go.

docs.title: Adaptations of existing tests
docs.text:
Two existing tests assert, by reading the source, that a path calls the shared passes. The assertion is unchanged; only the files it reads changed, because the bodies moved.

  • aur499_test.go TestAUR499PublishedBody: reads review_base_inputs.go and review_pr_inputs.go instead of main.go and pr.go for buildChangelogSection(.
  • passes_test.go TestAUR490SharedPasses: the same five calls per path, now asserted across the phase files that hold them.

No other existing test or acceptance script was edited.

docs.title: Acceptance (tests/acceptance/AUR-557.sh)
docs.text:
Selector Proves AC-001 The all selector of the existing acceptances in the subset below, run unedited on the refactored code. AC-001-full The all selector of all 15 existing acceptances the contract lists with a script (518 519 520 521 524 537 538 543 548 549 550 551 552 555 556). AUR-553 has no acceptance program in the repository and is not run. AC-002 TestAUR557PathsShareOnePipeline: a real --base run and a real --pr run execute the same contributor names, in the declared order, equal to assembleGatePipeline. AC-003 internal/gate pipeline tests: declared order; a failing contributor is inconclusive and never approved in block, warn and unset modes; fatal errors abort. AC-004 No function of cmd/aurumcode exceeds 150 lines. AC-002-MUT-001 In a copy, the --pr path alone drops the last contributor: AC-002 must fail and AUR-550's acceptance must fail. all AC-002, AC-003, AC-004, MUT-001 and AC-001 over the subset 519, 537, 538, 543, 524, 548, 550, 556 (the ones carrying source-anchored mutations and the gate wiring).

Timing, measured in go-shared with a shared GOCACHE (a go shim first on PATH pins it, since every nested script sets its own): the 15 all selectors take about 490 s together (518 cold 138 s, 538 107 s, the rest 8-32 s each). That is past the 450 s margin of the sealed profile's 600 s limit, so all carries the subset and AC-001-full carries every script.

The sealed profile's /tmp is a 512 MB tmpfs, which a cache shared by scripts that build mutated variants outgrows. The script therefore warms the cache once with the unmodified module, marks it, and deletes every entry created after the mark when a nested script or the mutation copy finishes. Measured with oci-run --profile go-unit-offline-v1 --card AUR-557 (all): exit_code 0 in 270 s.

docs.title: Anchors realigned (card v2)
docs.text:
AUR-522.sh and AUR-533.sh anchored mutations on lines the refactor moved. They are realigned with the same mutation and the same expected red:

  • AUR-522.sh AC-004-MUT-001: now anchored (unique) on the mergeReviewCoverage(result.Metadata, uninspectedPRNotices(p.diff, p.verifiedDir), ...) call in review_pr_analysis.go.
  • AUR-533.sh AC-003-MUT-002: now anchored (unique) on applyAnalysisDataGate(ctx, run.Cfg.AnalysisData, mode) in review_gate_contributors.go. The call is shared by both paths, so the mutation removes it for both; the --pr tests still go red.

AC-001-full now also runs 522, 533 and 559; all adds 522 and 533 to its subset.

docs.title: AUR-558 -- cmd/aurumcode organised by responsibility, with a structural guard
docs.text: A refactor with no change of behavior, continuing AUR-557.

docs.title: Decision logic into internal/gate
docs.text:
Before (cmd/aurumcode) After (internal/gate) evaluateGate, severityRankOf, effectiveSeverityRank, origin constants (policygate.go) policy.go: EvaluateGate, SeverityRankOf, EffectiveSeverityRank, OriginPolicy, OriginRepo matchException and its lines/markers (aur520.go) exceptions.go: MatchException, TruncateToUTCDate, AcceptedExceptionLine, ExpiredExceptionLine, ExceptionsConfigured, RepoIdentityUnavailableNotice applyAnalysisGate, analysisIssuesForGate, gateSASTIssues, foldGateSources (gate_sources.go) sources.go applySASTGate (aur548.go) sast.go: ApplySASTGate applyAnalysisDataGate (aur533.go) analysisdata.go applyDTrackGate, mergeDTrackGate, wrapWriterWithFilter (aur550.go) dtrack.go reuseOrStoreGateVerdict, the verdict key and store (aur524.go) verdict.go applyGateOutcome (main.go) outcome.go: ApplyOutcome the seven contributor adapters (review_gate_contributors.go) contributors.go: exported types with fields

What the gate needs from the command is injected, not imported: the prompt digest (VerdictReuseContributor.PromptDigest), and the review-context cache key (VerdictKeyInputs.ContextKey, a lazy func() string so a nil provider is only touched when a verdict can be reused, as before). The binary identity (binaryIdentity, which reads the command's version) stays in verdict_inputs.go and arrives in VerdictKeyInputs.BinaryIdentity.

review_gate.go is the only production file of cmd/aurumcode that imports internal/gate. It declares the pipeline (assembleGatePipeline) and the command's names for the package (gateDecision, gateRun, gateOriginRepo, and so on); every other file uses those names.

docs.title: AUR-559: prompt and skills without language names in Go
Design
docs.text:
• grammar.Provider gains IsComment(lang, line) (isComment, ok bool). The runtime adapter (internal/grammar/comment.go) parses the line with the named grammar and reports a comment when a node whose type contains comment (tree-sitter vocabulary shared by every grammar) starts at the first non-blank byte and reaches the end of the line. ok == false means the runtime has no such grammar.
  • internal/grammar/catalog/aliases.yml (embedded, version + aliases section) maps selector spellings to the runtime's canonical grammar names. Canonical names are never listed: they come from Provider.Languages(). LoadAliases(provider, policyRoot) is strict (unknown keys, or an alias whose target is not a grammar of the runtime, are load errors). A central policy overrides with .aurumcode/grammar/aliases.yml; its aliases section replaces the embedded one.
  • internal/prompt/commentfilter.go: isCommentLine(provider, line, language) has no language knowledge. A language without grammar is never a comment (no filter) and CommentFilterNotice appends a declared notice to the change-scope paragraph (ChangeScopeWith, used by ReviewChangeScope). HasSubstantiveCodeChange keeps its signature and delegates to HasSubstantiveCodeChangeWith(diff, provider).
  • internal/context/skills/languages.go: Languages resolves the file's language through Provider.Detect and selector names through the alias catalog. Set.SelectWith returns Selection{Skills, Warnings}; an unknown language in a selector produces a warning that Provider.Provide renders as a ### Skill selection warnings block. Set.Select keeps its signature.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
• Behavior change (intended): the old fallback "//, /*, */ is a comment" is gone. A line is a comment only if the grammar parses it as one, so a bare block-comment continuation line (* text) in a multi-line hunk is no longer filtered (a single line cannot be classified without its block context). Files without grammar get no filter, plus the notice.
  • Selector spellings that were accepted as raw file extensions now work only when listed in the alias catalog (the shipped catalog covers the common ones); anything else is declared as unknown instead of ignored. shell is an alias of the runtime's bash.
  • analyzer's language_catalog.yml is untouched.

docs.title: AUR-560: documentation site (MkDocs Material, container, GitHub Pages)
Design
docs.text:
• mkdocs.yml (root): docs_dir: docs, Material theme in pt-BR, navigation.tabs, navigation.indexes, navigation.top, search.suggest, search.highlight, content.code.copy, plugin search with lang: [pt] (static index, works offline), strict: true and link/anchor validation at warn level so --strict fails on a broken link, a page missing from the nav or a missing anchor. The nav is explicit and grouped by capability: Inicio, Comecando, Referencia, Guia corporativo, Qualidade e benchmark and Specs. There is no extra plugin, so the image alone builds the site.
  • Home page is docs/index.md: product overview with one section per capability, each linking its reference anchor in configuration.md and naming its tutorial. A tutorial that does not exist yet is cited as em breve (AUR-56x,tutorials/.md) without a link, so --strict stays green; AC-004 requires the link as soon as the file exists.
  • docs/README.md stays the repository entry point. MkDocs drops README.md when index.md exists (and the specs link ../README.md), so scripts/docs/hooks.py re-adds it as its own page at /README/ (exclude_docs lists /README.md only to silence the conflict warning). docs/site/ (the older hand-written interactive guide, published by pages.yml) is excluded except workflow.yml, which getting-started.md links.
  • scripts/docs/build.sh runs docker run ... <image@digest> build --strict; scripts/docs/serve.sh serves locally. Both read the single line of scripts/docs/image.lock, which the workflow reaches by calling build.sh. The Specs section (and Tutoriais when docs/tutorials exists) is not in mkdocs.yml: scripts/docs/hooks.py on_config injects it before page validation (specs/README.md, then specs/AUR-*.md in natural order; for tutorials tutorials/README.md, then tutorials/*.md). Nothing to maintain by hand; AC-002 reimplements the rule in bash and fails on any orphan page.
  • .github/workflows/docs.yml: push to main (paths docs/**, mkdocs.yml, scripts/docs/**, the workflow) and workflow_dispatch. Job build runs scripts/docs/build.sh (same image, --strict) and uploads site/; job deploy (needs: build, environment github-pages) is the only one with pages: write and id-token: write.

O que entrega

• demo/tutoriais/_lib/tutorial.sh: framework comum (fases, out/<caso>.log, --check por grep -F de cada linha de expected/<caso>.txt, imagem do produto por Dockerfile, provedor falso AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE, --network none, repositórios descartáveis em .estado/). docs.title: Decisões
docs.text:
• O produto, não um simulacro. Cada caso roda /app/aurumcode da imagem construída do Dockerfile da raiz, sem rede, com o provedor falso. A fase de PR é conferência do workflow, não revisão de PR (ver "Limites").
  • Blocos literais. O texto marca <!-- arquivo: PATH --> antes do bloco; o aceite compara byte a byte. Saídas esperadas marcam <!-- saida: caso -->; cada linha do bloco tem de existir em out/<caso>.log (AC-002).
  • Saída copiada, não escrita. expected/ guarda só linhas que provam o caso; o texto só mostra linhas presentes no out/.
  • .gitignore. O .gitignore da raiz ignora *.log; demo/tutoriais/.gitignore reabre out/ para os tutoriais (o out/ é evidência versionada).
  • Texto de rede omitido, declaradamente. Só em politica-central/analysis-data, o detalhe do erro de rede (varia por ambiente) é trocado por <detalhe de rede omitido do registro> por TUT_SED, documentado no run.sh.

docs.title: Achados sobre o produto (honestidade do tutorial)
docs.text:
1. Seleção por linguagem e apelidos não estão ligados ao review. .aurumcode/skills/<nome>/SKILL.md com languages: [...] (internal/context/skills, AUR-468/AUR-559) é biblioteca: só testes (tests/unit/AUR-468.go, internal/context/skills/aur559_test.go) chamam skills.Providers. A CLI usa review.context.skills (lista explícita) e .aurumcode/instructions/*.md com applyTo (escopo por caminho). O tutorial de skills prova o negativo (selecao-por-linguagem) e usa o escopo por caminho como seletor funcional. O bloco ### Skill selection warnings (apelido desconhecido) só existe na biblioteca; teste que o cobre, rodado no go-shared nesta execução: TestAUR559AliasResolvesAndUnknownIsDeclared PASS.
  2. Skill ausente no repositório é aviso, não erro. continuing without that context, e achados que citam os ids dessa skill são descartados; o parecer pode sair Approve. Na política central é erro de carga (exit 1). O tutorial registra isso.
  3. fix imprime um patch sem contexto (@@ -6,1 +6,1 @@): git apply exige --unidiff-zero (o docs/getting-started.md mostra git apply sem a flag).
  4. Cobertura parcial sem gate sai 0 com veredito Comment; só com gate.inconclusive: block reprova (exit 1, partial_coverage).
  5. analysis_data declarado numa política faz o review consultar o GitHub: sem rede é inconclusivo (analysis_data_unavailable).

docs.title: Limites
docs.text:
• Não há runner do GitHub nem servidor GitHub reutilizável fora dos testes Go (os falsos de cmd/aurumcode/*_test.go são httptest em Go); então o caso "revisão de PR" prova só a coerência do workflow do chamador com .github/workflows/review.yml (inputs, secrets, permissões, policy_*). O review --pr não é executado.
  • AURUMCODE_PROMPT_CAPTURE (observação do prompt) é variável interna de observação, usada só para mostrar o que chegou ao modelo.
  • AURUMCODE_CACHE_DIR não é definido: o aviso gate verdict reuse unavailable aparece nos logs e é esperado.

O primeiro é um GitHub falso e local (127.0.0.1) que só serve o que review --pr consulta e registra o que o produto publica; o segundo expõe tut_pr_servidor, aurum_pr (container em --network host, só para alcançar o loopback do host) e tut_pr_log. docs.title: Decisões
docs.text:
• O SAST usa o Semgrep real da imagem com uma regra local (sem rede); a falha do SAST é simulada por um semgrep falso na frente do PATH (gate/fakebin/), declarado no run.sh e no tutorial.
  • Conclusões do script são frases RESULTADO: afirmadas por expect_rc; o que não tem caso executado leva a marca "não demonstrado aqui" no texto.

docs.title: Não demonstrado aqui (declarado)
docs.text:
• Artefato de análise vencido (analysis_data_stale) e digest divergente: exigem um servidor de releases; só analysis_data_unavailable (sem rede) é executado.
  • SBOM na auditoria: exige Trivy e rede.
  • Upload ao Code Scanning (upload-sarif) e a proteção de branch: configuração do GitHub; a demo confere o workflow do chamador contra o review.yml real.
  • Compartilhamento da mesma chave de veredito entre --base e --pr (ver achado 4).
  • --pr roda contra o GitHub falso: prova o que o produto publica, não o comportamento do GitHub.

docs.title: Achados sobre o produto (o que o tutorial mediu)
docs.text:
1. A origem na linha de gate não é uniforme. A auditoria e o SARIF trazem o origin tipado (skills, analysis, sast), mas a linha impressa diz origem analysis só para a análise; para o SAST diz origem policy (de onde veio a configuração) e para a skill não diz nada. docs/configuration.md promete a origem "nas linhas de gate". Caso gate/fontes.
  2. Falha ao gravar a auditoria não reprova. --auditoria num diretório inexistente avisa em stderr e a saída segue 0 numa revisão limpa; um pipeline de compliance precisa conferir o arquivo. Caso auditoria-sarif/falha-caminho-invalido.
  3. A mensagem do gate é redigida de forma diferente do relatório. A linha de gate mostra [REDACTED] secret or credential assigned inline onde o relatório mostra Hardcoded secret or credential assigned inline.
  4. --base e --pr gravaram chaves de veredito diferentes neste experimento (mesmo SHA, política, modelo e identidade do repositório; diff do GitHub falso). Não é possível afirmar que seja defeito do produto: o diff do servidor falso pode diferir do real. Caso reaproveitamento/veredito-base-e-pr.
  5. O cache por arquivo atravessa uma mudança de política (a resposta do modelo não mudou); só o veredito é por política. Documentado nos tutoriais.
  6. Observado em experimento exploratório, não versionado: sem provedor, com --seguranca e inconclusive: warn, um achado [error] do passe de segurança (security/hardcoded-secret) apareceu no relatório e a saída foi 0 com fail_on: [high]. Precisa de um caso próprio antes de ser afirmado.

O que entrega
docs.text:

  • tests/acceptance/AUR-563.sh: all, AC-001..AC-004, AC-002-MUT-001; seletor desconhecido sai 64.

docs.title: Decisoes
docs.text:
• Mesmo contrato do AUR-561. Blocos <!-- arquivo: PATH --> identicos aos arquivos; <!-- saida: caso --> com linhas literais do out/; --check por grep -F; linhas RESULTADO: sao conclusao do script.
  • Nenhum digest digitado a mao. O unico lugar com digests e demo/gate-corporativo/images.lock; compose.yml do Dependency-Track usa ${DTRACK_IMAGE}/${POSTGRES_IMAGE} exportados pelo run.sh a partir dele. O Semgrep e o da imagem do produto (versao de .board/bootstrap/locks/scanners.yml).
  • Provedor sempre fixture; aurumcode sempre na imagem do produto, com --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)". Rede: none, exceto sbom-dependency-track (--network host: o gate so aceita https ou IP de loopback) e dados-de-analise (um servidor falso que atende como a API do GitHub dentro do mesmo container, com CA de demonstracao gerado a cada execucao em .estado/).
  • api.github.com no aceite. O produto fixa esse endereco para o analysis_data (nao ha variavel que o troque); o AC-003 o admite na lista de dominios, junto dos reservados. E a API publica do GitHub, nao dado interno.

docs.title: Achados sobre o produto
docs.text:
1. Corrida nas metricas do Dependency-Track (grave). O gate le as metricas assim que o servidor responde processing: false, e a avaliacao de politica pode terminar depois. Num servidor novo, a primeira revisao com lodash 4.17.15 leu policy_violations=0 e aprovou o que a politica reprova (2 de 2 vezes); em outra execucao, logo apos trocar a dependencia, leu a violacao antiga e reprovou. O tutorial contorna com um aquecimento e a funcao dt_assenta (linha assentamento: nos out/) e declara que e contorno do script. Causa nao investigada; vale um card (reler ate estabilizar).
  2. --semgrep-bin nao existe: o Semgrep e resolvido pelo PATH (cmd/aurumcode/aur548.go). O caso de falha poe um Semgrep falso a frente no PATH.
  3. O check_id leva o caminho do arquivo de regras (semgrep:regras.demo-sem-eval no repositorio; semgrep:policy.regras.demo-sem-eval sob politica em /policy). rule_packs local e relativo ao repositorio; sob politica precisa ser absoluto.
  4. Com o SAST inconclusivo o parecer ainda diz No issues found.; so as linhas SAST ... inconclusive mostram o estado real.
  5. O endereco da API do GitHub do analysis_data e fixo no binario; so o seam de teste Go o troca. AURUMCODE_GITHUB_API_URL vale so para o cliente de PR.
  6. aurumcode sign valida o arquivo do bundle, nao o exit do Cosign: Cosign que sai 0 sem bundle falha (cosign exited 0 but wrote no signature bundle). Sem quality_gates.supply_chain, sign sai 0 sem assinar. Falha de assinatura usa o exit 1 generico (exitQualityNotReviewed).
  7. xbom --help imprime so a linha de uso (sem lista de flags); a politica central precisa de .aurumcode/config.yml valido mesmo para xbom; um catalogo do repositorio ou da politica substitui o embutido por inteiro.
  8. Resultado inconclusivo de analysis_data ou do Dependency-Track deixa o veredito em Comment, nunca Approve, com warn ou block.
  9. O Trivy lista package-lock.json@None como componente de arquivo sem versao.

docs.title: Limites (o que NAO foi demonstrado)
docs.text:
• Pacote do registry do Semgrep com sucesso (p/...): exige rede; o caso prova so a falha sem rede (e nao distingue timeout de recusa de rede).
  • max_critical/max_high: o Trivy roda com --scanners license e o servidor nao tem feeds, entao critical/high ficam 0; so policy_violations e provado. dtrack_unreachable, dtrack_http_error e 403 nao foram executados.
  • Timeout do Dependency-Track: provado contra um servidor falso (sempre processing: true), nao contra o Dependency-Track real.
  • Assinatura keyless, upload do artefato e verify-blob keyless: so conferencia estatica (exigem o OIDC do GitHub Actions). Assinatura de imagem real (exige registry).
  • xBOM: envio ao Dependency-Track, modelo real, prompt sobrescrito pela politica.
  • analysis_data: GitHub real, release imutavel, repositorio privado com token, analysis_data_invalid, download da copia OSV. O workflow agendado so e conferido estaticamente. Nao ha runner real do GitHub em nenhum tutorial.

docs.title: AUR-564: tutoriais executáveis de qualquer linguagem, benchmark de recall e operação
O que entrega
docs.text:
• Três tutoriais em docs/tutorials/ (pt-BR), no padrão do AUR-561, linkados da página inicial (docs/index.md) e do índice docs/tutorials/README.md: qualquer-linguagem.md (5 casos e 1 falha), benchmark.md (4 casos e 1 falha) e operacao.md (6 casos e 1 falha).
  • As demonstrações em demo/tutoriais/{qualquer-linguagem,benchmark,operacao}/ (run.sh com uma fase por caso, expected/, out/ da última execução real). Não houve arquivo novo em _lib/.
  • tests/acceptance/AUR-564.sh: all, AC-001..AC-004, AC-002-MUT-001; seletor desconhecido sai 64.

docs.title: Decisões
docs.text:
• qualquer-linguagem roda o produto na imagem (_lib), com --network none, --user do chamador e provedor falso; o contexto estrutural é mostrado pelo prompt capturado (AURUMCODE_PROMPT_CAPTURE), com símbolos de nome único por gramática para provar a contribuição de cada uma.
  • benchmark e operacao não rodam o produto na imagem: o harness (tests/benchmark) e o oci-run são o objeto. Go só pelo go-shared; casos que alteram o corpus ou o repositório trabalham numa cópia em .estado/ (git archive HEAD ou clone local) e devolvem a posse ao usuário com chown dentro do container.
  • Tempos de go test e o caminho do módulo são normalizados no registro (<t>s, <modulo>), assim como os caminhos do worktree e do HOME na operação.
  • O aceite confere comandos e flags: aurumcode contra --help; .board/bin/* contra o disco; go-shared <sub>, flags do oci-run, go test -run X e -update-aur523 contra a fonte.
  • O AC-004 do card: cada script de .board/bin e cada profile do registro são citados em operacao.md (com crase), e o aceite confere com ls e o registro.

docs.title: Achados sobre o produto (honestidade dos tutoriais)
docs.text:
1. -update-aur523 sai com exit 1 ao acrescentar o primeiro caso novo, embora regrave manifest e relatório: o teste que confere o corpus roda antes do que o regrava. docs/benchmark.md não menciona isso. O tutorial manda rodar de novo sem a flag. (Fora dos paths do card: não corrigido.)
  2. O benchmark mede encanamento, não modelo: o "modelo" é um provedor falso por rótulo (hit/miss/silent/false_alarm). Com 2 defeitos por linguagem, o IC de Wilson de um recall 1.0 começa em 0.3424.
  3. Contexto estrutural é uma lista plana e ruidosa (List, util, Demo) e o YAML de CI não produz símbolo no exemplo.
  4. Seleção por languages: e apelidos não chegam ao review (AUR-565); só o applyTo de .aurumcode/instructions funciona.
  5. Profile fora do registro: trust-root-docker-v1 tem arquivo de profile e não tem entrada em registry.v1.json; release-build-v1 está em profile-owners.tsv e não existe no registro.
  6. Nem todo lock usa a imagem selada (go-git-offline-v1 usa golang@sha256:...), então o repin da imagem selada não os alcança.
  7. O aviso gate verdict reuse unavailable (AURUMCODE_CACHE_DIR not set) aparece em toda execução com gate sem cache.

docs.title: Causa da intermitência (exit 141) e correção
docs.text:
Sob set -o pipefail, consumidores que fecham o pipe cedo (| head -n1 dentro de $(...) e | grep -q .) fazem o grep da esquerda morrer com SIGPIPE (141) quando a saída é maior que o buffer do pipe, de forma intermitente. Nos quatro aceites (AUR-561.sh, 562.sh, 563.sh, 564.sh) head -n1 virou sed -n '1p' (lê tudo) e | grep -q . virou | awk 'END{exit NR==0}'. Nenhum head ou grep -q ao fim de pipe resta.

Prova: all dos quatro aceites, 3 vezes cada, 12 execuções simultâneas pelo go-shared, todas exit 0, nenhum 141. Mutação de domínio numa cópia (host fora da lista em docs/tutorials/gate.md): AUR-562.sh AC-004 e AUR-564.sh AC-004 reprovaram com url-real.

docs.title: AUR-566: fix emite diff unificado padrão com contexto
O problema
docs.text: O tutorial do AUR-561 mediu que aurumcode fix imprimia hunks sem linhas de contexto (@@ -6,1 +6,1 @@), que o git apply só aceita com --unidiff-zero, enquanto docs/getting-started.md mandava git apply sem a flag.

docs.title: O que muda
docs.text:
• internal/apply: BuildPlan(suggestions, fsys) e BuildPatch(suggestions, fsys) leem o arquivo de cada sugestão (por fs.FS; o fix passa os.DirFS(cwd)) e renderizam cada hunk com três linhas de contexto reais (contextLines), cabeçalhos --- a/x / +++ b/x e @@ -l,n +l,n @@ corretos. Sem dependência nova: o diff de linhas continua sendo o LCS próprio.
  • O contexto que o LCS da sugestão já continha é aparado e substituído pelo do arquivo, então cada lado tem no máximo três linhas.
  • Mudanças cujo contexto se toca (distância de até seis linhas) viram um só hunk; o número de linha do lado novo acompanha o deslocamento acumulado.
  • Arquivo sem newline final recebe \ No newline at end of file; acrescentar depois de uma última linha sem newline é recusado (falha fechada).
  • current_code que não bate com o arquivo, linha inexistente, arquivo ausente e sugestões sobrepostas fazem o plano falhar, nomeando arquivo e linha. Isso substitui a mensagem genérica "patch does not apply".
  • CreateFilePatch e DeleteFilePatch renderizam arquivo novo (--- /dev/null) e remoção (+++ /dev/null). O fix não os usa: uma sugestão sem current_code continua sendo descartada (o conteúdo das sugestões não muda, é non-goal); as funções são a API para quem criar ou apagar arquivos.
  • cmd/aurumcode: o fix valida com git apply --check sem flag e imprime o patch sem linha em branco final.
  • docs/getting-started.md, docs/tutorials/revisao.md e a demo demo/tutoriais/revisao (caso fix reexecutado, out/ regravado) usam git apply puro.

docs.title: Prova
docs.text: tests/acceptance/AUR-566.sh all: AC-001 (git apply sem flag num repositório de exemplo, correção no arquivo), AC-002 (contexto de três, cabeçalhos, arquivo novo e remoção aplicam com git apply; patch -p1 --dry-run quando patch existe), AC-003 (run.sh --check do tutorial), AC-001-MUT-001 (contexto zero reprova AC-001).

docs.title: Execução real
docs.text: bash demo/tutoriais/revisao/run.sh fix na imagem do produto (sem rede, uid do usuário): o patch saiu com @@ -3,6 +3,6 @@, git apply --check e git apply passaram sem flag, e a mesma sugestão, já velha, saiu com 1 e aurumcode fix: app.go:6: working tree does not match the suggestion's current_code.

docs.title: Limites
docs.text: Sem patch(1) no contêiner do Go, o patch -p1 --dry-run é exercido só onde o binário existe. O fix usa o diretório corrente como raiz dos caminhos.

docs.title: AUR-567: linha do gate mostra a origem tipada para toda fonte
O que entrega
docs.text:
• Um unico mapeamento de origem: internal/gate (OriginSkills, OriginAnalysis, OriginSAST, OriginSecurity, OriginDTrack, OriginAnalysisData). A linha do gate, BlockingFindings (auditoria e SARIF) e o Origin() de cada contribuinte usam o mesmo valor.
  • gate.FindingLine: a unica forma de uma linha de achado, <regra> - <mensagem> (severidade <s>, limiar <l>, origem <fonte>). No SAST a origem e sast, secao policy|repo (a secao de configuracao que decidiu, nunca no lugar da origem). O achado do Dependency-Track passa a trazer origin: dtrack na auditoria e (origem dtrack) na linha.
  • Mensagem consistente (causa, nao sintoma): o filtro de redacao do stderr le ...secret: <palavra> como um par chave/valor e trocava a primeira palavra da mensagem por [REDACTED]. O id da regra (analysis/hardcoded-secret) terminava em secret e a linha o juntava a mensagem por :. Agora a juncao e -; o filtro nao mudou.
  • Veredito e status (notas dos AUR-562 e AUR-568):
  • sem gate declarado, falha ao gravar auditoria/SARIF retem a aprovacao (ApplyArtifactFailures chama withholdApproval tambem sem gate): a review formal nunca e APPROVE antes do exit 1.
  • Decisao: com gate declarado a review formal segue o gate (gateAlignedReviewEvent): REQUEST_CHANGES so se o gate reprova; achado abaixo do limiar ou aprovacao retida e COMMENT; execucao limpa segue APPROVE. Sem gate, o comportamento historico (aviso ja pede mudancas). Antes, um aviso abaixo do limiar dava REQUEST_CHANGES com aurumcode/policy-gate verde. Registrado em docs/configuration.md e no tutorial.
  • Teste --pr dedicado do contribuinte security-pass (nota do AUR-569): achado de seguranca no --pr e exit 3, status failure, origem security no parecer e na auditoria.
  • Tutorial gate regravado (execucao real, imagem do produto); docs/configuration.md alinhado.
  • Adendo v2: o bloco de saida observada de docs/site/index.html que o aceite do AUR-497 compara byte a byte foi regravado com a saida real (cartoes 4 e 6, fix: o cabecalho do hunk tinha envelhecido); tests/acceptance/AUR-497.sh nao mudou e a comparacao segue byte a byte.

  • AC-002: TestAUR567GateLineAndReportShowTheSameMessage.
  • AC-003: tutorial e demo: bash demo/tutoriais/gate/run.sh --check e scripts/docs/build.sh; TestAUR567FormalReviewFollowsDeclaredGate, TestAUR567GateAlignedReviewEvent e a regressao em aur568_test.go (sem gate, a review nao e APPROVE).

docs.text:
• Decisao: a citacao (rule <id>: <titulo>) do relatorio e contrato fixado por varios cards done (reviewer.go, tests/unit, tests/e2e, tutoriais); nao muda. gate.FindingLine a escreve como (rule <id> - <titulo>) na linha do gate, entao a linha e o relatorio diferem so nesse separador, por causa da redacao, e a linha mostra Hardcoded Secrets (teste TestFindingLineSpellsTheRuleCitationWithoutAColon). O filtro nao foi tocado.

docs.title: Reancoragem da mutacao do AUR-538 (card v4)
docs.text: AUR-538.sh AC-001-MUT-001 saia com infrastructure/mutation-anchor-missing: a ancora (a linha de retencao com tres tabs em internal/gate/outcome.go) mudou de indentacao quando a retencao foi extraida para withholdApproval. A mutacao agora ancora na linha atual (result.Metadata[prompt.PolicyGateWithheldKey] = "true", um tab, exatamente uma ocorrencia) e a troca por _ = prompt.PolicyGateWithheldKey: mesma semantica (a revisao deixa de ser marcada como retida) e compila. docs.title: AUR-568: falha ao gravar auditoria ou SARIF nunca termina como sucesso
O que entrega
docs.text:
• internal/gate/artifacts.go: ArtifactFailure, os motivos audit_write_failed e sarif_write_failed e ApplyArtifactFailures, que dobra a falha na decisao do gate (inconclusivo pelo modo da politica quando gate esta declarado; aprovacao retida).
  • cmd/aurumcode/compliance_artifacts.go: writeComplianceArtifacts (uma funcao para --base e --pr) grava antes da publicacao e do exit, nomeia o caminho em stderr, aplica a falha ao gate e regrava o arquivo gravavel com a decisao final; devolve as falhas. --base e --pr retornam exitArtifactNotWritten (1) quando nenhum codigo do gate ja fecha a execucao.
  • Testes em cmd/aurumcode/aur568_test.go: pai e arquivo regular (ENOTDIR) e diretorio inexistente, para --auditoria e --sarif, com block, warn e sem gate, em --base e --pr, mais a regressao com caminho gravavel.
  • Tutorial auditoria-sarif (caso falha-caminho-invalido) regravado com a execucao real.

docs.title: Decisoes
docs.text:
• Exit sempre diferente de 0, tambem em warn: o modo da politica decide o status (failure ou inconclusivo) e o codigo (block: 1 pelo gate; demais: 1), nao se o artefato faltante e aceitavel.
  • Sem gate o status --check segue o de achados graves; so o exit muda.
  • Nao muda o formato da auditoria nem grava em lugar alternativo.

docs.title: AUR-569: achado determinístico acima de fail_on reprova em qualquer modo de inconclusivo
Reprodução (primeiro passo do card, commit b048183c)
docs.text:
Caso versionado demo/tutoriais/gate/achado-deterministico: política gate: {fail_on: [high], inconclusive: warn} (politica-alerta), --seguranca, sem provedor (TUT_FIXTURE=none), diff com dbPassword := "hunter2". Execução real na imagem do produto, antes da correção:

  • inconclusive: warn: exit_code=0; linhas policy gate: review inconclusive (quality_skipped) e o achado app.go:6: [error] ... (rule security/hardcoded-secret) no relatório; auditoria com origens: (nenhuma). FALHA ABERTA REPRODUZIDA.
  • inconclusive: block: exit_code=1, só pela ausência do parecer (quality_skipped); nenhuma linha de gate cita o achado.

docs.title: Causa raiz (mais ampla que o relato)
docs.text: Não era o modo de inconclusivo. Os achados do passe de segurança (security/*, review.SecurityScanWithCoverage) ficam fora de Review.Issues no --base (Run.Extra) e só chegavam ao gate pelo contribuinte policy-skills, que só conta ids citados por uma seção de skill da política. O contribuinte embedded-analysis só conta analysis/* (outro catálogo, que não casa dbPassword := "hunter2"). Logo um security/* nunca contava, em warn, block nem com provedor. O mesmo vale em --pr.

docs.title: Correção
docs.text:
• Novo contribuinte security-pass (internal/gate, depois de embedded-analysis): conta os achados do passe de segurança (campo Run.Security, preenchido por --base e --pr) com severidade >= fail_on, independentemente de gate.inconclusive: exit 3, linha com regra, severidade, limiar e origem security, e origin: security na auditoria.
  • Respeita config.ApplyRuleConfig, as exceções AUR-520 e gate.sources (conta sob a origem analysis, o catálogo embutido; sources: [skills] não conta). Não conta duas vezes um achado que o gate já tem (mesma regra, arquivo, linha).
  • O laço comum virou applyDeterministic, compartilhado com analysis.
  • Sem alterar o significado de warn para a ausência de parecer: sem achado determinístico, warn continua só avisando (exit 0); block continua exit 1.

docs.title: Aceite
docs.text:
• AC-001: caso versionado, --check verde, reprodução registrada aqui.
  • AC-002: TestAUR569SecurityFindingFailsGateInEveryInconclusiveMode (warn e block, exit 3).
  • AC-003: TestAUR569WithoutFindingWarnStillOnlyWarns, TestAUR569NoSecurityPassNoSecurityFinding e o caso do tutorial (diff sem segredo, exit 0).
  • AC-002-MUT-001: warn engolir o achado deixa AC-002 vermelho.
  • tests/acceptance/AUR-569.sh: all, AC-001..AC-003, AC-002-MUT-001; seletor desconhecido sai 64.

docs.text:

  • docs/specs/AUR-562.md ganhou uma linha, porque AUR-562.sh exige cada caso do run.sh registrado ali.

docs.title: AUR-570: o gate do Dependency-Track le as metricas so depois que assentaram
Defeito
docs.text: bom/token responde processing: false quando o SBOM foi ingerido. A avaliacao de politica e o recalculo das metricas terminam depois (medido no Dependency-Track 5.1.1: COMPLETED a ~1,47 s do envio, metricas atualizadas ~0,1 s depois). O gate lia metrics/project/{id}/current na primeira resposta e aprovava policy_violations=0 (achado 1 de docs/specs/AUR-563.md). Falha aberta.

docs.title: Comportamento (internal/dtrack/settle.go)
docs.text:
Depois do polling do token, Run chama SettledMetrics:

  1. GET /api/v1/metrics/project/{id}/refresh; qualquer status nao 2xx (403: a chave nao tem PORTFOLIO_MANAGEMENT, confirmado no servidor real) e tolerado e vira a nota dtrack_refresh_unavailable no parecer.
  2. Releitura de .../current a cada poll_interval_seconds. Uma leitura e fresca se lastOccurrence e posterior ao instante do upload (relogio do cliente) ou, quando nao, se lastVulnerabilityAnalysis de GET /api/v1/project/{id} e posterior ao upload. A segunda prova existe porque, medido no 5.1.1, lastOccurrence NAO se move quando as metricas recalculadas sao iguais as guardadas (reenviar o mesmo SBOM). Duas leituras frescas consecutivas com mesmos critical, high, policyViolationsTotal assentam; qualquer mudanca zera a contagem. 404 nas metricas espera.
  3. Sem assentar em timeout_seconds (janela propria, apos o token): ErrMetricsUnsettled, motivo dtrack_metrics_unsettled, inconclusivo pelo modo da politica (block reprova, warn nao aprova).

Sem campo de configuracao novo. Leituras = 2, fixo.

docs.title: Limites conhecidos
docs.text:
• A prova de frescor usa o relogio do cliente contra o do servidor; um servidor adiantado em relacao ao cliente enfraquece a prova por lastOccurrence (a estabilidade em duas leituras continua valendo).
  • Na prova por lastVulnerabilityAnalysis (SBOM inalterado), a politica ja avaliada e a anterior; uma politica alterada entre dois envios do mesmo SBOM so e vista se o servidor recalcular dentro da janela.
  • O tutorial roda contra o servidor real; os testes Go usam servidor falso.

docs.title: AUR-571: endereco da API do GitHub do analysis_data vem de configuracao
Contrato
docs.text:
• O resolvedor do analysis_data (internal/artifacts) e o cliente de PR (cmd/aurumcode/pr.go) leem a mesma variavel, AURUMCODE_GITHUB_API_URL, pela mesma funcao: config.GitHubAPIURL / config.ValidateGitHubAPIURL (internal/config/githubapi.go). Padrao: config.DefaultGitHubAPIURL (https://api.github.com), declarado nesse unico arquivo.
  • Aceito: https:// com host; http:// somente para IP de loopback literal (127.0.0.1, ::1). Recusado: http:// com nome ou IP nao loopback (inclusive localhost), outro esquema, credenciais, query ou fragmento. O erro nomeia a variavel.
  • No resolvedor, endereco invalido e analysis_data_invalid (inconclusivo pela politica, sem requisicao e sem recair no cache de outra origem); no cliente de PR, o review falha ao carregar com exit 1.
  • artifacts.Options.APIBase vazio, ou igual a DefaultAPIBase, significa "nao escolhido pelo chamador": vale a variavel. Qualquer outro valor (testes do pacote internal/gate) e usado como dado, validado do mesmo modo.

docs.title: AUR-572: ajuda completa por subcomando e parecer sem "No issues found." com inconclusivo
O problema
docs.text: Os tutoriais do AUR-563 mediram duas coisas: aurumcode --help listava só review e fix embora sbom, sign e xbom existam (e xbom --help imprimia uma linha de uso sem flags); e um SAST inconclusivo ainda imprimia No issues found., com o estado real só nas linhas SAST ... inconclusive (achados 3 e 5 de docs/specs/AUR-563.md).

docs.title: O que muda
docs.text:
• cmd/aurumcode/subcommands.go: um registro único (subcommands(): nome, resumo, exemplo, construtor do FlagSet, função). O despacho de run, o --help geral e o --help de cada subcomando leem esse registro; não há lista paralela. Cada subcomando declara suas flags em um construtor (newReviewFlagSet, newFixFlagSet, newSBOMFlagSet, newSignFlagSet, newXBOMFlagSet) usado pelo parser e pela ajuda, que imprime PrintDefaults do próprio FlagSet: a ajuda não pode listar flag que o parser não conhece nem esquecer uma que ele conhece.
  • Rodapé comum da ajuda de cada subcomando: Configuração e referência: docs/configuration.md (seção <título>), gerado uma vez em printSubcommandHelp a partir do campo docSection do registro (sem lista paralela).
  • parseSubcommandFlags unifica a convenção: --help pedido é stdout e saída 0; erro de uso é stderr e saída 2.
  • internal/render.NoFindingsLine(reason): No issues found. só quando o motivo de inconclusivo é vazio; senão Sem achados nas fontes concluídas; inconclusivo: <motivos>. O motivo é gate.Result.Reason, que já junta SAST, Dependency-Track, analysis_data, cobertura parcial e provedor (mesmo vocabulário do gate), sem repetição.
  • docs/getting-started.md e docs/configuration.md documentam as duas coisas.

Fora do escopo: flags novas; formato do parecer além dessa frase; o caminho --pr (o parecer publicado já traz o estado inconclusivo próprio).

docs.title: Prova
docs.text: tests/acceptance/AUR-572.sh all: AC-001 (a ajuda geral lista os cinco; cada <sub> --help traz toda flag do FlagSet, comparada por VisitAll), AC-002 (SAST inconclusivo -> sem No issues found. e com a frase; caso limpo mantém a frase), AC-003 (AUR-561..564.sh AC-003 verdes), AC-002-MUT-001 (voltar a imprimir No issues found. com inconclusivo reprova AC-002).

docs.title: AUR-573: CI verde e aceites de cards done voltam a rodar no main
Causa medida do CI vermelho

Measurement (before the fix)

Ran the real binary (review --base HEAD~1) over tests/fixtures/repos/git-demo with AURUMCODE_PROMPT_CAPTURE, inside the shared Go container. docs.title: AUR-575: o gate falha fechado por construção
Medido antes (auditoria de 2026-10-03, base e6b708fe)
docs.text:
1. config.Parse validava gate, exceções, analysis_data, ssor_dtrack e supply_chain, mas nunca quality_gates.sast (SastConfig.Validate só era chamado pelos testes): engine: gitleaks rodava o Semgrep calado e um rule_packs com cara de flag passava.
  2. O .aurumcode/config.yml do repositório era lido com yaml.Unmarshal leniente; só a política central fazia um segundo decode com KnownFields(true). gate: {fial_on: [error]} não declarava gate e aprovava.
  3. gate.inconclusive ausente valia "", tratado como warn em todo lugar: SAST habilitado com Semgrep ausente saía 0 com status success (alerta).
  4. Cada fonte decidia sozinha o modo: Dependency-Track e analysis_data calculavam Fail pelo modo, o SAST só marcava Inconclusive, o pipeline tratava o erro de contribuidor à parte, e a falha de artefato também.
  5. sources.go (loop determinístico: catálogo embutido e passe de segurança) e sast.go descartavam com continue uma severidade que SeverityRankOf não reconhecia.

docs.title: O que mudou
docs.text:
• internal/config/decode.go: decodeStrict (KnownFields(true), documento vazio = configuração zero) é o decoder de Parse; o decode extra da política em central.go saiu (a mensagem é a mesma: parsing <arquivo>: yaml: unmarshal errors: line N: field X not found in type ...).
  • Parse chama QualityGates.Sast.Validate().
  • internal/config/gate.go: resolveInconclusive(fallback) normaliza o valor; GateConfig.InconclusiveMode() resolve ausente para block quando o gate é declarado. internal/config/inconclusive.go: Config.InconclusiveMode() resolve ausente para block quando há gate ou scanner habilitado (SAST, Dependency-Track, analysis_data); warn só escrito.
  • internal/gate/pipeline.go: ApplyInconclusiveMode é o único ponto que transforma Inconclusive em Fail (modo block, ou modo ilegível); o pipeline aplica após cada contribuidor, e a falha de artefato pós-pipeline reaplica a mesma função. Dependency-Track, analysis_data, artefatos, erro de contribuidor e EvaluateGate só marcam Inconclusive (EvaluateGate ainda lê o modo para não graduar um run bloqueado). aurumcode sbom usa ApplyInconclusiveModeValue com o modo do gate.
  • internal/gate/policy.go: GateRankOf conta severidade desconhecida como error; usado em sast.go e sources.go.
  • Testes que afirmavam o padrão antigo (warn implícito) foram atualizados para o novo contrato; analysisdata_test.go usava a chave inexistente language na raiz (o decode estrito revelou; a chave real é review.language); aur572_test.go escreve inconclusive: warn porque testa a linha final do relatório, não o modo.
  • Tutorial do gate: política politica-sast-padrao (SAST habilitado, sem gate), caso com PATH=/sem-semgrep que sai 1; expected/ e out/ regravados com a imagem do produto; docs configuration.md, gate-corporativo.md e tutorials/gate.md atualizados.

docs.title: AUR-576: one review session serves --base and --pr
Measurement (before the change, base 1569d875)
docs.text:
• baseReview (review_base.go, ~45 fields) and prReview (review_pr.go, ~55 fields) held the same data under different names (repoCfg/cfg, codebaseContextText/codebaseText, contextBlockDigest/contextBlockDig, ruleCatalogDigest/ruleCatalogDig, rawIssues/rawIssuesSnapshot).
  • Two phase lists (runReview: resolveInputs, analyze, decideGate, publish; runPRReview: validate, resolveInputs, analyze, runGate, publish), each with its own analyze sub-list.
  • Two inconclusiveReason (main.go and review_pr_gate.go): base provider_failure/quality_skipped, PR the constant and model_parse_failure; the rest of the ranking was copied.
  • Two exit ladders: base (quality failed > gate > artifacts > fail-on) and PR (comment failures > --exigir-qualidade degraded > status failure > gate > artifacts > fail-on > --check status).
  • runSAST copied (only PR had sastReasonUnverifiedCheckout); writeComplianceArtifacts assembled twice, with run.IssuesForGate() on base and result.Issues on PR.
  • Security findings: base kept them in run.Extra and applied the rule config separately, and its raw verdict snapshot did NOT contain them; PR merged them into result.Issues before the snapshot.
  • os.Getenv("GITHUB_SHA") read in both gate phases (and AURUMCODE_BASE_SHA, GITHUB_REPOSITORY, LLM_MODEL, AURUMCODE_OUTPUT_FILE, AURUMCODE_PR_PERMISSION_MODE across the phases).
  • Package-variable seams: gatePipelineObserver, evaluateGate, newGatePipeline, diffContentDigest (review_gate.go), resolveWithFilesHook (verified_checkout.go), newCacheDigestBuilder (review_cache.go); Now: time.Now fixed in both gate phases.
  • runPRReview took 9 positional parameters.

docs.title: What changed
docs.text:
• internal/gate/reason.go: ModelOutcome (reviewed, skipped, provider failed, parse failed), typed Reason constants and RankReason, the one ranking (provider failure > skipped > model parse failure > degraded parse > SAST reason > partial coverage). Tokens are unchanged. NotReviewedRules maps an outcome to "not reviewed" (never, when quality is required, always); the requirement is a typed QualityRequirement (optional, required).
  • internal/gate/exit.go: ExitPolicy(ExitInputs) ExitDecision, one ladder of rungs with typed inputs and a named cause; ExitClean/ExitBehavioral/ ExitFindings. cmd's exitFindings, exitQualityNotReviewed, exitArtifactNotWritten now alias these values.
  • internal/review/session: Phase, Order (resolve, model, evidence, gate, publish), Run, and Source data: LocalDiff and PullRequest with their NotReviewedRules, where the security findings live and the notice printed when "not reviewed" decides. AUR-579 changes the model/evidence order by editing Order only.
  • cmd/aurumcode/review_session.go: reviewState (the shared fields, one name each), reviewDeps (clock, Semgrep runner, gate observer, codebase resolver, prompt digest builder, environment snapshot; zero fields take the production default), reviewEnv (read once by readReviewEnv), reviewIO.
  • cmd/aurumcode/review_evidence.go: the shared evidence steps: runSecurityPass, joinSecurityFindings (the one place that decides where security findings live), snapshotAndApplyRules (snapshot = issues + the kept-apart security findings, on both sources), runSAST(root, blocked), findingsAtThreshold, writeArtifacts (one assembly from the gate run: run.IssuesForGate()).
  • cmd/aurumcode/review_gate.go: the shared gate phase (runGate, gatePipelineInputs, executeGate with the injected observer), inconclusiveReason over gate.RankReason, decideExit over gate.ExitPolicy. The seams became plain calls or injected dependencies.
  • baseReview and prReview embed reviewState, implement session.Phases.Step, and keep only their own fields. review_base_gate.go and review_pr_gate.go are gone; failOnExit, exitCode and the two writeArtifacts are gone.
  • runPRReview(reviewIO, prReviewOptions): the PR number, repository, --publicar, --na-linha and --check joined the options struct. runReviewWith(reviewIO, args) is the entry that takes dependencies.
  • Tests that substituted package seams inject them through reviewDeps (aur524, aur536, aur543, review_gate_test via runReviewWith, runPR499With, runAUR536ReviewWith). No t.Setenv("PATH") was added (6 before, 6 after).

docs.title: Per-source mapping (data, not code)
docs.text:
Outcome --base --pr provider failed always not reviewed not reviewed only with --exigir-qualidade parse failed always not reviewed (not reachable today: base classifies every model error as provider failed) not reviewed only with --exigir-qualidade skipped gate decides; --exigir-qualidade classifies it as provider failed (AUR-458) not reachable

Unifying these divergences is a product decision for a later card; no e2e exit code changes here.

docs.title: Exit precedence (one ladder)
docs.text:
comment publish failure (1) > not reviewed (1) > status publish failure (1) > gate breach (3) > gate block (1) > artifact not written (1) > --fail-on (3)

--check status code. It is the union of the two old ladders: base had no publication rungs, and on every input both old ladders already agreed with it, so no fail-closed choice changed an exit. The notice printed when "not reviewed" decides is source data (only --pr prints the --exigir-qualidade line, as before).

docs.title: Snapshot change (AC-003)
docs.text: The --base raw verdict snapshot now includes the security pass's findings, as --pr's always did. The verdict-reuse key is unchanged; a verdict stored by an older binary without security findings can only be re-evaluated with fewer findings, and the gate's own security contributor still counts the current run's security findings.

docs.title: How AC-002 is proven
docs.text:
• TestAUR576SameInputsSameExitThroughTheSession (cmd/aurumcode): for each row it builds a reviewState per source with the same config, diff, model outcome, findings and injected dependencies (fixed clock, a Semgrep runner that is not installed, an empty environment), then runs the real evidence steps, the real gate pipeline (runGate) and the real exit decision (decideExit), and compares the exit codes and the published policy gate: lines. Rows: provider failure (block), parse failure (block), scanner missing, artifact not written over a --fail-on finding, a finding above the gate threshold, a finding above --fail-on, clean; a row whose gate must speak fails if it published no line. Declared divergent rows: provider failure under warn (--base 1, --pr 0) and provider failure with a breach (--base 1, --pr 3).
  • TestAUR576SameInputsSameExitOnBothSources (internal/review/session): the same table over RankReason, the sources' NotReviewedRules and ExitPolicy.
  • TestExitPolicyPrecedence, TestRankReasonOrder (internal/gate).
  • MUT-001 is three edits, each RED: a second exit ladder in the --base publisher (AC-001's AST test), a reordered shared ladder (the ladder and table tests), and a --base-only rung putting --fail-on above a missing artifact in decideExit (the behavioral table above).

docs.title: Environment still read outside the snapshot
docs.text: The review path no longer reads GITHUB_SHA, AURUMCODE_BASE_SHA, GITHUB_REPOSITORY, LLM_MODEL, AURUMCODE_OUTPUT_FILE or AURUMCODE_PR_PERMISSION_MODE outside readReviewEnv. Still read where they were: provider selection (LLM_API_KEY, LLM_BASE_URL, LLM_MODEL, AURUMCODE_LLM_FIXTURE, AURUMCODE_PROMPT_CAPTURE in main.go and the model cache key), the GitHub client (GITHUB_TOKEN, the API URL), the CI context file and AURUMCODE_POLICY (flag resolution). Moving the provider and client construction behind the session is left for the card that splits them (AUR-584).

docs.text:
Script Was Now AUR-519 MUT-001 main.go gateInconclusiveReason = "provider_failure" internal/gate/reason.go return ReasonProviderFailure -> return ReasonNone AUR-557 AC-002-MUT-001 review_pr_gate.go executeGate("--pr", ...) with newGatePipeline review_gate.go res, ok := s.executeGate(pipeline, reason), prefixed with a --pr-only gate.NewPipeline(...[:len-1]...) AUR-450 MUT-001 review_base_analysis.go printSecurityCoverage(b.stderr, ...) review_evidence.go printSecurityCoverage(s.stderr, ...) AUR-504 MUT-001 replacement os.Getenv("GITHUB_SHA") replacement p.env().githubSHA (the same snapshot) AUR-505 MUT-001 pr.go p.qualityDegraded = true pr.go p.model = modelParseFailed

AUR-519's re-anchored mutation now drops provider_failure on both paths, because the ranking is shared; it turns RED through the same test (TestAUR519GateInconclusiveProviderFailureBlocks).

docs.title: Measured before (base 85209c53, audit of 2026-10-03)
docs.text:
• Adding a scanner touched 12-14 files and 5 lists: the const/switch of gate.sources (config.GateConfig.ValidateSources), the fixed pointer QualityGatesConfig.Sast, the quality_gates.sast block of ApplyCentralPolicy, gate.OriginSAST, the dedicated gate.SASTContributor{SectionOrigin, Issues, Reason}, the SAST* fields of gatePipelineInputs, runSASTPass/realSemgrepRunner in cmd/aurumcode/sast_pass.go, the session's runSAST, RankReason's SASTReason.
  • SastConfig.Engine was decorative: EngineName() returned "semgrep" and the runner called analysis.NewRunner().Semgrep without reading it.
  • The SARIF rebuilt each finding's origin by a rule|path|line join with BlockingFindings and dropped every blocking finding no review issue carried: the Dependency-Track breach (ssor_dtrack) was in the audit and missing from the SARIF.
  • fmt.Sprintf("%s (rule %s)", f.Message, f.RuleID) was written in three places (gate/sources.go, cmd sast_pass.go, cmd passes.go).
  • The Semgrep execution lived in internal/analysis/semgrep.go, beside the embedded regex catalog and go vet.

docs.title: What changed
docs.text:
• internal/scanner (new): Scanner{Name(); Run(ctx, Request) (Report, error)}, Report{Findings, Complete, Version}, Finding.ToIssue(origin) (the one conversion; analysis.Finding is now an alias of scanner.Finding), Request{Root, Trust, Options, Command}, the registry (Register, Lookup, Names, NamesIn, Categories, KnownSource) of Engine{Scanner, Category, Origin, Validate}, and the Executor that runs an engine with a timeout and turns an error, a missing binary or Complete=false into the inconclusive reason <category or name>_{unavailable,execution_error,invalid_output,incomplete} (FailureReason), never into zero findings.
  • internal/scanner/semgrep: the Semgrep engine (code moved from internal/analysis/semgrep.go with its tests, plus the PATH runner from cmd). Category sast, origin sast, option rule_packs. The policy flags --disable-nosem and --x-ignore-semgrepignore-files are kept under Trust: TrustPolicy. internal/scanner/engines is the closed list of compiled engines (one blank import each); internal/config imports it, so every binary that parses a configuration holds the engines.
  • internal/config: quality_gates.scanners: [{engine, enabled, required, fail_on, options}] (scanners.go); quality_gates.sast is read as the semgrep entry (SastConfig.AsScanner, always required), and its engine must be a registered engine of category sast. Parse refuses an unknown engine (quality_gates.scanners[<engine>].engine: unknown engine ... (registered: semgrep)), an engine declared twice (sast alias included), a bad fail_on and options the engine refuses. mergeScanners (scanners_policy.go) replaces the quality_gates.sast block of ApplyCentralPolicy: engine by engine, a required policy entry wins and the repository's entry (including enabled: false) becomes the warning <key> do config do repositório foi ignorado: a política central decide sozinha (the same text as before for quality_gates.sast); a policy entry that is not required yields to the repository with its own named warning. FromPolicy(engine) records which effective entries are the policy's. gate.sources and gate.triage validate against skills, analysis and the registry (engine names and categories); sast remains the category of every SAST engine, and the error text keeps listing skills, analysis, sast.
  • internal/gate: sast.go became scanner.go with Scan (entry, engine, section, issues, reason) and ApplyScannerGate; ScannerContributor{Scans} replaces SASTContributor (pipeline name scanners); RankReason reads ScannerReason. SASTIssues, FoldSources and OriginSAST are gone.
  • cmd/aurumcode: scanner_pass.go replaces sast_pass.go: runScanners runs every enabled entry through reviewDeps.scanners (a scanner.Executor; the injected runner of the session is now the executor), joinScanners states each inconclusive scan. The gate phase passes the scans to the one contributor, the triage maps each scan by the engine's Answers. Nothing in cmd or gate names an engine.
  • internal/render/gatefindings.go: GateSARIFFindings.

docs.title: One gate finding for the audit and the SARIF (AC-005)
docs.text: Result.BlockingFindings is the one record of what counted: the audit's blocking_findings is written from it, and the SARIF now reads every origin from it too. The SARIF still lists the review's issues (they carry the message, the code context for the fingerprint, the assessment and the suppression, which the gate finding does not); the match by rule, path and line only attaches the gate finding's origin to that issue. What changed is that a blocking finding no issue carries is no longer dropped: it becomes its own SARIF result with its origin (ssor_dtrack, origin dtrack, message ssor_dtrack (origem dtrack)).

docs.title: Observable output
docs.text: The Semgrep engine keeps the origin sast: the gate line (origem sast, secao <policy|repo>), the inconclusive line (SAST (semgrep, origem sast, secao repo) inconclusivo (sast_unavailable)), the limitation (SAST (Semgrep) inconclusivo: ...), the audit and the SARIF are byte-identical for every existing configuration, so AUR-497's block and the gate and sast tutorials did not have to change. A new engine's origin is its name.

docs.title: AUR-578: the review prompt is a template with budgeted slots, sent as messages
Measurement (before the change, base e6b708fe)
docs.text:
• internal/prompt/templates/review.md received {{.Metrics}}/{{.CIContext}} while buildUserContent wrote ## Change Summary, ## Existing CI Context and ## Code Changes in Go; ## PR history, ## Codebase context, ## Review memory (builder.go), ## Review Coverage (coverage.go) and ## Repository context (config/provider.go) were Go string literals.
  • config.contextInjectingProvider appended the context block after the budgeted prompt (prompt+" "+block), outside TrimToFit/fixedOverhead, and its type assertion hid optional provider interfaces.
  • Reviewer.GenerateReviewWithContext (177 lines) sent System+" "+User as one string through a concrete *llm.Orchestrator; MaxTokens: 0 disabled the prompt budget by default.
  • DefaultRuleCatalog was a hand-written mirror of review/rules/*.yml; MaxRuleCatalogTokens = 512 was a Go constant.
  • ReviewIssue had no origin nor model assessment.
  • formatLanguages iterated a map: the ## Languages section of the system prompt came out in random order (measured: two runs of the same golden test differed at byte 1900). It is now sorted; this is the only byte change to an existing section, and it replaces a nondeterministic order with a fixed one.

docs.title: What changed
docs.text:
• internal/prompt/templates/review.md: the main body is unchanged (system message). Named {{define}} slots now hold every user-message section: user_header, pr_history, codebase_context, review_memory, deterministic_evidence + evidence_item, available_tools + tool_item, coverage, repository_context, repository_context_slot.
  • internal/prompt/slots.go, sections.go, evidence.go: slot rendering; BuildOptions gains Evidence, Tools, RepositoryContext. Each is counted in fixedOverhead (inside the budget). Evidence and tools admit whole items under their ceiling and render - N omitidos pelo orçamento desta seção. Empty input renders nothing (cmd bytes unchanged until AUR-579).
  • internal/prompt/templates/limits.yml + limits.go: default ceilings (prompt 120000, rule catalog 512, evidence 4096, tools 1024); MaxRuleCatalogTokens derives from it; PromptBuilder.SetSlotLimits.
  • budgeting.go: when every segment fits, TrimToFit keeps the diff order (a ceiling that trims nothing must not reorder hunks; the priority sort put f:10 before f:2). TestTrimToFit_Deterministic now pins that order.
  • internal/review/rules/catalog.go: leaf package embedding the rule YAMLs; prompt.DefaultRuleCatalog derives from it.
  • internal/llm/messages.go: MessageCompleter capability, FlattenMessages, SystemUserMessages, Unwrapper and As[T] (capability lookup through pass-through decorators); ResolveModelKey and AsToolCaller use As. Orchestrator.CompleteMessages sends messages to a capable provider and the flattened text otherwise (estimate always on the flattened text). litellm.Provider.CompleteMessages sends system and user separately.
  • internal/review: Reviewer depends on Completer; GenerateReviewWithContext is four stages (preparePrompt, complete, parse, applyGates, plus annotateResult), each under 70 lines. ReviewContext gains RepositoryContext, Evidence, Tools; every evidence/tool field is redacted. Config.PromptTokenBudget defaults from limits.yml and never caps the reply. PromptDigest and RequestCacheKey.
  • internal/review/cache/request_key.go: RequestKey(prompt, evidence, tool-results digests) and DigestOf.
  • pkg/types: ReviewIssue.Origin, ReviewIssue.Assessment (EvidenceAssessment, statuses confirmed|disputed|needs_context). The parser clears a model's origin and drops an assessment with an unknown status or no evidence id; the reviewer redacts the assessment.
  • internal/config/provider.go: the block is rendered by prompt.RenderRepositoryContext (same bytes, title in the template). wrap.go: contextInjectingProvider is documented as the compatibility path and deliberately does not implement Unwrapper.
  • Dead code removed: BuildReviewPrompt, buildReviewPromptFallback (iso_scores fallback), TruncatePrompt, formatDiffContent and their tests (builder_test.go). Zero production callers (grep over cmd, internal, tests).

docs.title: AUR-579: the model weighs the deterministic evidence
Measured before (base 19219477)
docs.text:
• session.Order was resolve, model, evidence, gate, publish: on both --base and --pr the model answered before the security pass, the embedded analysis and Semgrep ran; their findings were appended to the result afterwards and the model never saw them (ReviewContext.Evidence existed since AUR-578 and was never filled by cmd).
  • The repository context reached the model through config.WrapProviderWithWarnings, a decorator that hid the provider's capabilities (separate system/user messages); fixedModelProvider (--limite) did not implement llm.Unwrapper.
  • The model cache and verdict-reuse key (reviewContextCacheKey) carried no evidence digest; the per-file model cache stored issues only.
  • The model had no way to answer per evidence item, and nothing checked an evidence_id against what was offered.

docs.title: What changed
docs.text:
• internal/review/session/session.go: Order is resolve, evidence, model, gate, publish.
  • Evidence phase (cmd/aurumcode/review_evidence.go, review_base_analysis.go, review_pr_analysis.go): the security pass, the embedded analysis (staticAnalysisIssues) and SAST run first and touch no review result; each finding gets its engine origin (security, analysis, sast). offerEvidence (review_weighing.go) turns them into prompt.EvidenceItems in a fixed order (origin, file, line, rule) with ids E1..En, the redacted diff line as snippet and the side.
  • Model phase: both sources send ReviewContext.Evidence and ReviewContext.RepositoryContext; the context block is built by config.BuildContextBlockWithWarnings (buildRepositoryContext) and the provider is no longer wrapped. fixedModelProvider implements llm.Unwrapper (it forwards requests unchanged); profileProvider alters the request and deliberately does not. The phase ends with joinEvidence: the model's assessments are copied onto the evidence, the evidence joins the result exactly where it did before (security in the issues on --pr and apart on --base, analysis after the model's issues, SAST last), then the rule config, the verdict snapshot, the SAST notice and the coverage, so stdout/stderr keep their previous order.
  • Answer format: the deterministic_evidence slot of internal/prompt/templates/review.md (rendered only when evidence exists, so the system prompt and every evidence-free prompt keep their bytes) asks for evidence_assessments: evidence_id, status (confirmed|disputed|needs_context), justification, correlates_with, priority, suggestion, and says the engine already counts each item. pkg/types: ReviewResult.EvidenceAssessments, and EvidenceAssessment gains Correlates, Priority, Suggestion. The parser treats a malformed evidence_assessments as an optional section (discarded and recorded, not a degraded parse). internal/review/assessments.go (weighAssessments) keeps only assessments of offered ids with a known status (top-level and issue-level), first per id, normalizes priority, keeps only correlations to other offered ids, and names every refusal in assessment_discard_warning, printed on stderr by both sources. The model never writes Origin (the parser clears it; the engine sets it) and never changes a severity.
  • Sinks: terminal report (printAssessment: origem: <engine> | avaliacao do modelo: <status> [<id>] prioridade ... - <justification>, correlation, suggestion), audit (evidence_assessments[] with origin and assessment; proposed_exceptions), SARIF (properties.assessment beside properties.origin, only for assessed findings, so every other SARIF keeps its bytes).
  • Gate (internal/gate/triage.go, proposed.go, contributors.go): Run.Triage holds the disputed finding keys and the sources whose disputes demote. reviewState.triage (review_gate.go) fills the sources only without a central policy, from gate.triage; under a policy nothing is demoted, including a triage the policy itself declares. The analysis, security (under analysis), SAST (never for a policy-origin section) and repository skills contributors drop demoted findings and record them in Run.Demoted; each demotion is printed and added to the limitations. Every disputed finding that still counts becomes a proposed exception (ProposeExceptions / RenderProposedExceptions): the exceptions YAML with rule, path and the model's reason, and placeholders for owner, expiry and (without a verified identity) the repository. It is text only; nothing reads it back.
  • internal/config/gate.go: gate.triage (map source -> model|none), validated in Parse (unknown source or value is an error); default none.
  • Caches (AC-005): reviewState.contextCacheKey is the old context key when no evidence was offered (evidence-free runs keep their keys) and otherwise cache.RequestKey{PromptDigest: <old key>, EvidenceDigest: DigestOf(evidence)}; it feeds both the per-file cache lookup and the verdict-reuse ContextKey. A review that offered evidence bypasses the per-file model cache (errEvidenceNotCacheable): the cache stores issues, not assessments, so a hit would silently lose the model's verdict on the evidence. Reviewer.RequestCacheKey is not used directly because the cache is per file (its prompt digest covers the whole diff).
  • Offline fixture (internal/review/fixture_cases.go): a fixture whose JSON has the reserved key aurumcode_fixture answers by case (prompt_contains -> response, else default); every other fixture is returned verbatim as before.

docs.title: How the evidence section is proven not decorative (AC-004)
docs.text: The gate tutorial's fixtures answer with an assessment only when the prompt contains [E1] origem=analysis regra=analysis/hardcoded-secret, text that only the evidence slot emits; otherwise they answer approve with no assessment. The recorded expected therefore contains the model's assessment and the proposed exception only because the section reached the prompt. TestAUR579EvidenceSectionDecidesTheAnswer asserts the same through the real command, and the AC-004 mutation (renderEvidenceSlot returns "") turns it RED by assertion: without the section the same fixture answers its default, the report has no assessment and the proposed exception disappears, so the expected lines of gate/modelo-pondera would diverge.

docs.title: Fail-closed choices
docs.text:
• The model never writes Origin; an assessment with an unknown status, no id, or an id never offered is discarded and named on stderr.
  • The evidence ceiling limits only the prompt: the slot states "N omitidos" and every finding still reaches the gate (the gate reads the passes, never the offered list).
  • Under a central policy the assessment never changes the count; a dispute is only a proposal a human may copy.
  • renderSlot (internal/prompt/slots.go) still panics on a template error: this card did not touch slots.go (pending from AUR-578, left as is).
